title: Cafer Mahiroğlu soruşturmasında üçüncü dalga: Ece Üner ve Özgürdeniz Bayramoğlu gözaltında
content:
İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı, Halk TV’nin sahibi Cafer Mahiroğlu’na yönelik yürüttüğü soruşturma kapsamında 12 kişi hakkında yeni gözaltı kararı verdi.




Savcılık, 12 kişi hakkında ‘suçtan kaynaklanan mal varlığı değerlerini aklama’, ‘suç işlemek amacıyla örgüt kurma ve örgüte üye olma’, ‘halkı yanıltıcı bilgiyi alenen yayma’, ‘rüşvet’, ‘ihaleye fesat karıştırma’ ve ‘Vergi Usul Kanunu’na muhalefet’ suçlamalarıyla gözaltı talimatı verdiğini duyurdu.




Aralarında Halk TV sunucuları Ece Üner ve eşi Özgürdeniz Bayramoğlu’nun da bulunduğu dokuz kişi gözaltına alındı. Halk TV Haber Koordinatörü Hakan Kürşad Oğuz ise yurt dışında olduğu için gözaltına alınmadı.




Hakkında gözaltı kararı verilen isimler şunlar:







Ece Üner (Halk TV spikeri)




Deniz Bayramoğlu (Halk TV spikeri)




Haydar Rüzgar (Bustech firma yöneticisi)




Ulaş Eroğlu (İzmir Büyükşehir Belediyesi Makine İkmal Bakım ve Onarım Daire Başkanı)




Aşkın Tahan (İzmir Büyükşehir Belediyesi Makine İkmal Bakım ve Onarım Daire Başkanlığı personeli)




Ali Kemal Korgan (Korganlar isimli firma sahibi)




Hamza Okuyucu (HMF Taşımacılık firma sahibi)




Ahmet Keçiyokuşu( Bustech isimli firma yöneticisi)




Halit Akın (Bustech isimli firma satın alma müdürü)




Emre Kaya (Esbakım firma sahibi)




Kürşad Oğuz (Halk TV Haber Koordinatörü)




Recep Ersü (Repar isimli firma sahibi – başka bir soruşturma kapsamında tutuklu)







Başsavcılığın Halk TV’ye yönelik iddiaları




Cafer Mahiroğlu’na yönelik soruşturmada bugüne kadar 19 kişi gözaltına alındı, 8 kişi de tutuklandı.




Savcılık, Mahiroğlu’nun Halk TV’yi satın aldıktan sonra kanalın ekonomik sıkıntı yaşamaması için İzmir Büyükşehir Belediyesinden usulsüz ihaleler aldığını iddia ediyor.




2021’de İzmir’de kurulan Bustech Araç Bakım Onarım Hizmetleri AŞ’nin paravan şirket olduğunu, sahibinin Mahiroğlu olduğunu ve bu şirketin belediyenin araç bakım, onarım ve temizlik ihalelerini rüşvet karşılığında aldığını ileri sürüyor.




Bu ihalelerden elde edilen gelirlerin de Halk TV’nin yanı sıra Özdemir Üç Tekstil’e, Mahiroğlu’nun diğer şirketlerine ve yurt içi ve yurt dışındaki kişisel hesaplarına aktarıldığını iddialar arasında.




Paranın farklı hesaplar arasında kısa süre içinde birden fazla kez dolaşıma sokularak aklanmaya çalışıldığı öne süren savcılık, Bustech şirketinin dört yedek parça şirketiyle anlaşarak gerçekte yapılmayan mal ve hizmet alımları karşılığında yüzde 12 ila 14 oranında komisyonla sahte fatura düzenlettiğini de öne sürüyor.




Söz konusu faturalar karşılığında şirketlere verilmesi gereken çeklerin Halk TV’nin kasasında bulunduğunu ileri süren Başsavcılık, bu çeklerden elde edilen parayla Ece Üner ve Özgürdeniz Bayramoğlu’na aylık 1 milyon 650 bin TL kayıt dışı ödeme yapıldığını iddia etti.




Başsavcılık, bu ödemeler karşılığında Üner ve Bayramoğlu’na “talimatlı gerçeğe aykırı haberler yaptırıldığı” iddiasında bulundu.




(HA)

author: Unknown
title: Bayık: The PKK's struggle secured recognition of the Kurds' existence
content:
Kurdistan Communities Union (KCK) Executive Council Co-Chair Cemil Bayık discussed the conditions surrounding the establishment of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK), the sociological and political atmosphere of Kurdish society in the 1970s, the values created through half a century of struggle and the movement's strategy for the new period in a special program broadcast on Stêrk TV.




Cemil Bayık said that the PKK was founded at a time when Kurdish identity, language and culture were denied, genocidal policies were pursued, assimilation and economic impoverishment were widespread, and social struggles were subjected to severe repression. He said that half a century of struggle had, above all, instilled national consciousness in Kurdish society and enabled the Kurdish people to rise again. Bayık described the conditions of the period, saying, "They did not regard Kurds as human beings. For a Kurd to gain their acceptance, to be regarded as a human being, they had to abandon their Kurdish identity." He emphasized that economic policies were also an important part of the genocidal process, that Kurdistan's economic resources were plundered and that society was impoverished. Bayık said that the emergence of the PKK had initiated a new period of struggle and organization within Kurdish society, adding, "The movements that emerged before the PKK were divided along regional, sectarian, religious and tribal lines. The Kurdish struggle transcended the boundaries of a single part of Kurdistan and regional boundaries for the first time with the PKK."




Bayık said that the PKK had dissolved after the launch of the Peace and Democratic Society Process by Abdullah Öcalan on 27 February 2025, but that the decision to end the armed struggle did not mean that the struggle itself had ended. He emphasized that this was a change in strategy and method, adding that the PKK would continue its struggle and sustain the values it had created through different means and in a different form. Bayık said that communal organization would form the basis of the new period and emphasized the importance of communes in enabling society to meet its own needs, govern itself and develop a democratic life.




Half a century has passed since the establishment of the PKK. A struggle has been waged at every moment throughout this period. What were the social, economic, political and cultural conditions in Kurdistan before the PKK was founded?




Before answering this question, I would like to congratulate the people of Kurdistan and humanity on the anniversary of the founding of the PKK. The PKK was not founded under favorable conditions or on the basis of already established values. The conditions in which Kurdish society and the Kurdish people lived when the PKK was founded were extremely difficult. The Turkish state was pursuing a policy of genocide against Kurdish society and the Kurdish people. Through this policy, they had concluded that the Kurds and Kurdistan would never be able to rise again. Their policy aimed to turn Kurdistan entirely into a territory where the Turkish state could establish its own nation. They sought to eliminate the Kurdish people altogether. An extremely brutal policy was being pursued. What was written on Mount Ararat after the Ararat rebellion? "Kurdistan is buried here." In other words, there was no longer a Kurdish or Kurdistan question here. That was the conclusion they had reached.




They believed that the policies they had pursued against Kurdish society and the Kurdish people had made it impossible for such a question to emerge again or for the Kurds to survive as such. Their policy was based on eliminating the Kurdish language, identity, values, culture and economy, in other words, everything associated with the Kurds and Kurdistan. As a result, they had fragmented society. They had even created contradictions within Kurdish society. They had alienated Kurdish society from everything that belonged to it. People within Kurdish society had forgotten their enemies and had turned against one another. They had developed such a brutal policy within society. Kurdish society had lost everything as a result of the policies pursued by the Turkish state. It was no longer only the Turkish state that sought to eliminate the Kurds. These policies had alienated the Kurds from their own reality to such an extent that they were destroying themselves.




Why? Because they did not regard Kurds as human beings. For a Kurd to gain their acceptance, to be regarded as a human being, they had to abandon their Kurdish identity. They had to embrace Turkish identity. Only then could they physically survive. They were given no other means of survival. What kind of policy were they pursuing? How could they starve the Kurdish people and make them dependent on them? What could they do to ensure that the Kurdish people would no longer think about their national question, language, culture or values, defend their identity or struggle for themselves again? They complemented the policies they pursued in the military, political, social and cultural spheres with economic policies. They destroyed the economy of the people of Kurdistan and plundered its resources so that the Kurdish people would have no means of survival. How were they supposed to survive physically? Such a brutal policy had been developed.




Kurds could only physically survive by accepting Turkish identity




The Kurdish people had struggled many times, launched uprisings and demonstrated heroism. However, they had suffered defeats in these struggles. The policies pursued against the Kurdish people had broken their will, destroyed their hopes and undermined their morale. They had come to believe that they would never again be able to wage a struggle for themselves or defend their identity. They had lost hope and morale. The Turkish state therefore presented them with only one option. They could physically survive only if they accepted Turkish identity. Kurdish society and the Kurdish people were given no other means of survival. Assimilation was pursued intensively as a result of these policies and the repeated defeats suffered by Kurdish movements. This policy of annihilation and genocide was pursued relentlessly. Economic policies were also implemented extensively.




As a result, the Kurdish people came to see their Kurdish identity as a burden. How could they rid themselves of this burden? They could only escape it by becoming Turkish, and only then could they physically survive. These were the conditions under which Leader Apo (Abdullah Öcalan) began his struggle and the PKK was founded. These conditions were extremely difficult for the Kurdish people. No one imagined that a struggle could be developed in the name of the Kurds and Kurdistan under such circumstances. Everyone said, "The Kurdish question has now been eliminated." Even the Kurds themselves said, "It is difficult to revive a question that is already dead." They had reached this conclusion because the conditions facing Kurdish society and the Kurdish people were extremely severe. I do not think any other people in the world have been subjected to such a brutal attack. Leader Apo stood up for this society and the Kurdish people under those conditions. He developed a struggle for this people. How could he enable this society and the Kurdish people to rise again, instill hope and faith in them and develop a national struggle? He seriously considered these questions.




Various movements had emerged in other countries. You could not simply take them as your model because there is no place in the world like Kurdistan. The Kurdish question is greater than all other questions in the world because the Kurdish people are both divided into different parts and fragmented internally. They were also divided against one another. They had even begun to reproduce and experience among themselves what the occupying forces had imposed upon them. That was their condition. It was not easy to transform a society in such a state. It was extremely difficult and arduous. Leader Apo focused on how to transform this society and develop a society that would defend itself and struggle for its freedom under all circumstances. He developed a strategy for this purpose. He developed his tactics, leadership, organization and militants accordingly. What was the foundation upon which he developed all these elements? It was the spirit of self-sacrifice. Unless you develop this struggle on the basis of self-sacrifice, it is impossible to enable society in Kurdistan to rise from such a condition, revive itself and engage in a national struggle. Only self-sacrifice could achieve this. Leader Apo therefore sought to develop everything, from the leadership to the organization and from the organization to the militants, on the basis of self-sacrifice.




Defending Kurdish identity and Kurdistan was punishable by death




Those seeking to develop movements in Turkey or other countries had their own methods and approaches. However, Leader Apo did not adopt these as his model. He knew that it would be impossible to organize and develop the struggle by adopting the methods used in Turkey or elsewhere. The movement would have been eliminated at its very inception. Defending Kurdish identity and Kurdistan was already punishable by death. It was considered a serious crime. To escape execution, you had to refrain from defending the Kurds and Kurdistan or developing such a struggle. This was widely understood. Leader Apo therefore developed a different approach so that the state would not readily realize that a movement was being developed in the name of the Kurds and Kurdistan, allowing him to develop the movement. Under those conditions, not everyone dared to defend Kurdistan and the Kurdish people or develop a struggle for freedom, democracy and national rights in Kurdistan. It was extremely dangerous and difficult. Leader Apo was prepared to take all these risks. He approached the situation with courage, knowledge and consciousness. This was how he developed the struggle.




As I said, developing such a struggle required taking self-sacrifice as its foundation. Only in this way could you develop the struggle, create a spirit, build morale and instill faith. This was how you could enable the people to rise again. The Kurdish people rose from the brink of death, defended their identity, developed a struggle for themselves and embraced Leader Apo, the PKK and the struggle. This was how the 15 August offensive, the prison resistance and the popular uprisings (serhildans) developed. All these created a new spirit among the Kurdish people. It was not easy at the beginning. The Kurdish people did not initially embrace the movement because they did not believe that it would bring about change, progress or success. However, they saw that the movement developed its struggle among the people, addressed their problems and began resolving them. It developed an unprecedented struggle against occupation in the prisons. The guerrilla movement and popular uprisings subsequently developed on this basis. It was then that the people truly began to believe in the movement and embrace it.




What was Leader Apo's objective? It was to create a society that defended itself under all circumstances and struggled for its own freedom and democracy. This struggle not only enabled the people to overcome their previous condition but also gave rise to a people who have become a source of hope for the world today. The Kurdish people secured recognition of their existence throughout the world through this struggle. They defended their identity and declared, "I exist, and you cannot deny my existence." The Kurdish people were not recognized internationally either. They were denied recognition not only in Turkey but throughout the world. Everyone had accepted the policies pursued against Kurdish society and the Kurdish people and regarded them as normal. They said, "There used to be Kurds, but there are no Kurds anymore." The Kurds paid an enormous price and endured immense suffering through their struggle, proving that the Kurdish people had not died and did not want to die. The Kurdish people cherish their freedom and want to struggle for it under all circumstances. They secured recognition of this reality. This was extremely important. A new history emerged in Kurdistan through this struggle. The fact that the Kurdish people subsequently declared, "We are the PKK," and embraced the PKK was a result of this struggle.




There was the state's policy of denial. The state pursued this policy after the Kurdish uprisings and their suppression. On the other hand, there was also a form of self-denial among the Kurds themselves. They denied their identity, language and culture. There was an attempt to escape their own existence and identity. What kind of state of mind and psychological condition did this create among the Kurds?




Whatever the Turkish state has built, it has built with the assistance of the Kurds, while developing its war regime on the basis of the denial and genocide of the Kurds. This is why the regime in Turkey is a war regime. It was developed on the basis of the denial and annihilation of the Kurds. Anyone who studies history carefully can understand this. Whenever the Turkish people found themselves in difficult circumstances or faced danger and realized that they needed the Kurdish people, they approached the Kurds and formed alliances with them. These alliances enabled them to overcome their difficulties and escape danger. Once they had overcome these difficulties, they again denied the Kurds and turned against them. They adopted the annihilation of the Kurds as their fundamental policy. There is no need to discuss history at great length. It would be better to briefly address a few aspects of the republican period of the Turkish state. The Kurds were included in Turkey's constitution in 1921. The Kurds were not denied. Why? Because the Ottoman Empire had been defeated. The state and Turkish society were facing grave danger. They therefore realized that they needed the Kurds.




They approached the Kurds for this reason. They included the Kurds in Turkey's fundamental law, namely its constitution, to secure Kurdish assistance. Mustafa Kemal even said that the Kurds would be granted autonomy during a meeting with the press in Izmit. There was no denial of the Kurds in Turkey until 1923. There was even recognition of the Kurds, an intention to develop Kurdish autonomy and public acknowledgment of this. Various agreements were reached and alliances were formed when the state gained recognition at Lausanne. Consequently, the Turkish state no longer needed the Kurds. They began drafting a new constitution in 1924. They did not include the Kurds in this constitution. The Kurds had previously been included in the constitution, but they were subsequently excluded. Various laws and measures were then introduced, including the Eastern Reform Plan and the Law on the Maintenance of Order, along with numerous other related laws. They sought to legalize and provide a legal basis for the policies they were pursuing against the Kurds through these laws. A policy of genocide was being pursued against the Kurds. They pursued a policy aimed at eliminating the Kurds and Kurdistan in every respect. They also removed everything associated with the Kurds and Kurdistan from their documents. In other words, they sought to portray history as though the Kurds had never existed.




Whatever had been achieved was portrayed as having been achieved by the Turks alone, rather than through an alliance with the Kurds. They erased all these facts from history and official documents. This was their approach. What did they do as a result? They pursued an extremely brutal policy against the Kurds until the 1940s. Whenever resistance emerged in Kurdistan until the 1940s, they suppressed it. There were executions, forced displacements and massacres. Assimilation was subsequently intensified. Economic plunder and starvation were imposed. The Kurds lost hope, and their morale, faith and will were broken. They lost faith in themselves. The Turkish state presented them with only one option. What was it? "You will become Turkish. If you become Turkish, you can physically survive." Consequently, the Kurdish people became alienated from their identity, values, culture and themselves, and forgot who they were. The state reached a conclusion after the 1940s, having established its domination over Kurdish society and the Kurdish people in every respect. It believed that it had achieved its objective. There would never again be a movement in Kurdistan in the name of the Kurds. They could turn Kurdistan into their own country and establish the complete domination of their nation-state over Kurdistan. This was the conclusion they reached. Anyone can clearly see this in history.




You said that the years between the 1940s and the 1970s were, in a sense, a period in which Kurdish rebellions and popular uprisings were suppressed. There were other Kurdish organizations during that period. Although they had shortcomings and consisted of small groups, they waged certain struggles or raised certain issues. However, the PKK emerged in the 1970s, after 1968. Let me ask a related question. The Kurdistan you described did not have a particularly developed social structure of workers and laborers under the conditions of that period. Yet the Kurdistan Workers’ Party, the PKK, emerged. You are also one of its founders. Where did the name PKK come from?




It is true that there were certain Kurdish parties before the PKK was founded. However, no one knew about them or even knew that such parties existed. Why? Because they had no visible struggle. No one had witnessed any of their activities. No one knew that such parties existed. However, we knew that there were certain parties of this kind. When we wanted to establish the PKK, we said, "We will not be like those parties." We had to distinguish ourselves in every respect. We had to be able to meet the needs and demands of Kurdish society. You could not bring the Kurdish people back from the brink of death with the existing parties. It was impossible. Had they been capable of rescuing the people from that condition, they would have done so in one way or another. Yet parties and organizations had been established without developing any struggle. They did not even mention the name of Kurdistan. They were afraid even of that. They lacked the courage to defend Kurdish society and the Kurdish people or develop a national movement, a movement for freedom and democracy, in the name of this society. They were extremely afraid. They had therefore established parties that existed in name only. They had no activities. That was why we said, "We will never be like them." Ultimately, we proved that we were not like them. We demonstrated our differences in every respect, not only to the Kurdish people but also to the world.




Not everyone initially accepted or joined the PKK when it was founded. There were even numerous attacks against the PKK. There were ideological and political attacks. Organizational and military attacks subsequently developed. Fronts were also formed against the PKK. It faced attacks of such magnitude. The PKK emerged under extremely difficult conditions, as I said earlier. No one believed that this party would develop such a struggle or bring about change and progress. People initially approached it with caution. However, the PKK pursued its own objectives and political line, and as a movement founded entirely on self-sacrifice, it gained acceptance among the people through its actions. Other movements in Kurdistan, whether Kurdish movements or those identified with the Turkish left, weakened and became ineffective. The PKK developed rapidly. Kurdish society rallied around the PKK. Why? Because people saw that the PKK was resolving their problems. The PKK stood against traitors and collaborators and developed resistance in the prisons. People began to believe in the movement when they saw this. They realized that this movement was unlike previous movements. It did not wage the same kind of war as its predecessors and was different in every respect. This boosted morale and created hope and faith. People initially approached it cautiously, but subsequently joined and became part of the movement.




We initially began under the name Kurdistan Revolutionaries. Some even called us "Apocular" (followers of Apo). Everyone gave us different names. Some even mocked us. Such attitudes existed. However, we paid no attention to them. We focused on ourselves, our objectives, our political line and our principles. We remained committed to our objectives on this basis. We subsequently transformed the struggle we had developed under the name Kurdistan Revolutionaries into a youth movement. We developed a struggle as a youth movement and eventually established a party. This was how we reached the stage of forming a party. However, discussions continued when we decided to establish a party. We would either develop the youth movement and wage the struggle on that basis or establish a party through the youth movement. We discussed this extensively. Ultimately, we decided to transform the movement into a party and develop the struggle under the name of a party. We also considered what the party should be called when we decided to develop the struggle in this form. We discussed this as well. At the end of these discussions, we adopted the name PKK. We wanted it to be a party of workers and laborers.




The PKK created a new history in Kurdistan




The working class was not particularly developed in Kurdistan. Why, then, did we choose and adopt this name? There was both the influence of real socialism and the struggle of the Vietnamese people at the time. The Vietnamese people had also developed their struggle through the Workers’ Party. This influenced us. The PKK was founded in the atmosphere of real socialism and under its influence. Those struggling for socialism at the time adopted either the name workers or communist. We adopted the name workers. Why? Because Kurdish society in Kurdistan was genuinely a working society. It could be said that the overwhelming majority were laborers and workers. They worked everywhere. They worked not only in Kurdistan but also went to Turkey's metropolitan cities to work as laborers. That was why we adopted this name. Choosing such a name was not particularly wrong at the time. As I said, the PKK was founded under the influence of real socialism, but there was also the Vietnam War and the Vietnamese struggle. There was a Workers’ Party in Vietnam as well. Kurdish society was impoverished, and the majority were workers. We were also a socialist movement. We therefore did not consider it wrong to adopt the name workers. This was why we chose the name Kurdistan Workers’ Party.




What did the PKK prove? It proved that establishing the PKK and developing a struggle under its name at that time had been the right decision. The history that unfolded was shaped on this basis. The Kurds gained recognition, defended their identity and secured international recognition of their existence through the PKK's struggle. This proved that establishing the PKK and developing a struggle under its name in the atmosphere of that period had not been wrong. I can say this. The PKK created a new history in Kurdistan. It developed a history of national struggle. Through this struggle, it fostered a powerful sense of unity and a strong spirit among the Kurdish people. The Kurdish people emerged from the brink of death, revived themselves, defended their identity and secured international recognition of their existence through the struggle of the PKK.

author: Unknown
title: DEM Party: The constitutional status of the Kurdistan Region must be protected
content:
The Central Executive Board of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) issued a statement concerning the constitutional status of the Başûrê Kurdistan (Southern Kurdistan) administration and recent developments in the region.




The statement described the legitimate, legal and democratic status of the Kurdistan Region, guaranteed under Iraq’s 2005 Federal Constitution, as an expression of the Kurdish people’s historical achievements and the democratic will of the Kurds and all other communities in the region. It emphasised that protecting and strengthening this status is important not only for the Kurdish people, but also for Iraq’s social peace, political stability and democratic future.




The statement noted that tensions have escalated in recent days over the management of border crossings and energy resources, once again highlighting the importance of federalism and constitutional balances. It also drew attention to the need to resolve the administrative, economic and legal disputes between Baghdad and the Kurdistan Regional Government.




The statement said: “Administrative, economic and legal disputes arising between Baghdad and the Regional Government must be resolved within the constitutional framework, through dialogue and negotiations, rather than through unilateral decisions, rhetoric that escalates tensions or militaristic approaches. The Federal Government of Iraq must act through collective consensus, adhering to the spirit of the Constitution and the legitimate rights of the Kurdish people. This is the only path towards a lasting solution.”




The statement also addressed political actors and institutions in Başûrê Kurdistan, emphasising the importance of prioritising democratic consensus during this critical period, resolving disputes through dialogue, and strengthening social unity and institutional functioning.




DEM Party stated that it supports safeguarding the constitutional status and achievements of the Kurdish people and resolving all disputes through peaceful and democratic negotiations. It added that protecting rights and the people's democratic will on the basis of mutual respect would contribute to Iraq's democratisation, as well as regional peace and stability.

author: Shan Kenshin Ecaldre
title: Rights groups condemn killing of farmer organizer, tricycle driver in Batangas
content:
Jane Lee (middle) with other relatives of victims of extrajudicial killings join a protest in front of Camp Aguinaldo July 21, 2019 demanding accountability to the death of their loved ones. (Photo by Kodao Productions)

The group said the incidents reflect a recurring pattern in which civilians killed in military operations are subsequently presented as members of armed groups.

On November 17, Gilbert Orr was on his way to meet farmers. Jayson Cortas was driving a rented tricycle, earning a living for his family. Neither would make it home that night.

The two civilians were killed in an alleged military-police operation in Barangay Bataan, San Juan, Batangas, at around 9 p.m. that day, according to human rights groups in Southern Tagalog.

Elements of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) and Philippine National Police (PNP), led by the Regional Mobile Force Battalion (RMFB), reportedly opened fire on the two while they were traveling.

Karapatan Southern Tagalog condemned the killings. According to the group, Orr had previously worked in the labor movement, organizing workers through a union. He later chose to serve farming communities, helping organize peasants in their struggle for land and livelihood.

On the night he was killed, he was reportedly heading to a farming community to help unite residents opposing mining operations in San Juan.

Cortas, meanwhile, was simply earning a living. He drove a rented tricycle to provide for his children and his pregnant partner.

“He was only driving a tricycle. And now he will never come home to me,” his partner said in a video post of Karapatan Timog Katagalugan.

Following the killings, PCOL Gerry Laylo, chief of the Mimaropa Police Regional Intelligence Division, reportedly claimed that the two were members of the New People’s Army (NPA). Laylo also cited supposed warrants of arrest for murder and alleged violations of the Anti-Terrorism Act.

Karapatan Southern Tagalog and Tanggol Batangan rejected the claims, maintaining that Orr and Cortas were civilians.

The groups questioned the police account, particularly the attempt to associate the victims with the armed movement despite their identification as a community organizer and an ordinary driver.

For human rights defenders, the allegations cannot serve as justification for the deaths of the two men. They called for accountability from the state forces involved and demanded that the circumstances of the killings be established.

Tanggol Batangan also recalled the killings of nine-year-old Kyllene Casao in Taysan and Maximino Digno, a farmer with psychosocial disabilities, in Calaca in 2022. Both were reportedly tagged by the military as casualties of armed encounters.

The group said the incidents reflect a recurring pattern in which civilians killed in military operations are subsequently presented as members of armed groups.

Orr’s killing also raises concerns over the risks faced by community organizers opposing development projects in Southern Tagalog.

Before his death, Orr had been working among farmers, helping them organize against mining operations in San Juan.

Progressive groups have raised concerns over the Luzon Economic Corridor, citing their potential implications for communities, the environment, and national sovereignty.

Karapatan Southern Tagalog linked the killings to the government’s intensified efforts to suppress opposition to these projects, particularly amid the ASEAN Summit and the visit of US President Donald Trump.

The group argued that those organizing communities to defend their land, livelihood, and environment have increasingly become targets of state violence.

The killings also came amid the recent arrest of 276 participants of the Timog Katagalugan Lakbayani delegation in Manila. Although subsequently released, the participants continue to demand accountability for the arrests and alleged abuses committed by state forces.

Karapatan Southern Tagalog called for assistance to ensure the safe retrieval of the victims’ remains and appealed for legal and financial support for their families.

Tanggol Batangan joined the victims’ relatives and the people of Batangas in demanding truth, justice, and accountability from the AFP and PNP.

For their families, the loss cannot be reduced to police allegations or official accounts of an operation. Two men were killed while one was working to organize farmers and the other was earning a living for his family.

Their deaths demand answers. And their families deserve justice. (RVO)

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: DAR urged to side with the landless Bukidnon farmers
content:
BTLM members stand in front of land they had been tilling within Central Mindanao University in Barangay Dologon, Maramag, Bukidnon. Photo by Franck Dick Rosete/Bulatlat

MARAMAG, Bukidnon — Farmers within a state university here welcomed the recent development in their pursuit of land ownership.

This came after the Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR) had already conducted its area validation and survey on the land that the concerned farmers had been tilling within Central Mindanao University (CMU) in Barangay Dologon, Maramag, Bukidnon.

The farmers belong to the Bukidnon Free Farmers and Agricultural Laborers Organization (Buffalo), the Triad Agricultural Manpower of Rural Active Workers (Tamaraw), the Landless Tillers Inhabitants of Musuan (Limus), and the Musuan Inhabitants’ Landless Farmers Association (Milfa). They are collectively known as BTLM, with more or less 700 members.

Now, they urged the government agency to conclude the process in favor of the landless peasants.

“This is to have a boundary line between the farmers and Central Mindanao University (CMU) and to avoid conflict,” Herman Santillan, who has been designated as BTLM spokesperson, told Bulatlat in the vernacular.

The three-day land validation and area survey of DAR started on October 6, more than four months from the issuance of Agrarian Reform Secretary Conrado Estrella III’s order declaring all CMU lands “not actually, directly, and exclusively utilized for educational purposes” included in agrarian reform coverage under Executive Order No. 75-2019.

For them, this is the closest to victory for nearly two decades of fighting for land ownership. They are now waiting for the next stage.

CONTEXT: How the issue between BTLM farmers and CMU started

Abdullah Linog, DAR Northern Mindanao assistant director for operations, confirmed that the regional office has already received the transmittal of its Bukidnon office, containing the classification of CMU lands, but it has yet to determine which land can be covered by agrarian reform.

Santillan, however, said that he saw the transmittal from the Bukidnon Provincial Agrarian Reform Office indicating that a total of 1,037 hectares of lands were intended for the agrarian reform beneficiaries.

To respect the status quo, BTLM farmers have not tilled the land. However, they have been maintaining their presence by staying in their makeshift shelter.

Read: Bukidnon farmers guard disputed land due to unsettled demand

They founded the makeshift shelter after their houses were demolished and their ready-to-harvest palay were uprooted in 2024. Because of this, they are planning to file damages against CMU due to the alleged questionable demolition.

“We really file damages because we have all the evidence,” Santillan said. (RVO)

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: ASEAN mass arrests fuel renewed push for New Public Assembly Act
content:
Police arrest protesters, including members of alternative media and student publications, in Sucat, Muntinlupa City, on November 15, 2026. The protesters are part of a delegation who are set to join a protest in Manila against Pax Silica and US President Donald Trump's visit. Photo from Bayan Laguna

The right to assemble and express dissent is constitutionally guaranteed and should not be treated as a privilege granted by authorities.

By Reachelyn Esona Bulatlat.com

It was past 2 p.m on November 15 when hundreds of protesters were arrested in what was described as the largest single-day mass arrest under the administration of Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

Before progressive groups from Southern Tagalog could join the anti Pax-Silica and Trump Out protest at Liwasang Bonifacio in Manila, the Southern Police District blocked and arrested nearly 300 protesters at Sucat People’s Park in Muntinlupa City. Among those who were arrested were 19 student journalists and alternative reporters.

Read: Police violently disperse, arrest hundreds in Muntinlupa protest

The arrested protesters faced inquest proceedings over alleged violations of Batas Pambansa Blg. 880, or the Public Assembly Act of 1985, as well as alarms and scandals, and resistance and disobedience to a person in authority. They were eventually released after prosecutors granted the motion filed by their lawyers.

The arrests, however, renewed a long-standing concern among human rights defenders: instead of protecting the people’s right to peaceful assembly, B.P Blg. 880 has been used to restrict and penalize the exercise of that right.

At a public forum on the human rights legislative agenda organized by Karapatan on November 20, Kabataan Party-list Representative Atty. Renee Co discussed House Bill No. 4574, or the proposed New Public Assembly Act. The bill seeks to repeal the Marcosian decree Batas Pambansa 880 and establish a new legal framework that strengthens the protection of the people’s right to freedom of assembly.

Read: Repressive decrees, issuances, legacies of Marcos dictatorship, remain in force

Co cited a series of arrests and restrictions involving protesters in Muntinlupa, Bulacan, Liwasang Bonifacio, Cebu, and other areas, as well as students who participated in university walkouts. She said authorities have invoked BP 880 to justify restricting assemblies, particularly those held outside designated freedom parks without permits.

Under the existing law, organizers are generally required to secure a permit for public assemblies, except in designated freedom parks and certain other circumstances.

The proposed HB 4574 seeks to change this framework.

According to the bill’s explanatory note, it removes the “no permit, no rally” policy and replaces it with a notice system. Rather than requiring organizers to obtain permission from authorities, the proposed system would require them to notify the appropriate authorities of their planned assembly, with the presumption that assemblies are peaceful.

The bill also provides for the automatic designation of public parks, halls, and plazas as freedom parks in cities and municipalities that fail to designate such spaces. This provision aims to ensure that people have accessible venues where they can exercise their right to peaceful assembly.

These proposed changes are rooted in a broader argument raised by the National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers (NUPL): the right to assemble and express dissent is constitutionally guaranteed and should not be treated as a privilege granted by authorities.

“Our rights do not require permits,” NUPL said.

The Commission on Human Rights (CHR) likewise emphasized that freedom of expression and peaceful assembly must be respected, as guaranteed under Article III, Section 4 of the 1987 Constitution.

During the same forum, Karapatan Secretary General Cristina Palabay called for the passage of a new law to replace B.P Blg. 880, arguing that the existing legislation is a remnant of the Marcos dictatorship and no longer responds to the realities faced by protesters today.

Despite these calls, HB 4574 has yet to advance beyond the committee level. Co said the bill was filed last year but has seen little progress, as it is not among the administration’s legislative priorities. She stressed the need to broaden public awareness on the right to peaceful assembly and build public support for the bill to help move it forward in Congress.

The debate over the proposed law comes as protesters continue to face complaints under B.P Blg. 880. The preliminary investigation into the case of the Southern Tagalog protesters, who are still facing allegations of violating the said law, began on November 25.

As the cases move forward, human rights defenders continue to press for the passage of HB 4574, arguing that a law should truly honor the people’s right to peaceful assembly. (RVO)

title: T'es exploité·e ? Arrête. / Une émission de Minuit Décousu
content:
«

 

Le travailleureuse vend sa force de travail à un patron, en échange d'un salaire, qu'il ou elle est contraint de faire, parce qu'on ne possède pas les moyens de production, genre les outils, l'usine pour produire des trucs, les terres pour cultiver, un parc immobilier à louer... Bref, quand le seul truc qu'on possède c'est sa force de travail, bah on l'échange contre un salaire, qui nous permet de bouffer, de se loger, de se payer un peu de fun en vacances ou au bar, et d'élever ses enfants qui pourrint à leur tour vendre leur force de travail et perpétuer le capitalisme.

 

»




150 ans après les premières définitions marxistes, le concept d'exploitation pur jus a un peu bougé. La théorie de la valeur travail a été contestée, on a aussi dit que l'exploitation ne pouvait pas se réduire au travail de production, ou que le tout donnait une vision trop simplifiée du monde du travail. C'est pourquoi cette semaine, Minuit Décousu a choisi d'en découdre avec l'exploitation et le travail pour voir que ces définitions ont pu être retravaillées à plein d'endroits, élargies et approfondies. title: Construire une société non-marchande : un chantier ouvert à toustes
content:
Il s'agira au cours de ce moment de réfléchir ensemble, à partir de nos propres pratiques, à des stratégies révolutionnaires de dépassement de l'économie marchande.




En l'occurrence à Lyon et dans d'autres endroits en France, ont été tentées depuis une dizaine d'année des «

 

provisions communes

 

» consistant à mettre en commun du temps de travail sans comptabilité, ni notion d'échange, pour produire une partie de notre subsistance. La démarche se veut la plus ouverte et accueillante possible, universelle, sans chercher à atteindre une autonomie matérielle aussi illusoire qu'inutile politiquement, dans la mesure où un collectif qui serait sorti du capitalisme actuellement ne pourrait l'être que grâce à des privilèges, dans des conditions non reproductibles.




Le livre qui servira d'introduction à la discussion, 

«

 

La provision commune. Une brèche à agrandir dans la société marchande

 

»

, défend l'importance de l'abolition de l'échange marchand pour sortir de la course à la productivité dans laquelle l'humanité s'est enfermée. A un niveau individuel, cela se traduit par l'impossibilité de se projeter dans un emploi rémunéré pour toute personne qui désire être utile ou simplement ne pas aggraver la situation sous prétexte de devoir «

 

gagner sa vie

 

». Le livre défend la nécessité de penser et mettre en place une séparation entre activités marchandes et activité non-marchandes, à rebours de l'économie sociale et solidaire qui entend pacifier la contradiction entre utilité sociale et rentabilité.




Dans un deuxième temps, nous pourrons débattre - y compris au sein d'une partie de notre collectif qui sera présent- de l'importance politique de l'autoproduction, définie dans son sens fort comme la production par des non-professionnels, et donc comme une subversion possible de la frontière entre qui peut produire et ne le peut pas. La provision commune constitue ainsi une autoproduction «

 

survitaminée

 

», consciente des limites de l'autoproduction ordinaire qu'il s'agit de dépasser.




La provision commune permet donc de réfléchir à la portée politique des pratiques sociales bien plus largement diffusées, quoique marginalisée, qui l'englobent : les activités de subsistance et les activités hors emploi. Notre groupe de lecture souhaite ainsi lancer en 2027 une lecture critique et collective d'enquêtes sociologiques sur ces thèmes, au travers d'une première bibliographie présentée ci-dessous.

author: Unknown
title: Groupe de parole MeToo inceste et pédocriminalité Lyon
content:
Dans chaque groupe, deux personnes du collectif s'occupent de la modération et du soutien émotionnel individuel (si besoin, si une personne s'extrait du groupe). Ces personnes sont elles-mêmes concernées et prennent part aux échanges.




Le groupe est consacré aux personnes victimes d'inceste et de pédocriminalité, non aux personnes autrices de ces actes, même si elles ont elles-mêmes été victimes.


Le groupe de parole commence par une explication du déroulé. Ensuite, un tour de parole sert à se présenter (prénom, pronoms), à dire comment on se sent en ce moment et le sujet que l'on veut amener. Après, ça reste libre et d'autres sujets de la thématique peuvent être abordés.


Une vigilance à la répartition de la parole est faite mais il n'est pas obligatoire de s'exprimer.




Groupe sur inscription car limité à 10 personnes. Anonymat garanti, possibilité de se présenter sous pseudo dès l'inscription.




En partageant nos expériences et nos sentiments par la parole et par l'écoute, nous cherchons avant tout à rompre notre isolement, et à trouver une aide et un réconfort moral mutuel. Nous souhaitons également susciter notre capacité à demander de l'aide, c'est pourquoi il est complémentaire et ne se substitue pas à une thérapie souvent nécessaire (bien que coûteuse...).




Prochain groupe de parole : 


Lundi 14 décembre 2026 à 19h au Jusqu'ici.

author: anarchist*innen
title: Deutschland-Griechenland: Reiseverbot und repressive Maßnahmen gegen Anarchist*innen
content:
Information bezüglich einer Ausreiseverweigerung, die am 22.11.26 durch die Bundespolizei gegen eine Person entschieden und durchgesetzt wurde.




Am Sonntag, den 22. November, wurde einer Person, die für die Demonstration in Gedenken an Kyriakos Xymitiris am 31.10.2025 in Athen angeklagt ist, die Ausreise aus Deutschland verweigert. Sein Reisepass wurde abgenommen und eine Meldeauflage für den 24. November in einer Berliner Polizeistation erlassen. Dadurch war ihm die Teilnahme an seinem eigenen Prozess im Gericht Evelpidon in Athen am 24. November nicht möglich. Eine andere Person, Halterin eines griechischen Passes, welche mit ihm hätte fliegen sollen, wurde ebenso von der Bundespolizei an der Ausreise gehindert.




Die Geschehnisse trugen sich am Frankfurter Flughafen zu, wo zunächst die andere Person nach der Passkontrolle dazu aufgefordert wurde, mit zur Polizeistation des Flughafens zu kommen. Zusammen kamen die zwei Gefährt*innen zur Station, wo sie getrennt wurden und alle Sachen durchsucht wurden. Der Person, die angeblich nicht Ziel der Polizeimaßnahme war, wurde gesagt, dass die Polizei die Absicht hätte, eine Nackt- und auch Rektaluntersuchung durchzuführen. Die Verweigerung der Kooperation und die Forderung eines Gerichtsbeschlusses für dieses Vorgehen führte dazu, dass der leitende Beamte von der Entscheidung absah, nur um als Grund anzugeben, dass er dies tue, da er eine Kooperation der Person für das noch anstehende Verfahren erwarte.




Dann wurden beide Personen getrennt voneinander zum Verhör gebracht, welches der Entscheidung darüber dienen sollte, ob sie das Recht zur Ausreise hätten.




Der Person, die ursprünglich Ziel der polizeilichen Aktion war, wurde kurz ein Schrieb in griechischer Sprache mit dem übersetzten Titel „Belehrung von Personen bei präventiven freiheitsentziehenden/-beschränkenden Maßnahmen“ gezeigt. Darin war als Grund angekreuzt: „Identitätsfeststellung oder Überprüfung der Berechtigung zum Grenzübertritt“. Die Polizei fragte nach dem Grund der Reise nach Athen. Die Person machte keine Angaben außer dem Zeigen ihres griechischen Passes. Die Polizei entschied dann offenbar, die Ausreise nicht offiziell zu verbieten und lies sie gehen ohne eine rechtliche Erklärung zu machen oder eine offizielle Entscheidung zu verkünden. Dies geschah zu einem Zeitpunkt als das Gate zum Flugzeug nach Athen schon geschossen und das Boarding nicht mehr möglich war.




Der anderen Person übergab die Polizei einen Schrieb auf Deutsch mit dem selben Titel wie oben genannt und zusätzlich ein vierseitiges Dokument, welches die Absicht der Polizei erklärte, ihm die Ausreise in jedes andere Land bis zum 24. November um 24:00 zu untersagen. Weiter wurde darin die Absicht genannt, ihm eine Meldeauflage für den 24. November in einer Polizeistation in Berlin Friedrichshain aufzuerlegen. Im Falle einer Nicht-Einhaltung sollte eine Strafe von 100 Euro anfallen.




Der wesentliche Teil der vier Seiten Text beschrieb die Begründung der Polizei für ihre Absichten. Hier eine Zusammenfassung der Formulierungen aus der Feder der Polizei:




-nach polizeilicher Information gibt es eine Ankündigung einer “Solidaritätsversammlung für inhaftierte, flüchtige und verfolgte Aktivistinnen und Aktivisten”1 für den 24.11., bei welcher es sich um eine Versammlung des gewaltorientierten, griechischen Anarchistmus handelt


-diese Veranstaltung is öffentlich auf athens.indymedia.org angekündigt


-Veranstaltungen, die in der Vergangenheit auf athens.indymedia.org angekündigt wurden, führten meistens zu Ausschreitungen gegenüber Einsatzkräften und zu einer lokalen, nationalen und internationalen Berichterstattung


-als Beispiel wird die Gedenkveranstaltung für Kyriakos Xymitiris am 31.10.2026 genannt, wo es in den letzten Jahren zu verschiedensten Straftaten (eine längere Aufzählung folgt) kam




-polizeiliche Informationen über den Gefährten, insbesondere eine lange Liste an verschiedensten Straftatbeständen (für die er niemals verurteilt oder auch nur offiziell beschuldigt wurde)


-polizeiliche Informationen über einige politische Veranstaltungen, auf denen er gesehen wurde


-Annahmen darüber, dass er Teil einer in Berlin agierenden Struktur ist, die sich einerseits auf die Ereignisse des 31. Oktober 2024, Kyriakos Xymitiris und die Anarchist*innen Marianna Manoura und Dimitra Zarafeta bezieht, andererseits mit der Rigaer94 in Verbindung steht


-polizeiliche Informationen über allgemeine Reisebewegungen zwischen Griechenland und Deutschland und Bezugnahmen politischer Aktivitäten in Deutschland auf Griechenland, wobei als Beispiel ein Brandanschlag zum Gedenken an Kyriakos Xymitiris erwähnt wird, sowie die Installation einer selbst gestalteten Gedenkstätte für Kyriakos Xymitiris in Berlin




-die Verbindung des Gefährten zur Rigaer94


-Straftaten, die im “Umfeld der Rigaer94” stattgefunden haben und die Bezeichnung der Rigaer94 als Ausgangspunkt für Gewalttaten


-die Räumungsankündigung eines Gerichts gegen die Rigaer94 für Mitte Dezember 2026 und der Aufruf und die Ankündigung der Rigaer94 zur Verteidigung, welche sich auf das Prosfygika in Athen und das Evagelismos in Heraklion sowie auf K.X., M.M. und D.Z. beziehen




-polizeiliche Informationen über die Demo am 31.10.25 (erster Jahrestag des Todes von Kyriakos Xymitiris), welche besagt, dass dort die Polizei angegriffen wurde und der Gefährte einer von zunächst 13 Festgenommenen, deren Zahl später auf 5 reduziert wurde, war


-Berichterstattung über diese Demonstration in den Massenmedien




Die im Dokument festgehaltene Schlussfolgerung der Polizei aus all dem ist, dass die Reise des Gefährten nach Athen aller Wahrscheinlichkeit nach dem Zweck dienen sollte, einerseits sich an der Versammlung am 24. November 2026 zu beteiligen, bei der es angeblich sehr wahrscheinlich zu gewaltsamen Ausschreitungen mit der Polizei hätte kommen sollen, andererseits, gewaltbereite griechische Anarchisten für eine gewaltsame Verteidung der Rigaer94 zu mobilisieren. Dadurch würde er das Ansehen der BRD in einem fremden Land beschädigen. Daher und weil er keine anderen plausiblen Gründe für die Reise vortrug, sollte ihm die Ausreise untersagt werden.




Der Gefährte machte keine Angaben zu all diesen Annahmen und wenige Minuten später wurde durch die selbe Bundespolizeidienststelle, die sie aufgestellt hatte, offiziell entschieden, dass aufgrund all dieser Annahmen die erwähnten Maßnahmen getroffen werden: sein Reisepass wurde sichergestellt, die Meldeauflage auf der Polizeiwache sowie die Reiseuntersagung (nur nach Griechenland) erlassen und bei Nichteinhaltung eine Strafverfolgung angekündigt. Dann wurde er aus dem Gewahrsam entlassen.




Beschriebenes Prozedere ist für Anarchist*innen in Deutschland bisher relativ unbekannt. In der Vergangenheit wurden Reisebeschränkungen meistens angewendet, um Leute davon abzuhalten, zu großen Protesten während Staats- und Wirtschaftsgipfeln zu fahren. Die angeführten Gründe in hiesigem Fall belegen, dass die deutsche Polizei von der griechischen Polizei weiß, dass der Gefährte am 24. November vor Gericht angeklagt war. Daher ist die angeführte Absicht, den Gefährten von der Teilnahme an angeblichen Ausschreitungen innerhalb des Gerichts abhalten zu wollen, vorgeschoben.




Die Maßnahme verunmöglichte es dem Betroffenen, an seinem Prozess am 24. November in Athen teilzunehmen. Die deutsche Polizei hat binnen Minuten einen Beschluss erlassen, um ihm die Ausreise zu verbieten, ohne dass ein vorheriger Gerichtsbeschluss eine solche Einschränkung rechtfertigte. Auf diese Weise haben die Strafverfolgungsbehörden direkt in ein Gerichtsverfahren in einem anderen Land eingegriffen und einen Angeklagten jeder Möglichkeit, an seinem eigenen Gerichtsverfahren teilzunehmen, beraubt. Die Bundespolizei kann auf Grundlage von Spekulationen, willkürlichen Einschätzungen und Szenarien der politische Aktivität des Gefährten und anderer Aktiver in wenigen Minuten entscheiden, ob jemand das Recht hat zu reisen oder nicht. Dieser Fall zeigt einmal mehr das Gewaltmonopol, das die Exekutive bei der Bewegungskontrolle von Menschen inne hat, wenn sie ihre Verdächtigungen in tatsächliche Beschränkungen der Freiheit umwandelt. Ein polizeiliche Spekulation rund um die Möglichkeit, dass es bei einer Versammlung «Ausschreitungen» geben könnte, reicht aus, um jemandem den Grenzübertritt zu verbieten, ohne dass es konkrete Beweise dafür gäbe, dass er sich daran beteiligen würde oder gar sich strafrechtlich relevanter Praxen bedienen würde. Und all das im Wissen darüber, dass der Gefährte am selben Tag auf der Anklagebank dem Gericht gegenüber sitzen würde, um an der Verhandlung teilzunehmen, bei der es um ihn selbst geht.




Was sich in diesem Fall zeigt, ist die alleinige und riesige Macht der Polizeibehörden in Deutschland wie in Europa, wie außerordentliche Gerichte zu funktionieren. Polizisten konstruieren Risikoprofile, sammeln Verdächtigungen und Informationen, vergeben politische Zuschreibungen wie z.B. „Linksextremist“ und verordnen Einschränkungen ohne ihre Behauptungen in Gerichtssälen beweisen zu müssen. So werden Verdächtigungen, die nicht für eine Anklage vor Gericht ausreichen würde, zu einer ausreichenden Grundlage für Freiheitseinschränkungen einzelner. Da im Namen der Prävention immer mehr Gesetzeslücken geöffnet werden, erlangen die Strafverfolgungsbehörden ein immer stärkeres Monopol darauf, über unsere Leben zu entscheiden ohne jegliche Möglichkeit zur legalen Verteidigung wie sie ein Gerichtsverfahren hätte.




Die Tatsache, dass politisch aktive Menschen und speziell auch die zwei hier genannten Personen in den letzten zwölf Monaten mehrere Male ihre Flug- oder Zugverbindungen durch (bis dahin „normale“) Polizeikontrollen nicht erreicht haben, spricht dafür, dass der Staat eine Strategie der Rache und willkürlichen Maßnahmen gegen ausgewählte Personen verfolgt. In diesem Fall ist es offensichtlich die grenzüberschreitende Solidarität für Gefangene und das Gedenken an einen bewaffneten Kämpfer, die die Polizei und Geheimdienste dazu veranlasst haben, die neuesten Maßnahmen präventiver Gesetze anzuwenden, die exakt den Charakter eines autoritären Polizeistaats ausmachen. Was am 22. November in der Polizeistation im Frankfurter Flughafen passierte, ist eine extralegale Intervention gegen und Bestrafung von Anarchist*innen. Bestrafung nicht deshalb, weil es für sie tragisch wäre, ein Gerichtsverfahren zu verpassen, sondern weil dieses Regime die Isolation vertieft, die Grenzen und Gefängnismauern ihnen und mit ihnen der ganzen Gesellschaft auferlegen. Die Betroffenen und solidarische Strukturen werden diese Aktionen nicht unbeantwortet lassen. Sie werden legal angefochten werden und darüber hinaus werden polizeiliche Verbote und Anordnungen niemals akzeptiert werden.




Niemand ist allein in den Fängen des Staates


Solidarität ist unsere Waffe


Kyriakos Xymitiris immer präsent


Solidarität mit den gefangenen Gefährtinnen Marianna Manoura und Dimitra Zarafeta


Freiheit für alle Gefangenen




Ps: Der Genosse ist am 24.11.26 nicht der polizeilichen Meldeauflage nachgekommen.




Anarchist*innen




passiert am 22.11.2026

author: Pudelfreund
title: TSP: „Bedrohung“ für die Beamten: Polizist erschießt Pudel bei Einsatz in Berliner Hotel
content:
Weil ein Mann mit einem waffenähnlichen Gegenstand über den Breitscheidplatz lief, alarmierten Zeugen die Polizei. In einem Hotel machten Beamte den Verdächtigen ausfindig. Es fielen Schüsse.




Ein Polizist hat in der Nacht zu Mittwoch einen Hund in einem Hotel in der Berliner Kantstraße erschossen. Das Tier – es handelte sich nach Polizeiangaben wohl um einen Pudel – sei „eine Art Bedrohung“ für den Beamten gewesen, sagte eine Polizeisprecherin. Zum Schutz des Lebens habe er mit seiner Dienstwaffe auf das Tier geschossen. Es sei wohl noch vor Ort gestorben. Wie viele Schüsse abgegeben worden sind, war den Angaben zufolge zunächst unklar.




Zu dem Polizeieinsatz war es gekommen, weil Zeugen einen Mann mit einem waffenähnlichen Gegenstand auf dem Breitscheidplatz in Charlottenburg gesehen hatten. Wenig später, gegen 4 Uhr, klopften die Beamten der Polizei zufolge an die Tür eines Zimmers im Hotel „The Cloud One“ in der Nähe, in dem sie den Mann vermuteten.




Der Verdächtige habe die Tür geöffnet und die Beamten mit dem waffenähnlichen Gegenstand bedroht. Einen ersten Schuss habe ein Beamter bereits zu diesem Zeitpunkt abgegeben – jedoch ohne jemanden zu verletzen.




Dann sei der Hund aus dem Zimmer gerannt und von einem Beamten erschossen worden. Der 63-jährige Tatverdächtige sei festgenommen und in ein Krankenhaus gebracht worden, weil er psychisch auffällig gewesen sein soll. Bei dem waffenähnlichen Gegenstand handelte es sich nach Angaben einer Polizeisprecherin um ein Tierabwehr-Spray in Form einer Pistole. (dpa, Tsp)
