title: Women in Southern Kurdistan face violence, impunity and social pressure
content:
Femicide, domestic violence, forced marriage, economic dependence and gender inequality continue to threaten women's lives in Southern Kurdistan (Başûr). The March 8 Network, which reported that 69 women were killed in 2025, recorded 46 femicides as of October 2026. Women journalists and activists face political repression and digital violence, while Yazidi women continue their struggle for justice, overcoming displacement and rebuilding their lives following ISIS attacks.




Women's lives in Southern Kurdistan are shaped by interconnected social, economic, political and legal inequalities. Femicide, domestic violence, child and forced marriage, female genital mutilation, discrimination in employment, economic dependence and repression in the public sphere are among the fundamental problems threatening women's right to life and freedom.




Various legal reforms have been introduced in the field of women's rights, but their failure to translate into everyday life demonstrates the seriousness of the problem. Significant shortcomings remain in protecting women from violence, enabling them to achieve economic independence, ensuring their equal participation in political and social life and allowing them to organize independently.




Statements issued by women's rights organizations and reports published by international institutions in 2026 also indicate that this situation remains unchanged. Data on femicide, digital violence and women's access to justice particularly demonstrate the need to reassess existing protection mechanisms.




Legal regulations remain only on paper




The Southern Kurdistan Region adopted Law No. 8 on Combating Domestic Violence in 2011. The law established an important legal framework for preventing domestic violence and protecting survivors.




However, the adoption of the law does not mean that women have access to safety and justice in practice. Significant shortcomings remain in the effective handling of women's complaints, the prosecution of perpetrators, the implementation of protection orders and the provision of adequate living conditions for women.




Research published by Amnesty International in 2024 pointed to serious difficulties in holding perpetrators of domestic violence accountable. A report published by the European Union Agency for Asylum (EUAA) in November 2026 also draws attention to the inadequacy of shelters in the Southern Kurdistan Region and the legal and institutional barriers to independent accommodation services for survivors of violence.




Women forced to leave abusive households struggle to rebuild their lives due to economic and social circumstances. This demonstrates that protection mechanisms must go beyond providing temporary accommodation. Conditions must be created in which women can live safely, work, receive an education and make their own decisions.




Child and forced marriages threaten the future of girls




Child and forced marriages are among the major problems restricting women's freedom in Southern Kurdistan. These practices directly affect girls' right to education, physical and psychological development, economic independence and ability to make decisions about their future.




Data from the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) show that 27.9 percent of women aged 20 to 24 in Iraq were married before the age of 18. Although this figure applies to Iraq as a whole, it reveals the extent of child marriage in the country.




Poverty, unequal access to education, family pressure and traditional social norms are among the factors behind early marriage. Forced marriages deprive women and children of the right to make decisions about their own lives.




Female genital mutilation: A violation of bodily integrity




Female genital mutilation (FGM) is another major problem that must be addressed in Southern Kurdistan. The practice affects the bodily integrity and physical and psychological health of women and girls, constituting a violation of fundamental human rights.




UNFPA data indicated that the prevalence of female genital mutilation across Iraq stood at 7.4 percent, while the figure reached 37.5 percent in the Southern Kurdistan Region.




Economic dependence is a barrier to women's freedom




Women's limited participation in economic life constitutes a significant dimension of gender inequality in Southern Kurdistan. Unemployment, precarious employment, low wages and the disproportionate burden of unpaid care work placed on women deepen economic dependence.




The Kurdistan Region Statistics Office's labor force data for 2021 showed that women's labor force participation rate stood at 16.5 percent, compared with 73.5 percent for men. The same data put women's unemployment rate at 29.6 percent and men's unemployment rate at 13.6 percent.




Childcare, care for the elderly, domestic work and other family responsibilities fall largely on women's shoulders. This reduces the time women can devote to education, employment and participation in social life.




Data on Iraq from the United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN Women) indicate that women spend 24.1 percent of their time on unpaid care and domestic work, compared with 4.2 percent for men.




Economic dependence also makes it more difficult for women to leave abusive relationships. Women without their own income, access to housing or social security may be forced to remain in environments where they experience violence.




Women journalists and activists face political and social pressure




The problems women face in Southern Kurdistan are not confined to the domestic sphere. Women journalists, human rights defenders and activists also face restrictions on freedom of expression, political repression, threats and digital violence.




Violations against journalists and media workers also affect women's participation in the public sphere. A country assessment on the Kurdistan Region published by the United Kingdom government in September 2026 states that journalists and activists may face detention and physical attacks over their online content, while women journalists are particularly vulnerable to discrimination, harassment and blackmail.




Women journalists face censorship, threats and obstruction of their reporting because of their professional activities, while also having to confront sexist attacks because they are women.




Digital violence is emerging as another form of repression restricting women's presence in the public sphere. Threats, insults, blackmail, the unauthorized disclosure of personal information and coordinated smear campaigns through digital media directly affect women's freedom of expression.




A study on digital violence against women in the Kurdistan Region, published by the SecDev Foundation in February 2026, reveals that the problem is not limited to isolated incidents but constitutes a structural issue linked to shortcomings in legal and institutional frameworks, education and digital governance.




Digital violence affects not only women's online safety but also their participation in social and political life. Threats and blackmail can force women to refrain from expressing their opinions, continuing their journalistic activities or participating in social struggles.




Yazidi women continue their struggle for justice and life




The ISIS attack on Shengal on 3 August 2014 marked the beginning of a devastating genocide and widespread social destruction for the Yazidi people. Thousands of people were massacred, and thousands of women and children were abducted. Yazidi women were subjected to systematic sexual violence, enslavement, torture and forced marriage.




Twelve years after the genocide, the problems faced by Yazidi women and their families persist. The unknown fate of abducted women and children, displacement, housing, healthcare, education, employment and access to justice remain central issues in their ongoing struggle.




Independent women's organization is a force in the struggle for freedom




Strengthening women's rights in Southern Kurdistan cannot be achieved through the implementation of existing laws alone. Opportunities for women to organize independently must also be expanded, and women must actively participate in social decision-making processes.




Women's organizations are important actors that support survivors of violence, combat gender inequality, demand legal reforms and strengthen women's participation in political life. Organizations and initiatives such as the March 8 Network, Asuda for Combating Violence against Women, the Emma Organization, the Kurdish Women's Relations Organization (REPAK), the Kurdistan Women's Union and the Yazidi Women's Freedom Movement (TAJÊ) struggle against femicide, domestic violence, impunity and gender inequality.




These organizations work to protect women's legal and social rights, support survivors of violence, strengthen women's economic independence and ensure their equal participation in political life. Their work constitutes important examples of women's solidarity and independent organization.

title: Mehmet Uçum cannot distort the facts
content:
Mehmet Uçum has once again written an article distorting the facts. It appears that Mehmet Uçum has been assigned such a task. He reflects the views of the state side in the Peace and Democratic Society Process. He is being made to write these views. In this respect, what Mehmet Uçum writes reveals the approach of those who instruct him to write.




He criticized the language used by the movement's leadership and members of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party). He is thus attempting to prevent the movement's leadership and DEM Party members from explaining the facts to the public. One purpose of this article is also to exert pressure on the movement's leadership and DEM Party members.




The difficulties in securing broad social support for the process are entirely the responsibility of the Justice and Development Party (AKP) government. The pro-AKP media does not speak of a peace and democratic resolution process. It speaks of eliminating terrorism and disarmament. The attacks and attempts at liquidation that have continued for decades are now presented as being pursued through different means. The AKP government has not prepared its own political base for this process and is trying every possible means and method to turn opposition political circles against it. It is attempting to turn a significant portion of society against the process through provocative practices. Mehmet Uçum makes baseless accusations against the movement's leadership and DEM Party members to conceal this reality.




If there is a Peace and Democratic Society Process today, it is thanks to the approach of Kurdish People’s Leader Abdullah Öcalan and the unprecedented steps taken by the Kurdish Freedom Movement in the context of such conflicts. The process continues today because of the Kurdish side's flexible approach and its efforts to encourage the AKP government to take steps. There is a widespread public perception that the Kurdish side is taking steps while the government is doing nothing. Mehmet Uçum is also attempting to conceal this public perception and the reaction against the government.




The Kurdish Freedom Movement has taken steps to eliminate all risks of confrontation with the Turkish military. It has left no armed forces inside Turkey and has withdrawn its armed forces from areas close to the Turkish border and the Turkish army. Downplaying these steps could result in the sabotage of the process. According to Mehmet Uçum, these steps are not particularly significant. He suggests that they should be unarmed wherever they are. He is almost suggesting that they should be left at the mercy of predators. The leadership and cadres of this movement must protect themselves until they return to Turkey. Otherwise, they could be eliminated in various ways. The movement's leadership has already stated that no one should expect them to seek refuge elsewhere. However, they insist that they will return to Turkey if a legal and judicial environment conducive to democratic politics is established. Devlet Bahçeli said after the weapons-burning initiative on 11 July 2025 that he wished the necessary laws had been enacted so that they could return.




Have laws enabling democratic politics been enacted, only for the Kurdish side to say that it will not lay down its arms or return to Turkey? If Turkey's existing laws and judicial system remain in place, those returning to Turkey will eventually be imprisoned for violating one law or another. Would anyone in their right mind take a step that would lead to their arrest? In fact, the issue of disarmament has already been resolved. Its implementation requires facilitating returns to Turkey. It is the AKP government's responsibility to make this possible. The Anti-Terror Law remains in force. This law should have been amended so that it no longer constitutes an obstacle to democratic political struggle. We have given just one example, because there are laws under which those engaged in democratic political struggle can immediately be arrested.




All the steps taken by the Kurdish side to date have been aimed at laying down arms and returning to Turkey. No one has said that they would refuse to lay down arms. On the contrary, the criticism has been that Turkey is failing to create the political and legal conditions necessary for complete disarmament. Is the AKP government planning to launch another war once the guerrilla forces have withdrawn completely? How else can its failure to take steps that would accelerate the process be explained? Perhaps there are other reasons for its failure to act. Some circles suggest that the AKP government wants to prolong the process and enter the election period under these conditions.




We cannot know exactly why the AKP is not taking steps. The AKP government may have different calculations. It may instrumentalize the process, as it has done in the past. However, there is one thing that both we and the public know: despite the significant steps taken by the movement's leadership, the AKP has not taken any substantial steps. It has yet to fulfill many of the promises it made during the meetings on Imralı.




Mehmet Uçum reveals his true intentions by telling people not to speak too much about Abdullah Öcalan. In a sense, he is asking them to bury their leader alive there. A people or an organization that fails to stand by its leader cannot defend its existence or its right to a free and democratic life. The Kurds continue their struggle for a free and democratic life by standing by their leader. Mehmet Uçum knows the sensitivities of the Kurdish people and therefore says that the question cannot be resolved without Abdullah Öcalan. This rhetoric merely serves to conceal efforts to make people forget the Kurdish People's Leader. Mehmet Uçum also knows that this people and this movement will do everything necessary and will not take a single step back from standing by their leader and keeping his situation on the agenda.




Mehmet Uçum accuses the DEM Party. Yet DEM Party officials have adopted an approach suggesting that positive steps have been taken, even though the AKP government has taken no significant steps. Slightly expanding the living quarters on Imralı and allowing two or three people to visit does not constitute a substantial improvement. The new accommodation had already been built a year ago, but Abdullah Öcalan had not moved there until now to avoid misunderstandings. However, meetings have reportedly been held there. Mehmet Uçum's criticism of the DEM Party, even as its officials seek to create a positive atmosphere, constitutes a method of exerting pressure through special warfare.




Mehmet Uçum must not forget that he is dealing with a movement that has been engaged in political struggle for 53 years. Those who fail to take this movement seriously and approach it through special warfare methods, schemes and tactics will be disappointed.




Source: Yeni Yaşam Newspaper

author: Unknown
title: YRK reports Iranian airstrikes in Pêncewîn region
content:
Iranian regime forces once again attacked positions of the Eastern Kurdistan Defense Units (YRK) in the border area of Pêncewîn in Southern Kurdistan on Tuesday evening. According to the YRK Press Center, four consecutive airstrikes were carried out within an hour, beginning at 9 p.m. on November 24.




“Our forces suffered neither casualties nor material damage in these attacks. All our units are safe,” the organization stated.




The YRK described the bombardment as part of a series of Iranian attacks on various areas of Kurdistan in recent days. “The attacks are an expression of the Iranian regime’s ongoing policy of war, which targets not only the YRK but also the people and nature of Kurdistan.”




In its statement, the guerrilla organization characterized the repeated attacks as a sign of weakness on the part of the Iranian regime, which it said was attempting to compensate for its limitations and military shortcomings through airstrikes. “Such attacks not only fail to change the actual situation on the ground but also reveal the regime’s fear and helplessness in the face of the peoples’ demands,” the statement concluded.

title: Parliamentary Monitoring Committee to consist of 19 members
content:
In a letter signed by Numan Kurtulmuş and sent to political parties by the Parliament Speaker’s Office, the parties were asked to submit the names of their members for the Monitoring Commission, to be established pursuant to Article 7, Paragraph 5 of the “Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Cohesion,” by 5 p.m. on Monday, November 30, 2026.




The distribution of seats among political parties on the committee has also been finalized. Accordingly, the AKP will be represented by nine MPs, the YENİ Party by three, the DEM Party by two, the MHP by two, the CHP by one, the İYİ Party by one, and the YENİ YOL Party by one. The committee will thus consist of 19 members.




The seats allocated to political parties that do not participate in the committee are expected to be redistributed among the other political parties.

author: Harriet Williamson
title: US Military Set to Detonate Toxic Lead Bomb in Iowa
content:
Children, pregnant women and chronically ill people in Iowa are being advised to evacuate as the US army prepares to blow up a stockpile of munitions laced with lead on Wednesday. 




Nearly five tonnes of unstable bomb-making chemicals stored at a base in Middletown, Iowa, are scheduled for detonation despite serious risks to human health. 




The detonation is expected to send a toxic plume of lead-containing dust particles over eastern Iowa and into the neighbouring state of Illinois, where toxins will likely settle on farmland, homes and playgrounds. 




There is no safe level of exposure to lead, which is a neurotoxin. 




350 farms could be exposed

 to the toxic lead dust, according to the US Department of Agriculture. 




Children and pregnant women are particularly at risk as exposure to lead can interfere with fetal brain development, cause cognitive damage and increase the likelihood of miscarriages and premature births. 




In adults, lead exposure is linked to decreased kidney function, fertility issues and heart problems, along with

 increased risks

 of various cancers.




Iowa has the 

second-highest rate of cancer

 among US states, and is one of only three states where rates of cancer are rising. 




A lawsuit was filed by environmental groups to block the detonation, but the US Circuit Court of Appeals ruled on Monday that it could go ahead.




Journalist Abby Martin called it “an emergency of [the US army’s] own making because of their own negligence and disregard”. 




She told

 BreakThrough News on Tuesday

: “I just can’t wrap my mind around the fact that an industry that has a budget of over $1tn cannot incorporate a safe disposal mechanism for these toxic chemicals it is constantly manufacturing.




“I think at the end of the day, they just know they can override local governments.”




Federal officials say the detonation is needed because the degraded material could explode on its own. 




The US army initially contracted a company to chemically neutralise the weapons after it became aware of the degrading cache at a military base in March, 

the New York Times reported

. However, it cancelled the deal just two months later and decided to blow up the munitions instead. 




Environmental 

assessment documents

 from the US military state that while the chemical route for disposal “offered environmental protections by avoiding a blast plume, it was eliminated from detailed study due to unacceptable risk to human safety”. This was because the process required more “hands-on” handling by workers over long days.




The Department of Health and Human Services (HSS) told pregnant women, children and those with chronic illnesses 

to evacuate on Tuesday

, with HHS principal deputy assistant secretary for preparedness and response saying “you definitely want to be out of that area”.




The Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown makes medium and large calibre munitions for the US Department of Defense.

author: Unknown
title: De Gennaro si è suicidato. Noi a Genova c’eravamo, ricordiamo e non perdoniamo
content:
Da 

Osservatorio Repressione




Mentre politica e media celebrano il “servitore dello Stato”, noi ricordiamo Carlo Giuliani, la Diaz, Bolzaneto e le migliaia di persone colpite dalla repressione. La morte dell’ex capo della Polizia non cancella le responsabilità istituzionali del G8 del 2001.




Gianni De Gennaro, 78 anni, ex capo della Polizia e dell’intelligence italiana, si è tolto la vita con un colpo di pistola nella sua casa di campagna a Montiano, in Toscana. Il suo corpo è stato ritrovato questa mattina, 21 novembre, dopo che dalla sera precedente non aveva più dato notizie di sé. La morte arriva a pochi giorni dalla notizia dell’indagine della Procura di Caltanissetta che lo vedeva accusato di depistaggio nell’ambito degli accertamenti sulla strage di via D’Amelio e sulla scomparsa dell’agenda rossa di Paolo Borsellino.




Già si moltiplicano le dichiarazioni di cordoglio, i riconoscimenti istituzionali, le celebrazioni del grande investigatore e del fedele servitore dello Stato. Una narrazione che rischia di lasciare sullo sfondo ciò che per noi non può essere dimenticato. Perché Gianni De Gennaro era il capo della Polizia durante il G8 di Genova del luglio 2001. E noi a Genova c’eravamo. Ricordiamo quello che accadde, ricordiamo chi impartiva gli ordini, chi dirigeva gli apparati, chi costruì false ricostruzioni e chi, nonostante tutto, continuò a occupare i vertici dello Stato. Non intendiamo partecipare a nessuna operazione di riabilitazione postuma.




Ricordiamo Carlo Giuliani, ucciso in piazza Alimonda. Ricordiamo le persone massacrate nella scuola Diaz, quelle trascinate nella caserma di Bolzaneto, torturate, umiliate, private dei diritti più elementari. Ricordiamo i feriti, le persone colpite dalle cariche, quelle che non denunciarono le violenze subite, chi per anni ha dovuto affrontare processi, spese legali, condanne e conseguenze personali devastanti. Ricordiamo le vite segnate per sempre da quelle giornate e la lunga battaglia per smontare menzogne, falsificazioni e depistaggi. Non era stato il sasso, non era stato l’estintore, non erano stati i manifestanti a produrre quella sospensione materiale dei diritti. Era stato lo Stato, attraverso i suoi apparati coercitivi.




De Gennaro era al vertice di quell’apparato. Fu processato per induzione alla falsa testimonianza e definitivamente assolto dalla Cassazione nel 2011. Ma l’assoluzione penale non cancella la questione della responsabilità politica e istituzionale di chi dirigeva la Polizia durante una delle più gravi operazioni repressive della storia repubblicana. E non cancella il fatto che, dopo Genova, De Gennaro abbia continuato la propria carriera ai vertici della sicurezza nazionale, del coordinamento dei servizi segreti, del governo e dell’industria strategica, sostenuto da esecutivi di diverso orientamento politico. Mentre le vittime cercavano giustizia, il capo della Polizia di Genova 2001 continuava ad accumulare incarichi e potere.




C’è poi un nome che collega due pagine particolarmente oscure della storia italiana: Arnaldo La Barbera. L’ex dirigente della Squadra mobile di Palermo, figura centrale nel depistaggio delle indagini sulla strage Borsellino, venne inviato a Genova proprio da De Gennaro dopo l’uccisione di Carlo Giuliani e partecipò alla gestione delle operazioni culminate nell’irruzione alla Diaz. La nuova inchiesta di Caltanissetta chiamava in causa De Gennaro per una distinta ipotesi di depistaggio, relativa alle presunte pressioni esercitate su Salvatore Contorno affinché non rendesse dichiarazioni ai magistrati e all’occultamento di documentazione. Accuse ancora da accertare, per le quali il giudice aveva respinto la richiesta di arresti domiciliari avanzata dalla Procura.




La sua morte lascia inevitabilmente senza una risposta giudiziaria definitiva quelle contestazioni nei suoi confronti. Ma non deve interrompere la ricerca della verità sulle stragi, sui depistaggi e sulle responsabilità degli apparati. Né può diventare il pretesto per trasformare un’indagine della magistratura in una persecuzione giudiziaria, come già suggeriscono alcune reazioni politiche.




Non sappiamo quali ragioni personali abbiano condotto De Gennaro a togliersi la vita e non intendiamo attribuirgliene. Non proviamo gioia per la sua morte e non consideriamo il suicidio una forma di giustizia. La pietà umana non è in discussione. Ma non ci si chieda di cancellare il giudizio su ciò che De Gennaro ha rappresentato, né di unirci al coro delle celebrazioni istituzionali. Il rispetto per una persona morta non comporta l’obbligo di dimenticare le responsabilità di un’intera stagione di potere.




Per noi il punto resta Genova. Resta la violenza dello Stato, resta l’impunità, resta la continuità degli apparati repressivi che da allora hanno progressivamente trasformato il conflitto sociale in una questione di ordine pubblico. E restano le persone che quella violenza l’hanno subita, spesso pagando conseguenze che durano ancora oggi.




Noi a Genova c’eravamo. Ricordiamo e non perdoniamo. Non abbiamo dimenticato Carlo Giuliani, la Diaz, Bolzaneto e tutte le persone alle quali lo Stato ha spezzato o segnato la vita. Non sarà la morte di Gianni De Gennaro a farci cambiare idea sulla storia di quei giorni.

author: Unknown
title: “Non si può morire di indifferenza”. Continua la mobilitazione nelle università per Alessandro Ingusci.
content:
Pubblichiamo il comunicato congiunto diffuso da Collettivo Universitario Autonomo di Torino, Collettivo Universitario Autonomo di Pisa e Aula Studio Liberata di Cosenza.




Alessandro Ingusci, studente di fisica al primo anno, è morto all’interno della Sapienza di Roma mentre conduceva una lotta ostinata e coraggiosa per la giustizia abitativa e il diritto allo studio. 




Alessandro infatti, nonostante l’età e le precarie condizioni di salute, viveva in presidio nel cortile della Sapienza e stava conducendo uno sciopero della fame contro l’indifferenza di una governance che l’ha lasciato senza casa e senza tutele.




Dobbiamo categoricamente rifiutarci di liquidare la morte di Alessandro Ingusci ad una “tragedia”, perché ci sono responsabilità precise che ricadono sull’università della Sapienza e sulle istituzioni preposte a garantire l’accesso allo studio e soluzioni abitative alle persone che ne necessitano. Alessandro è stato ucciso da un sistema che nega la dignità di base alle persone rubando soldi alle politiche abitative, alla sanità e all’istruzione per regalarne alla guerra.

È una violenza strutturale che mette il profitto al primo posto ad ogni costo. Il costo oggi è stato quello della vita di Alessandro, ma è un costo che milioni di persone pagano quotidianamente. 




Quando succedono cose come questa, diventa evidente quanto poco conti la nostra vita per il governo e per gli sfruttatori. I responsabili di questa morte rappresentano gli interessi di una classe che non è disposta a rinunciare ai propri profitti senza una forza popolare che sia in grado di impoglierlo. Sono innumerevoli le persone che perdono la vita o la salute a causa dell’indifferenza e della povertà nella solitudine e nel silenzio, ma Alessandro ha scelto di rendere la propria condizione individuale un patrimonio collettivo, una responsabilità di lotta collettiva, per cui abbiamo il dovere di mobilitarci in massa, come si è fatto a Madrid dove dallo sgombero del 87enne Maria del Carmen Abascal che ne ha provocato la morte, è iniziata un’onda di proteste di massa che ha portato alla caduta del governo Sanchez.




In tutto il Paese, dalle metropoli alle città di provincia, da mesi è sorto un movimento di protesta contro il carovita e la guerra, e contro il governo Meloni, nemico della popolazione. In queste settimane sono state occupate scuole e università, sono stati chiamati scioperi generali in cui ci siamo rifiutati di continuare a lavorare per fare la fame. La questione abitativa, le borse di studio e ciò che loro chiamano “diritto allo studio”, sono questioni centrali: rappresentano i servizi e le necessità fondamentali che abbiamo per vivere, e per poter immaginare un futuro dignitoso. 




Dobbiamo continuare a mobilitarci per riprenderci pezzo dopo pezzo ciò che ci fa respirare: una borsa di studio, uno stipendio adeguato, una casa sicura. Non possiamo permettere che altri ancora arrivino a pagare un prezzo tanto alto a causa delle politiche criminali e assassine del governo.




La lotta di Alessandro vive con noi, pagherete tutto!

author: anred
title: Gordon o el peligroso límite entre la ficción y la tergiversación de la historia
content:
Una mirada y una lectura sobre la miniserie de Netflix que hoy genera debates entre protagonistas de la época, pero que también ofrece una versión simplificada y cuestionable a quienes no la vivieron. ¿Quién fue Gordon? ¿Un monstruo individual o una pieza eficaz del terrorismo de Estado previo al golpe y del Estado Terrorista instalado por la dictadura? Y lo central: ¿Cuáles son los límites éticos de una obra de ficción si ofrece una recreación distorsionada de la realidad?

 

Por Daniel Cecchini*, para La Tecl@ Eñe.







«Esta serie está inspirada en hechos reales y de público conocimiento. Las escenas mostradas no pretenden ser un reflejo fiel de la realidad. Algunos sucesos, personajes y diálogos son producto de la creatividad, la ficción y poseen propósitos narrativos», dice la típica advertencia que se puede leer al inicio de capa episodio de 

Gordon

, la miniserie creada por Pablo Trapero, producida por Adrián Suar y protagonizada por Rodrigo De la Serna. Es la fórmula de rigor en este tipo de casos y suele tener límites difusos a la hora de su desarrollo. Porque entre las ficciones basadas en hechos reales se corre el riesgo – o en la intención – de la tergiversación de la historia.




La utilización de escenas de ficción para contar una historia real es un recurso válido que incluso le sirvió a Rodolfo Walsh para dar una impactante eficacia narrativa a 

Operación Masacre

, la investigación de los fusilamientos de civiles perpetrados por la autodenominada Revolución Libertadora en el basural de José León Suárez. Por ejemplo, en el capítulo 3, titulado «Don Horacio», Walsh hace una presentación de Di Chiano que Tom Wolfe podría utilizar como modelo de su recomendación de describir a los personajes a partir de los rasgos. El lector termina con la imagen de un hombre tranquilo, bien de su casa, sin mayores ideas políticas ni pretensiones personales, dedicado a una apacible vida familiar. En el capítulo 14, el teniente coronel Desiderio Fernández Suárez abre de un empujón la puerta de la casa de don Horacio y entra gritando «¿Dónde está Tanco?», con una pistola .45 en la mano. Di Chiano, aterrorizado, levanta las manos sin soltar una bolsa de agua caliente que tiene en una de ellas. Nunca sabremos cuán rigurosamente cierta es la escena, pero Walsh logra su propósito: mostrar la brutal violencia de la irrupción policial – el empujón, el grito, la .45 empuñada – en contraste con el terror de un hombre pacífico que levanta las manos sin siquiera atinar a soltar un inocente adminículo doméstico. Simboliza la violencia que la dictadura ejerce sobre la población civil. Eso es ficción basada en hechos reales, porque nada de lo que se cuenta tergiversa los hechos de la historia.




Otro caso, para entrar en el género cinematográfico, más cercano a 

Gordon

, es el de 

Argentina 1985

, la película sobre el juicio a las juntas militares dirigida por Santiago Mitre y protagonizada por Ricardo Darín en el papel del fiscal Julio César Strassera. El guion utiliza la figura del hijo de Strassera en algunas escenas para reflejar mejor ciertas tensiones del momento histórico y las dudas sobre el veredicto. Son escenas de ficción que el propio hijo del fiscal aclaró que nunca ocurrieron pero que contribuyen a darle dramatismo al relato sin traicionar los hechos: no cambian la historia, ni pretenden hacerlo. Al contrario, buscan reflejarla mejor, desde cierta cotidianeidad.




En 

Gordon

, en cambio, sobran las tergiversaciones – que hay que diferenciar de las «ficciones basadas en hechos reales» – y hay omisiones que ocultan una parte que no debería soslayarse del pasado político de nuestro país. Voy a señalar algunas de ellas, las que creo que no se pueden dejar pasar porque cambian los hechos históricos.




La «Operación Cóndor» y sus protagonistas

:

 la serie comienza con el secuestro y desvío del avión de Aerolíneas hacia las Malvinas que un grupo de jóvenes peronistas realizó el 28 de septiembre de 1966, para después situar a varios de ellos, convertidos en integrantes del grupo de ultraderecha peronista Concentración Nacional Universitaria (CNU), en relación con Aníbal Gordon. Tomemos dos casos. Uno es una persona real, Alejandro Giovenco, primer jefe operativo de la CNU a nivel nacional; otro es un personaje ficticio, el joven Acosta. Deliberadamente o no, se omite el recorrido político de muchos de aquellos militantes hacia la izquierda peronista, como es el caso de Dardo Cabo, a quien ni se muestra ni menciona. Es decir, se muestra un devenir político de los «cóndores» exclusivamente hacia la ultraderecha y, por generalización, convierte a todos ellos en «fachos».




Gordon y la CNU

:

 Aníbal Gordon tiene su primer contacto con la CNU a mediados de 1974, cuando «baja» con un grupo de tareas de la proto Triple A para darle capacitación militar -en realidad, en secuestros y asesinatos – a la patota de la CNU platense. Su primera operación pública en conjunto se desarrolla en agosto de ese año, con los secuestros y asesinatos del sindicalista combativo Carlos Enio Pierini, el militante histórico de la Resistencia Peronista Horacio Chávez, su hijo también llamado Horacio, y el militante de la Juventud Universitaria Peronista (JUP) Luis Macor. Gordon y su gente operan ocasionalmente con la CNU hasta mediados de 1975. No existe ninguna relación de Gordon con la CNU antes de ese año, por lo tanto, no pudo estar presente en el asesinato de Silvia Filler en Mar del Plata, el primer crimen político de la organización, en diciembre de 1971, ni mucho menos causar la muerte con una granada “tocada” de Alejandro Giovenco, que sí murió por la explosión de uno de esos artefactos, pero de manera accidental. Al poner a Gordon dentro de la CNU – o con ella – en su primera etapa se tergiversa el origen y el desarrollo de esa organización que nace como grupo de choque universitario y termina como patota parapolicial al servicio del terrorismo de Estado previo al golpe. En otras palabras, la serie tergiversa una historia política que hoy, cuando se están llevando a cabo juicios por crímenes de lesa humanidad que tienen como acusados a miembros de la CNU, es imprescindible que se conozca con exactitud.




La distorsión de la militancia revolucionaria

:

 la miniserie de Trapero es prolífica en este punto. Primero: pone a militantes de la tendencia revolucionaria del peronismo como participantes en el secuestro del ejecutivo de Fíat Oberdan Sallustro, una operación realizada por el Ejército Revolucionario del Pueblo (ERP). A eso se suman sábanas pintadas con consignas de unidad de las organizaciones guerrilleras, algo que sí existió, pero que al meter a integrantes de Montoneros en una operación del ERP termina confundiendo. Es una banalización de las diferencias y las discusiones políticas entre las organizaciones revolucionarias de los ’70, y si se la aprecia con mala leche, les quita identidad. Segundo: la escena que muestra a una combatiente embarazada de muchos meses en el secuestro de Sallustro es aberrante y si se le busca una intencionalidad política al ponerla en la serie no puede ser otra que la de mostrar a los militantes revolucionarios como irresponsables y sin el más mínimo respeto por la vida. Tercero: en más de una ocasión – sobre todo a través del personaje de la guerrillera Graciela – se muestra a los militantes revolucionarios como indisciplinados, capaces de hacer operaciones en solitario y por cuenta propia, y movidos por sentimientos personales de venganza. Es una tergiversación que pretende negar la formación política y la disciplina que caracterizaban a los integrantes de las organizaciones revolucionarias. Hay más, pero creo que con estas es suficiente.




Gordon, Suárez Mason y el Batallón 601 de Inteligencia del Ejército

:

 Aníbal Gordon operó a las órdenes del Batallón 601 por lo menos desde octubre de 1975, durante el gobierno peronista, luego de que se firmaran los decretos de «aniquilamiento de la subversión». La serie lo ubica presionando para entrar al 601 después del golpe y rechazado por Suárez Mason, que parece mostrar desagrado y descalificar la manera de operar de Gordon. Un enfoque que al espectador inocente puede llevarlo a una conclusión como esta: los milicos eran mejores – o más decentes – que las bandas parapoliciales del terrorismo de Estado previo al golpe. Es todo lo contrario: Gordon era perfectamente funcional y no tuvo secuestrar a una ninguna abogada del 601para ser aceptado. Fue siempre una pieza eficaz de la represión ilegal, antes y después del golpe.




El tipo desequilibrado emocionalmente

:

 sobre todo en el último capítulo, titulado llamativamente «Vampiro», se muestra a Gordon como un ser desequilibrado, obsesionado por la militante secuestrada, bañándose la cara con su sangre después de torturarla y matarla. Muestra a un monstruo y con eso se pone en la vereda opuesta a Hannah Arendt cuando describa la banalidad del mal. Gordon no es ningún loquito, es una fría pieza, totalmente consciente de su función, dentro la maquinaria con que se perpetró el genocidio argentino. No mostrarlo como lo que realmente fue es pervertir la historia.




22 de noviembre de 2026.




*Periodista.




Fuente: 

https://lateclaenerevista.com/gordon-o-el-peligroso-limite-entre-la-ficcion-y-la-tergiversacion-de-la-historia-por-daniel-cecchini/

author: Unknown
title: There this understanding of Transmasc/Transfem that is not an identity per say but the way you transition from your asab and more importantly how you are seen by society not your personal identity. So. A feminine enby who uses they/them is transmasc bc they are transition away from femininity and “femaleness” ; vice versa for a butch transfem with they/them pronouns. This is why many nonbinary ppl who were CAMAB see themselves as transfem regardless if they see themselves as women/or fem-aligned bc the world sees themselves as trans women and thus affected by transmisogyny. Idk how to think of it bc I do understand  where they are coming from. I
content:
Oh yeah, that's a very common misconception outside of the nonbinary community about the use of transition labels! I'm happy to explain. 

First off, the transmasc/transfem labels have evolved over time. They started gaining traction in the early 2000s — although they had existed since at least the '90s — and were used as a catch-all term for anyone who was trans, without having to necessarily identify as transsexual or binary transgender. Like many historical labels, they have existed for most of their history as nebulous terms with no set definition, just a general vibe.

To start, I want to note that some of the earlier attempts at defining those labels did try to describe them in terms of what one is transitioning away from, instead of what one's actual gender identity is.

For example, 

advocate S. Leigh Thompson (who is a trans man) proposed this definition in 2006

: 

Transmasculine: Any person who was assigned female at birth but feels that is an incomplete or incorrect description of their gender.

That being said, those sorts of definitions never really became the predominant ones inside of nonbinary communities. And as of right now, they are actively disliked by most. For one, they don't take into account intersex people, who might have a complex history with gender and might use "contradictory" labels like AFAB transfem or AMAB transmasc. Furthermore, those definitions just.. don't make sense from a nonbinary perspective. Which is a big problem, since the labels transfem/transmasc are supposed to be used to include (some of) us.

Those definitions stem from the exorsexist idea that there is only one possible direction of transition: away from your "biological sex" and towards the "opposite sex". But gender is more complex than a line that goes from "man" to "woman" in which getting away from "man" necessarily pushes you towards "woman" and vice versa. For example, a medically-transitioning transneutral person might wish to remove their gendered characteristics (breasts, facial hair, etc.), but not wish to gain the ones associated with the opposite sex, like a binary-aligned trans person typically would. Even though they are transitioning away from typical presentations of their assigned sex-gender, their transition is also atypical for transfems/transmascs norms, and categorizing them as either of those just based on their AGAB would be reductive. Not to mention that social transition (being recognized as one's actual gender by society) is an integral part of transitioning, too. Categorizing a trans person as transmasc or transfem when they don't consider their gender identity masculine nor feminine is basically misgendering. At the end of the day, you (general you) are still telling someone who sees themselves as neutral, or androgynous, or fluid, or anything else they might identity as, that they need to be categorized based on the gender binary.

This framework also leads to the false idea that nonbinary people will always have more in common with binary trans people of the same "biological sex" than a nonbinary person of the "opposite" one with a similar gender identity. This is simply not the case, and in nonbinary spaces we rarely divide ourselves based on AGAB. A transmasculine or transfeminine enban might feel understood and included in trans man/woman spaces, but that's because they are transitioning towards masculinity/femininity just like them, not because AGAB inherently creates a connection between trans people. I, for one, feel a lot more understood amongst other neutral/unaligned people than I do around more binary-aligned people with my same AGAB.

Now, there are people who, despite being told all of this, will still argue in favor of using the labels in the way you (asker) have observed from others. Often under the guise of "society at large is transphobic and doesn't recognize nonbinary genders, so your oppression can only be described accurately if the labels indicate what you're transitioning away from". And my question to them is: if society is transphobic and doesn't recognize me as my actual gender, shouldn't a trans advocacy movement strive to change that, instead of telling trans people their identity doesn't exist? Furthermore: why does transness always need to be defined in terms of suffering? Why should an identity label be assigned to me based on how society (mis)treats me, instead of giving me the agency to choose the words to describe my own experience?

And, if you allow me to be petty for a second, the trans people arguing for using transfem and transmasc in that way are exhibiting a real "rules for thee but not for me" attitude. Because if someone said "trans women and trans men are not recognized as their actual genders by society at large, so we're going to use these labels that actively misgender them to describe their transition" they would, rightfully, lose their minds. But when it comes to nonbinary people, it's suddenly fine to force us in gendered categories that don't match our actual gender, based entirely on our AGAB. It's a double standard, and antithetical to what trans advocacy should stand for. 

At the end of the day, enben deserve to have words to describe our transition without forcibly binarizing us and our experiences. This is why we have labels such as transneutral and transandrogynous, and sometimes I wonder if more people would identify with them if they were more widely known and widely accepted.

Our identities and our language shouldn't revolve around what bigots think of us. To circle back to the example you brought up: an unaligned nonbinary person should be able to say "I'm unaligned and I've faced a lot of transmisogyny in my life" and be taken seriously, without their identity being called into question, without having to disclose their AGAB to "prove it", and without having to adopt the transfem label (if it doesn't resonate with them) just to be included. Unfortunately, as it currently is, a lot of us feel like we have to binarize our identity in order to receive solidarity.

I hope this explains it, and I'm glad you brought up the topic, anon! I have been meaning to talk about this for a while.
