title: Noviembre y diciembre. «El arte de luchar», una exposición sobre la Revolución Social de 1936 a través del arte
content:
La CNT de Burgos, en colaboración con la Fundación Anselmo Lorenzo (FAL) y Espacio Tangente, organiza 

«El arte de luchar. La Revolución Social a través del arte (1936-1939)»

, una exposición que propone un recorrido por las diferentes expresiones artísticas vinculadas a la Revolución Social de 1936.




La muestra reúne materiales de distintas disciplinas, como estampas, música, literatura, poesía, cartelería, fotografía y cine, para acercarse a la experiencia revolucionaria y a su legado cultural.




La exposición podrá visitarse del 

27 de noviembre al 23 de diciembre de 2026

, de lunes a viernes, de 18:30 a 21:30 horas, en Espacio Tangente (calle Valentín Jalón, 10, Burgos).




Programa de actividades




La programación incluye varias actividades complementarias:







27 de noviembre, 20:00 h. Inauguración.

 Charla sobre recuperación y conservación de archivos históricos y visita guiada a la exposición. En Espacio Tangente.




3 de diciembre, 18:30 h. Taller de fotografía.

 Demostración de fotografía estenopeica y revelado directo positivo. Inscripción previa en 

info@espaciotangente.net

 (máximo 10 personas).




11 de diciembre, 19:30 h. Club del Disco.

 En la biblioteca de Espacio Tangente. El disco se anunciará en @clubdeldisco_burgos.




18 de diciembre, 19:00 h. Proyecciones.

 Sesión de películas de S.I.E. Films: 

Reportaje del movimiento revolucionario en Barcelona

, 

El último minuto

 y 

Aurora de esperanza

. En CNT Burgos.




21 de diciembre, 18:30 h. Taller de cartelería y serigrafía.

 Inscripción previa en 

info@espaciotangente.net

 (máximo 10 personas).




23 de diciembre. Clausura.

 A las 18:00 h, charla-café «La Revolución 90 años después», en CNT Burgos, y a las 20:00 h, visita guiada y clausura en Espacio Tangente.







También se han programado visitas guiadas a la exposición los días 

27 de noviembre, 1, 15 y 23 de diciembre

, a las 20:00 horas.




Una propuesta para acercarse a la historia de la Revolución Social y a la creatividad artística que acompañó a uno de los procesos de transformación social más importantes de nuestra historia.










La entrada 

Noviembre y diciembre. «El arte de luchar», una exposición sobre la Revolución Social de 1936 a través del arte

 se publicó primero en 

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

.

author: Unknown
title: Ephéméride des luttes : 24 novembre
content:
L'éphéméride des luttes du 24 novembre a plus d'une dent contre les agissements de la police et de ceux à qui elle obéit servilement. Aujourd'hui, la répression est réprimée.




1874 :

 Aux États-Unis, J.-F. Glidden dépose le brevet du fil barbelé. C'est en partie grâce à cette invention que la 'conquête de l'ouest' se fera, en brisant les grandes étendues sauvages et en segmentant la terre avec des armes, secondée par les fusils et les maladies. « Ce ne furent ni les chemins de fer, ni les lois sur la terre qui permirent l'avancée du fermier au-delà du Missouri, mais bien le fil de fer barbelé ». 




Walter P.Webb cité dans 

Histoire politique du fil barbelé

 d'Olivier Razac.




1898 :

 A Rome, conférence internationale qui marque le début de la coopération internationale des forces de police dans la surveillance et la répression des anarchistes .




1917 :

 A Milwaukee aux États-Unis, une bombe anarchiste éclate au commissariat après que la police la découvre dans la cave d'une église, tuant 9 policiers.




 

 

 

 




1971 :

 A Milan, durs affrontements entre la police et les manifestant-e-s étudiant-e-s.




 A Strabane en Irlande du Nord, fusillade de l'IRA contre des soldats britanniques.

 Le même jour, un démineur de l'armée britannique meurt dans l'explosion d'une bombe de l'IRA a Lurgan.




1974 :

 A Florence, les 'groupes armés de résistance Jules Bonnot' attaquent un siège de la Démocratie Chrétienne à l'aide d'engins incendiaires.




1977 :

 A Paris, affrontements entre les autonomes et la police suite à l'expulsion de plusieurs squats du quatorzième arrondissement.




1979 :

 A Golfech, près de Toulouse, manifestation antinucléaire et incendie d'un local EDF dans la nuit. Le soir, c'est la naissance de Radio Golfech.




1983 :

 A Rathfarnham près de Dublin, l'IRA kidnappe l'entrepreneur américain Don Tidey, qui sera libéré en décembre.




1991 :

 Dans la prison de Crumlin, l'explosion d'une bombe préparée par des militants républicains de l'IRA fait plusieurs blessés.




2010 :

 A Londres, Rome et Padoue, des affrontements ont lieu lors de manifestations universitaires.




2011 :

 A Santiago du Chili, des affrontements avec la police ont lieu à la fois dans une manifestation Mapuche contre la construction d'un aéroport sur leurs terres dans le sud du pays, ainsi que lors d'une manifestation étudiante.




 A Athènes, c'est lors d'une manifestation contre l'austérité européenne que le même genre de situation se produit.




2014 :

 A Ferguson, Oakland et New York aux Etats-Unis, des émeutes éclatent après la relaxe du policier qui avait tué le jeune Mike Brown. Ce meurtre a été à l'origine du mouvement Black Lives Matters.




 A Notre-Dame-des-Landes, les affrontements se poursuivent contre la police qui cherche à évacuer la ZAD au cours de l'opération César. Plusieurs vidéos 

ici

.




2015 :

 A Athènes, attentat à l'explosif contre le siège du patronat grec en plein nuit.




 A Chicago, l'assassinat du jeune Laquan MacDonald par la police déclenche une émeute lors d'une manifestation de protestation.




2018 :

 A 

Marseille

, c'est la manif "de masse" pour la Plaine, pour faire tomber le mur et pour l'arrêt du chantier. Autour de 2000 personnes participent, un mur est érigé sur la Canebière avant que la manif ne remonte vers la Plaine où des affrontements éclatent alors que 30 fourgons de CRS sont en place, appuyés par un hélicoptère survolant la manifestation depuis le départ.







Voir aussi 

l'éphéméride anarchiste

 du 24 novembre.

author: Kodao Productions
title: Church demands Pastor’s immediate release
content:
The police arrested a pastor of the United Church of Christ in the Philippines (UCCP) as he landed at Ninoy Aquino International Airport early Tuesday morning and is now detained in Calamba, Laguna.




Reverend Edwin Egar is undergoing arrest proceedings by the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group, UCCP said. Altermidya reported he is being accused of terrorism financing charges, a bailable offense.




The Church said its pastor is an active worker within the United Batangas Conference of its South Luzon Jurisdiction.




“His ministry has extended well beyond the confines of the church; he has been actively responsive to the calls and needs of the marginalized sectors in the region,” it said.




The Reverend was reportedly fresh from a missionary stint abroad.




The UCCP said Rev. Egar’s assistance to those suffering is not a crime but a living expression of faith. It called on authorities to ensure the reverend’s safety, respect his human rights and right to due process, and immediately clarify the legal basis for his arrest.




“Any deprivation of liberty or violation of an individual’s rights must be addressed with the utmost seriousness. The dignity, freedom, and rights of any person cannot be cast aside. As a Church and as people of faith, it is our duty to take a stand against injustice and to defend the oppressed,” UCCP added.




The UCCP said it demands its pastor’s immediate release. # 

(Raymund B. Villanueva)

Church demands Pastor’s immediate release

 appeared first on 

Kodao Productions

author: Önder Algedik
title: COP31 collapsed in Türkiye. The hosts’ fossil ties did not
content:
The COP31 talks in Antalya ended on November 22 without a decision. It was the first such failure since Copenhagen in 2009. In Australia, the argument is about Chris Bowen.

Here is what the argument leaves out.

Saudi Arabia kept a fixed position through the second week: The text must not mention fossil fuels and should boost carbon capture, delegates told Reuters. NPR reports that Saudi Arabia and Russia blocked fossil fuels from the final agreement. The European Union (EU) also hardened its position, according to Reuters.

The rejection came from the other side.

The EU, several small island states and other vulnerable countries said they could not accept a text that failed to mention oil, gas and coal. Ireland’s climate minister, speaking for the EU, said the COP was “hijacked by some oil states”.

Vanuatu’s delegation called the silence on fossil fuels unacceptable. Least developed countries and the African Union also objected over finance, accusing the EU of failing to honour past commitments. The Marshall Islands delegation said the Pacific was “let down on all sides”.

The people who said no to a text without fossil fuels were the people most exposed to them. They are not the people who wrote it that way.

Saudi, Chinese and Russian officials frequently visited the presidency offices, as Saturday became Sunday, delegates told Reuters, while other groups struggled to secure meetings.

Negotiators from Europe, small island states, Latin America, Asia and Africa said Saudi Arabia had disproportionate access. The Turkish presidency said no group or country received preferential treatment!

I cannot prove a link between what Türkiye signs and who gets a meeting. The ties themselves are public. Türkiye and Saudi Arabia signed a renewable energy agreement worth about US$2 billion in February. It entered into force on October 21 and a further memorandum was signed in Antalya on November 10, witnessed by President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan.

On November 5, four days before COP31 opened, the Turkish parliament ratified the Mecca defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, by 279 votes to 119.

Then, the day after the COP31 talks collapsed, the Russian gas corporation Novatek’s chairperson said in China that it had signed an liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply contract with Türkiye. The counterparty, volume and term were not disclosed.

Türkiye presided over COP31, through Murat Kurum, its environment, urbanisation and climate change minister. Australia led the negotiations, through the Climate Change and Energy Minister Bowen, with “exclusive authority ” over them.

That matters more than the blame game in Canberra suggests.

Bowen’s 18-page draft of November 16 called for a phase-out of fossil fuels. By Thursday, it was nine pages without fossil fuels and the Pacific Resilience Facility Australia had championed.

Bowen presented the final text with Kurum. The ABC’s Laura Tingle reported that he conceded red lines on fossil fuels and finance had blocked a deal. She also noted that Türkiye effectively set the conditions while Australia carried the negotiating burden.

Coalition Opposition leader Angus Taylor, who wants Australia to scrap its already weak net zero targets, said Bowen should resign. Albanese answered by invoking the national interest. Nobody mentioned the coal and gas mine expansions.

Australia was named Fossil of the Day as the first draft came out, with the Climate Action Network counting 38 coal and gas approvals since 2022. On October 14, the federal government approved 30 million tonnes more coal at Boggabri, until 2040.

Most emissions from such projects occur overseas.

One host approves projects. The other signs contracts. The units differ; an approval is not a contract. The direction is the same.

By my count, Türkiye has signed 19 fossil fuel agreements since September 2025, plus six nuclear and mining deals, which I count separately. Novatek would be the 20th. In the venue, 103 fossil fuel and polluting organisations registered. Sixty were fossil fuel interests and 45 came as Türkiye’s guests.

For the Pacific and the vulnerable countries, the talks’ collapse is a loss they can name. For the fossil order it costs nothing. It can lose a text. It cannot afford to lose a mine, a pipeline or a contract that runs for decades and none of those were on the table in Antalya. A text decides what governments agree to say. Approvals and contracts decide what they do.

So the useful measure of COP31 is not whether a paragraph survived. It is what was approved or signed while it was being drafted. By that measure, the summit did not fail the fossil order. It worked.

Our demands are structural: No new coal, oil or gas projects, starting with the extensions in Australia’s approvals queue and the contracts on Türkiye’s desk; an end to fossil fuel subsidies; public ownership of energy; free public transport.

These are the demands of a climate revolution, not of a better summit.

Count the approvals. Count the contracts. Then write the text.

[Önder Algedik is a climate researcher and activist with 350Ankara. His new book, Ya Fosil Düzen Ya Devrim (Fossil Order or Revolution), is published by İletişim.]

author: Dulce Amor Rodriguez
title: Women seek justice for Duterte drug war victims
content:
Photo by Jonathan Sta. Rosa/NCCP

Trigger warning: details of violence and death

Seeing her son crying as she was about to leave for the market, she gave him a piece of candy. She later found him dead upon coming back home.

Emily Soriano was among the women whose loved ones were killed during former president Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war. They shared their accounts of the killings, highlighting their continuing struggle for justice with leaders of the World Council of Churches (WCC).

Members of Rise Up for Life and for Rights, a network of relatives of people killed during the anti-drug campaign, recounted their experiences during a dialogue organized by the National Council of Churches in the Philippines (NCCP).

The dialogue formed part of Thursdays in Black, a WCC campaign that seeks to end violence against women.

Aside from Soriano, Normita Lopez recounted how police shot her son despite his attempt to surrender. According to her, witnesses saw him raise both hands and plead with the police not to shoot but an officer pushed him down and shot him four times in the body and once in his right hand.

For her part, Jane Lee said that people ignored their pleas for justice before the WCC facilitated her travel to bring the families’ stories to the United Nations.

Estrella Nonay said, “I didn’t know how to get justice, so I joined Rise Up because I believe that if one of us gets justice, it is also justice for my son.”

“We are sharing with you sacred stories. Now that you have heard them, you are witnesses. We invite the WCC to stand in solidarity with the families of the victims in their quest for justice,” Deaconess Norma Dollaga of Rise Up said.

Rev. Merlyn Hyde Riley, vice-moderator of the WCC Central Committee, said that the testimonies exposed deeper structural, political, economic, social, and spiritual issues behind the killings. “No human being deserves to be treated in the ways you have described your loved ones having been treated,” Hyde Riley said.

Rev. Dr. Karen Georgia Thompson, general minister and president of the United Church of Christ and president of the World Communion of Reformed Churches, also called on churches to confront state violence against poor and marginalized communities.

She said that poor and marginalized communities bear the brunt of programs designed to harm them and urged churches to uphold human rights and dignity. (DAA)

author: Rizomatica
title: Seis en huelga en la cárcel, en sus casas un gran nudo en las gargantas
content:
Revisando hoy las redes sociales me entero de que seis de los dieciocho condenados por el caso Molino Grollmus iniciaron una huelga de hambre seca en la cárcel de Biobío. Uno de ellos es José Melgarejo Calbullanca, a quien represento. La noticia me golpea, porque de todo lo que he visto de la cárcel aplicada a los mapuche, lo más duro, sin duda, es la huelga. Duro para el preso y duro para su familia, porque no solo deja de alimentarse el huelguista: les aseguro que la garganta de sus mujeres y de sus madres difícilmente traga, de solo saber que allá adentro los suyos están dispuestos a morir por justicia.




Por: 

Daniela Sierra

, Abogada.




Una huelga no es una medida de presión, ni una puesta en escena. Sin agua, el cuerpo empieza a apagarse en días, no en semanas. A eso no se llega por cálculo; se llega cuando ya no quedan puertas que golpear.




¿Qué piden? Lo primero, que se anule un juicio en que se condenó con testigos que nadie vio. Así de simple. En el caso de José, dos de los testigos con identidad reservada nunca pisaron la sala: la Fiscalía renunció a ellos, y lo que supuestamente dijeron lo contaron unos policías, de oídas. Los jueces no les vieron la cara, la defensa no pudo hacerles una sola pregunta, y con eso a José le dieron más de ochenta años de cárcel.




La Convención Americana garantiza a todo acusado el derecho a interrogar a quien lo acusa (art. 8.2 f), y el Código Procesal Penal obliga a condenar solo con la prueba rendida en el juicio (art. 340). La Corte Interamericana ya se lo dijo a Chile en 2014, y en un caso mapuche, Norín Catrimán: no se puede condenar únicamente o en grado decisivo con testigos de identidad reservada. Y eso era con testigos que al menos declararon. Aquí, ni eso.




Tampoco se pide impunidad, como tanto les gusta repetir. Si la Corte Suprema anula, la ley ordena un juicio nuevo (art. 386 del Código Procesal Penal), esta vez con las reglas del juego, y si la prueba no alcanza, la absolución. Eso se resuelve el jueves en la Corte Suprema, que es donde se tiene que resolver; no en La Moneda ni en ninguna reunión con ministros.




Lo segundo que piden huele, para algunos, a privilegio: un módulo para presos mapuche en Biobío, que puedan entrar la machi y el logko, comer su comida, vestir su ropa, hablar chedungun, tener trabajo y talleres. Privilegio, dicen, como si rezar, comer lo propio y hablar la lengua de la abuela fueran lujos de hotel.




Pero el Convenio 169 de la OIT, vigente en Chile desde 2009, obliga a proteger las prácticas espirituales de los pueblos indígenas (art. 5), a considerar su cultura cuando se les impone una pena (art. 10) y a darles una salud que respete su propia medicina (art. 25). Las Reglas Mandela de Naciones Unidas exigen respetar las creencias de cada preso, ofrecerle educación y trabajo, y permitirle practicar su fe con alguien de su propia tradición (reglas 2, 4, 65 y 66). Y el Reglamento de Establecimientos Penitenciarios dice algo que debería bastar: fuera de los derechos que la condena le quita, el preso conserva la misma condición jurídica que cualquier ciudadano libre (art. 2).




Lo más curioso es que nada de esto es nuevo. Gendarmería informó a la Corte de Apelaciones de Temuco que su módulo de comuneros tiene encomiendas con alimentación culturalmente pertinente, acceso a lawen, medicina tradicional y machi, y talleres de trabajo. Es decir, lo que se pide en Biobío ya existe en Temuco. Entonces la pregunta no es por qué regalarles un privilegio, sino por qué un mapuche pierde derechos según la cárcel a la que lo manden.




El Estado tiene a estos seis hombres bajo su custodia y responde por su vida. Pero la salida no está en sentarse a mirar cuánto aguanta el cuerpo. Está en que la Corte Suprema aplique el estándar que ya se le impuso a Chile.




Lo que piden es juicio justo, no impunidad. Lo mínimo, eso que la humanidad ya pagó con demasiada sangre. Y que, mientras tanto, allá afuera, sus mujeres, sus madres, puedan volver a respirar a la espera del futuro abrazo de los suyos.







*Enviado a la radio




Esta información se publicó en 

Radio Kurruf

.

author: Rizomatica
title: Comunicado inicio huelga de hambre Presos Políticos Mapuche del caso Grollmus
content:
«Comunicado inicio huelga de hambre ppm caso grollmus, 23/11/2026.




Marimari kom pu che, pu logko, pu werken, pu machi, pu weychabe, pu lob.




El día de hoy, nosotros, los abajo firmantes, venimos a informar a la opinión publica nacional e internacional, que tras largos procesos de discusión entre nosotros, prisioneros políticos mapuche lavkenche, y nuestros lov y comunidades, hemos tomado la decisión de iniciar una movilización consistente en una huelga de hambre de carácter seca e indefinida, esto como medio para exigir el petitorio que detallamos a continuación:




1) Nulidad y absolución para nosotros, los 18 Presos Políticos Mapuche recientemente condenados injustamente por el Caso Molino Grollmus. El tribunal de Cañete resolvió una pena ponderada de 1055 años, resolución judicial morbosa basada únicamente en 4 relatos de testigos protegidos y sin absolutamente ninguna prueba técnica o científica de corroboración.




2) Creación de un Modulo para Prisioneros Políticos Mapuche en el CP Biobio, para condenados e imputados, donde se garanticen no privilegios sino derechos internacional y nacionalmente consagrados.




• Este módulo garantizará espacio de cocina e ingreso tolerante y mayor de alimentos en la lista de providencias.




• Derecho a practicar ceremonias mapuche (acceso de pu machi, pu logko y pu werken )




• 100 cupos de enrolamiento por comuneros.




• Mayor encomienda, días de visita y venusterio.




• Garantía de usar vestimenta tradicional




• Acceso a Salud Intercultural (machi, lawentuchebe, ngutamchebe, pewmatube)




3) Plan de intervención con profesionales mapuche, con competencias culturales y profesionales, dupla psicólogo y trabajador social intercultural.




4) Área laboral donde se garantice acceso a talleres de trabajo para condenados e imputados.




5) Área educacional, talleres de mapudugun y cultura por profesionales competentes.




Las demandas anteriormente expuestas son justas y legitimas y deberán garantizarse mediante las firmas de las autoridades competentes. Llamamos de forma activa a nuestro pueblo a la solidaridad y movilización por la libertad y mejores condiciones carcelarias para los presos políticos mapuche. Creemos que el camino de la Unidad Nacional dotara a nuestro pueblo de la fuerza social para continuar luchando por la recuperación de nuestro territorio, así como por la retirada de las fuerzas de ocupación del Gulumapu, por la autonomía y autodeterminación del Wallmapu.




Finalmente exigimos el traslado de vuelta a Concepción del comunero Federico Astete Catrileo, recluido en la cárcel de Valdivia, y el fin a su injustificado régimen de alta seguridad y aislamiento.




Nelson Alonso Llempi

Jose Melgarejo Calbullanca




David Mariñan Millahual




Javier Mariñan Millahual.




¡Marichiwew!




CP Bío Bío

Pu Machi, pu Lonko, pu Wuenen, pu Werken, pu Weichave, pu Kona.




Rekuluwaiñ ka yavuluwaiñ ni ta tuvachi weichan.

title: Primeros Auxilios en contexto de manifestación callejera, segunda edición
content:
Movilización de jubiladxs el 24 de septiembre del año 2025. Fotografía: Andrés Manrique (ANRed).




Muchas veces, el primer objetivo de la represión es inducir temor para desairar primero y después desarticular las resistencias populares. Contra ello, ANRed libera la segunda edición de

 “Primeros Auxilios en contexto de manifestación callejera”

, una recopilación de medidas y cuidados básicos a la hora de hacernos de las calles.




Saber de primeros auxilios en contextos donde predomina la violencia puede ser un aporte muy valioso, que tiene en sí mismo un efecto tranquilizador. Además, las personas que no recibieron entrenamiento en primeros auxilios suelen dudar al momento de actuar, o tienen miedo de ayudar por falta de seguridad para recordar las maniobras.




Si bien no frenará la decisión política de mutilar, intentamos generar conciencia sobre la importancia de cuidar nuestros cuerpos, con los que trabajamos y sostenemos nuestras vidas y las de otros, y enfatizamos en aquellas cosas que sí podemos hacer para cuidarnos. En particular, esta guía está orientada a la prevención.




Recordamos que los cuidados son siempre una tarea colectiva, históricamente menospreciada pero fundamental para cualquier resistencia. Este es nuestro aporte.




Estamos hace 32 años en las calles, practicando la comunicación alternativa, comunitaria y popular. Acompañando las luchas siempre, mostrando lo que otros omiten y silencian.

author: Esperanza
title: RED ESTUDIANTIL TEMUCO: «Nos interesa generar una alianza social que sea capaz de soportar la arremetida neoriberal que estamos viviendo en este Gobierno».
content:
Tras conocer el proyecto de presupuesto de gobierno para el 2027, se registraron diversas manifestaciones para expresar el descontento social en algunas ciudades del país. Temuco fue una de ellas y en ese contexto conversamos con uno de los representantes de la Red Estudiantil Temuco.




Giordano Leonelli, estudiante Sociología Ufro y parte de la Red Estudiantil Temuco, una alianza entre la Universidad Católica de Temuco, La Universidad de La Frontera y estudiantes secundarios para activar movilizaciones en la ciudad de Temuco.




Hace algunas semanas, se vieron concentraciones y marchas que recorrieron el centro de la ciudad, convocadas por el sector estudiantil. Movilizaciones que surgen principalmente como respuesta tras conocerse los anuncios de recortes en el área de educación para el próximo año. 







«Sabemos las consecuencias que van a tener, van a ser despidos de funcionarios, peores condiciones para estudiar, peor infraestructura. Así como un debilitamiento de la educación pública, lo que nos parece bastante problemático». Giordano Leonelli, Red Estudiantil Temuco.







Como Red, ven la necesidad que el movimiento estudiantil se debe volver a rearticular, tal como en años anteriores. En esa misma línea realizaron un pliego de demandas para presentar un petitorio a nivel Temuco y sumado a ello se levantó un petitorio con alcance a nivel nacional que no solo reúne demandas sobre los recorte a la educación, sino también considera problemáticas asociadas a la salud, el medioambiente, el trabajo, la criminalización a la protesta popular, entre otros puntos.







«Nos interesa generar una alianza social que sea capaz de soportar la arremetida neoriberal que estamos viviendo en este Gobierno». Leonelli describe que trabajan por una articulación social, no partidista,que responda a los intereses de la población.







Se espera que para inicio de 2027 surjan nuevas movilizaciones con la consigna de frenar los recortes, todo en medio de un complejo escenario económico que enfrenta el país, en lo inmediato, la 

Red estudiantil Temuco llama sumarse como bloque a la Jornada de Protesta Nacional convocada por profesores y sindicatos de trabajadores para el martes 24 de noviembre, en la Plaza del Hospital en Temuco, desde las 16:30 hrs.

author: Owen Marsden-Readford
title: The irrationality of the AI bubble is the irrationality of the market
content:
The AI investment boom is one of the largest bets in the history of capitalism. Money is pouring into the tech industry. Global AI spending is forecast to reach $2.7 trillion this year and $10 trillion cumulatively by 2032. The priorities of the system are obscene. Ending world hunger, according to the United Nations World Food Programme, would cost $40 billion per year. Amazon is spending over four times this on AI infrastructure this year.

In Australia alone, $150 billion is committed to building AI infrastructure over the next five years. That money could be life-changing for workers if it was used for almost anything else. Diverting the money from the data centre buildout could fund Australia’s health and Medicare budget for one year. Imagine the improvements we could make to an over-stretched and under-funded hospital system. With $150 billion, we could house the 200,000 households on the public housing waiting list at an average cost of just under half a million dollars and still have $50 billion left over. 

The $150 billion committed to data centres could also be used to pay for the Labor government’s aged care expansion package 38 times over. Or we could fund a significant chunk of the green transition needed to limit runaway climate change. The Australian Energy Market Operator places the cost of decarbonising the National Electricity Market by 2050 at $122 billion.

​Alas, the ever-rational invisible hand of the market has decided that we need more data centres to power Elon Musk’s Grok AI and its

 epic, vulgar roasts

.

​That the AI boom is socially destructive is irrelevant to investors. Data centres guzzle fossil fuels and water and are a significant source of noise pollution, emitting a constant low, droning hum. Most of the data centre buildout is happening in working-class and poorer communities in Western Sydney, not in Mosman or Toorak.

In recent weeks, the AI stock market boom has faced a sharp downturn. This is not because the world’s capitalists have taken notice of the socially and environmentally destructive nature of the industry, but because they are concerned that future windfall profits may not materialise.

​AI is now integrated into the militaries across the world, the result of an AI arms race. The results are terrifying. Take Russia’s

 

ZALA Lancet drone

, which uses AI to spot and dive bomb targets free from human oversight.

​Bosses are using AI as an excuse to sack workers. In the past few weeks alone, Qantas, NAB and Canva have announced over 4,000 redundancies cumulatively. Moreover, the data centre buildout is pushing inflation upwards, which the Reserve Bank is using as an excuse to raise interest rates, pushing unemployment higher. It is yet another way the AI boom is coming at the expense of the working class.

​The insanities of the AI boom are the insanities of the market. It is only in a capitalist society driven by profit and competition that it makes sense for trillions of dollars to be ploughed into AI while working-class needs are neglected. For anything that would benefit the working class, governments and capitalists across the world cry poor. Yet when there’s a share market boom, trillions find their way into it with no thought for what society actually needs. 

It’s not like people are crying out for data centres. In the US midterm elections, when data centres were on the ballot, voters rejected data centre expansion or approved local restrictions in 40 out of 41 ballot measures. AI data centres are unpopular yet continue to be imposed on ordinary people. Genuine democracy and the capitalist market are incompatible.

Under capitalism, production occurs to enrich the capitalist class, not to meet human needs. Karl Marx wrote in Capital: “Accumulate, accumulate! That is Moses and the prophets!” In a market economy, maximising shareholder value counts for more than the cries of hungry children or the plight of the homeless. 

​The AI boom is making many capitalists astronomically rich. Tech billionaires gained a combined $845 billion through the first nine months of this year. The stock market has reached record highs multiple times in 2026. The benefits of the AI bubble concentrate at the top, in the hands of corporate executives, financiers and the rich more generally. Workers, on the other hand, receive almost nothing. There is no boom in wages. Huge speculative wealth sits alongside stagnant or falling living standards.

​No boom, however, can last forever. After the Global Financial Crisis, the banks were bailed out while the working class faced cuts to jobs, social services and wages. An AI crash would be no different. If the bubble bursts, big tech will scream for government money, and the working class will be made to front the cost. On top of this, between 7 percent and 12 percent of the average superannuation portfolio is invested in AI and big tech. A crisis will wipe out a sizable chunk of ordinary people’s retirement savings.

​All the risks are obvious, yet the AI investment mania continues apace. Such is the irrationality of the market.

author: Kodao Productions
title: Donald Trump extorts the Philippines
content:
The latest boast of lame duck US President Donald Trump that the Philippines has agreed to source all of its energy and food imports from the US is as credible as his claim that the Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni pleaded for a photo with him, or his insistence with Russian President Vladimir Putin that the Israelis adore him as to name a plaza in his honor, forcing Putin to deliver a snarky riposte: “Donald, Israel should rename their country after you.” Trump didn’t understand the insult, which was not lost in the translation.




Perhaps as worse was the yarn that Mexico had permitted US forces to operate within its territory, which President Caludia Sheinbaum debunked, saying US troops should stick to their US bases, or the brag of years past that Mexico would pay for the thousands of kilometers of durable and impenetrable fence he was building to separate it from the US. Americans paid for the few kilometers of the overpriced fence built by Trump minions.




Trump is a media hog, like the 

bangka

 in a drinking spree who conjures stories the way Rodrigo Duterte does, and the usual result is that out of the 10 stories dished out, 11 are false. Trump was battered worldwide for insulting Meloni and Italy and the Mexican people made him the butt of jokes for years for being such a *puerile, reckless and bad storyteller. First of all, he cannot be serious about anything or anybody, save perhaps for his nanny Natalie Harp, and he can hardly understand what he is punishing the media industry with.




As in the case of Fox News before, the defense was that audiences knew that Tucker Carlson was not credible, so it is their call whether to believe him or despise him. Trump is worse that Carlson since the more he talks, the deeper he burrows in his rabbit hole. The guy simply is a congenital liar. Believe him at your peril. So when this clown spewed his latest insult, that the Philippines agreed to buy all its energy and farm imports from the United States otherwise the Mutual Defense Treaty (MDT) cannot be invoked to defend the country from a possible Chinese attack, Malacanang should have taken a forceful response.




The retort to this extortion by Trump was a pablum, with the Palace saying Manila only tackled possible energy imports, noting that the Philippines doesn’t import gas from the US. As the US is saying it would export LNG, it is time for Manila to join the fun. Government is not saying that the US already exports shiploads of farm commodities to the country, from potatoes to specialty rice (with so many hundredweights—59.09 kilos each), as well as wheat, milk, meat and others. The response was **anodyne, not meant to be an underhanded compliment to a court jester and not a double-bladed 

beinte nuebe

 from Batangas that could bury deeply into Trump’s carcass.




The administration should have been forthright to tell Trump that a global trading system operates in which the Philippines takes part and that the parity rights ended in 1974, when the Marcos dictatorship that Trump supported to the hilt was in its full bloom. Seventeen years later, the US military bases were kicked out of the Philippines for being precisely the bases of the country’s insecurity. Flashback to the confrontation with Malaysia over the Sabah issue and the US never sided with the Philippines despite the possibility of hostilities. The UK sided with Malaysia and the country was left in the lurch. The ironclad guarantee that US forces would come to fight for the Philippines evaporated.




As the late warmonger Henry Kissinger said being an enemy of the US is dangerous but being a friend of the US is fatal. The French knew it (the US hasn’t paid the money it owed Paris for supporting the US revolution against British colonialism), African countries understood it and Latin American nations had despised the Monroe Doctrine since 1823 and its latest reiteration, the Trump Latrine. By trying to make Trump look good with illogical statements, the Philippine government is massaging his fragile but galactic ego. This is like pulling blood out of stone or pulling hen’s teeth.




It is pretty clear, to most Filipinos anyway but not to Malacanang and the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA), that on a humdrum day at the White House, Trump would always consult his crystal ball of lies and issue statements that have nothing to do with reality, or even with the agreements and side deals that he had cut. Trump is too much of a coward as to fight a pitched battle with enemies his size. He could not even pursue his idiotic campaign to use high tariffs inflicted on his trading partners to generate so much cash as to render income taxes unnecessary. After the Nov. 3 midterm debacle, Trump is left with a trio of discordant voices—Natalie Harp, Steven Cheung and Stephen Miller – along with the Opus Dei zealot Leonard Leo and the promoters of Project 2025, some of whom have already beaten a hasty retreat. As to the equally narcissistic Elon Musk, he is now waving the white flag to the Democrats. #




= = = = =




WORDS OF THE DAY




Puerile

 – childishly silly, immature, or lacking seriousness.




Anodyne

 – relieving or soothing pain, or—more commonly in everyday speech—inoffensive, bland, and unlikely to cause controversy.

Donald Trump extorts the Philippines

Kodao Productions

author: Unknown
title: Kayyım atanan HalkTV'den nöbeti "Halk Televizyonu" devraldı
content:
Halk TV'ye 14 Ekim'de kayyım atanmasının ardından kanaldan ayrılan gazeteciler, Halk Televizyonu adıyla yeni bir yayın platformu kurdu. İlk canlı yayın, gazeteci Gökhan Kayış'ın sunumuyla 23 Kasım akşamı gerçekleştirildi.




Kayış, açılışta Uğur Dündar, Serhan Asker, Dinçer Gökçe ve avukat Seraf Özer'i ağırladı. Yayına gazeteciler, siyasetçiler ve meslek örgütü temsilcileri de canlı bağlantılarla katıldı.




Kayış, yeni yayın girişiminin nasıl ortaya çıktığını şu sözlerle anlattı:







“Kayyum atandıktan sonra dedik ki kardeşim bu memleketi bırakıp gidecek halimiz yok. Umutsuzluğa kapılacak halimiz de yok.”







Gazeteciliği sürdürebilecekleri yeni bir alan oluşturduklarını belirten Kayış, “Biz de bütün her şeye inat, bütün kayyum uygulamalarına inat Halk Televizyonunun macerasını başlattık” dedi.




Uğur Dündar: “Halkın gerçekleri öğrenme hakkına hizmet" 




Açılış yayınına katılan Uğur Dündar, gazeteciliğin temel işlevinin kamuoyunu bilgilendirmek olduğunu vurguladı:







“Gazeteciliği kaba anlamıyla tanımlarsak halkın gerçekleri öğrenme hakkına yapılan bir hizmettir gazetecilik mesleği.”







Dündar, iktidarların kamuoyunun gerçeklere ulaşmasını engellemeye çalışabildiğini belirterek araştırmacı gazeteciliğin karşılaştığı baskılara dikkat çekti.







“Görevimiz bu işi yaptığımız sürece doğruları, sadece doğruları, sonuna kadar doğruları söylemektir. Ve bunu yaparken de evrensel meslek ilkelerimize sıkı sıkıya bağlı kalmaktır.”







Dündar, yeni girişimin ekonomik dayanışma boyutuna da değindi. Halk TV'den ayrılan çalışanlar arasında ciddi geçim sıkıntısı yaşayanlar olduğunu belirterek YouTube gelirlerinin bu kişilere destek amacıyla kullanılabileceğini söyledi.







“Eğer bu kanal YouTube'dan para kazanırsa, ne kadar çok kazanırsa kazansın lütfen bana tek kuruş vermeyin. İhtiyacı olan arkadaşlarımıza dağıtın.”







TGC: “Basın hürdür, sansür edilemez”




Türkiye Gazeteciler Cemiyeti temsilcisi Sibel Güneş, canlı bağlantıyla katıldığı yayında medya kuruluşlarına yönelik kayyım uygulamalarını eleştirdi.




Güneş, son iki yılda çok sayıda televizyon kanalının yayınlarının sona erdiğini belirterek Halk TV, Tele1 ve Sözcü TV çalışanlarının karşılaştığı sorunlara dikkat çekti.




Anayasa'nın 28. ve 30. Maddelerini hatırlatan Güneş, şöyle konuştu:







“Anayasa 28. maddesi basın hürdür, sansür edilemez diyor. 30. madde de çok net basın araçlarının işletilmekten alıkonulamayacağını ifade ediyor.”







Güneş, Halk TV'ye yönelik soruşturmanın doğrudan yayın içerikleriyle ilgili olmadığını, buna rağmen yayınların durdurulduğunu söyledi.







“Biz haberin serbest dolaşımını istiyoruz ve sizler gibi değerli meslektaşlarımızın, üyelerimizin görevlerini yapabilir olmasını istiyoruz.”







“Bu yaptığınız şey bir yumruk sıkmaktır”




Yayına katılan gazeteci Zafer Arapkirli de yeni girişimi basın üzerindeki baskılara karşı bir dayanışma örneği olarak değerlendirdi.







“Bu yaptığınız şey bir yumruk sıkmaktır Gökhan. Yani baskıya karşı, istibdata karşı, faşizme karşı, bağımsız medyanın gırtlağını sıkmaya çalışan o kötü güçlere karşı bir yumruk sıkmaktır.”







Arapkirli, bağımsız haberciliğin farklı mecralarda sürdürülmesi gerektiğini belirterek şöyle devam etti:







“Bugün Halk Televizyonu, öbür gün başka bir kanal, başka bir gün başka bir kanal.”







Serhan Asker ise Halk TV'de yaptığı programların izleyicilerle kurduğu ilişkiye dikkat çekti. Kayyım sonrasında eski programlarının yayımlanmaya devam ettiğini, buna karşılık çalışanların iş ve sosyal haklarına ilişkin sorunların çözülemediğini söyledi.







“Yani işten çıktık, haklı fesihle ihtar gönderdik. Görüşelim, konuşalım diyoruz. Bir görüşme iklimi de bulamadık ne yazık ki.”







İlk yayında 100 bin abone




Açılış yayını sırasında kanalın YouTube abone sayısı hızla yükseldi. Yayının başlangıcında yaklaşık 39 bin olarak açıklanan sayı, programın üçüncü saatini geçmesinin ardından 100 bine ulaştı.




Kayış, yayın sırasında izleyicilere teşekkür ederken yeni platformun yalnızca bir gelir kaynağı olarak görülmemesi gerektiğini söyledi:




“Gerçekten vazgeçmememizin sebebi memleket meselesi. Sadece gelir kapısı olarak bakmıyoruz.”




Halk Televizyonu ekibi, haber ve programlarını YouTube ile sosyal medya hesapları üzerinden sürdürmeyi hedefliyor.




(AEK)

title: Even Hegseth’s Former Chief of Staff Says It’s Time for Him to Be Ousted
content:
The secretary’s former top aide blasted the Iran war as a “shitshow.”

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth’s former chief of staff has said that the secretary should resign over his handling of the Iran war and internal Pentagon affairs, adding to calls for Hegseth’s ousting after he narrowly survived an impeachment attempt earlier this month.

In an interview with Politico, former top Hegseth aide Joe Kasper said that the secretary has become obsessed with his ego and image, as well as his mission to drastically remake the Pentagon in his violent, white supremacist image. Hegseth’s focus on boosting himself and his “showmanship” are getting in the way of his “ability to be effective,” Kasper said.

Kasper, who was Hegseth’s chief of staff for the first three months of President Donald Trump’s current term, rattled off a list of what he feels are Hegseth’s failures. For one, the U.S. war on Iran, in which the U.S. has killed thousands of civilians in Iran, has been a “shitshow,” he said — a popular view even among some Republicans in Congress and in the administration.

The Iran War was a major focus of Rep. Thomas Massie’s (R-Kentucky) impeachment attempt earlier this month. Massie’s articles accused Hegseth of violating the law in waging the war without Congress’s approval while violating civilian protection laws both in strikes on Iran and in the U.S.’s boat strike campaign.

Massie’s impeachment articles narrowly failed, after several Democrats missed the vote, but Democrats are preparing to target him again when they take over Congress.

Meanwhile, Kasper also criticized Hegseth for gutting top leadership at the Pentagon, seemingly specifically targeting senior Black and female figures in the military.

“At almost every high-profile position, or every senior leader position, there’s a vacancy,” he said.

Those fired included three top Pentagon officials who were dismissed last year, during Kasper’s time in the Pentagon, over supposed leaks to the media. Kasper said there was no evidence that those officials had ever leaked any information at all — and Hegseth recently subjected dozens of members of the Joint Staff to polygraph tests in order to seek out more alleged leakers.

Interestingly, Kasper seems to have been personally involved in those three officials’ ousting, even though he now says that there was no evidence of leaks. Last year, Politico reported that Kasper was a major player in their dismissals, done in “an attempt to consolidate power.” Kasper denied that claim, which came from sources familiar with the matter.

Kasper departed the Pentagon shortly after those dismissals, without any public bad blood between him and Hegseth, who sang his praises after he left.

Kasper also criticized Hegseth for a recent incident in which Hegseth and his staff were reprimanded for laughing at a Veterans Day ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier; “distractions” like his testosterone testing and supplement initiative; and his inability to work with other figures on Capitol Hill, like those in Congress.

“He’s not just burned bridges up on the Hill,” Kasper said. “He’s napalmed them.”

He predicted that Hegseth is going to be ousted in one way or the other. “He’s going to be suffocated, and it’s not like it’s going to be a slow suffocation. It’s going to be a quick asphyxiation.”

author: Daron Letts
title: Forensic psychiatrist testifies in 1st-degree murder trial
content:
A man who allegedly killed his wife was not “completely psychotic” at the time she was shot, a forensic psychiatrist told an Iqaluit courtroom Monday.




 Dr. Maryana Kravtsenyuk testified Monday during the 

first-degree murder trial of Danny Paul Eyaituk, an Iqaluit man charged with first-degree murder in the death of 

his wife Annie Tracy Oqaituq, 36, who was found dead in their Sanikiluaq home on April 19, 2024.




The trial began June 9 in Sanikiluaq and continued until June 25 but stopped while 

Kravtsenyuk was on the stand

 due to witness, judge, counsel and courtroom availability, defence lawyer Alan Regel said in an email to Nunatsiaq News.




Canada’s Criminal Code says a person cannot be held responsible for a crime committed while suffering from a mental health disorder that makes them incapable of appreciating the nature of the act.




Regel had asked Kravtsenyuk to prepare a report to assess whether Eyaituk could be found not criminally responsible.




The report established that Eyaituk has suffered from mental illness, including paranoia, since childhood and that he was addicted to cannabis and cocaine at the time of the alleged incident.




Drug use can be a contributing factor in sudden changes in mental health, Kravtsenyuk said in the report. Eyaituk’s mental health breakdowns were exacerbated by substance use and stress from conflict in his marriage, she added.
















Late Monday morning, Regel asked Kravtsenyuk about Eyaituk’s state of mind on the day Oqaituq died.




“He did not appear completely detached from reality or profoundly confused regarding the consequences of the alleged act,” she replied, quoting from her report.




Eyaituk appeared alert in court, wearing a blue sweatshirt with a crucifix around his neck. His hair was tied back in a short ponytail.




The first half of the proceeding lacked an Inuktitut interpreter, for which Justice Susan Cooper apologized.




She scheduled final submissions for Tuesday morning, as long as an interpreter could go over the morning’s proceedings with Eyaituk on Monday afternoon.

author: Valerie Anne
title: Liv Hewson Opens Up to Drew Barrymore About the Early Parts of Their Career
content:
feature image photo by The Drew Barrymore Show/Ash Bean via Getty Images

Yellowjackets star Liv Hewson reunited with their former Santa Clarita Diet co-star Drew Barrymore on Drew’s talk show this week.

In the interview, they discuss all sorts of topics, including but not limited to Yellowjackets, of course. Drew presents Liv with gifts for what she thought was their engagement, but Liv reveals that actually they got married already. (There are actually really cute pics that pop up behind them of the couple as well in the clip, so you should check it out.) Drew’s now-wedding gifts are two beautiful candlesticks Drew said represents the two of them living together in harmony.

Liv talks about meeting their now-spouse on the set of Yellowjackets when they were AD, and recounts seeing them for the first time and having a “who IS that” moment immediately.

Drew shows Liv a clip of another of their Santa Clarita Diet co-stars, Skyler Gisondo, asking Liv to share dating advice, and their advice boils down to the fact that people want to feel safe and that should be a priority in any relationship, not just romantic. (This is not really here nor there but I could listen to Liv talk for hours. They have such a calming presence and such a thoughtful way of speaking and you can tell, even just from little clips and interviews, that they are a deeply intelligent person, both intellectually and emotionally, and I just really love hearing them talk about pretty much anything.)

The pair also talks about Molly Ringwald coming on Yellowjackets to play Van’s mother, and Liv says they really hit the jackpot when it came to fictional moms, having now had two legends (Molly and Drew herself) play their mom on television.

Liv also talks about how they felt like they were living in a “defensive crouch” for a long time; they came to the US to work when they were 20 and felt like they had to go back in the closet as nonbinary when they started working in Hollywood, but that Drew and the cast of Santa Clarita Diet became a soft place for them to land and they are really grateful to her for that.

It’s a very sweet interview and as sad as I am to see Yellowjackets come to an end, I’m really excited to see what Liv will get up to next, mostly because they are extremely talented and should be cast in whatever the hell they want, but also because, selfishly, I want to watch them on more press tours.

+ Miley Cyrus also got married, to drummer Maxx Morando

+ Cynthia Erivo will be hosting the Rockefeller Center tree lighting and Christmas special, alongside special guests that include Alanis Morrisette and Kelly Clarkson

+ A wild Lea DeLaria popped up in the show CIA playing someone named Marbles and it was such a bit part but I am already obsessed and hope we see more Marbles in the future

+ Hunter Schafer is kicking ass and taking names in her new series, Bladerunner 2099

+ Speaking of Hunter Schafer, she said she tried polyamory but is more into monogamy; she supports it of course but says there’s too much scheduling for her

+ Tennis legend Billie Jean King hopes her documentary Give Me the Ball! will help “any gay kid or trans kid”

+ Jennifer Love Hewitt is going to reunite with I Know What You Did Last Summer costar Ryan Phillippe in an upcoming 911/911: Nashville crossover (I know this is a stretch to include here but both shows do have queer women on them and also J.Love was one of my roots so LET ME HAVE THIS)

+ There’s something fruity going on with Venita and Salley on the reality show Southern Charm

+ Also: YELLOWJACKETS IS BACK which means so are Kayla’s recaps so be sure to check those out

title: Elektronik belge uygulamalarında yeni düzenleme Resmi Gazete'de
content:
Fotoğraf: Kampus Production/Pexels

Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı (GİB) tarafından hazırlanan "Vergi Usul Kanunu Genel Tebliği'nde Değişiklik Yapılmasına Dair Tebliğ" Resmi Gazete'de yayımlandı.

"Bilgi Fişi" tanımını yürürlükten kaldıran düzenleme, e-Arşiv Fatura uygulamasına dahil olmayan mükelleflere yeni belge düzenleme seçenekleri sundu. Bu mükellefler, 1 Ocak 2027'den itibaren faturalarını Güvenli Mobil Ödeme ve Elektronik Belge Yönetim Sistemi, Taksi Mali Cihazlar veya izin verilen Yeni Nesil Ödeme Kaydedici Cihazlar (YN ÖKC) üzerinden e-Arşiv Fatura olarak düzenleyebilecek.

Yerli ve yabancı film gösteren sinema işletmeleri, belirlenen usul ve esaslar doğrultusunda e-Bilet uygulamasına geçerek giriş biletlerini elektronik ortamda düzenlemek zorunda olacak.

İlgili bölümün başlığı, sinema işletmelerinin e-Bilet kullanma zorunluluğunu esas alacak şekilde değiştirildi. Yeni nesil ödeme kaydedici cihazlardan düzenlenen e-Bilet bilgi fişi ve aylık satış raporuna ilişkin ifadeler kaldırıldı.

e-Bilette eğlence vergisine ilişkin bölümde de bilgi fişleri ve aylık satış raporlarına yönelik atıflar çıkarıldı.

Elektronik belge düzenlenmesine izin verilen yeni nesil ödeme kaydedici cihazların arızalanması veya çalınması, kağıt belge düzenlenebilecek durumlar arasına alındı.

Bu imkânın kullanılabilmesi için arıza veya hırsızlık durumunun ispatlanması ya da belgelendirilmesi gerekecek.

Serbest meslek faaliyeti yürüten hekimlerden, e-Serbest Meslek Makbuzu uygulamasına dahil olan ve 593 sıra numaralı tebliğ kapsamında bu makbuzu düzenleyen yeni nesil ödeme kaydedici cihaz kullananlar, cihazlarını iş yerlerinde bulundurmaları şartıyla POS cihazlarını bulundurmak ve kullanmak zorunda olmayacak.

Tebliğ 1 Ocak 2027 tarihinde yürürlüğe girecek ve hükümlerini Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı yürütecek.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Christian Ferrer: A Testimonial
content:
The World’s Grand Guffaw




Diego Sztulwark




Lobo Suelto

, 22/11/2026




The very recent death of Christian Ferrer deepens our affection for him and allows us to revisit a host of conversations, readings and moments with a sense of gratitude. It is not a bad place to start: the nobility of the sentiments from which one thinks and writes — his rejection of resentment and bad faith — was a decisive matter for him.







Like so many other students at the Faculty of Social Sciences at the University of Buenos Aires (UBA) in the 1990s, I first learnt of Christian through the magazine 

El Ojo Mocho

. Those of us who were not studying Communication—and were therefore not his students—came into contact with him through his articles, rather than through that soft, measured tone with which he captivated endless cohorts of students. As a student activist in the mid-1990s, I did not have any particular fondness for him. Although I read his work with keen curiosity, I was drawn to that libertarian streak (please, let’s not get sidetracked by the infamous connotations of that little word; we’re being serious here) and his penchant for all manner of strange objects.




One summer in the second half of the 1990s – I can’t remember whether it was ’96 or ’97 – I bumped into 

Horacio González

 and Christian on a lovely beach in Rocha, Uruguay: Punta del Diablo. I’d just started as a teaching assistant in 

Rubén Dri

’s philosophy department, and I was racing against the clock, reading Hegel as much as I possibly could. One afternoon, Horacio and Christian, who were strolling along while arguing, came into the cabin where I was studying. One of the topics of their dispute was the university. Horacio, with a sardonic tone, was of the view that one should not consider the university in terms of admission or assessment criteria, and made mocking remarks such as “with anarchists, you always end up discussing order”. On one of those days, Christian advised me to abandon my utopian attempts to understand Kant and Hegel and to devote my efforts instead to reading Nietzsche. His work was more vital. It’s not a question, he said, of learning theoretical systems, but of having real conversations with genuinely provocative, powerful interlocutors. I tried to ignore him, but I failed.




In a sense, it was always like that with Christian. Whenever I tried to get closer to him, to share my concerns with him in militant language, I found myself faced with someone who, while listening, would lay down his own conditions: “Where you say “politics”, I hear “power””. He wasn’t interested in militant ideology, but he was interested in the country, Argentina, and history, the world. He could talk about that with great erudition, for hours on end. In that sense, listening to Christian was a learning experience. I tried to ignore his political anarchism, but – once again – I failed. Not because it made me change course, no. But it did create the conditions within me to become an attentive reader of his ideas. A reader, in the sense of needing to weigh up my own thoughts against his. A few days ago, 

Santiago López Petit

 was in Buenos Aires, reminding us that it is one thing to “engage in politics”, and quite another to “lead a political life”. The essence of the critique, which I admired in Christian, ran from the latter to the former. The weight of that distinction does not create a political system, but it does create a certain—undoubtedly virtuous—way of being. Having read Osvaldo Bayer and Gilles Deleuze, I never had any doubts about the appeal of the great libertarian ethic, nor about the superiority of what some philosophers call “ontological anarchism”: constituent praxis, set against a backdrop of a non-hierarchical nature.




But with Christian, one could not talk about theory. On one occasion he invited me to write something for a faculty journal that he edited. I think it was around 2001. He said to me, mockingly: “Write about political theory; I know nothing about that”. It was not, of course, that he was ignorant of theory; the matter simply made him sarcastic. His readings of Schopenhauer, Benjamin, Debord, Foucault and Deleuze were more incisive than many of the systematisations of those theories that are in circulation (the repetition of the conceptual system must have seemed to him like a way of thinking that was alien, not his own). Quite simply, he had no interest—for radical, profound reasons—in that realm. His reasons were set out at length in a work of his that I found dazzling: 

La amargura metódica. Vida y obra de Ezequiel Martínez Estrada

 [

Methodical bitterness. The Life and work of 

Ezequiel Martínez Estrada

](2014); a name that was foreign—intimately foreign—for a way of thinking that was his own. At the height of his militant enthusiasm for 

Kirchnerism

, Ferrer embodied a kind of dissent for which there was no clear place. Dedicated to his son Simón, his sister Yvonne, and three leading Argentine intellectuals – 

Héctor Schmucler

, Horacio González and 

Tomás Abraham

 – this substantial volume cast the author of 

Radiografía de la pampa

 as a sort of intellectual and moral model and, from that vantage point, strongly criticised the political and intellectual styles of the “decade of victory”. Christian proposed “deceiving oneself as little as possible”.




The bitterness of the method neither evokes nor implies any sadness, but rather disillusionment. From an existential point of view, it springs from love and compassion. From a cognitive point of view, it is a vast endeavour of knowledge without theory. If it needs to be a method – a method that consists of detecting constants amidst dazzling novelties – it is out of a pure desire to understand. Against the illusion/hope that takes the form of adherence to the present and even enthusiasm for current affairs; fashion, its logic, as an object of suspicion; against illusion/hope, suspicion, so as not to be disarmed by the seduction of power; not to accept any politics incapable of breaking the “infernal circle of the governed”. From the point of view of writing, bitterness entails a selection of affections. Those with which one writes, prepares lessons, takes part in round-table discussions, and converses at length with friends. The things Christian used to do. (He once said to me: “You have to be reading and writing, and nothing else.”) We are approaching something very central, which I believe can be put as follows: the attention he felt it was right to devote to what he called “stimuli and obsessions”. I hypothesise that this was a major subject of reflection for him. That which is discovered outside or inside, but through the body, that which one does not know where it leads and which – to find out – requires freedom of inquiry and of language. The drama of the thinker not in the abstract, but in their capacity to embody their concerns and discoveries: Martínez Estrada or 

Nicolás Guillén

.




Christian’s other text, which I find pivotal, exquisite and concise, is called 

Los destructores de máquinas

 [

The Machine Breakers

] (2015). It is, if anything, even more relevant today than when he wrote it. It was published in a collection of his articles compiled by the National Library’s publishing house. It deals with the Luddites. The essay is hilarious, incisive, meticulous and politically sharp. Ned Ludd, the fictional leader of the workers who smashed machines – whom today’s streaming-era intelligentsia has rebranded as “Luddites” – lends his name to the movement that so alarmed the British government that it mobilised penal reforms and numerous military contingents to defend the industrial apparatus. And it teaches us that those workers were not misguided conservatives seeking to halt the evolution of the sacrosanct forces of production, but activists whose awareness of the danger led them to reject the acceleration of productive and technological flows whose scale, speed and abstraction could devastate the community without any regulation whatsoever, in the service of capital accumulation. The din of progress, says a hyper-Benjaminian Ferrer, drowns out the voice of the defeated. His writings from those years invited us to think of Argentina not only as the country of human rights, but also as the land of soya fields—”

yuyito

“

[1]

 as a metonym—which brings with it phenomena of technological dependence, land concentration and an entire model of knowledge. Ferrer explored these and other issues in his university teaching while, at the same time, editing the journal 

Artefacto. Pensamientos sobre la técnica

 with a group of colleagues (

Flavia Costa

, 

Margarita Martínez

 and 

Pablo Esteban Rodríguez

 are, for me, names I cannot overlook, because it was through them that I kept abreast of their discussions and received every issue of the journal).




In our sporadic, intimate and always lengthy conversations amongst friends – sometimes at his home, sometimes at a nearby Russian restaurant he liked, and sometimes over the telephone – we would engage in exhaustive discussions. On one occasion that is particularly relevant here, he told me of a public debate with a feminist activist who challenged him on his stance regarding the state of gender relations. Christian replied, with his characteristic methodical bitterness, that the form of anarchism that interested him suggested non-coexistence as a highly prophylactic method. One of his obsessions was to distinguish desire from—and liberate it from—all moralism. On another occasion, he urged me not to be swayed by the biblio-technological apparatus upon which certain intellectual discourses are based, since everything hinged on the freedom with which one engaged with books. After an old-fashioned round-table discussion dominated by slogans, he said, “One must not become a statue that makes proclamations”. When Horacio passed away, he left me a message that read: “Something colossal is leaving our world”. I am recording some memorable phrases that came to mind while listening to him, in our conversations, as he reviewed the intellectual world, the state of the country, and decisions relating to ways of life, including sexuality (his refusal to mix the language of desire with that of rights), or his fatherhood (we have children of the same age).




Two lengthy conversations he had with González offer a rich insight into Ferrer’s art of conversation. In an extract from one of these – in issue 11 of the 

Revista de la Biblioteca Nacional

 (2010) – referring to the courage of Argentine intellectuals in going against the consensus, we read: “León (

Rozitchner

) belonged to a dissident movement that no longer has a place in Argentina. Today we are living through a more cynical era; consequently, the game of dissent plays out within an intellectual arena not unlike that of the circus. The idea of the critical intellectual has become an attitude—at times buffoonish—that operates from within that game. No one understood this better than 

Fogwill

, who circled round that game all the time, with that vehement, yet measured, psychopathy, which consisted of frightening writers—something which, incidentally, does not require much courage—with constant feints and harassment directed at limited audiences, allowing him to continue circulating in cultural circles; in short, the point is to keep the topic in the spotlight and to keep promoting a certain type of intellectual figure. It is not dissent; it is a performance. In contrast, 

Oscar del Barco

’s letter (“

no matarás

” [“

Thou shalt not kill

“]), or when León took a stand regarding support from the left for the Falklands War, still falls within the realm of dissent in its classical sense: opposing a majority and risking everything—or at least something.” This sort of comment, in which shrewd observation serves as the basis for a lucid critique of gestures missing from our culture, could not fail to make an impression on his interlocutors. In an excerpt from another conversation, published in the book 

Gonzaleanas. Conversaciones sin apuro

 (2021), Ferrer states: “The question is why one chooses to study. When I chose sociology, it was during the dictatorship. Then I gave it up and later returned to it. What I wanted was to understand the human soul. I don’t know if the desire to change society was that strong within me. I did want to understand history. And that was linked to understanding the human soul.”




Many of these issues recur in his latest book, 

El cielo fuera de quicio, proteccionismo y librecambio

 (2025). A hilarious and rigorous essay on Maoism and libertarian neo-fascism: Mao and Hayek. The two great surviving illusions/hopes of the last century: Austrian and Chinese. It is a post-pandemic book which, in line with his previous writings, deals with the dangers of allowing oneself to be swept away by a desire to believe. Despite his reticence and his criticism of the “public intellectual”, Christian had not been so reluctant in recent years to speak to the media. In the final months of his life, he was interviewed at length. During a recent visit to 

Los osos de Grafton

, he pointed out that the danger of beliefs increases when they are shielded by a state that grants a licence to kill. The last time I saw him, he was presenting a remarkable book by 

Eduardo Grüner

 on Sartre. When he took the floor, he said he had taken relatively little interest in that author, but a great deal in Grüner. This was because contemporary thought could not simply maintain the illusion/hope of “commitment” without taking stock – bitterly – of the point they had reached. For instance – he remarked provocatively – what happened with Ben Bella in Algeria, or with Maduro in Venezuela. The predictable discussion that followed was cut short due to lack of time, and because Christian, with his weak heart, knew that any upset should be avoided. But following that presentation, we had our last, very long telephone conversation. Among other things, we spoke, at my request, about Che Guevara. He might not have sympathised with Guevara, let alone with Guevarism as a political culture (he once told me that the hegemonic cultures of Argentine youth activism, which at the time were Peronism and Guevarism, suffered from a striking poverty in terms of countercultural sensibility), but as soon as he realised I wasn’t asking him about the historical figure but about a personal obsession – how to write about Che today – he said something along the lines of: to deal with such a figure, one should avoid both demolition and hagiography: “invent a Che Guevara”. Nothing less.




These and other suggestions, which I am now keeping to myself, are not isolated memories, but strands of a way of thinking that arise – as he himself explained when he came to the Grafton “cave” – from perceiving the extent to which no conceptual rigour is capable of definitively accounting for the amorphous, fluid and ultimately mysterious nature of the world, whose great roar of laughter destroys all ideological fixity and all existential solemnity.







[1]

 

Yuyito

 is a Spanish diminutive of 

yuyo

, referring to a small wild plant, weed, or medicinal herb—especially common in Argentina and Uruguay—or used colloquially as a term of endearment or nickname.

author: Shireen Akram-Boshar
title: ICE Arrests at Airports Ahead of Holiday Draw Condemnation From Lawmakers
content:
Recent footage of ICE abducting people at a Seattle airport is “horrific” and “chilling,” said Gov. Bob Ferguson.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has abducted multiple people from airports ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday, sparking outrage among onlookers and renewed calls for the agency to be abolished.

This past weekend, masked ICE agents arrested two people on an airport jet bridge in Seattle as passengers boarded a flight to Los Angeles. Video of the arrests, which has gone viral on social media, shows multiple ICE agents dragging a passenger before restraining her, handcuffing her, and pulling her off of the jet bridge. As the arrest is taking place, the woman desperately cries out that she and her father are in the U.S. on work permits. Other passengers scream in horror and attempt to intervene — demanding that the masked agents identify themselves and show warrants — only to be shoved by agents.

The two arrested were later identified as Sofia Larrondo Hernandez Mejia and her father, Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, who is a Mexican national. A lawyer representing them stated that they were on their way to a family baptism.

Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson (D) described the footage as “horrific” and “chilling,” stating that ICE “is beyond reform” and echoing calls for the agency to be abolished.

“ICE is completely and totally out of control. Like many Americans, I’m outraged by masked agents, who do not identify themselves, dragging people off jetways as they board a flight, creating chaos in our communities,” Ferguson said in a statement.

The November 21 incident sparked a protest at the Seattle airport on Sunday, with demonstrators calling for the abolition of ICE.

The abductions come following a separate incident on November 19, when ICE arrested a Princeton University PhD student in D.C.’s Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport as she was returning from presenting her research at a conference.

Eva Yi Xie, a third-year neuroscience student, came to the U.S. with her parents from China as a child in 2016 and has had a pending asylum application for a decade. According to her lawyer, Xie had a court date scheduled for January 2028, and a valid work permit.

ICE detained Xie in a holding center in Virginia before moving her to an immigrant jail elsewhere in the state. On Friday, a federal judge ordered ICE not to move Xie out of Virginia, and to respond to her lawyer’s petition for habeas corpus, which stated that ICE had no grounds to arrest Xie without a warrant.

In 2020, after being named a finalist in a prestigious high school research competition, Xie wrote that her parents “were compelled to flee to America to seek refuge after being politically persecuted.”

According to the Amica Center for Immigrant Rights, at least five people, including Xie, have been detained by ICE at Virginia’s Dulles and Reagan National airports in recent weeks.

This summer, ICE expanded its arrests at airports, increasingly coordinating and sharing information with TSA and targeting travelers on domestic flights — not those with deportation orders as previously targeted, but often people with expired visas or pending asylum applications. Throughout the summer, ICE arrests at airports averaged 20 to 40 per day. At the time, immigrant rights groups had advised individuals without permanent status to reconsider taking domestic flights.

Last week, prior to the recent abductions, Democratic Senators Jacky Rosen (Nevada) and Alex Padilla (California) introduced a bill to limit ICE operations at airports. The legislation would prevent ICE agents from accessing passenger data without a warrant and require ICE to notify airlines and airports ahead of their arrests.

“ICE is out of control, and these are bare minimum standards for reining it in,” said Padilla.

According to The Guardian, ICE’s arrests at airports are part of its shift in strategy from “blitzes” in major cities — like the Trump administration’s Operation Metro Surge in Minnesota — to a quieter but seemingly equally violent approach. The agency is still arresting and detaining people in record numbers, but is focused on conducting more stealthy and rapid arrests, in order to evade public pushback.

title: Katar: Ortadoğu ABD-İran arasında yeni bir gerilimi kaldıramaz
content:
Katar Başbakanı ve Dışişleri Bakanı Şeyh Muhammed bin Abdurrahman Al Sani, Ortadoğu’nun ABD ile İran arasında yeni bir gerilimi kaldıramayacağını belirterek, iki ülkeyle de müzakere sürecini canlandırmak için çalıştıklarını söyledi.

Al Sani, Katar merkezli Al Jazeera televizyonuna yaptığı açıklamada, ABD ile stratejik diyaloğun Katar’ın ilişkilerinde temel öneme sahip olduğunu ve savunma alanındaki işbirliğini güçlendirmeyi hedeflediklerini ifade etti.

Bölgedeki gerilimin tırmanmasının önlenmesi gerektiğine işaret eden Al Sani, Katar’ın hem İran hem de ABD ile temaslarını sürdürdüğünü kaydetti.

Al Sani ile ABD Dışişleri Bakanı Marco Rubio, ABD'nin başkenti Washington DC'deki Dışişleri Bakanlığında bir araya gelmişti.

Katar, ABD ile İran arasındaki görüş ayrılıklarının giderilmesi ve bölgedeki çatışmaların sona erdirilmesi amacıyla yürütülen diplomatik girişimlerde aktif arabulucu rolü üstleniyor.
