How to break the cycle of Indonesian forest fires?

 appeared first on 

Kodao Productions

.

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Amid continuing displacement, Marawi students face educational barriers
content:
The 2024 data of the Philippine Statistics Authority showed that the BARMM had the lowest basic literacy rate among all regions in the country at 81 percent. Lanao del Sur ranked third among the region’s five provinces.







MARAWI CITY, Lanao del Sur — Affecting one’s education due to financial difficulties is a typical problem of poor communities in many parts of the country. But for families displaced after the Marawi Siege in 2017, having such a problem amid their continuing displacement hits differently.




There were many occasions that the children of Nurania Unte, 33, were not able to go to school due to financial constraints. Her family is now living in Hijrah village, Barangay Sultan Corobong, a remote temporary shelter in the Islamic City of Marawi.







Nurania Unte, an internally displaced person, watches people outside her house in Hijrah village, Barangay Sultan Corobog, one of the remote temporary shelters in Marawi City. Photo by Franck Dick Rosete/Bulatlat







Her husband’s average salary in a week, ranging from P2,500 to P4,000 (approximately US$39 to $62), for working as a construction worker remains insufficient to meet their daily needs. Since it is a project-based work, there are days when the family breadwinner is jobless.




To ensure school attendance, Unte’s three children, in many instances, were forced to walk for more or less 30 minutes from their temporary shelter to the nearest Dulay Elementary School as they cannot afford the P20 fare. 




“Almost all families here have the same problem,” she told 

Bulatlat

 in Filipino.




Before the five-month Marawi Siege, Unte used to live in Barangay Papandayan. The village was not part of the 24 barangays classified as most affected areas (MAA). But the lack of financial capacity to repair their house left her family with no choice but to bear the dire situation in the shelter.




Barangay Sultan Corobong, previously part of Barangay Dulay Proper, is one of the newly created villages in Marawi, following the reported increase in the population in certain areas after the siege.




The community in Hijrah village, home of reported around 1,000 internally displaced persons (IDPs), needs free transportation as the reported cost of a back-and-forth fare stood at P240 (US$3.75) going to the city proper. “The residents here don’t have stable jobs,” Nasser Dimaampo Bongcaran, the temporary shelter president, said in Filipino.







Photo shows some of the temporary housing units in Hijrah village, Barangay Sultan, Corobong, Marawi City. Photo by Franck Dick Rosete/Bulatlat







Jelilah Casarigan, mother of seven, recalled the days that her eldest daughter ended up making the sacrifice by not being able to go to school to prioritize other siblings, and she cries every time it happens.




“My child is diligent in her studies,” Casarigan, who lives in the Bakwit village, a temporary shelter in Barangay Pindolonan, Saguiaran, Lanao del Sur, told 

Bulatlat 

in Filipino. “Sometimes we struggle with our finances because my [construction worker] husband does not always have a job.”




The 2025 data of the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) showed that Lanao del Sur registered the second highest unemployment rate among five provinces in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) at 7.99 percent, which translates to 44,000 unemployed individuals.







https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/30904271/visualisation.json?ref=embed-script







Unlike the IDPs in Hiraj village, families residing in the Bakwit village, on top of the utility bills, have started paying P500 (approximately $8) for monthly rent just this year, following the eviction notice they had received from the landowner.




Read:

 

Displaced Marawi residents face eviction from temporary shelter




The Casarigan family was awarded a permanent shelter in Saguiaran town, a few kilometers away from Marawi City, but they have yet to transfer since there was no electricity and water connections yet. 




Same struggles




Families in permanent shelters have been dealing with the same struggles. Ibralyn Macaraguit, mother of six, gives P70 ($1.09) to one of her children studying high school a day, of which P60 ($0.98) serves as the back-and-forth fare.




The lack of local transportation also gives them headaches, leaving her child to go on foot for more or less 30 minutes from Racman Pimping Maniri Dumarpa (RPMD) National Science High School in Barangay Papandayan going to their house in Darussalam village, a permanent shelter located in Barangay Dulay Proper.




The same with Unte and Casarigan, there were many instances that Macaraguit’s children were unable to go to school—twice a week sometimes—due to financial hardships.







Ibralyn Macaraguit, an internally displaced person (IDP) living in Darussalam village, a permanent shelter in Barangay Dulay Proper, Marawi City, prepares a hot drink for his son. Photo by Franck Dick Rosete/Bulatlat







Macaraguit’s husband only makes a daily average income of P500 ($8) as a tricycle driver. For them, this is insufficient for a family of five. She tried to sell snacks within the community to have extra income but it is not sustainable in a place where its people are also financially struggling.




Their situation, she said, is far different prior to the war, recounting moments when the market—where they would sell fish—was just a few steps away from their house in Barangay Datu Naga, one of the villages classified as MAA and one of the four barangays where many of their residents were permanently displaced.




She told 

Bulatlat

 that their house prior to the siege was located around the area now where a ferris wheel was built. 




The ferris wheel was installed along with other infrastructure projects, such as the four-hectare Sarimanok Sports Stadium, the Marawi Convention Center, the School of Living Tradition building, the Lake Lanao Promenade, and Peace Memorial Park, to name a few, as part of the government’s so-called rehabilitation efforts.




Aside from Datu Naga, many residents from barangays Sabala Manao, Datu sa Dansalan, and Dansalan, whose land titles sit on the “reclamation area” owned by the government—which were highly contested by residents—are no longer able to return because of these government infrastructure. 



















Photos show pre-siege (left) and post-siege (right) satellite images covering barangays Sabala Manao, Dansalan, Datu sa Dansalan, and Datu Naga in Marawi City. Screengrab from Google Earth







In Norsalam village in Barangay Patani, the so-called farthest permanent shelter in Marawi City, several housing units seemed unoccupied. In fact, some of them were almost covered by vegetation.






















Photos show several housing units in Norsalam village, Barangay Patani, Marawi City, (bottom) and housing units in the same village almost covered by vegetation (top). Photo by Franck Dick Rosete/Bulatlat







According to the Reclaiming Marawi Movement (RMM), a group of IDPs campaigning for their return, several beneficiaries opted not to live in the said village due to its remote location, where residents spend more or less P200 ($3.12) for transportation.







A mother, together with her child, bears the heat and walks along the road going to Norsalam village in Barangay Patani, Marawi City. Photo by Franck Dick Rosete/Bulatlat







Effects of absenteeism, displacement




According to the result of the 2022 Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA), the Philippines had the highest rate of long-term absenteeism compared to all participating nations. 




PISA, which is run by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), is an international assessment which measures the ability of students aged 15 years old to use their reading, mathematics, and science knowledge and skills to meet real-life challenges.




The 2022 assessment revealed that 30.3 percent of 15-year-old-students in the country in that year had reported that they had experienced in their studying journey having been absent from school for three consecutive months, of whom 19.3 percent had experienced twice or more.




Several factors of long-term absenteeism in the country were cited. These included students who had been affected by calamities and had to work, as well as their difficulties in paying school fees and in transportation.




A June 2026 report released by OECD titled “

Every Day Counts: Understanding, Preventing, and Responding to School Attendance Problems

” indicated that absences of students weaken their academic performance, as it reduces access to instruction, feedback, assessment, and peer learning.




Read:

 

18 million ‘functionally illiterate’ grads linked to public education woes




The report added that absences in primary education are linked to weaker development of foundation skills, while absences can be harmful during lower secondary education because they coincide with important academic and developmental transitions.




The 2024 PSA data showed that the BARMM had the lowest basic literacy rate among all regions in the country at 81 percent, or 3,601 out of 4,446 children aged five and over. Lanao del Sur ranked third among the region’s five provinces.







https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/30899236/visualisation.json?ref=embed-script







The repercussions of displacement in terms of mental health and stability, on the other hand, can affect children’s ability to learn, according to a 2019 research conducted by the Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre (IDMC), the world’s leading source of data and analysis on internal displacement.




Waiting for compensation




For Macaraguit, the monetary compensation for Marawi Siege victims would benefit them, especially for her children’s education. More than three years since she filed her claim in July 2023, she told 

Bulatlat

 in an interview on October 20 that she has yet to receive compensation.




“We should be the priority because we are the ones who can no longer return,” she said in the vernacular, expressing her frustrations.




Read:

 

Group opposes Marawi Siege compensation planned changes




Section 29 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the Marawi Siege Victims Compensation Act provides that lawful owners of residential, cultural, and commercial structures, as well as other properties owned by renters and sharers in 24 barangays under MAA and eight barangays classified as other affected areas (OAA) that were destroyed by the war are eligible to receive compensation from the government.




The family of Casarigan only received P28,000 ($437) in compensation, a share given by a relative since their damaged house in Barangay Marinaut was owned by his grandfather. Unte, meanwhile, is not eligible for the program.




According to the Marawi Compensation Board (MCB), the government body that awards monetary compensation, a total of P3.112 billion ($48,611) in compensation were awarded for the first half of this year, way higher compared to the P1.922 billion ($30,023) awarded in the entire calendar year 2025.




Overall, since 2023, a total of P6.154 billion ($96,129) in compensation were awarded cumulatively to 3,699 claimants, as of June 2026.




In its 2025 annual report, MCB explained the difference between total claims and total claimants, saying there were claimants who have multiple claims. 




Bulatlat

 reached out to the board on November 1 through email to get the exact total resolved claims as of June 2026, but there has been no response as of this writing. As of last year, however, a total of 3,187 claims had been resolved since 2023, amounting to P3.044 billion ($47,549). This is around 22 percent of the estimated total claims to be resolved by 2028—MCB’s final year.













Thirty-six percent of the 100 paid claimants interviewed by MCB in 2025 said that they used the compensation for house repair, of whom 21 percent had reportedly returned to their homes. 




Some respondents also said that they used the compensation for their livelihood and their children’s educational needs.







https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/30763343/visualisation.json?ref=embed-script







Since they were permanently displaced, Macaraguit plans to use the compensation for business capital. She wants to reclaim their life before the war while living in a permanent shelter.




Incomplete recovery




On October 20, the Special Committee on Marawi Recovery, Reconstruction, and Rehabilitation presented its report before the Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament. Overall findings reportedly showed progress in the rehabilitation in terms of housing, infrastructure, and utilities, among others. But Marawi recovery remains incomplete.




Citing the July 2026 data of the National Housing Authority (NHA), Member of Parliament Said Shiek, then-committee chairperson, reported 1,712 completed permanent housing units, of which 1,598 were already awarded to the family-beneficiaries.




The NHA-built permanent shelters were on top of the permanent housing units turned over by the United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) and the BARMM’s Marawi Rehabilitation Program (MRP).




Read:

 

After 9 years, Marawi displaced families have yet to return to their homes




The panel has no available data pertaining to the total current occupants in temporary and permanent shelters. BARMM’s MRP, meanwhile, has recorded 83,223 displaced persons as of August 2026, but it clarified that the data does not represent the full extent of the current displacement.




One of the recommendations provided by the committee was to fully operationalize the Rights of Internally Displaced Persons of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region Act of 2024 in achieving “durable solutions” for IDPs.




Under the law, a durable solution is achieved when displaced families resume their normal lives and no longer need specific assistance in relation to their displacement. The BARMM government and the local government concerned have the primary duties to help IDPs to have sustainable integration either to their original homes, to their shelters, or to other parts of the country.




Read:

 

Displaced Marawi survivors still long for justice




At present, dilapidated shelters, limited access to water supply, lack of livelihood, unreceived compensation, and problems in transportation have been plaguing families living in temporary and permanent shelters.



















Photos show dilapidated portions of some temporary shelters in the Bakwit village, Barangay Pindolonan, Saguiaran, Lanao del Sur. Photo by Franck Dick Rosete/Bulatlat







On October 17, the ninth year of the “liberation” of Marawi City from the ISIS-inspired Maute Group was commemorated. But for Moro Consensus Group, a Bangsamoro-based civil society organization, there was no genuine liberation while many 

Meranaws

 have remained exiled. 

(DAA, RVO)







Bulatlat produced this story through a grant under the Public Journalism Grant Project of the International Media Support (IMS) in partnership with Asia Society Philippines (ASPH).




The post 

Amid continuing displacement, Marawi students face educational barriers

 appeared first on 

Bulatlat

.

author: Gwenael Velge
title: Behind the myth of the green data centre
content:
A recent Guardian article provides a glimpse into what good practice looks like when it comes to data centres: The EcoDataCenter’s 80 MW facility in Falun Swede is built from timber, runs on hydro and wind power and pipes its waste heat into the town’s district heating.

Yet, the article concludes with a hollow cliché — there are better and worse ways to do data centres. This really means that there are better and worse ways to do capitalism.

How many data centres the world needs is largely a question of demand, we are told. “How much more AI do we require, and how much do the benefits offset the harms?,” the Guardian asked.

Which community, river or forest “demands” hyperscale data centres?

What is posed as a neutral given — supply and demand — is really a political choice set by capital looking for returns. The cost, however, eventually falls on people and ecosystems at the local and planetary level.

For this exact reason, the Falun project deserves attention. The local council there started the project in 2010, years before the AI boom. Suppliers were local, the power is renewable and the waste heat warms homes.

Falun’s origin shows that when a community plans infrastructure around its needs and resources, it can do it well. It does not show that hyperscale data centres are either necessary or “sustainable”.

The article provides us with useful ratios for Falun: A power usage effectiveness (PUE) of 1.15 against a European Union average of 1.36; a carbon usage effectiveness (CUE) of 1.17 grams per kilowatt-hour against 414 in the United States.

These numbers speak of efficiency per unit. But we are never provided with a total and that is what we must consider if we are to tackle global warming.

The primary question should be how much heat and emissions can we afford; how efficient each unit is comes second.

Getting it the wrong way around leads to a paradox in which efficiency feeds growth.

In 1865, the economist William Stanley Jevons pointed out that more efficient steam engines did not reduce Britain’s coal use; they increased it, because cheaper power found more uses.

The same logic applies to computing. Political economist Grace Blakeley points out that Morgan Stanley’s forecasts of US data centre power demand already include Nvidia’s next generation of far more efficient chips and still projects a shortfall of 107 gigawatts (GW) — 18 New Yorks worth of electricity — by 2029.

Efficient computing is cheaper, which expands demand, which requires more power, which generates more waste — heat, emissions, tailings and pollution.

Aren’t these “sustainable data centres” powered by renewables though?

The historian Jean-Baptiste Fressoz has shown that there has never been an energy transition; there has only ever been energy addition.

Coal did not replace wood: Britain used more timber to prop up its coal mines than its whole economy had burned as fuel a century earlier. Humanity burns more wood, coal, oil and gas today than at any point in history.

Under this historical-material lens, renewables are simply one more source of energy for accumulation, not a means towards energy transition.

In Thermal contradictions of electronic capital, Grégoire Chamayou traces a similar computing history. Each time chips hit a thermal wall, engineers find a fix: cooling fins, air conditioning, cooler chip designs and now immersion in liquid.

The engineering fix solves capital’s eternal problem — falling profitability — so that accumulation can resume and reach a higher peak. In effect, the engineering fix is to increase the speed at which the thermal cost can be externalised into the surrounding eco-social environment.

Data centres are a case in point; they are literally “hyperscaled heat machines”; all the energy that goes in comes out as heat.

In other words, accumulation is exponentially costly, it must find forever more efficient ways to externalise waste.

On a finite planet, this runaway waste accumulation eventually meets hard physical limits — planetary boundaries.

Under the accumulation paradigm “efficiency” and “sustainability” are themselves co-opted and become a means for further accumulation, whether materially via engineering fixes, or rhetorically as legitimating spin.

What the system refuses to acknowledge is the material absurdity of exponential growth.

The physicist Tom Murphy has calculated that even if we had a magic wand and solved carbon emissions today, yet kept growing at 2.3% a year, waste heat alone would bring the Earth’s surface to boiling point in about 400 years.

Exponential growth on a finite planet is simply not among the material possibilities, for anyone, whatever the technology.

Falun’s expansion is a case in point.

The sustainability officer reports that: “[O]ur core components into what we sell are land and power. It’s a very linear business in that way. It’s very hard to have exponential growth because we work with physical constraints.”

Yet EcoDataCenter’s next site, in Borlänge, is three times larger (240 MW).

Meta is building a 723 MW facility in Luleå, Sweden; Brookfield plans 750 MW in Strängnäs, Sweden, and Google has broken ground in Horndal, Sweden. All profess to follow the “Nordic model”.

EcoDataCenter’s sustainability chief says hyperscalers are “definitely needed in the ecosystem”. Why? We aren’t told.

As long as accumulation is the goal, a “sustainable hyperscale data centre” is little more than greenwashing. It is an example of profit without corresponding socio-physical costs.

A “sustainable data centre” is tantamount to “sustainable mining” or “sustainable capitalism”. It is a story we’d like to believe, but which has no historical precedent or material grounding.

Consequently, the burden of proof belongs with those promising green growth and “sustainable heat machines”. Why and how will this time be any different?

Meanwhile, the questions that actually matter are: What should we use our limited energy budget for and how should it be distributed?

The irony is that Falun’s virtues came from public planning, not from the market. A council designed it to serve a town; capital now holds it up as proof that profit-seeking hyperscale data centres can be green.

How much to build is a political question and it requires a political answer. There is no such thing as abstract “demand”; there is capital demanding growth while people and ecosystems demand a liveable planet.

[Gwenaël Velge is a research associate with the Mineral Policy Institute and School of Humanities and Social Sciences at Murdoch University. He is a member of Socialist Alliance.]

author: Kodao Productions
title: Gormless* Sara defense narratives
content:
At this stage, it is impossible for the defense panel of Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio for a reset after successive days of testimonies from their witnesses that weakened the case of their principal, antagonized the senators who are sitting in judgment of their client, and tested the credulity of the parties-in-interest to this case, the millions of citizens who are befuddled by the legal theory behind the defense.




Ranged against the findings of forensic analyst Atty. Alexander Cabrera who used a fine comb to sift through Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs), tax filings, documents, business registration records, bank transactions and the use of manager’s checks to hide wealth, inward remittances, corporate financial reports, and concluded under a conservative framework that Sara had amassed P817.87-million in hidden wealth. Using a broader framework, her wealth would zoom to P1.5-billion. In response to this, the other Sara defense panel in social media insisted that the amount of P817.87-million was an “invention.”




It is an “invention” that could not be pierced by the dagger of Atty. Rainer de la Fuente, which the defense presented in the hope of dismantling the testimony of Atty. Cabrera, a certified public accountant (CPA) who spent 35 years at a big-league accounting and auditing firm and even became its chairman. In contrast, Atty. de la Fuente spent 25 months at the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) where he was supposed to learn the ropes of financial investigation to ferret out fraud, money laundering and illegal transactions. Atty. de la Fuente a perfect witness, not for the defense but for the prosecution since he admitted in court that he had not read Cabrera’s report to maintain himself on an even keel, unbiased and not affected by any bias.




It is a strange testimony that immediately impeaches his relevance to the trial since he, not of a motion in **limine could not perform the duty of a witness hostile to the prosecution. Since they could no longer question the ***facticity of Cabrera’s brief, they are stuck with it, and de la Fuente’s refusal to comment on the findings of the prosecution’s expert witness. To add insult to injury, de la Fuente admitted that while two weeks is a short time to stitch together an ironclad narrative, it is possible it can be an unassailable report. Worse, de la Fuente admitted that the Sara’s documents are littered with red flags.




It was unfortunate for the defense to rely on Atty. de la Fuente as their pointman in destroying the testimony of Cabrera. By not reading the Cabrera report and not debunking it in court, the defense was left to tackle extraneous issues about money laundering, which is a matter totally different from the issue of ill-gotten wealth, a distinction that was pointed out by Rep. Chel Diokno, who invited Atty. Mark Vinluan to produce any mention of money laundering in Article 2, the remaining article for the impeachment trial, after three articles were withdrawn.




Neither were the witnesses from the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) any better than Atty. de la Fuente. The DTI admitted it was not into examining the books of any company under its jurisdiction even as it confirmed that it oversees food processors exporting other markets, like China. Yet, DTI was surprised to know that Cale88 Foods had only two employees despite exporting shiploads of banana chips. It also struck the DTI that they granted export incentives to a company owned by Sara’s husband, Atty. Manases Carpio, and their family dentist. It never conducted physical inspections of the Cale88 factory. Last year, without the DTI’s knowledge, the company was “sold” to Pitipong Pitipong Phils., another company owned by the Dutertes. In July 2026, all the bank accounts of Cale88 were closed in time for the impeachment trial.




It was also an ugly move for the defense to dispense with the 16 bank employees who were crucial for the defense to demolish whatever there was to demolish in the prosecution’s mountain of evidence, let alone the Cabrera report that Sara’s lawyers were not prepared to controvert. The people were denied the chance to hear it direct from the horse’s mouth, especially from a bank executive who disclosed that Sara, indeed, had dollar accounts. Adding more mystery to the defense tactics is the sudden inability of two witnesses to take the stand on Nov. 26 and 27, thus extending the trial into December 2026. The defense is trying to prolong its agony by relying on non-performing witnesses, along with those who suffer from a new disease – mandatory amnesia.




With Sara not appearing at the impeachment court, the burden of proving that she is innocent beyond reasonable doubt shifts to herself. Sara is the best prosecution witness against Sara, which explains why she is scared to death in making a court appearance. In a case like hers, not even Clarence Darrow could win any favorable decision. The 16 or so defense lawyers have already done their worst. Putting Sara on the dock would lessen their burden and allow them to breathe a decent whiff of ****mephitic air in Manila Bay. That’s what you get for loving her. #




= = = = =




WORDS OF THE DAY




Gormless

 – 

stupid, lacking intelligence, or slow to understand.




Limine

 – threshold, doorstep.




Facticity

 – the quality or state of being a fact, or the actual, real nature of something.




Mephitic

 – foul-smelling, noxious, or poisonous.




The post 

Gormless* Sara defense narratives

 appeared first on 

Kodao Productions

.

author: Acratosaurio rex
title: Las elecciones generales asimétricas
content:
Repito: que votes o no votes, a mí personalmente me da igual. Yo solo estoy dando mi opinión: Decía que los millonarios no votan y se abstienen, porque saben que su dinero, sus propiedades, sus inversiones, tienen mucha más fuerza a la hora de protegerse, que la papeleta de un pelón para designar un 

diputao

. El ricachón: una llamada de teléfono, una sugerencia de sus abogados, algunos toques aquí y allí de sus esbirros, y le montan una fiesta en el Gobierno.




Compara ese esfuerzo y sus riesgos, con la que tienes que liar tú para que se den cuenta de que existes. ¿Preparaste la última Huelga General? Reuniones por doquier, preparativos, viajes aquí, vueltas allá, gastos en materiales, propaganda, abogados, logística, coordinación, legalización, más reuniones… Semanas y semanas de desgaste, acampadas… Llega el Gran Día, de noche, lloviendo, millones de personas en la calle, amenazas patronales, y te encuentras a unos pistoleros a sueldo con armadura y con un orinal en la cabeza gaseando, apaleando, pateando, empujando, deteniendo. Todo tu esfuerzo y tus riesgos de despidos, ruinas económicas, pérdidas salariales…




Para que el gobierno saliente y el entrante, unos hijos sin madre, se enteren, ¡por fin!, de que hay un problema. Para que se hable un poco del tema de la vivienda. Para que lo metan en agenda. Oh sí. 




Y entretanto, fondos, bancos, sociedades, grandes patrimonios y empresarios, hacen, deshacen, roban, manipulan, conspiran, saquean, asesinan, te cortan la garganta, exhiben sus atrofiados genitales y se forran. ¿Quiénes sois, de dónde venís, hombres inmundos? ¿Pudiera ser que surgisteis del coito casual de una garrapata y un piojo?




La verdad, como que si los ricos pensaran que las elecciones podrían hacer peligrar sus chanchullos, lo mismo hasta las prohibían. Y me da que si las dejan correr, es porque saben que no suponen riesgo alguno. ¡En serio, maldita sea! Hay que ser un completo alcornoque, un tarugo, un zoquete, para creer que en esa trampa, puede haber algo interesante, cuando lo que hay realmente, es una guerra asimétrica.

author: Unknown
title: Rudolf Rocker - Nationalisme et culture
content:
Auteur·e

: Rudolf Rocker

Titre

: Nationalisme et culture

Date

: septembre 2008




RUDOLF ROCKER NATIONALISME & CULTURE







 Rudolf Rocker Dessin de son fils Fermin 




Présentation




Le 28 février

, les cendres du Reichstag encore fumantes, les Rocker décident que, pour eux aussi, c’est le moment d’abandonner l’Allemagne. Ils pensent aller voir le vieux compagnon Wilhelm Werner pour essayer de résoudre avec lui les nombreux problèmes qui surgissent devant un départ précipité, et Milly sort pour faire quelques courses pendant que Rudolf rassemble les feuilles d’un livre qu’il vient de terminer quelques jours auparavant. 




 Mais Milly ne fait pas ses courses. Dans la rue, un marchand ambulant ami l’informe 

sotto voce

 qu’Erich Mühsam vient d’être enlevé par la police secrète. 




 Mühsam habite le même quartier de Berlin que Rocker, et ils se voient presque quotidiennement dans ces temps agités où les SA, troupes de choc du NSDAP

[1]

, font régner la terreur brune. 




 Tous les révolutionnaires, tous les opposants au nazisme, étaient en danger de mort, surtout Erich Mühsam, Juif, anarchiste connu, actif participant avec Gustav Landauer aux événements révolutionnaires de Munich en 1919 (République des conseils de Bavière). Werner et Rocker, deux jours avant l’incendie du Reichstag, avaient convaincu Mühsam, réticent, de sortir du pays sans tarder. Cependant, il voulait laisser les affaires en ordre et retarda son départ. Hésitation qui lui fut fatale. Zensl, sa compagne, racontera qu’il avait le billet pour Prague dans sa poche au moment de son arrestation.

[2]




 Dans la banlieue sud de Berlin, dans ce faubourg de Britz, il y avait très peu de gens dans la rue les jours de travail, et en s’assurant de sa fenêtre qu’il n’y avait pas de mouvements suspects aux alentours, Milly Witkop et Rudolf Rocker, entreprennent la fuite d’une Allemagne livrée maintenant à la furie destructrice du nazisme. Ils ne portent pas de valises pour ne pas éveiller des soupçons, et Rocker prend sous le bras le manuscrit de 

Nationalisme et culture

, fruit d’un long travail commencé à l’époque de son premier exil en 1892. 




 Les idées qui imprègnent les pages de ce livre se sont formées petit à petit dans l’esprit de l’auteur, au cours de son chemin militant et de l’errance, premièrement à Paris puis à Londres, et elles ont pu s’exprimer par bribes dans des articles et des conférences jusqu’à la brutale interruption imposée par la guerre de 1914 et l’internement pendant quatre ans dans des camps, l’Olympia et l’Alexandra Palace, où il a été jeté par le gouvernement britannique en tant qu’« expatrié ennemi ». 




 Expulsé vers l’Allemagne en 1918 avant l’armistice, il arrive, au bout de diverses péripéties, à se réfugier en Hollande. Et, à la fin de l’année, Rocker est à nouveau dans son pays d’origine après vingt-six ans d’absence. L’agitation politique y est fébrile entre les insurrections spartakistes et la révolution de Munich, et elles sont suivies d’une répression sanglante. Ces temps-là n’étaient pas propices au travail intellectuel et d’autres tâches plus urgentes sollicitent Rocker. 




 En décembre 1919, se réunissait à Berlin le douzième congrès de la FVDG (

Freie Verinigung deutscher Gewerkschaften

) où Rocker présente les principes de l’organisation révolutionnaire anarcho-syndicaliste. Ce congrès propose aux vieilles associations qui composent la FVDG, dissoute pendant la guerre, de changer de nom et d’agir dorénavant en tant que 

Freie Arbeiter Union Deutschland

 (FAUD), comme il avait été décidé à la Conférence de Düsseldorf en septembre de la même année. La force numérique du mouvement se multiplia atteignant le chiffre de 150 000 membres en 1921. Rocker s’engage profondément dans la construction de l’organisation ouvrière, et il parcourt le pays en donnant des conférences, en participant à des meetings publics et à des réunions organisationnelles. « Quelle que soit – écrit-il dans ses Mémoires – la façon dont on juge la situation en Europe après la Première Guerre mondiale, il est indubitable que la conflagration avait créé une situation révolutionnaire qui justifiait des attitudes d’attente porteuses de grands espoirs. » 




 À ce moment, Trotsky et Lossovsky cherchent à mettre sur pied l’Internationale syndicale rouge, et invitent à Moscou pour le 1er mai 1921, les syndicalistes et les révolutionnaires, y compris les anarchistes, de tous les pays, mais il est clair que l’ISR resterait soumise à la politique du Kominterm. Les syndicalistes anti-autoritaires

[3]

, syndicalistes révolutionnaires et anarchistes, doivent réagir sans perdre de temps et ils réunissent une conférence internationale à Berlin en décembre 1920. Ont participé à cette conférence les fédérations ouvrières de Suède, de Hollande, d’Allemagne et d’Argentine et y sont représentés le Comité syndicaliste révolutionnaire (France), les 

Shop Stewards and Worker Councils

 (Royaume-Uni) et les IWW (États-Unis). Les fédérations anarcho-syndicalistes d’Espagne, d’Italie, du Portugal et de Norvège envoient par écrit leur adhésion. La Conférence prend deux résolutions importantes qui sont autant de recommandations pour les délégués qui seront présents au prochain congrès de Moscou : l’une affirme que la construction socialiste et la mise en marche de la production et de la distribution des produits du travail doivent dépendre des organisations économiques dans chaque pays, et l’autre déclare que l’Internationale syndicale rouge pourra remplir sa fonction seulement si elle reste indépendante de la tutelle de tout parti politique.

[4]

author: anonerror
title: 29N ¡¡¡A las urnas, anarquistas de todas las tendencias!!! -
content:
Vaya por delante que el sacrosanto respecto de los dogmas es una autentica calamidad y que el meditado criterio de cada cual es la mejor brújula para orientar su quehacer al margen de cualquier tabú impuesto por las ortodoxias ideológicas, incluida por supuesto la anarquista.




Aun así, llama poderosamente la atención el hecho de que ciertos anarquistas que, tapándose discretamente las narices solían acudir ritualmente a las urnas casi a hurtadillas y sin hacer gala de ello, han decidido hacerlo ahora a plena luz del día y hasta con orgullo, publicitando con vehemencia e insistencia su decisión.




Dicen que las circunstancias mandan, y que el deber antifascista nos conmina a plantarle cara depositando nuestra papeleta en las urnas del 29N. Un boletín de voto que, por cierto,lo queramos o no, nos hace participesdel normal funcionamiento del sistema político-social establecido.




Es más, consideran que en las actuales circunstancias su papel consiste, entre otras cosas, en convencer a tantos compañeros y compañeras como puedan para que les imiten, haciendo choruscon todas las formaciones políticas que llaman a acudir a las urnas para barrar el paso al fascismo.




Arguyen que no les gusta del todo la opción por la cual votarán, pero que se trata de optar por el mal menor acallando el duendecillo que les recuerda el hecho de que por mera definición el mal menor no dejara nunca de ser un mal.




Como por lo general suelen tener cierta cultura política son plenamente conscientes de que el hecho de participar en el juego electoral parlamentario significa legitimar un sistema que, además del monopolio de la fuerza legitima, requieretambién de esa legitimación para poder mantenerse.




Lo que estos y estas anarquistas pasan por alto es que una de las múltiples causas que impulsan el desarrollo del fascismo es precisamente la gestión de un sistema que, esté quien esté en la sala de mandos gubernamental, genera bolsas de pobreza, precariedad laboral, frustración por las sempiternas promesas incumplidas, asegura el mantenimiento o el incremento de las desigualdades, y un larguísimo etcétera… Contribuir con la papeleta depositada en la urna a legitimar el modo de gobernabilidad del actual sistema capitalista es precisamente hacerle el juego al desarrollo de la opción fascista en una población drásticamente castigada por ese sistema.




En definitiva, el supuesto remedio contra el mal mayor, es decir la papeleta antifascista encargada de propiciar el mal menor, resulta ser un potente adyuvante para el desarrollo del mal mayor, colaborando sin quererlo en la creación de algunas de sus condiciones de desarrollo.




Contra el señuelo de las urnas la lucha para obstaculizar los avances del  fascismo es la que se enfrenta al sistema instituido, en todos los sectores de la sociedad donde alcanzamos a debilitar ese sistema y no en unas urnas que le son imprescindibles porque lo consolidan.




Al concluir este breve escrito abro el paraguas porque es bastante probable que los y las “anarquistas” con sentido de la responsabilidad política no escatimarán esfuerzos para situarme como un tonto útil, o incluso como un cómplice, del fascismo al que la abstención, según su punto de vista, facilitaría el paso.




 




Por 

Tomás Ibáñez

, noviembre 2029

title: Iranian regime detains Hazim Haşimî in Awdanan
content:
Following protests in the Awdanan district over a traffic accident involving a bus transporting workers from the Dehloran Refinery, in which 13 workers lost their lives, the number of people detained has risen to 13.




According to Kolber News, forces affiliated with the Iranian regime, along with masked groups, raided the home and workplace of Hemze Haşimî and Hisên Haşimî in the city of Awdanan, in Ilam Province. During the raid, Hazim Haşimî was beaten and tortured before being detained without a court warrant and taken to an unknown location.




It was reported that, during Hazim Haşimî’s arrest, armed individuals pointed their weapons at his mother and demanded that she hand over her other son, Husên Haşimî. The armed individuals also reportedly threatened and assaulted other members of the family.

title: Yeni Parti’li Murat Emir: “İzleme Komisyonu kararı, barış irademizde bir değişiklik anlamına gelmez”
content:
Yeni Parti Grup Başkanvekili Murat Emir, partisinin Meclis bünyesinde kurulması planlanan İzleme Komisyonu'na üye vermeme kararına ilişkin kapsamlı bir açıklama yayımladı. Emir sosyal medya hesabından yayımladığı açıklamada, komisyonda yer almama kararının barış iradesinden vazgeçildiği anlamına gelmeyeceğini vurguladı.

Emir, "Barışa verdiğimiz destek, iktidarın her tercihine peşinen verilmiş onay olarak anlaşılamaz. Demokratikleşmenin ertelenmesine itirazımız da toplumsal barıştan vazgeçtiğimiz anlamına gelmez. Şehit ailelerinin ve gazilerimizin hassasiyetlerini, çatışmalarda evladını kaybetmiş ailelerin acısını, yıllardır adalet bekleyenlerin sesini aynı sorumlulukla dikkate alıyoruz" ifadelerini kullandı. Barışın pazarlık konusu yapılamayacağını ancak demokrasi olmadan da kalıcı barışın kurulamayacağını vurgulayan Emir, iktidarın anayasal yükümlülüklerini sürecin sonuna ertelemesine tepki gösterdi.

Demokratikleşmenin artık ertelenemeyeceğini vurgulayan Emir, “Barış pazarlık konusu yapılamaz ancak, demokrasi olmadan da kalıcı barışın kurulamayacağı unutulmamalıdır. Silahların susmasını hiçbir siyasi pazarlığın şartına bağlamıyoruz. Aynı şekilde, Anayasa’nın uygulanmasının ve yurttaşların haklarına kavuşmasının da bir pazarlığın sonucuna ertelenmesini kabul etmiyoruz” vurgusu yaptı.

Kalıcı barışın demokratik güvencelerini istemenin, silahsızlanmanın önüne yeni bir şart koymak olmadığını belirten Emir, “İktidarın zaten yerine getirmekle yükümlü olduğu sorumluluklar barışın ön şartı olamayacağı gibi, mahkeme kararlarına uymak için veya kayyım uygulamasına artık son vermek için sürecin tamamlanması beklenemez. Basın ve ifade özgürlüğünün önündeki engellerin kaldırılması, iktidarın uygun zaman geldiğinde sunacağı bir imkân olarak görülemez. Biz, toplumsal barış umudunun otoriter uygulamalara gerekçe yapılmasına itiraz ediyoruz. Barışı savunmanın bedeli, hukuksuzluklar karşısında susmak olmamalıdır” ifadelerini kullandı.

Komisyon raporunun 6.5’inci bölümünde yer alan, yürütme içinde bir izleme mekanizması oluşturulması ve hazırlanacak raporların TBMM’ye sunulmasının öngörüldüğünü hatırlatan Emir şu ifadelere yer verdi:

“Bu bölümde, milletvekillerinden oluşacak yeni bir izleme komisyonu kurulması önerisi bulunmamaktadır. Rapordaki ifade açıktır: Yürütme tarafından bu konuda hazırlanacak raporların TBMM’ye sunulması gerekli görülmektedir. 6.1’inci bölümde ise tespit ve teyidin nesnel, ölçülebilir ve denetlenebilir ölçütlerle, şeffaf biçimde yürütülmesi istenmektedir. Sonradan kabul edilen 7595 sayılı Kanun’un 7’nci maddesinin beşinci fıkrasında Meclis bünyesinde İzleme Komisyonu kurulması düzenlenmiştir. Raporun önerileri ile sonradan kanunlaştırılan hükümleri birbirine karıştırmadan konuşmak gerekir.”

Yeni Parti’nin Çerçeve Yasa’ya verdiği desteğin, silahların susması için üstlenilen sorumluluğun gereği olarak tanımlayan Emir, “Bu destek, yasanın uygulanışına ilişkin eleştiri ve denetim hakkımızdan vazgeçtiğimiz anlamına gelmez. Yeni kurulması planlanan İzleme Komisyonu’na ilişkin kararımız da bu siyasi sorumluluk içinde değerlendirilmelidir. Aynı raporun yedinci bölümünde AYM ve AİHM kararlarına uyulması, ifade ve basın özgürlüğünün güçlendirilmesi, infazda adalet, siyasi partilerin kurumsal kimliklerinin korunması ve görevden uzaklaştırılan belediye başkanlarının yerine belediye meclislerinin seçim yapması yönünde öneriler de bulunmaktadır. İktidar temsilcilerinin de kabul ettiği bu öneriler, raporun ayrılmaz parçasıdır. Altıncı bölümü uygularken yedinci bölümü belirsiz bir geleceğe bırakamazsınız. Biz imzamızın sorumluluğunu taşıyoruz. Aynı sorumluluğu, rapora imza atan herkesten bekliyoruz” ifadelerine yer verdi.

title: Συγκέντρωση αλληλεγγύης για τον Β.Μ., Δευτέρα 23/11 στις 9:00 στα δικαστήρια Πάτρας
content:
ΣΥΓΚΕΝΤΡΩΣΗ ΑΛΛΗΛΕΓΓΥΗΣ ΔΕΥΤΕΡΑ 23/11 ΣΤΙΣ 09:00 ΣΤΑ ΔΙΚΑΣΤΗΡΙΑ ΠΑΤΡΑΣ ΓΙΑ ΤΟΝ ΑΝΑΡΧΙΚΟ ΣΥΝΤΡΟΦΟ Β.Μ




Ο ΑΓΩΝΑΣ ΕΝΑΝΤΙΑ ΣΤΟ ΦΑΣΙΣΜΟ ΔΕ ΜΠΟΡΕΙ ΠΑΡΑ ΝΑ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΑΓΩΝΑΣ ΕΝΑΝΤΙΑ ΣΤΟ ΚΡΑΤΟΣ & ΤΟ ΚΕΦΑΛΑΙΟ




Στις 18 Σεπτέμβρη του 2025 είχαν συμπληρωθεί δώδεκα χρόνια από τη δολοφονία του αντιφασίστα Παύλου Φύσσα από το τάγμα εφόδου της Χρυσής Αυγής στο Κερατσίνι. Δώδεκα χρόνια από μια οργανωμένη πολιτική δολοφονία που ήρθε ως συνέχεια δεκάδων φασιστικών επιθέσεων απέναντι σε μετανάστες, αγωνιστές και όποιον στεκόταν απέναντι στον εθνικισμό, τον ρατσισμό και τον φασισμό.




Εκείνη την περίοδο, μέσα στη συνθήκη των μνημονίων, της οικονομικής κρίσης, της φτώχειας και της κοινωνικής εξαθλίωσης, οι νεοναζί αξιοποιήθηκαν ως συστημικό εργαλείο τρομοκράτησης της κοινωνίας και εκτόνωσης της οργής προς τους πιο αδύναμους. Με την ανοχή, την κάλυψη και τη στήριξη κράτους, αφεντικών και ΜΜΕ, επιχειρήθηκε να μετατραπεί η κοινωνική αγανάκτηση σε μίσος απέναντι στους καταπιεσμένους αντί να στραφεί απέναντι στους πραγματικούς υπεύθυνους.




Η 18η Σεπτέμβρη δεν αποτελεί απλώς μια ημερομηνία μνήμης. Παραμένει μέχρι σήμερα -13 χρόνια μετά- μια υπενθύμιση ότι ο φασισμός δεν τελείωσε, ούτε εξαφανίστηκε μέσα από δικαστικές αποφάσεις και καταδίκες βιτρίνας. Ο φασισμός εξακολουθεί να υπάρχει μέσα στην κρατική βία, την καταστολή, τον κοινωνικό κανιβαλισμό, την εκμετάλλευση, το δυσβάσταχο κόστος ζωής και τη φτωχοποίηση που επιβάλλεται καθημερινά από το κράτος και το κεφάλαιο πάνω στην κοινωνία.




Για αυτόν ακριβώς τον λόγο ο σύντροφός μας Β. Μ. βρέθηκε στις 18 Σεπτέμβρη του 2025 στον δρόμο, μαζί με χιλιάδες άλλους ανθρώπους, στην αντιφασιστική πορεία στην Πάτρα. Από νωρίς η αστυνομία είχε επιλέξει να αντιμετωπίσει τη διαδήλωση με όρους καταστολής. Πραγματοποιήθηκαν προληπτικές προσαγωγές, υπήρχε συνεχής ασφυκτική παρουσία των δυνάμεων καταστολής και λίγο πριν την ολοκλήρωση της πορείας οι διμοιρίες επιτέθηκαν με χημικά και γκλοπ απέναντι στους διαδηλωτές. Μέσα σε αυτή την επίθεση συνελήφθηκε ο σύντροφος και οδηγήθηκε στο αστυνομικό μέγαρο με κατηγορίες πλημμεληματικού χαρακτήρα.




Η σύλληψή του δεν είναι ένα «μεμονωμένο περιστατικό». Εντάσσεται στη συνολικότερη προσπάθεια τρομοκράτησης όσων συνεχίζουν να αγωνίζονται, να αντιστέκονται και να βγαίνουν στον δρόμο ενάντια στις επιλογές των κυρίαρχων. Ζούμε σε μια περίοδο όπου η κρατική αυθαιρεσία, η επιτήρηση, η καταστολή και η βία γίνονται καθημερινότητα. Την ίδια στιγμή που περνούν αντεργατικά μέτρα, που ξηλώνουν το 8ωρο στην εργασία, που έχουμε εκατόμβες δολοφονημένων και σακατεμένων εργατών και εργατριών στα κάτεργα της μισθωτής σκλαβιάς για τα κέρδη των αφεντικών, την περίοδο που η ζωή μας γίνεται ολοένα και πιο φθηνή, που τα κρατικά εγκλήματα στα Τέμπη και στην Πύλο μένουν ατιμώρητα, το κράτος επιλέγει να στοχοποιεί αγωνιστές και κοινωνικούς αγώνες. Σε κάθε περίπτωση, ο αυταρχισμός και ο κρατικός ολοκληρωτισμός δεν είναι παρέκκλιση. Αντιθέτως, είναι αναγκαίο εργαλείο ενός συστήματος που βασίζεται στην εκμετάλλευση, την ανισότητα και τον φόβο.




Τη Δευτέρα 23/11 ο σύντροφός μας θα βρεθεί στα δικαστήρια και θα υπερασπιστεί την πολιτική και κοινωνική του αγωνιστική επιλογή να διαδηλώσει στην πόλη που ζει, εργάζεται και δραστηριοποιείται, πως ο φασισμός, ειτε κρατικός είτε παρακρατικός, δεν αντιμετωπίζεται ούτε με επετειακές δηλώσεις ούτε μέσα στις δικαστικές αίθουσες. Αντιμετωπίζεται καθημερινά μέσα στην κοινωνία, στους δρόμους, στις γειτονιές, στους χώρους δουλειάς και όπου εμφανίζεται.




Απέναντι στην κρατική και παρακρατική βία, απέναντι στην απομόνωση και τον κοινωνικό φόβο, η μόνη πραγματική απάντηση είναι η συλλογική αντίσταση, η αλληλεγγύη και η αυτοοργάνωση των από τα κάτω. Να βάλουμε τις βάσεις για τον επαναστατικό μετασχηματισμό της κοινωνίας, τη χειραφέτηση των από τα κάτω, την κοινωνική επανάσταση, την αναρχία και τον ελευθεριακό κομμουνισμό.




ΣΥΓΚΕΝΤΡΩΣΗ ΑΛΛΗΛΕΓΓΥΗΣ ΔΕΥΤΕΡΑ 23/11 ΣΤΙΣ 09:00 ΣΤΑ ΔΙΚΑΣΤΗΡΙΑ ΠΑΤΡΑΣ ΓΙΑ ΤΟΝ ΑΝΑΡΧΙΚΟ ΣΥΝΤΡΟΦΟ Β.Μ

title: Antalya’daki COP31’de anlaşma sağlanamadı
content:
Antalya’da düzenlenen ve Türkiye’nin ev sahibi olduğu Birleşmiş Milletler İklim Değişikliği Konferansı'da (COP31) anlaşma sağlanamadı. COP, son 17 yıldır ilk defa anlaşma sağlanmadan sona ermiş oldu.

BBC’nin haberine göre, fosil yakıtlardan uzaklaşma taahhüdü anlaşmadan tamamen çıkarıldı. Hazırlanan dördüncü taslakta da kömür, petrol ve doğal gazdan uzaklaşılmasına ilişkin herhangi bir ifadeye yer verilmedi. Bunun üzerine Avrupa Birliği (AB), fosil yakıtlardan uzaklaşma taahhüdünün anlaşmaya yeniden eklenmesini istedi. Ancak son taslakta bu yönde bir ifade bulunmadı ve AB, metni kabul etmedi.

Petrol üreticisi ülkelerin fosil yakıtlardan uzaklaşılmasına dair taahhüde karşı çıktığı belirtildi. Suudi Arabistan öncülüğündeki petrol üreticisi ülkeler, fosil yakıtlara ilişkin ifadelerin anlaşmadan çıkarılmasını istedi. Rusya da bu talebi destekledi ve AB’yi doğrudan eleştirdi.

AB, petrol üreticisi ülkeleri müzakereleri engellemekle suçlarken, bir AB temsilcisi de bazı petrol üreticisi ülkelerin görüşmeleri kendi çıkarları doğrultusunda yönlendirdiğini ileri sürdü.

COP31'de AB heyetini temsil eden İrlanda İklim Bakanı Darragh O'Brien da, anlaşma taslağı için, "Önümüze konulan taslaklar, karşı karşıya olduğumuz iklim acil durumunu ele almaya bile başlamıyor” ifadelerini kullandı.

Kapanışta konuşan Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakanı Murat Kurum ise, “Salonda bu metne karşı çıkan taraflar olduğu açık. Bu belge üzerinde uzlaşı olmadığını kabul ediyoruz. Bu nedenle bu kararlar kabul edilmemiştir” dedi.

Ayrıca dünya basınında Türkiye’nin isminin çok az yer bulması da dikkat çekti.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Alerta
title: Παρέμβαση στην πλατεία Χαριλάου από τη Rabbia Viola ενάντια στην έμφυλη βία (φωτογραφίες)
content:
Παρέμβαση στην πλατεία Χαριλάου από τη Rabbia Viola ενάντια στην έμφυλη βία.




Παρέμβαση ενάντια στην έμφυλη βία, ενόψει της 25ης Νοεμβρίου, πραγματοποίησε η 

συλλογικότητα για τον ελευθεριακό φεμινισμό Rabbia Viola

 στην πλατεία Χαριλάου το πρωί της Κυριακής 22 Νοέμβρη. Στην παρέμβαση μοιράστηκε το παρακάτω κείμενο:




Καμία άλλη δολοφονημένη




Κανένα άλλο δολοφονημένο




Το 2026 δεν έχει ακόμα τελειώσει και από τον νομό Ροδόπης μέχρι την Κρήτη μετράμε 18 γυναικοκτονίες. Για εμάς δεν αποτελούν έναν ακόμα αριθμό στη λίστα των δολοφονημένων από την πατριαρχία, αλλά γειτόνισσες, φίλες, συναδέλφισσες, μητέρες, αδερφές — και ίσως η επόμενη να είναι μια από εμάς όσο η πατριαρχία παραμένει ριζωμένη στην κοινωνία.




Ενδεικτικά αναφέρουμε κάποιες μόνο από τις υποθέσεις της φετινής χρονιάς:







26 Φεβρουαρίου, Κασσάνδρα Χαλκιδικής:

 Εντοπίζεται διαμελισμένη σορός γυναίκας σε δασώδη περιοχή — η απόλυτη αντικειμενοποίηση του γυναικείου σώματος που πετιέται σαν σκουπίδι.




28 Φεβρουαρίου, Κολωνός:

 Η 31χρονη Νεκταρία δολοφονείται στο σπίτι της από τον σύντροφό της, ο οποίος αρχικά βάφτισε τον ξυλοδαρμό «παθολογικά αίτια», μετατρέποντας τον θεσμό της οικογένειας σε άβατο ατιμωρησίας.




30 Μαρτίου, Ζωγράφου & Εύοσμος:

 Την ίδια μέρα, μητέρα και κόρη δολοφονούνται στου Ζωγράφου από συγγενή για τον έλεγχο της περιουσίας, ενώ στον Εύοσμο μια 59χρονη στραγγαλίζεται με ζώνη στο διαμέρισμά της — η έσχατη πράξη φίμωσης και σωματικής κυριαρχίας.




22 Απριλίου, Δαφνές Ηρακλείου:

 Εντοπίζεται νεκρή στο αυτοκίνητό της η 43χρονη Ελευθερία Γιακουμάκη, πυροβολημένη στον κρόταφο από τον 40χρονο πρώην σύντροφό της. Παράλληλα τον Απρίλιο ξεκίνησε και η δίκη για τη δολοφονία της 32χρονης στους Αμπελόκηπους (Νοέμβριος 2024), όπου ο συζυγοκτόνος την έπνιξε, την έκρυψε στο πατάρι και τώρα επικαλείται «βρασμό ψυχής».




1 Ιουνίου, Καλαμάτα:

 Η 39χρονη Βασιλική δολοφονείται στο σπίτι της από τον σύζυγό της, με τα παιδιά στο διπλανό δωμάτιο. Ο δράστης της είχε απαγορεύσει να εργάζεται, επιβάλλοντάς της οικονομική εξάρτηση, απομόνωση και καθεστώς ομηρίας. Παρά τις φωνές που άκουγαν οι γείτονες και την απεύθυνσή της σε συμβουλευτικό κέντρο, έμεινε απροστάτευτη, ενώ τα ΜΜΕ έσπευσαν να ξεπλύνουν τον γυναικοκτόνο ως «καλό οικογενειάρχη», αναπαράγοντας το victim blaming.




9 & 15 Ιουνίου, Αίγιο & Δράμα:

 Στο Αίγιο δολοφονούνται μια 54χρονη γυναίκα και ο 26χρονος γιος της, ενώ στη Δράμα η 45χρονη αστυνομικός Αντιγόνη μαχαιρώνεται επτά φορές από τον εν διαστάσει σύζυγό της — επίσης ένστολο, ξεγυμνώνοντας την αυταπάτη της «κρατικής προστασίας».




23 & 26 Αυγούστου, Νέα Σμύρνη & Διαλαμπή Ροδόπης:

 Στη Νέα Σμύρνη μια 45χρονη εκτελείται στην είσοδο του σπιτιού της επειδή τόλμησε να χωρίσει, ενώ στη Ροδόπη μια 44χρονη μητέρα σφαγιάζεται από τον εν διαστάσει σύζυγό της την ημέρα των γενεθλίων της κόρης τους.




21 Σεπτεμβρίου & 24 Οκτωβρίου, Ηγουμενίτσα & Μενίδι:

 Η 25χρονη Πηνελόπη μαχαιρώνεται θανάσιμα σε πάρκο από τον 27χρονο σύντροφό της, ενώ στο Μενίδι μια 89χρονη δολοφονείται από τον ανιψιό της — απόδειξη πως η πατριαρχική βία χτυπά κάθε ηλικία.




Αρχές Νοεμβρίου, Άγιος Παντελεήμονας:

 Η σορός μιας 24χρονης μετανάστριας από την Μπουρκίνα Φάσο βρίσκεται πεταμένη σε βαλίτσα σε κάδο απορριμμάτων, συμπυκνώνοντας την έμφυλη, φυλετική και ταξική καταπίεση.




19 Νοεμβρίου 

, περιοχή Ακρόπολης: 

μια 61χρονη γυναίκα δολοφονήθηκε από τον 63χρονο συζυγός της ο οποίος την ξυλοκόπησε και η γυναίκα κατέληξε. Η ενδοοικογενειακή βία κλιμακώνεται όσο ο καιρός περνά και οι κακοποιητές φτάνουν στο σημείο της γυναικοκτονίας αν το θύμα δεν προλάβει να απεμπλακεί από το βίαιο περιβάλλον.







Οι γυναικοκτονίες δεν είναι «εγκλήματα πάθους» ούτε οφείλονται στην «κακιά στιγμή» ή σε ψυχιατρικά αίτια. Εδράζονται στην ανισότητα των φύλων και την αντίληψη πως η γυναίκα είναι «ιδιοκτησία» που πρέπει να τιμωρηθεί όταν διεκδικεί την αυτονομία της. Το αφήγημα του «εν βρασμώ» αποτελεί απλώς νομικό εργαλείο ελάφρυνσης που υποτιμά τη συστηματική κακοποίηση που προηγήθηκε.




Παράλληλα, η έμφυλη βία τέμνεται με τις ταξικές και φυλετικές ανισότητες: όταν μια γυναίκα είναι φτωχή, μετανάστρια, προσφύγισσα ή σεξεργάτρια, η ζωή της λογίζεται από κράτος και κοινωνία ως «περιθωριακή» και αναλώσιμη, απογυμνώνοντας τη δολοφονία της από την έμφυλη και ρατσιστική της διάσταση.




Για όλες τις αδικοχαμένες αδερφές μας συνεχίζουμε να παλεύουμε ενάντια σε κάθε εξουσιαστικό μηχανισμό που επιβάλλει θάνατο.




Είμαστε πολλές, δεν κάνουμε ησυχία, το κράτος να τσακίσουμε και την Πατριαρχία.




Η πατριαρχία βιάζει και σκοτώνει — στο δρόμο, στη δουλειά, ποτέ καμία μόνη




Rabbia Viola

title: DEM Party delegation travels to İmralı to meet with Öcalan
content:
The İmralı delegation of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) has traveled to the Turkish prison island of Imrali on Sunday to meet with Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan. The delegation consists of members of parliament Pervin Buldan and Mithat Sancar, and lawyer Faik Özgür Erol from Asrın Law Office.




The DEM Party İmralı delegation last visited Öcalan on September 13.




DEM Party Co-Chair Tuncer Bakırhan stated during his party’s parliamentary group meeting on November 17 that Öcalan had been moved to a residential area specially built for him on Imrali. Accordingly, his working conditions have also changed following the relocation. In addition, his secretarial support has been increased to enable him to work more quickly and effectively, Bakırhan stated.




The changes are linked to the ongoing peace and democratization process. In his speech, Bakırhan emphasized that, following the cessation of armed hostilities and the initiation of dialogue, the focus must now be on establishing the legal and political foundations and opening up space for democratic politics.

title: Guerrillas on the PKK’s 48th founding anniversary: We will fulfill our responsibilities
content:
The Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK) was founded on November 27, 1978, in the village of Fis in the Lice district of Amed (Diyarbakır). Speaking to ANF in Behdînan ahead of the 48th anniversary of the party’s founding, HPG and YJA-Star guerrillas said they regarded November 27 as a national festival.




Delal Çiya, Elî Dirêj, Amed Derik, and Ezîz Derwêş shared their assessments of the PKK’s influence in Kurdistan and the Middle East, the women’s movement, and the Peace and Democratic Society Process.




YJA-Star guerrilla Delal Çiya:

 We celebrate the anniversary of our party, the PKK, in the person of Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan], the martyrs of the revolution, and the entire people of Kurdistan. This is truly a very meaningful and important day. Thanks to the efforts of the comrades who took part in the founding of the party alongside the Leader and devoted themselves to it, the party has endured to this day, undergoing change and transformation and bringing about new developments within its own ranks. The struggle continues and grows stronger through the efforts of the comrades who have resisted and given their lives. With comrades Haki Karer, Mazlum Doğan, and Sakine Cansız resisting in prison and raising the slogan “Berxwedan Jiyane” [Resistance is Life], the resistance gained momentum. At the same time, our party also carried out a revolution within its own ranks, giving rise to the “Jin Jiyan Azadî” [Woman, Life, Freedom] revolution, which continues to this day. Women came to know themselves, grew stronger, and developed a will of their own. Once again, we celebrate our party’s anniversary in the person of the Leader, our fallen comrades, and all our peoples.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/1cd1cc58_20261120113206_2026-11-23-behdinan-delal-ciya-yja-star-gerillasi-27-mijdar-roja-cejna-netewi-ye-1.mp4










HPG guerrilla Elî Dirêj:

 We congratulate Leader Apo, all the martyrs of the revolution, and our patriotic people on the founding anniversary of our party. November 27 holds a very special meaning for us. The PKK was founded following the martyrdom of Comrade Haki Karer. The Kurdish people, who have endured great massacres throughout history, have remained standing through tremendous resistance. We must uphold this resistance. November 27 holds a special significance and spiritual value for us. Strengthening the struggle that has brought us to this day, in the spirit of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, is a fundamental duty for us. Our task is to further strengthen the struggle and demonstrate our commitment and dedication with this spirit and enthusiasm.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/57672db1_20261120113259_2026-11-23-behdinan-eli-direj-hpg-gerillasi-27-mijdar-roja-cejna-netewi-ye-1.mp4










YJA-Star guerrilla Amed Dêrik:

 November 27 had a profound impact not only in Kurdistan but also across the Middle East. Our martyrs brought the struggle to this stage. Even today, it is their efforts and legacy that continue to bring society together. We congratulate Leader Apo on our martyrs on this occasion. Our party upholds important values. The efforts made over the years have made the struggle even more necessary today. We learned from our martyrs to persevere in the pursuit of a free life. With this awareness, we have sought to fulfill our duties and responsibilities. On this basis, it is the duty of all of us to uphold this process. We will fulfill our responsibilities both as a people and as guerrillas. In this spirit, we wish everyone a happy anniversary of our party’s founding.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/ce4c1c15_20261120113135_2026-11-23-behdinan-amed-derik-yja-star-gerillasi-27-mijdar-roja-cejna-netewi-ye-1.mp4










HPG guerrilla Ezîz Derwêş:

 The anniversary of our party’s founding is a day of celebration for us. Every year, we celebrate this occasion and honor the legacy of our fallen comrades. Our party has endured to this day thanks to the efforts of our fallen comrades; it was founded and sustained through the efforts of the Leader. In light of this, we must uphold our party and prove ourselves worthy of the martyrs, who embody the values of our party. By honoring and upholding the legacy of our martyrs, we can also uphold our party. We have pledged to our martyrs that we will fulfill our duties and responsibilities under all circumstances and realize their dreams. To ensure that we can continue celebrating our party’s anniversary every year, we will preserve the legacy of Leader Apo, our fallen comrades, and our resisting people, and we will remain committed to them.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/33f6ba1c_20261120113338_2026-11-23-behdinan-eziz-derwes-hpg-gerillasi-27-mijdar-roja-cejna-netewi-ye-1.mp4

title: Sabahattin Tekin released after 30 years in prison
content:
After 30 years in prison, political prisoner Sabahattin Tekin has been released from Maltepe No. 1 L-Type Prison in Istanbul. He was welcomed outside the prison by his family, representatives of MATUHAY-DER (Marmara Association for Solidarity and Mutual Assistance with the Families of Prisoners and Convicts) and more than a hundred other people.




Immediately after his release, Tekin drew attention to the plight of ill prisoners. He stated that prison conditions were extremely harsh for many of those affected and that their immediate release was therefore necessary. He particularly highlighted the cases of 84-year-old Ali Rıza Yurtdaş and Halis Seven, both of whom remain imprisoned in Maltepe Prison.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/376d4686_20261122095937_2026-11-22-istanbul-sebahattin-tekin-30-yillik-tutsak-tahliye-edildi-1.mp4










Tekin sharply criticized the Turkish Forensic Medicine Institute, whose reports play a significant role in determining whether ill prisoners are fit to remain in detention. He described the institution’s decisions as a form of torture.




Tekin called for support for the Peace and Democratic Society Process. He stressed that democratization and the building of a democratic society continued to require collective commitment. “Our task and our responsibility are to expand this struggle,” he declared. Tekin emphasized that social resistance had given him strength throughout his three decades in prison. He also expressed his determination to continue working for democratic development and the peace process following his release.

title: Protests in Qamişlo: 25 Rojava University students injured
content:
A total of 25 students were injured on November 16 in Qamişlo during protests against the planned incorporation of Rojava University into Syria’s state higher education system. The university’s Student Council announced the figures at a press conference on Sunday. For the first time, the council also confirmed that shots had been fired on university grounds during the crackdown. The council condemned the use of tear gas and firearms against the protesters as a serious violation of the university’s autonomy and the safety of its students.




The statement was issued on the university campus in Qamişlo in the presence of students. Mehebad Adil Serhan read it in Kurdish, while Fadiya Ebdullah read it in English. The Student Council explained that the delay in issuing the statement was due to its efforts over the past few days to care for the injured students and investigate the consequences of the events.




Dispute over the future of Rojava University




The clashes were triggered by a visit from a delegation from Damascus on Monday. The delegation held talks with the university administration about the planned incorporation of Rojava University into al-Furat University in Hesekê. Following the meeting, students demanded information about the decisions reached and the future of their university. When the delegation refused to make a statement, the students blocked its departure.




The conflict stems from two measures introduced by Syria’s transitional government. In addition to the planned incorporation of Rojava University into al-Furat University, the dispute concerns the Ministry of Education’s decision to revoke the recognition of equivalency for degrees awarded by certain faculties. Students regard these measures as an attack on their university’s independent academic and institutional identity.




The protests were therefore directed not merely against an administrative restructuring, but also against interference in academic self-governance and the students’ future. When the students insisted on receiving information about the planned changes, security forces of the transitional government attacked the protesters.




“Unjustifiable under any circumstances”




The Student Council described the actions as a serious violation of university autonomy and a direct threat to the safety and health of students. The protests, it said, had been an expression of legitimate demands and a commitment to preserving the academic and administrative independence of their university. Rather than resorting to violence, it added, those responsible should have sought dialogue and listened to the students’ concerns.




“What we witnessed on university grounds was the use of tear gas and firearms, which left 25 students injured. These shocking scenes are unacceptable under any circumstances and cannot be justified in any way,” the council stated. It condemned the use of military force, weapons, tear gas, and smoke agents on campus as “an attack on the inviolability of the educational institution and the dignity of all students.”




The statement did not specify whether the students’ injuries were caused by tear gas, gunfire, or other forms of violence.




Protection against reprisals and preservation of university autonomy




The council also strongly opposed any potential reprisals related to the protests. “We firmly reject any decision or measure aimed at arresting or prosecuting students for their participation in the peaceful defense of their rights,” the statement read. Such actions would further exacerbate tensions within the university, the Student Council warned and therefore demanded binding guarantees for students’ safety and protection against intimidation, pressure, and all forms of discrimination.




Regarding the university’s future, the council reaffirmed its commitment to preserving its academic and administrative independence. “Students must be able to voice their concerns peacefully and participate in decisions affecting their education and the university’s institutional future. We reject the imposition of decisions with far-reaching consequences without dialogue and mutual understanding,” the council declared. It also stressed that students must not be made to bear the consequences of decisions that jeopardize their academic future.




Appeal to international academic and human rights organizations




The Student Council called on international academic institutions, human rights organizations, and student representative bodies to examine the events in Qamişlo, support those affected, and advocate for measures to prevent such attacks from recurring. In closing, the council emphasized the university’s responsibility to society: “The university is a place of science, dialogue, and the education of future generations—not a place for intimidation and violence against those making peaceful demands. The voices of students must be heard. Their dignity, their safety, and their right to education are red lines that must not be crossed.”

title: Men demonstrate against violence against women in Qamişlo
content:
In Qamişlo, men organized a demonstration to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on November 25. The demonstration highlighted society’s responsibility to combat patriarchal violence and emphasized the importance of equality and mutual respect.




Participants carried banners bearing slogans such as “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” (Woman, Life, Freedom), “Women are the source of life,” and “When women are free, society is free.” Other slogans paid tribute to the women’s revolution in Rojava: “The Revolution of the Braids has broken the shackles of silence” and “The Revolution of the Braids continues.”













Violence against women affects society as a whole




Following the demonstration, a joint statement was read out in Kurdish by Ebas Mihemed and in Arabic by Mihemed Kozî. In the statement, participants condemned all forms of violence against women and emphasized that combating such violence is a responsibility shared by society as a whole.




“We stand up for human rights and the dignity of women. We condemn every form of violence against women. Violence is not merely an individual problem, but a social and humanitarian issue that threatens the future of society,” the statement read.




Stressing that violence violates women’s fundamental rights to life, safety, freedom, and equality, demonstrators urged families, educational institutions, civil society organizations, and all other members of society to respect and protect women’s rights and reject all forms of violence.













Silence will not end violence




The participants also emphasized the need for women and men to live together as equals, stressing that mutual respect and equality must form the foundation of social relations. In closing, they warned against allowing violence against women to persist through silence and inaction: “As long as violence is met with silence, it cannot be overcome. To put an end to violence, everyone must take responsibility and actively fight against it.”

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish women demonstrate against femicide in Düsseldorf
content:
The Kurdish women’s movement held a demonstration in Düsseldorf to draw attention to the ongoing violence against women and the rising number of femicides. Ahead of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on November 25, participants from various cities across North Rhine-Westphalia gathered to emphasize the collective struggle against patriarchal violence and the need for stronger organization among women.




The protest was organized by the North Rhine-Westphalia branch of the Association of Kurdish Women in Germany (YJK-E). Demonstrators carried purple flags and the colors of the Kurdish women’s movement. Banners bore slogans including “Through organized resistance, we will stop femicides and wars” and “We are ashamed of a masculinity that kills women.”










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/deb67b61_20261121160534_2026-11-21-dusseldorf-25-kasim-kadina-yonelik-siddete-karsi-uluslararasi-mucadele-gunu-yuruyus-1.mp4










Murdered women remembered




Carrying portraits of revolutionaries Sakine Cansız, Fidan Doğan, Leyla Şaylemez, and Evîn Goyî, participants commemorated four members of the Kurdish freedom movement who were assassinated in politically motivated attacks in Paris. Images of other women who had been killed were also carried during the protest. The slogan “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” (Woman, Life, Freedom) rang out repeatedly. The demonstration thus combined remembrance of murdered women with a call to organize against femicide, patriarchal structures of domination, and war.




Women’s movement announces further activities




Şevin Sincar spoke on behalf of the Kurdish women’s movement, focusing particularly on violence against women in Germany and the rising number of femicides. She also outlined planned activities as part of the campaign against violence against women and femicide. Sincar emphasized that combating patriarchal violence must not be limited to individual days of protest. She stressed the importance of raising awareness across society, expanding solidarity networks, and strengthening the organized women’s struggle. The women’s movement said it would continue its activities against femicide and male violence in the coming period.

title: YRK reports ongoing attacks by the Iranian regime in East Kurdistan
content:
The Press and Liaison Center of the East Kurdistan Defense Units (YRK) issued a statement providing information about ongoing attacks by the Iranian regime in East Kurdistan (Rojhilat).




According to the statement on Sunday, the Iranian regime has once again bombarded the Serçûrî district of Merîwan using drones and 120 mm mortars. It said the attacks were launched from the military base in the village of Derê and surrounding positions.




According to the statement, the attacks caused damage to the local environment, landscape, natural resources, and wildlife.




The YRK confirmed that no fatalities occurred in their ranks as a result of the attacks.




The YRK also reported that the Iranian regime was preparing for a large-scale military operation in Serdeşt. It stated that the regime was preventing civilians from entering or leaving the area and attempting to create an atmosphere of fear and anxiety.




The YRK declared that it would respond to any attack carried out against its forces by the Iranian regime within the framework of “legitimate self-defense” and emphasized that it was prepared for any eventuality.

title: Protest against two years of state-appointed trustees in Dersim
content:
A rally was held in Seyîd Riza Square in Dersim (Turkish: Tunceli) to mark the second anniversary of the appointment of state-appointed trustees to the municipalities of Dersim and Ovacık district. The demonstration was organized by the Labor and Democracy Platform and attended by local residents and representatives of political parties and civil society organizations. Participants demanded the removal of the trustees and the reinstatement of the democratically elected municipal administrations.




“Social peace cannot be achieved through the appointment of trustees”




Demonstrators carried a banner reading: “The appointment of trustees is an attack on the will of the people and public resources. We do not accept it.” The platform’s joint statement was read out by Özcan Ateş, Co-Chair of the DEM Party’s provincial branch in Dersim. He criticized the fact that the democratically expressed will of the people of Dersim and Ovacık had been disregarded for two years.




Referring to the ongoing Peace and Democratic Society Process, Ateş stated that ending the system of trustees was a necessary prerequisite for credible democratization. “Peace can only be achieved if democratic rights are genuinely guaranteed. Without recognizing the will of the people, a democratic society cannot be built. Social peace cannot be achieved through the policy of appointing trustees,” Ateş emphasized.




Birsen Orhan: State-appointed trustees must be removed




Birsen Orhan, the elected Co-Mayor of Dersim who was replaced by a state-appointed trustee, then took the floor. She criticized the consequences of two years of trustee administration, highlighting in particular the dismissal of municipal employees who have been unable to return to their jobs despite court rulings.




Orhan also recalled the case of Gülistan Doku, a university student who disappeared in 2020 and whose fate has remained a matter of concern for the people of Dersim for years. Tuncay Sonel, the governor and state-appointed trustee at the time, is currently in pretrial detention in connection with the suspected femicide of the then 21-year-old woman.




“For two years, the will of the people has been disregarded, and this disregard is even being portrayed as a success story,” Orhan said. She stressed that respecting democratic decisions was a fundamental prerequisite for the ongoing peace process. “The appointment of trustees contradicts the spirit of this process, and these administrations must be revoked.”




Trustee administration also targets identity




The ousted Co-Mayor Cevdet Konak also offered a critical assessment of the state-appointed administration in Dersim. He said the past two years had been marked by losses and institutional decline. He stressed that the interventions had targeted not only the elected municipal representatives but also the city’s social and cultural identity.




“The trustee administration was also imposed on the language, identity, faith, and memory of Dersim. Decisions are being made without transparency and with the public excluded from the process,” Konak stated. He demanded public accountability for the past two years: “Disclose what you have done over these two years. Can you do that? No, you cannot. You talk about the public interest and building trust. Why, then, have you closed the places where the people of Dersim could express themselves?”




Konak pointed to the contradiction between the peace process and continued state control over municipalities. “While we are engaged in a peace process, our will continues to be overridden by a state-appointed trustee. We say: Restore our democratic self-governance and remove the trustees.”




Criticism of environmental destruction and economic interests




Mustafa Sarıgül, the elected Mayor of Ovacık who was replaced by a state-appointed trustee, recalled that municipal officials had been elected to office by the people. “Only the people can remove us from office,” he declared.




Sarıgül noted that they had worked to protect the language, nature, and social identity of their region during their time in office. He particularly criticized the ongoing destruction of Dersim’s natural environment and the commercial exploitation of its landscape.




“Recently, the beauty of Dersim has been praised everywhere. If that is the case, why are roads being built through our forests, our natural environment being destroyed, and our natural resources being handed over to capital?” Sarıgül asked. He emphasized that regardless of how long the trustee administration remained in place, the people would continue their collective resistance against these policies.




Call for democratic steps in the peace process




DEM Party MP Ayten Kordu criticized the continued use of state-appointed trustees as a routine instrument for exercising political power. She argued that the practice was far from being abolished and persisted as a form of state control over democratically elected municipalities.




Representatives of other political parties also referred to the ongoing Peace and Democratic Society Process. They called for concrete steps toward democratization, particularly an end to trustee administrations and the restoration of municipal authority to elected representatives.
