title: Alfred de Zayas: Why should Kurds be denied the right to self-determination? - Part Two
content:
Alfred de Zayas, an expert in international law and human rights who served as the United Nations (UN) Independent Expert on the Promotion of a Democratic and Equitable International Order from 2012 to 2018, spoke to ANF about the Kurdish people's right to self-determination and autonomy, the possibilities of obtaining status within the UN, the treatment of stateless peoples and double standards in international law.




The first part of this interview can be found 

here

. 




Under Article 4 of the United Nations Charter, UN membership is open only to states. However, there are peoples such as the Kurds who do not have their own state. How can these peoples obtain a status or the right to representation within the UN?




This is first and foremost a political issue. From a legal perspective, it is quite straightforward because the Palestinians have managed to obtain a certain degree of international recognition. We know about the genocides committed against Palestinians and the ethnic cleansing they have suffered. There is growing sympathy for the Palestinian people. By contrast, almost nothing is known about the Kurds. What do we see about the Kurds in the press? The first thing that comes to people's minds is "terrorism".




Turkey has demonised Abdullah Öcalan and the Kurds in Turkey to such an extent that a large proportion of people have accepted this propaganda. Therefore, this propaganda must be countered. The mechanisms known as the "Special Procedures" of the UN Human Rights Council must be activated. These mechanisms include special rapporteurs working in different fields. It is extremely important that what is happening in the Kurdish regions of Turkey, Iran, Iraq and Syria be made known through the UN and these rapporteurs. Therefore, the first step is to provide information.




Once awareness has been raised about the injustices suffered by the Kurdish people, a political coalition could emerge to support, first, extensive autonomy for the Kurdish people and then, if the people so wish, the right to secession. I believe that the United Nations has failed to fulfil its responsibility towards the Kurdish people. The UN has also failed in its duty to the world by not organising referendums where they were needed.




Referendums were held in East Timor, South Sudan and during the process of separation between Ethiopia and Eritrea. However, these initiatives came far too late. Action was taken only after tens of thousands of people had lost their lives. Preventive action should have been taken instead. You should also be very familiar with the Constitution of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), because UNESCO's responsibilities include protecting Kurdish culture, identity, language, cultural heritage and collective memory. UNESCO has organised numerous international conferences on these issues.




For example, I would like to recall the conference held in Barcelona in November and December 1998. Following that conference, a declaration was adopted on using the right to self-determination as a strategy for preventing conflicts. The right to self-determination does not cause war. On the contrary, the unjust denial of this right leads to violence. If we want to preserve local, regional and international peace, we must resolve these issues.




As we have seen in the case of Palestine, when a people is subjected to colonisation or an apartheid regime, the United Nations has a clear role and responsibility to fulfil.




But the UN has done nothing.




'

The UN has surrendered to political interests'




What concerns me deeply is the way the UN has surrendered to political interests. Let me give you an example. About a year ago, on 17 November 2025, the UN Security Council adopted Resolution 2803. This resolution envisaged the creation of a so-called "Board of Peace" associated with Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu.




What does this mean? It is completely absurd, appalling and unacceptable. The UN Security Council cannot delegate its own obligations to a supposedly private body called the "Board of Peace". This is a fundamental contradiction and an entirely unacceptable situation.




I was genuinely surprised that Russia and China abstained from the vote. They should have exercised their veto powers. This was precisely a situation in which a veto would have been justified, even necessary. The issue was not merely about Gaza or Palestine. In my opinion, Donald Trump's objective with this "Board of Peace" was to replace the UN. In reality, it was an attempt to transfer the responsibilities of the UN Security Council into Donald Trump's hands.




'International law must protect the fundamental rights of Kurds'




Beyond the right to self-determination, the political, cultural and linguistic rights of the Kurdish people in the countries where they live are also important issues under international law. What legal mechanisms can be used to bring the human rights violations suffered by Kurds in these countries onto the international legal agenda?




International law is clear on this matter. It recognises not only the rights of peoples but also the rights of minorities. Minority rights are not limited to the right to freedom from discrimination. They are also positive rights. They include the right of a minority to preserve its culture, speak its own language and maintain its own institutions. This is what international law provides for in theory.




As you know, Turkey is not a member of the European Union (EU). However, it is a member of the Council of Europe and a party to the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR). Therefore, applications should also be made to the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) concerning violations of Kurdish rights in Turkey.




The European Convention on Human Rights system also provides for interstate applications. In other words, a state party to the Convention can bring an application against another state, including Turkey, for violations of the rights guaranteed under the Convention.




This mechanism also exists under the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (ICERD). Where the necessary conditions are met, interstate complaints, as well as individual complaints, can be submitted to the Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination (CERD).




There are already numerous cases concerning Israel. In particular, I would like to recall the proceedings initiated by Palestine against Israel before CERD. Numerous cases have also been examined by the Committee Against Torture (CAT).




It is also worth recalling that Article 41 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) provides for an interstate complaint mechanism under certain conditions. If I am not mistaken, approximately 172 states are parties to this Covenant. Therefore, although it is not entirely universal, it comes quite close.




Under this mechanism, states that have accepted the relevant competence of the committee can allege that another state which has accepted the same procedure has violated the Covenant.




In the case of Turkey, numerous articles of the Covenant can be invoked. Article 1 concerns the right of peoples to self-determination. Article 6 protects the right to life, Article 7 prohibits torture, and Article 14 guarantees the right to a fair trial and the independence of the courts. Article 25 concerns participation in political life, Article 26 guarantees equality and prohibits discrimination, and Article 27 protects minority rights.




'States do not dare to act'




I would like to see a state use the existing mechanisms to bring the situation of the Kurdish people before the UN Human Rights Committee. So far, no state has dared to do so. I do not understand why. This is precisely where you have a major responsibility. First, you must inform people about all the available legal avenues and international mechanisms, including interstate complaint procedures.




Perhaps a state could be found that is willing to undertake such an initiative against Turkey. This is an issue of universal importance. States parties to the Covenant have a legitimate interest in demanding compliance with its provisions.




I am very familiar with the procedures of the UN Human Rights Committee. I personally participated in drafting the committee's rules of procedure at the time. Therefore, I know very well how it operates. The legal avenues exist. However, the greatest obstacle is the lack of information and awareness. The world does not know enough about the situation of the Kurds.




Unfortunately, Turkey has succeeded in demonising the Kurds, just as Israel has done with the Palestinians. This perception, based on portraying Kurds as "terrorists", must be challenged. People need to understand that the Kurds have long possessed the right to self-determination.




You have spoken about the right of peoples to resist occupation and oppression under international law and emphasised that the Kurds are under occupation. In this context, could the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), which has now dissolved itself, have been considered a resistance movement? How should we interpret the EU's continued designation of the PKK as a "terrorist" organisation despite its dissolution and insistence on peace?




The problem is that the European Union is morally bankrupt. This may sound somewhat radical to you, but that is how I see the situation. For decades, the European Union has provided military, economic, political, diplomatic and media support to a state that I believe is responsible for genocide.




What values do Europeans actually defend? They no longer have any moral authority. They repeat the propaganda used by Israel against Palestinians. At the same time, they make use of Turkey's propaganda against the Kurds. This is easy to do because trade relations continue.




'The EU is morally bankrupt'




If you want to convince Erdoğan or the Turkish government that this situation can no longer continue, you can take action in the field of trade. You can stop selling certain products to Turkey or purchasing products from Turkey.




The same applies to the policies of the US and Donald Trump. Why do states continue to buy Boeing aircraft? Why do they buy military equipment manufactured by Lockheed Martin or Raytheon, or F-35 and F-16 fighter jets produced by the American defence industry? Why do they continue purchasing US Treasury bonds? These practices must end.




This is precisely the fundamental principle of the BDS movement, which stands for Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions. If this strategy were applied not only to Israel but also to the US, changes would occur. When economic interests begin to suffer, there can be significant political consequences. However, we need to be conscious of this. What concerns me is that we continue to act as though nothing has happened and carry on with business as usual.




Numerous statements are made in support of Palestinians, and strong language is used. But is anything concrete actually being done to save these people, who are suffering and facing severe oppression? No. We are merely talking. As I said earlier, I find it shameful that António Guterres has not used the term "genocide" when condemning crimes committed by Israel. I also find it shameful that, in my opinion, the United Nations continues to repeat Turkey's propaganda against the Kurds.




We live in a deeply flawed world. We need a forum where states can discuss peace, development, climate and the major challenges facing the world. We need to find global solutions to global problems. We need coordination, dialogue and a better understanding of one another.




I am deeply committed to the United Nations General Assembly and its universal character. I would also like the UN Human Rights Council to be based on universal participation rather than a system consisting of only 47 elected states. I know how these elections are conducted and all the political manoeuvring that accompanies them. I also know about the negotiations, reciprocal interests and agreements between states to secure a seat on the Human Rights Council.




If the Human Rights Council were transformed into a genuine human rights general assembly in which all states had equal voting rights, the world would be a much better place. The system would function much better and would be far less vulnerable to political manoeuvring. In any case, the Kurds know their rights. What matters to them is defending their culture, language and heritage. You are Kurdish, and you can be proud of being Kurdish.




Therefore, continue to struggle through peaceful means, as you have done until now. Continue to convince the world and inform international public opinion about your situation and your rights.




Who is Alfred de Zayas?




Alfred de Zayas is a lawyer, historian, academic and author known for his work on international law, human rights and the right of peoples to self-determination. He studied law at Harvard University and obtained a doctorate in history from the University of Göttingen in Germany. He is a professor of international law and history at the Geneva School of Diplomacy in Switzerland.




Between 1980 and 2003, de Zayas worked as a lawyer in the United Nations human rights offices in Geneva, serving as secretary of the UN Human Rights Committee and head of its petitions unit. From 2012 to 2018, he served as the first UN Independent Expert on the Promotion of a Democratic and Equitable International Order, appointed by the UN Human Rights Council. During this period, he submitted 14 reports to the UN General Assembly and the Human Rights Council.




De Zayas has written numerous books and academic articles on international law, minority rights, genocide, self-determination and UN reform. His works include Building a Just World Order and United Nations Human Rights Committee Case Law.







Alfred de Zayas: Why should Kurds be denied the right to self-determination? - Part One

The right of peoples to self-determination is one of the fundamental principles of international law. However, its implementation remains contested because of the political and economic interests o...

title: Batı: Maintenance and production overlapped at HABAŞ
content:
The working conditions, subcontracting system, lack of occupational health and safety measures, and trade union organisation at the HABAŞ iron and steel plant in Aliağa, Izmir, have come under scrutiny following the workplace massacre. Nineteen metalworkers lost their lives at the plant. Even before their colleagues trapped beneath the rubble could be recovered, production continued, and workers were called in for their shifts. Outrage grew further when workers were prohibited from bringing mobile phones into the factory, reportedly on the orders of HABAŞ owner Mehmet Rüştü Başaran, who had been released under house arrest and issued the instruction from his waterfront mansion in Istanbul. Workers protesting this brutal system of exploitation, built on their own blood, were then confronted by the state's gendarmerie. Lawyer Lütfi Sabri Batı, who represents workers in the industrial areas between Soma and Izmir, spoke to ANF about the conditions facing workers caught between the threat of death and the fear of unemployment, under a system involving employers, the state and company-friendly unions. Batı said that workers returned to their jobs on the morning of 16 November in all sections of the plant except the unit where the explosion occurred. He recalled Article 13 of Occupational Health and Safety Law No. 6331, saying, "Workers have the right to refuse to work in the face of serious and imminent danger. They need to submit a written application and exercise this right."




'

Only 500 to 600 of HABAŞ's approximately 6,000 workers are directly employed'




Lawyer Lütfi Sabri Batı said that the HABAŞ facility in Aliağa, where 19 workers lost their lives, covers an extensive industrial area of approximately 10 square kilometres and carries out various metal production activities, including steel, iron and steel, and aluminium production. Batı said that approximately 6,000 workers are employed at HABAŞ's metal smelting and refining facilities, which also have their own private port. Only 500 to 600 of these workers are directly employed by HABAŞ, while the rest work for subcontracting companies. Batı said that between 20 and 25 different subcontracting companies reportedly operate across the extensive production facilities. Batı said: "HABAŞ essentially operates through subcontracting companies. Job insecurity is extremely high. The company is classified as a heavy and hazardous workplace, with temperatures reaching 400 degrees. Many workers are not directly employed by HABAŞ. HABAŞ's directly employed workers are organised in Türk Metal, a union affiliated with the Confederation of Turkish Trade Unions (Türk-Iş). Türk Metal does not attempt to organise the subcontracted workers, nor does it allow another union to operate within these facilities. Because there is a gentlemen's agreement between the three trade union confederations in the metal sector, the United Metalworkers' Union (Birleşik Metal-Iş), affiliated with the Confederation of Progressive Trade Unions of Turkey (DISK), cannot organise here. It cannot even call Türk Metal a company-friendly union. This situation could change if workers collectively joined another union, but organising is difficult because most are employed through subcontractors. As a result, Türk Metal has effectively established a monopoly over these facilities."




'

Experienced workers are dismissed with severance pay and rehired on lower wages'




Batı visited the families of workers killed in the massacre to offer his condolences and met with five families. He said that most HABAŞ workers come from other provinces and work under extremely difficult conditions. Batı said that he met the families of Özcan Efe, Ferhat Maraşlı, Ersin Oğuz, Kadir Kaan Özçelik and Yasin Taşçı, five of the 19 workers who lost their lives. Batı said: "Özcan Efe was from Ağrı but lived with his family in Manisa. He was the father of one child and was directly employed by HABAŞ. Ferhat Maraşlı had also been a directly employed worker for 16 years. Ersin Oğuz belonged to the Çepni Alevi community and lived in Kınık. He was also the first cousin of the wife of Tahir Çetin, a founding member and honorary president of the Independent Mineworkers' Union (Bağımsız Maden-Iş), who died in a traffic accident. Ersin worked there as a subcontracted worker. Kadir Kaan Özçelik was a 25-year-old engineer. He also worked at HABAŞ through a subcontractor. Yasin Taşçı was directly employed. Workers employed by subcontracting companies in particular work their regular shifts plus four hours of overtime, bringing their daily working hours to 12. Subcontracted workers earn approximately 30,000 Turkish lira. They try to increase their wages to 40,000 lira by working overtime on their weekly days off. They are forced to sacrifice even their right to rest for approximately 10,000 lira in additional income. There is a system in these facilities under which directly employed workers receive pay increases according to their years of service. But particularly over the past two years, a different practice has been introduced for experienced workers. They tell experienced workers, 'Take your severance pay and leave.' They pay the workers their compensation and dismiss them. If the same worker wants to return to HABAŞ, they are forced to accept a 30 percent reduction in their salary. The company simply claims that their previous wages were too high. In other words, over the past two years, HABAŞ has been dismissing directly employed workers after paying their severance, then rehiring them at wages 30 percent lower, effectively resetting their seniority."




'The subcontracting system is a sham, and conditions are worse than in the mines'




Batı continued: "There is also a sham subcontracting system here. In reality, all the subcontractors are connected to the main company in one way or another. The same system probably exists at HABAŞ. Subcontracting companies recruit workers through a system similar to the labour recruiters known as dayıbaşı in the Soma mines. For example, workers hired for cleaning duties may also be assigned to production. The facility also has its own port, so there are separate subcontractors for port operations. In reality, an entire complex of companies operates within the facility because so many different activities take place simultaneously. Scrap metal arrives, is melted down and then processed into new products. The products must also be packaged, shipped and transported. Subcontractors have been assigned to every one of these auxiliary operations. The working conditions imposed at these facilities are so appalling that even miners would struggle to work there. Conditions are worse than in the mines."




'

Production was not stopped during crane maintenance on the day of the explosion'




Batı said that the explosion occurred on 9 November 2026, normally a weekly rest day, when workers had come to the factory to earn additional income through overtime. Batı also said: "When we spoke to the family of Ersin Oğuz, who died in the explosion, they told us that the workers had gone to the iron and steel plant that day to work overtime. Maintenance work was being carried out on the day of the explosion. In other words, maintenance was taking place in an area where production was also continuing. Özcan Efe, whose family we spoke to, was at the factory that day to carry out maintenance on the crane used to transport the molten metal ladles. We do not know whether the crane was faulty or whether this was routine maintenance. But the fundamental problem is that production should normally stop when maintenance is being carried out in a workplace. You should not operate machinery for production while simultaneously carrying out maintenance on it. Yet production was not stopped during maintenance at this facility. Consequently, there were many workers at the factory that day, and something probably triggered an incident during maintenance, causing the explosion. There was already a ladle containing molten metal at a temperature of around 1,000 degrees. Steel is also melted using natural gas. The crane struck the ladle, its chains failed to hold it, and the ladle overturned. It may have struck the natural gas pipes, or something spilling from it may have struck the pipes. Either possibility could have occurred. The molten metal inside the ladle had a minimum temperature of 1,000 degrees. Apart from the maintenance workers, 50 workers were on duty that day. So far, 19 workers are reported to have died, but searches are continuing for other workers trapped beneath the rubble. For example, we received information that the owner of the subcontracting company where Özcan Efe worked went there to search for his workers. The bodies of many workers have still not been recovered, and they are probably unrecognisable."




'Production continued while workers' bodies remained under the rubble'




Batı said that production continued at the factory even while the bodies of workers remained trapped beneath the rubble. He said that the explosion occurred during the morning shift, at approximately 11:30 am to noon, but production at the other facilities continued until 4 pm. Batı said that although production was subsequently suspended in the days following the massacre, workers continued to be transported to the factory by shuttle buses in three shifts. Batı said: "On the day of the explosion, Türk Metal told the workers, 'Occupational health and safety conditions at the workplace are satisfactory. Continue working.' Yet the workers' bodies had not even been recovered from the rubble. Workers were transported to the factory by shuttle buses, but production had stopped. They were kept inside without being assigned any work. Most recently, the employer also ordered that workers be prohibited from bringing their phones into the facility. They were probably trying to conceal evidence. They introduced the phone ban to prevent workers from entering and taking photographs, but they were unable to enforce it. Workers reacted against the ban. Workers who wanted to protest against Türk Metal during its public statement were beaten. Türk Metal brought its own members outside for the statement and attempted to have the factory workers who wanted to protest against the union attacked by the crowd. To allow Türk Metal to make its statement, the gendarmerie first removed the HABAŞ workers from the area and then detained them."




'Occupational safety exists only on paper, with no inspections in the explosion unit'




Batı said that HABAŞ has a long record of workplace deaths, claiming that more than 100 workers have been killed in workplace incidents at the facility since the 1990s. He said that 550 officially recorded workplace accidents occurred between 2021 and 2024, while the number reached 240 in 2025 alone, indicating a significant increase. Batı also recalled that Eyüp Eğinli, a 20-year-old subcontracted worker, was killed in a workplace incident on 5 November, just four days before the major explosion on 9 November. He said that the massacre had been foreseeable. Batı said that inspections at HABAŞ, as at other workplaces, were largely a formality. He said: "A worker I spoke to told me that occupational health and safety specialists had never entered the sections where the explosion occurred. There cannot be a section of a workplace that occupational health and safety personnel never inspect. Occupational health and safety exists on paper, but no inspections were actually carried out. These specialists work under Joint Health and Safety Units (ÖSGB). These units operate as joint-stock companies. Such companies sign contracts with other companies to provide occupational health and safety services. Consequently, the company responsible for inspections receives its payment from the very employers it is supposed to inspect. That is how the system works. Unfortunately, this is a reality in Turkey."




'

Workers now have to make a choice'




Batı said that workers were ordered to return to work on the morning of 16 November in all sections of the factory except the unit where the explosion occurred, despite the earlier suspension of production and the continuing search for workers trapped beneath the rubble. He recalled that Occupational Health and Safety Law No. 6331 gives workers the right to refuse to work in dangerous conditions. He explained that workers must submit a written application to their employer to exercise this right. Batı stressed that workers must overcome their fear of dismissal and struggle to protect their lives. Batı said: "The working class is strong when it becomes a class for itself, and it is workers' organisation that makes this possible. Therefore, workers must organise. They can establish workers' assemblies, form committees or join genuine trade unions. If genuine trade unions refuse to accept them because of a gentlemen's agreement or for some other reason, workers should establish their own independent unions, just like the Warehouse, Port, Shipyard and Maritime Workers' Union (DGD-Sen), the Independent Mineworkers' Union (Bağımsız Maden-Iş) and the United Textile, Weaving and Leather Workers' Union (BIRTEK-SEN). Six workers die every day in this country. Workers now have to make a choice. Either they overcome their fears and join genuine trade unions and organisations, or, if that is not possible, they establish their own unions and organisations. Otherwise, they might as well side with the employers and accept that workers can be killed. There is no middle ground anymore."

title: Kurdish Film Festival in Zurich: Let our stories not be forgotten
content:
The Kurdish Film Festival, which began on 19 November in Zurich, offered a packed programme. Organised by the Zurich Kurdish Film Festival Association, the event is being held with the support of the City of Zurich Department of Culture (Stadt Zürich Kultur), the Canton of Zurich’s Cultural Funding Office (Kanton Zürich Kulturförderung/Swisslos), Temperatio and the Migros Culture Percentage (Migros Kulturprozent).




Taking place for the first time, the festival brings together films by filmmakers from different parts of Kurdistan and the diaspora.




The programme on Saturday, 21 November, featured films exploring war, migration, women's struggles and the lives of Kurdish people across different geographical regions.




Xavier Koller’s 

Reise der Hoffnung

 (

Journey of Hope

) tells the story of a Kurdish family’s journey as they attempt to reach Switzerland. Meanwhile, Hasan Oswald’s documentary 

Mediha

 introduced audiences to the struggle for survival of a young Êzidî woman who survived attacks by ISIS.




The programme also included 

Arzela from Amed

 by Elif Yiğit and Johannes Paech; 

Dream’s Gate

 by Negin Ahmadi, which focuses on women fighters in Rojava; and 

All the Mountains Give

, a documentary by Arash Rakhsha about the lives of kolbers (cross-border porters).







 







Today, Sunday, the festival’s final day, screenings will include productions from Rojava’s cinema scene.




Zîlan Hemo’s documentary 

The Traveling Cinema (Sînema Gerok)

 tells the story of İsmail Mamo, who is working to bring cinema to villages in Kobanê. Meanwhile, Sevînaz Evidkê’s film 

Berbû

 focuses on the experiences of women displaced during attacks on Serêkaniyê.




The final day’s programme will also feature the documentary 

Kardeş Türküler ile 30 Yıl

 (

30 Years with Kardeş Türküler

) and 

Paradies!

 by Kurdwin Ayub. The festival will conclude at 6pm with a screening of 

The Last Word from Bavê Tayar

, directed by Ghamkin Saleh.







Alongside film screenings, the festival also features discussions with directors, workshops for children and cultural events. Activities are taking place at various cinema and cultural venues across Zurich.




There is great interest in Kurdish culture




Speaking to ANF, Deniz Ökmen, one of the festival’s organisers, explained that the idea for the festival emerged last year following a film screening they attended in Zurich.







Ökmen said their aim was to introduce Kurdish cinema not only to Kurds living in the diaspora but also to Swiss society.




“We asked ourselves: Why shouldn't we show Kurdish films and Kurdish art both to our people living in the diaspora and to the Swiss people with whom we share our lives? A few of us came together and established the Zurich Kurdish Film Festival Association,” he said.




Ökmen explained that, while putting together the festival programme, they had made a particular effort to include films from all four parts of Kurdistan. He added that despite this being the festival’s first edition, it had attracted a great deal of interest.




“We selected films from Rojhilat, Rojava, Bakur and Başûr. Despite this being our first festival, every screening was fully attended. In fact, we even had to accommodate many people by having them sit on the floor. We saw that people have a tremendous interest in Kurdish culture. Throughout this process, we also rediscovered just how rich Kurdish art and cinema really are,” he said.







We want to make the festival an annual event




Emphasising that the festival had attracted interest not only from Kurds but also from Swiss society, Ökmen said that approximately half of the audience was Kurdish, while the other half came from different communities.




“The most beautiful thing is that we are able to introduce Kurdish culture not only to our people in the diaspora but also to the communities we live alongside. Our Swiss friends are also involved in the festival. It makes us especially happy when Swiss people attending the screenings greet us in Kurdish,” he said.




Stating that they hoped to continue the festival in future years with even greater participation, Ökmen continued: “We started out as an amateur group, but we encountered an enormous amount of demand. Next year, we want to begin preparations earlier, expand the festival and make it more professional. This interest gives us the motivation to organise the festival again and establish it as an annual tradition.”




We must keep our culture and language alive




Hevi Öcal, one of the festival’s volunteer supporters, who was born and raised in exile in Switzerland, highlighted the importance of passing Kurdish culture and language on to future generations.







She said: “I am volunteering here because I think it is wonderful that our people are organising a Kurdish cultural festival in Switzerland for the first time. I feel incredibly proud of our people. I wanted to be part of this and contribute to ensuring that events like this continue in the future. In this way, we can continue watching wonderful films and telling our own stories. I want our voices to be heard, for us not to be forgotten, and for our language not to be forgotten either. This is very important to me.




It is especially meaningful to me that we are able to pass our culture on to future generations. After all, I was born here too. I grew up between two cultures. That is why, if we are not to forget our own culture and want to keep it alive forever, we need to practise it more and make sure it continues to live on.”

title: Certificates awarded to students completing Kurdish language courses in Mannheim
content:
A certificate ceremony was held at the Democratic Kurdish Community Centre in Mannheim, Germany, for students who had successfully completed Kurdish language courses. Attended by numerous Kurdish families living in Mannheim and the surrounding areas, the ceremony highlighted the importance of preserving, developing and passing the Kurdish language on to future generations.







Certificates were presented by the Mothers of Martyrs to numerous students who had successfully completed two terms of Kurdish language courses organised across Germany.




During the ceremony, Osman Kapan, a writer and member of the Kurdish Institute of Germany, as well as Erk, Selamet, Rojda Yıldız and Zeynep Kayaş, delivered speeches. Ruken Akça, Co-Chair of the Confederation of Kurdish Communities in Germany (KON-MED), also gave a brief address.







 







If a language goes, everything goes




In his speech, writer Osman Kapan described language as the cornerstone of a people's identity, culture and collective memory, stressing that keeping the mother tongue alive is a shared responsibility.







Emphasising the importance of children learning Kurdish from an early age and using it in their daily lives, Kapan said that Kurdish families living in Europe, in particular, must ensure that their children maintain their connection to their mother tongue in societies where other languages are dominant.







Kapan stated that families should speak Kurdish at home, develop their children's awareness of the language and pass their mother tongue on to future generations. He added that Kurdish can only be kept alive not simply through speaking it, but also through reading, writing, education and cultural activities that contribute to its development.







The ceremony highlighted the need to strengthen educational initiatives, cultural activities and collective efforts to develop the Kurdish language, conveying the message that “if a language goes, everything goes” taking centre stage.







It was emphasised that protecting Kurdish means not only preserving the legacy of the past but also safeguarding the future and the identity of new generations.




The ceremony also highlighted the achievements of students who had taken part in Kurdish language education, with calls for mother-tongue initiatives to continue and expand.

author: Unknown
title: Kezban Doğan: Collective struggle against femicide is essential - Part One
content:
As activities continue in Germany to mark 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, the Kurdish Women's Movement has launched a new campaign to strengthen the collective struggle against femicide. The preparatory phase, running from 1 November to 8 March, aims to reach different sections of society through training sessions, seminars, panels, demonstrations and other activities.




Kezban Doğan, term spokesperson for the Kurdish Women's Union in Germany (YJK-E), said that treating femicides solely as individual crimes obscures the underlying causes of the problem. She spoke to ANF about a range of issues, from femicides in Germany and the difficulties faced by refugee women to state policies and the patriarchal mentality.







 







'The true scale of femicide is not disclosed'




Kezban Doğan said that the failure to publish comprehensive statistics on femicide was a major problem. She noted that governments compile daily figures during wars, disasters and economic crises but do not adopt the same approach to femicide. Doğan argued that this was a policy aimed at preventing a public response.




Kezban Doğan said: "The figures and statistics released in Germany are not simply statistics. In fact, this is one of the biggest problems. When a war breaks out anywhere in the world, daily figures are compiled for that country. When a disaster occurs, a record of the casualties is produced, even if official figures are unavailable. Similarly, when inflation or another economic problem arises, figures are compiled.




Unfortunately, however, we cannot access such comprehensive statistics or figures when it comes to femicide. We can regard this as a policy pursued by states, particularly nation-states. In fact, I would say that this is definitely the case. When figures are made public, they provoke a reaction, a response from society. I believe the reason the total figures are not disclosed is precisely to prevent that public response.




The United Nations says that a woman is killed every five minutes worldwide. If we calculate what that means, we can imagine the number of women killed over 24 hours. I believe the failure to present these statistics comprehensively is intended to prevent society from reacting to this reality."




Kezban Doğan also drew attention to figures on femicide in Germany, saying that some sources had recorded 105 cases and others 108 by October 2026. She added that two more women had been killed in November. She said: "One was a foreign woman staying in a women's shelter, while the other lost her life under different circumstances. This also reveals the state's policies. I think we need to examine this issue in greater depth." 




Doğan stressed that femicides committed in Germany over the past six years needed to be examined comprehensively, including deaths recorded as suicides and other dimensions of violence against women.




'Violence against women increased during the coronavirus pandemic'




Kezban Doğan recalled that violence against women increased dramatically during the coronavirus pandemic and that women's shelters had no places left. She also criticised government officials at the time for explaining domestic violence in terms of men's psychological difficulties.




Doğan said: "Violence against women increased enormously during that period. There were no places left in women's shelters in Germany. This was not simply because there were too few shelters, but also because they were experiencing overwhelming demand. Yet when we look at the statements made in parliament by government officials, particularly interior ministers and other ministers, they claimed that men were experiencing crises and depression and were therefore turning to domestic violence.




We should have examined this much more deeply at the time. Unfortunately, we failed to get to the heart of the issue or monitor it adequately. If we could obtain comprehensive official statistics on femicide and violence against women from 2020 to the present, just as we obtain figures on wars, we would see a much larger number and a far more serious picture. We need to examine both its psychological and social dimensions. We did not do enough at the time, but we must do so today."




'Women also face violence along migration routes'




Kezban Doğan also addressed the claim that Kurdish women account for 10 percent of women killed in Germany. She stressed that Kurdish women's experiences of migration to Europe differ from those of men, noting that women face multiple forms of oppression in their homelands from states, dominant powers, families, tribal structures and their immediate surroundings.




Doğan said that women had been forced to seek refuge in Europe because of oppression, torture, detention and threats to their lives, rather than seeing Europe simply as a place of liberation. She emphasised that women also experience rape, violence and forced prostitution along migration routes.




Kezban Doğan said: "Kurdish women already faced problems with dominant powers, colonial policies and the state in the countries where they lived, on their own lands. They also faced problems within their families, tribal structures and society. Thirdly, they experienced problems within their immediate families and closest surroundings, involving their children, husbands, siblings and fathers.




Women were forced to seek refuge in Europe because of the oppression, torture, detention and threats to their lives, not because they saw Europe as a place of liberation. But before reaching Europe, there is also the journey itself, the story of how they arrived. When you ask men about their migration journeys, their accounts tend to focus more on physical hardships and financial difficulties. But when we examine women's experiences, we see rape, violence, being forced into prostitution and many other serious problems. These journeys also have devastating consequences for women who manage to reach Germany. Unfortunately, many women fall into the hands of prostitution networks along the way or are killed. Their names and identities disappear, and their fate remains unknown."




Kezban Doğan said that women's problems did not end when they reached Germany. Instead, they encountered new forms of violence and oppression in refugee camps, where their psychological, financial, healthcare and educational needs were not adequately met.




Doğan continued: "After arriving in Germany, the same problems begin again, this time in refugee camps. The state already regards you as a burden. Yet under many of the international conventions Germany has signed, the psychological, financial, healthcare and educational needs of people arriving as refugees must be addressed. Instead, the opposite happens.




If we look at the past ten years, particularly the period beginning with developments in Rojava, even examining the years after 2014 provides one of the clearest examples. Women want to escape as quickly as possible and leave behind the conditions imposed on them as a burden. Yet there, too, they are pushed into the hands of prostitution networks and forced into drug use. To survive, they bury all their psychological suffering inside themselves and try to find a place in society."




Kezban Doğan said that refugee camps lacked therapy centres and that psychological and educational support was inadequate. She stressed that women's lack of knowledge about their rights and the support mechanisms available to them further aggravated their difficulties.




Doğan said: "There are no therapy centres, and psychologists and educational specialists are not brought in. In reality, you live a kind of open-prison existence. The only difference is that you are not living alongside your neighbours or being subjected to direct physical torture. But you are still exposed to psychological and economic abuse and violence. Many women do not know enough about their circumstances or their rights, so they do not know where to apply, who can support them or with whom they can build solidarity. Unfortunately, this can lead them in the wrong direction. The state, in particular, pushes women towards these situations."




'

Men establish their power over women'




Kezban Doğan said that the conditions associated with being a migrant or refugee further aggravated women's problems. She stressed that, alongside racism and discrimination, patriarchal relations within Kurdish society also needed to be questioned.




Doğan said: "We also need to look at the position of men within Kurdish society. You are now a migrant, a refugee, and different conditions are imposed on you. You are not regarded as a human being. Racism is already rampant. Within all these circumstances, women find themselves trapped and once again subjected to extremely difficult conditions. Unfortunately, there is a truth expressed by Abdullah Öcalan: The Kurdish man is the slave of the state, while the Kurdish woman is the slave of the slave. Unfortunately, Kurdish men establish their own power over women. They express all the crises and problems they experience by subjecting women to violence, killing women and taking their lives. In doing so, they are actually destroying their own future. But are they aware of this? I do not think so. If they were aware, if such awareness had been developed, we would not be discussing these issues today."

author: Freedom Editor
title: Microscopic mutual aid
content:
From the deepest root to the highest leaf and every acorn, bacteria and fungi cooperate with each other and their host to survive

1.8 billion years ago the mitochondria, “the powerhouse of the cell,” moved within a host cell for protection. Neither side was exploited, and equilibrium was achieved. To this day, DNA is segregated between the mitochondria and the nucleus reminding us of cellular cooperation.

In her work, On the Origin of Mitosing Cells (1967), Lynn Margulis posited that structures such as the mitochondria originated from smaller specialised cells taking refuge within larger cells. 60 years after Kropotkin, Margulis’ Endosymbiotic Theory challenged the expectations of Darwinian evolution and was rejected by 15 journals. Endosymbiosis is now a respected cornerstone of evolutionary biology.

Our cells and ecosystems exemplify cooperation, not competition. Mutual aid is the biochemical basis of multicellular life meeting required energy demands; the mitochondria was a volunteer, but now it is part of the cooperative powerhouse of the cell(s).

I research microbiomes of terrestrial plants, using advanced molecular techniques to untangle form and function in microscopic communities.

Mutual aid has been the foundation of my research. From the deepest root to the highest leaf and every acorn, bacteria and fungi cooperate with each other and their host to survive, ward off disease, and improve overall wellbeing. If natural selection is the play, molecular mutual aid is the stage, the lights, the assistant, the director, and the crowd.

Microbiomes are complex systems that include beneficial, neutral or pathogenic individuals. As scientific knowledge expands, we are beginning to understand that the difference between a beneficial and detrimental microbe could be triggered by environmental stress. The shift is not governed by a central mechanism, but by a quorum of functionally cooperative bacteria following a unifying imperative: “common survival at all costs”.

Capitalism is fundamentally Darwinian: proliferate or perish, outcompete your rivals, grow exponentially. However, bacteria have shown us that natural selection is not exponential, and neither should be our methods of measuring economic progress.

The Escherichia coli (E. coli) Long-Term Evolution Experiment (LTEE) is the clearest demonstration of natural selection to date. Founded by Richard Lenski of Michigan State University in 1988, LTEE has observed the equivalent of more than 2,000,000 years of human evolution over 75,000 generations taking advantage of the rapid rate of replication in E. coli. Every day 1% fractions of the previous community are transferred into fresh medium; each day represents more than six generations.

Using molecular techniques, the group was able to track the rate of evolution within their E. coli lineages. They predicted that rate of evolution would be hyperbolic: a period of exponential development followed by a plateau, an upper ceiling. However, it was discovered that there is no upper ceiling. Exponential improvement in E. coli fitness is succeeded by incremental developments. Adaptations become exponentially rarer but never cease.

Put simply, evolutionary adaptations become less dramatic, the return on investment diminishes as the E. coli was already adapted to a cosy temperature of 37°C for the equivalent of 2,000,000 human years.

On our own, human scale, we have seen epochs of exponential growth, such as the industrial or agricultural revolutions, where outputs were tangible and material. Accelerationists wish you to believe that the incessant integration of the latest greatest technology – currently AI – will usher in a new revolution despite diminishing returns. But we are already at the point of diminishing returns. Why are data centres becoming larger instead of smaller and more efficient? Why is my chocolate bar shrinking? Culturally, how much did music change between 1960-90, compared to between 1990-2020?

I have seen in my own data that pathogenic fungi are often present and quantifiable up to 25% of community composition, but no signs of disease are present. Certainly, there are outright pathogens that cause disease. But if you placed them in a hermetically sealed box with their host, their long-term existence is not feasible. They infect, they multiply, the host dies, their population dies after consuming all the resources.

Exponential growth of a singular microbe is the hallmark of disease, and we understand that environmental stress exacerbates symptoms. Similarly, GDP is an exponential metric placed above ecosystems, climate, and quality of life. Quantifying the stressors that push GDP beyond capital accumulation may provide an opening for the preservation of natural systems.

It is now popular knowledge that eating a healthy diet contributes to a thriving and functional “gut microbiome” which directly assists digestion. But few people are aware of how they run on the principles of mutual aid on a cellular level.

Understanding these communities, which have persisted throughout evolution, could provide a mathematical basis for economic deceleration and degrowth.

This article was first published in the Autumn/Winter edition of Freedom anarchist journal

title: TBMM’de bu hafta: Bütçe görüşmelerinin komisyon aşaması sona eriyor
content:
TBMM’de bu hafta da yoğun. Plan ve Bütçe Komisyonu’nda pazartesi günü Enerji ve Tabii Kaynaklar Bakanlığı, salı günü Ulaştırma ve Altyapı Bakanlığı, çarşamba günü Tarım ve Orman Bakanlığı, perşembe günü Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakanlığı’nın bütçeleri görüşülecek. Cuma günü ise Cumhurbaşkanlığı bütçesinin yanı sıra 2027 Gelir Bütçesi, 2027 Yılı Merkezi Yönetim Bütçe Kanunu Teklifi ile 2025 Yılı Merkezi Yönetim Kesin Hesap Kanunu Teklifi’nin maddeleri oylanacak. Böylece, 27 Ekim’de başlayan bütçe görüşmeleri bir ayın ardından tamamlanmış olacak.




Bayındırlık, İmar, Ulaştırma ve Turizm Komisyonu’nda salı günü 7183 Sayılı Türkiye Turizm Tanıtım ve Geliştirme Ajansı Hakkında Kanun uyarınca Sayıştay Başkanlığınca düzenlenen 2025 Yılı raporunun sunulduğuna dair Sayıştay Tezkeresi ele alınacak.




Milli Savunma Komisyonu’nda çarşamba günü Çalışma ve Değerlendirme Toplantısı yapılacak.




Konaklama Platformları'na ilişkin yasa görüşülecek




Genel Kurul’da Yabancı Dijital Konaklama Platformları Kanun Teklifi’nin görüşmelerine başlanması bekleniyor.




Teklifle yabancı dijital konaklama platformlarının elektronik ortamda yurt içinde gerçekleştirdikleri faaliyetlerin hukuki zemine kavuşturulması amaçlanıyor. Bu kapsamda söz konusu platformların faaliyet alanlarının belirlenmesi, sektörde adil rekabet koşullarının tesis edilmesi, bu platformlara Bakanlık tarafından izin belgesi verilmesi, Türkiye’de temsilci bulundurma yükümlülüğü getirilmesi, yükümlülüklere aykırılık halinde uygulanacak idari yaptırımların düzenlenmesi, Türk hukukunun uygulanması ve Türk mahkemelerinin yetkili kılınması öngörülüyor.




Teklif, yabancı dijital konaklama platformlarına Kültür ve Turizm Bakanlığı’ndan izin belgesi alma zorunluluğu getiriyor. Türkiye’de tüketicilere hizmet sunan yabancı platformların faaliyetleri izin, kayıt ve denetim kapsamına alınacak. Teklifin yasalaşmasıyla Türkiye’den Booking’e erişim sağlanmaya başlanacak.




Dışişleri Komisyonu'nda gündem ABD ve İsrail ilişkileri




Dışişleri Komisyonu çarşamba günü toplanacak. Dışişleri Bakanlığı komisyon üyelerine “ABD ve İsrail'deki Seçim Sonuçlarının İkili İlişkilerimize ve Bölgesel Gelişmelere Etkisi” konulu bilgilendirme yapacak. Dışişleri Bakanlığı yetkilileri ayrıca “APEC Çerçevesinde Gerçekleştirilen Üçlü Zirvenin ve Zirvede Alınan Kararların Bölgesel ve Küresel Gelişmelere Etkisi” konulu sunum gerçekleştirecek.




Komisyon gündeminde ayrıca Türkiye Cumhuriyeti ile Büyük Britanya ve Kuzey İrlanda Birleşik Krallığı Arasında Serbest Ticaret Anlaşmasının Ticarette Teknik Engeller Faslında Değişiklik Yapılmasına İlişkin Olarak 7 Mayıs 2025 Tarihli Mektupların Teatisi Yoluyla İmzalanan Anlaşmanın Onaylanmasının Uygun Bulunduğuna Dair Kanun Teklifi, Türkiye Cumhuriyeti Hükümeti ile Asya Kalkınma Bankası Arasında Asya Kalkınma Bankasının Bölgesel Ofisinin Kurulmasına İlişkin Anlaşmayı Tadil Eden 1 Numaralı Protokolün Onaylanmasının Uygun Bulunduğuna Dair Kanun Teklifi, Türkiye Cumhuriyeti Hükümeti ile Asya Kalkınma Bankası Arasındaki Teknik Destek Çerçeve Anlaşmasının Onaylanmasının Uygun Bulunduğuna Dair Kanun Teklifi, Uluslararası Telekomünikasyon Birliği Kuruluş Yasası ve Sözleşmesinde Değişiklik Yapan Guadalajara Tam Yetkili Temsilciler Konferansı Sonuç Belgelerinin Onaylanmasının Uygun Bulunduğuna Dair Kanun Teklifi, Türkiye Cumhuriyeti Hükümeti ile Sırbistan Cumhuriyeti Hükümeti Arasında Askeri Çerçeve Anlaşmasının Onaylanmasının Uygun Bulunduğuna Dair Kanun Teklifi, Avrupa Haberleşme Ofisi (ECO) Kuruluş Sözleşmesinin Onaylanmasının Uygun Bulunduğuna Dair Kanun Teklifi, Türkiye Cumhuriyeti Hükümeti ile Çad Cumhuriyeti Hükümeti Arasında Askeri İş Birliği Çerçeve Anlaşmasının Notalarla Birlikte Onaylanmasının Uygun Bulunduğuna Dair Kanun Teklifi ile ilgili uygun bulma kanun teklifleri bulunuyor.




KİT Komisyonu’nda bu hafta Türkiye Taşkömürü Kurumu ile Müesseseleri, Türkiye Kömür İşletmeleri Kurumu Genel Müdürlüğü ve Türkiye Vakıflar Bankası TAO ve Bağlı Kuruluşları’nın hesapları incelenecek.




Siyasi partilerin grup toplantılarının salı ve çarşamba günleri yapılması planlanıyor.

title: İstanbul'da sıcaklık 11 derece birden düşecek: Sağanak ve lodos etkili olacak
content:
Fotoğraf: Misael Silvera/Unsplash

İstanbul'da yeni haftayla birlikte hava sıcaklıklarının düşmesi bekleniyor. Balkanlar üzerinden gelecek soğuk hava dalgası ve yağışlı sistemin etkisiyle kentte sıcaklık salı gününden itibaren 11 dereceye kadar azalacak.

Haftanın ilk günlerinde etkili olacak lodos fırtınasının ardından akşam saatlerinde sağanak yağış bekleniyor. Bugün ve yarın 17-20 derece arasında seyredecek sıcaklık, salı gününden itibaren 6-9 dereceye kadar düşecek.

İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyesi Afet İşleri ve Risk Yönetimi Dairesi Başkanlığı (AKOM), Orta Akdeniz üzerinden gelen alçak basınç sistemlerinin etkisini sürdürdüğü İstanbul'a Balkanlar üzerinden yeni bir serin ve yağışlı hava dalgasının geleceğini belirterek yurttaşları soğuk hava ve yağışa karşı uyardı.

İstanbul'da önümüzdeki günlerde beklenen hava durumu şöyle:

23 Kasım Pazartesi: Lodos fırtınası ve akşam saatlerinde yağmur bekleniyor. Sıcaklık 12-20 derece arasında olacak.

24 Kasım Salı: Parçalı bulutlu, sabah saatlerinde yağmurlu. Sıcaklık 6-9 dereceye düşecek.

25 Kasım Çarşamba: Parçalı ve az bulutlu. Sıcaklık 4-10 derece arasında seyredecek. Yağış beklenmiyor.

26 Kasım Perşembe: Parçalı bulutlu. Sıcaklık 4-12 derece olacak.

author: Unknown
title: Bir kişi tutuklandı: Gaziosmanpaşa'daki yangında 12 yaşındaki çocuk yaşamını yitirdi
content:
Fotoğraf: DHA / Kolaj: Evrensel

İstanbul Gaziosmanpaşa'ya bağlı Barbaros Hayrettinpaşa Mahallesi’nde 19 Kasım Perşembe günü saat 23.15 sıralarında 5 katlı binanın 1’inci katındaki dairede yangın çıktı. Kısa sürede binayı saran duman nedeniyle en üst kattaki dairede bulunan Ömer Ege Özyurt (12), D.Ö. (6) ve E.Ö. (13) ile birlikte toplam 6 kişi dumandan etkilendi.

İhbar üzerine olay yerine ilgili ekipler sevk edildi. Sağlık ekiplerinin ilk müdahalesinin ardından hastaneye kaldırılan yaralılardan 3'ü tedavilerinin ardından taburcu edilirken, çocuklardan D.Ö.’nün hayati tehlikesinin sürdüğü, E.Ö.’nün ise yoğun bakımdaki tedavisinin devam ettiği bildirildi.

Dumandan etkilenerek hastaneye kaldırılan 12 yaşındaki Ömer Ege Özyurt, hayatını kaybetti. Özyurt’un futbola Kemerburgaz Spor Kulübü’nde başladığı ve bu sezon Yıldırım Bosna Spor Kulübü’nde forma giydiği öğrenildi.

Yangının çıkış nedenine ilişkin başlatılan incelemede, alevlerin yükseldiği dairede oturan Günay F.’nin (50) ısıtıcıyı açık unutması sonucu yangının çıktığı tespit edildi. Gözaltına alınan Günay F., emniyetteki işlemlerinin ardından sevk edildiği adliyede "yangın" ve "taksirle öldürme" suçlamalarıyla çıkarıldığı mahkemece tutuklandı.

author: Danilo Arao
title: Pagbabalik-tanaw
content:
Kayang kaya dahil kakayanin. May tagumpay dahil babakahin.

Sa nalalapit na pagtatapos ng 2026, mainam na balikan ang kalendaryong hindi na mabasa sa sobrang daming nakasulat.

Mula Enero hanggang Nobyembre, punong-puno ang iskedyul ng mga responsibilidad na kahit paano’y hinarap naman. Kahit ang susunod na buwan ng Disyembre, may mangilan-ngilan ding nakasulat kahit nakatakda itong panahon ng limitado pahinga. Opo, kailangan nang umupo’t humiga nang medyo matagal ang nakatatanda!

Kababalik lang mula sa sabbatical noong 2025, muling nagturo sa Unibersidad ng Pilipinas (UP) Diliman ngayong taon. Mas mataas na ang kumpiyansa sa gawaing pang-akademiko sa dalawang dahilan.

Una, natapos na ang doktoral na pag-aaral sa Alemanya noong 2024. Ikalawa, tumaas na ang posisyon at naging ganap na propesor (full professor) noong 2025, matapos ang 11 taon bilang kawaksing propesor (associate professor) at 11 pang taon bilang katuwang na propesor (assistant professor).

Sa wakas, nakamit din ang pang-akademikong “tagumpay” dahil sa tatlong letrang P, H at D na puwede nang ilagay sa dulo ng pangalan (at siyempre’y puwede na ring gamitin ang salitang “Doktor” kahit na hindi naman nagrereseta!).

Nagresulta ang bagong titulo’t ranggo sa mga bagong oportunidad. Matapos na maging ganap na kasapi (regular member) ng National Research Council of the Philippines (NRCP) noong Marso 2026, nakuha ang prestihiyosong NRCP Gabay Award para sa pananaliksik na may malaking pakinabang sa paghuhubog ng polisiya ng gobyerno.

Sa partikular, ito ay pagkilala sa ginawa ng Kontra Daya sa pagbubuo ng data set ng mga grupong partylist na tumakbo sa halalan noong 2025. Kahit na bagong miyembro pa lang, sinubukang magsumite ng dokumentasyon, lalo na ang paggamit ng iba’t ibang sangay ng gobyerno sa ginawang pananaliksik ng Kontra Daya, at pinalad namang kilalanin ng mga eksperto’t hurado ang kolektibong pinaghirapan ng grupo.

Sa mismong unibersidad, may ilang awards at grants na inaplayan at pinalad ring maaprubahan lahat. Sadyang nakakagulat ang 100% na approval rate pero nangyari talaga ito. Nagkaroon tuloy ng limitadong pondo para sa patuloy na pagtuturo, pananaliksik at gawaing ekstensiyon. Sa kabila ng patuloy na pagtaas ng presyo ng mga bilihin, nakayang bilhin ang mga kinakailangang gamit ngayong taon.

Dahil dito, mas maganda na ang kinakalabasan ng mga online na interbyu, pati na rin ang mga online na lektyur at talumpati sa loob at labas ng bansa. Pabirong hirit ng ilang kaibigan, kasama yata sa gastusin ang pagpaparetoke. Hindi po. Ilaw at kamera lang ang katapat ng bagong hilamos na mukha. (Huwag nang pag-usapan ang ilan pang bagong biniling gamit, salamat sa awards at grants.)

Sa taong ito, lumabas din ang tatlong librong inedit para sa isang dayuhang pabliser. Medyo mahal ito kung ibebenta sa mga kakilala sa Pilipinas kaya ginamit na lang ang bahagi ng pondo ng awards at grants para bilhin ang ilang kopya nito at ipamigay sa silid-aklatan ng mga piling unibersidad.

Kaya ngayon, libre itong mababasa ng maraming estudyanteng may panahong magpunta sa silid-aklatan. Nakakaintindi naman sila ng wikang Ingles kaya hindi malaking problema ang pagbabasa.

Pero kung nais ng nakasulat sa wikang Filipino, tinatayang lalabas sa Disyembre (sana lang!) ang ikapitong libro ng mga sanaysay. Matapos ang medyo mahabang panahon ng malalimang ebalwasyon at teknikal na pinalisasyon, mahahawakan na sa kamay ang ilang taong pinaghirapang buuin.

Kumpara sa mga naunang anim na libro, espesyal ang paparating na libro dahil tumulong ang mismong anak sa lettering ng pabalat ng libro. Siya rin ang gumawa ng ilustrasyon ng mga kabanata.

Sa madaling salita, awtor ang ama samantalang ilustrador ang anak. Siyempre’y may susing papel din ang asawang tinulungan ang anak sa gawain, bukod pa sa maraming suhestiyong parating sinusunod ng asawa sa usaping libro at buhay (o pabirong sabi sa wikang Ingles, “Yesband”).

Malapit nang matapos ang taong 2026. Nababawasan na ang mga nakasulat sa kalendaryo. Panahon nang maghabol para matapos ang kailangang matapos. Inaasahan ang limitadong pahinga sa mga natitira pang araw.

Kayang-kaya dahil kakayanin. May tagumpay dahil babakahin.

Para makipag-ugnayan sa awtor, pumunta sa https://risingsun.dannyarao.com

author: Natália Perez
title: ‘Conforme ganhamos mais espaço, vamos ter mais visibilidade’, diz a escritora Lilia Guerra
content:
A edição de 2026 do Prêmio Jabuti, o mais tradicional prêmio literário do Brasil, registrou um marco histórico: pela primeira vez, uma escritora negra, Eliana Alves Cruz, venceu na categoria Romance Literário. 

O prêmio ampliou o debate sobre o reconhecimento da produção de pessoas negras na literatura brasileira.




Para conversar sobre as transformações do mercado editorial e compartilhar seu processo de escrita, o Pauta Pública recebe Lilia Guerra, romancista, contista e cronista, que acaba de lançar seu nono livro, Velha Guarda, pela editora Todavia. Ao longo da conversa com Andrea Dip, Lilia destaca a importância dessas conquistas.




“Conforme a gente ganha espaço, a tendência é que nós vamos ter mais visibilidade […] porque a nossa literatura ficava muito confinada aos nossos lugares, aos lugares que a gente frequentava. Não porque nós não estivéssemos escrevendo ou produzindo arte, mas agora a distribuição tem sido mais ampla”.




Leia os principais pontos da conversa e ouça o podcast completo abaixo.























































EP 243


											As histórias que sempre estiveram por aqui – com Lilia Guerra							













20 de novembro de 2026


					·
				


				Escritora fala sobre livro que retrata o êxodo de famílias negras do centro à periferia de São Paulo





























































0:00




-:–



















15




15
































































Veja mais episódios desta série










Lilia, como começou o seu envolvimento com a literatura? Como a literatura entrou na sua vida e, quando você decidiu o tipo de história que gostaria de contar?




A literatura entrou na minha vida muito cedo como leitora, assim que eu comecei a ter contato com o processo de alfabetização. Eu venho de uma família administrada por mulheres, mulheres negras, por trabalhadoras domésticas de pouco estudo. A minha avó não era alfabetizada; era com ela que eu ficava, enquanto minha mãe trabalhava. Eu acompanhava minha avó nas casas onde ela prestava serviços, mas eu morava perto de uma biblioteca.




Eu sou paulistana, nasci em São Paulo e sempre morei aqui, morava em uma região central da cidade. Sobretudo agora, depois de 40 anos morando no extremo da cidade, eu posso dizer que era uma região central. Eu tive a sorte de ter uma biblioteca praticamente no quintal da minha casa, e a minha mãe se apropriou desse espaço público e me apresentou esse equipamento que é a biblioteca de rua, de porta aberta. 




Eu sempre digo que a minha mãe viu na biblioteca um lugar onde não precisava pagar ingresso para entrar. Não precisava se preparar; como assistir a um filme no cinema, não precisava se organizar: comprar entrada, pensar que dia ir, torcer para que o filme não saia de cartaz antes. Já a biblioteca estava sempre lá para mim e não só como um lugar onde eu ia para ler; tinha dias que eu ia para a biblioteca para ficar de papo para o ar ou para ficar deitada na sala de almofadas olhando para cima. Isso também era bom para mim, ter a biblioteca como esse lugar acolhedor onde eu ia, porque ali era o meu mundo.




Sempre tive contato com a leitura; os livros eram mais ou menos meus brinquedos. Para mim, tornou-se um passatempo, de fato, ir até a biblioteca e, assim, o meu processo de leitora foi mudando com o tempo, mas escrever mesmo, eu nunca pensei em escrever.

 Ultimamente tenho recebido muito as perguntas: “Quando você começou a pensar em escrever?” e “Você já tinha pensado em ser escritora?”. Eu venho refletindo sobre isso e entendo que sempre gostei muito de escrever, mas eu nunca pensei em ser uma escritora – até porque, quando eu era criança, eu convivia muito com as trabalhadoras domésticas e já conseguia vislumbrar minha carreira como uma delas. Eu pensava que também seria uma trabalhadora doméstica quando mais velha. 




Nunca pensei em escrever, mais tarde, na adolescência, quando eu comecei a pensar em me profissionalizar, em escolher um curso – hoje, sou técnica em enfermagem –, continuei tendo os livros como amigos e companheiros, mas só pensei em escrever quando entrei em contato com informações que a minha família não tinha sobre nós, sobre a nossa origem. 




A questão da ausência paterna é algo que sempre me pegou muito, porque eu sou uma pessoa que não tem o nome do pai no documento. Quando comecei a pesquisar sobre essas informações, essas lacunas, esses vazios na história da minha família, eu, fatalmente comecei a fazer anotações e a entrevistar pessoas organicamente. Logo entendi que, para saber dessa história, não podia falar só com o pessoal de minha casa. Comecei a falar com outras pessoas também e fazer anotações. Sobretudo com a minha mãe e essas conversas me fizeram entender que seria muito importante para ela que essas histórias fossem publicizadas. Então, eu comecei a planejar escrever, mas a minha ideia era escrever só um livro, com as histórias que pesquisei, com as respostas que obtive, mas não deu. Já estou no nono livro: Velha Guarda.




Está aqui comigo, do meu lado, porque ele é recém-nascido, chegou em casa há pouco tempo. 

Velha Guarda fala sobre o êxodo, justamente das pessoas que moravam nas regiões mais centrais da cidade de São Paulo e tiveram que se mudar por conta da questão do aluguel. Fala sobre moradia popular e esse êxodo, que começa em 1976, no final da década de 80, e vai até meados de 90.




Nele acompanhamos a turma que mora na Vila 23, inicialmente, no bairro de Sesmaria, e que chega até o conjunto habitacional Cordilheiras. Acompanhamos tudo que aconteceu nesse movimento, todas as mudanças, as transições na vida das personagens e – não diferente dos outros livros –, aqui o ambiente e os lugares também são personagens e narradores dessa história, que, embora tenha São Paulo como cenário, as ruas e os bairros são lugares fictícios. 



















“Velha Guarda”, novo romance de Lilia Guerra







Os seus livros têm uma característica marcante de serem povoados por múltiplas vozes, muitos personagens, alguns até aparecem em mais de um livro. Como é a escolha de retratar essa coletividade?




Eu gosto muito de gente, gosto muito de nome. Nisso, volto ao convívio com as trabalhadoras domésticas que não tinham seus nomes. Os nomes não eram importantes nos lugares onde elas circulavam. Eu me lembro de mais de um caso em que, às vezes, os nomes eram trocados aleatoriamente: a pessoa chamava Ana – como é o caso da minha mãe – e no trabalho era chamada sempre de Maria. Algo para deixar muito bem marcado que o nome delas não importava, a história delas não importava.




Então, eu fiquei com essa coisa de me importar sempre muito com os nomes. Quando eu frequentei algumas oficinas de criação literária, nas aulas, me lembro de ter esses toques sobre essa multidão que aparece nas histórias, sobre fazer um corte: “É muita gente, são muitos personagens”, orientações sobre uma possível dificuldade dos leitores para identificar as pessoas, mas foi um tipo de lição e de conselho que eu não consegui seguir.




Eu digo que comparo um livro com um ônibus e, para mim, um ônibus vazio não faz sentido, então o livro também não. Também ficava sempre naquela “E se for o meu último livro? Se eu não escrever outro, por que eu vou deixar o pessoal de fora? Não, vamos parar em todos os pontos e todo mundo vai embarcar, quem puder vai se ajeitando aí”, eu sempre fazia essa comparação, começou assim.




Eu gosto mesmo de ver o livro muito bem povoado. Acho que, como moro em um conjunto habitacional, é muita gente transitando; utilizo o transporte público quase integralmente, é o que mais utilizo, também está sempre cheio, e trabalho em serviço público, também multidão.

 Então, eu tenho o hábito de estar sempre cercada de muita gente e acho que isso se reflete nos livros também. Às vezes faço planos de dar uma economizada, mas, quando vejo já entrou mais gente e, aí vamos dar conta de todo mundo.




A literatura tem uma outra maneira de tratar os assuntos, então, para escritores no Pauta, sempre perguntamos: você acha que a literatura é o lugar também de furar bolhas, por não chegar com um discurso que é estritamente militante ou que de cara não pareça político? As respostas variam desde “Se isso acontecer, ótimo, mas não é o meu primeiro objetivo”, até “Sim, fazemos para isso”. O que você acha?




Eu já vivi, vivo e quero continuar vivendo momentos diferentes, e ter muita liberdade para escrever. Gosto de dizer que tem dias que eu quero realmente escrever sobre uma pauta, sobre um assunto, e tem dias que eu quero escrever sobre qualquer coisa, sobre um guarda-chuva, sobre um copo. Acho que vivemos esses momentos diferentes e isso tem que ser igualitário, porque outros autores – como uma grande leitora de crônicas, e como os assuntos nas crônicas –, são muito diversos.




Acredito que essa liberdade temos que ter. 

Se eu quero falar sobre alguma coisa que pode até soar panfletária para alguém, tudo bem, mas eu quero ter liberdade para fabular e trazer personagens que vivem histórias diversas. Este é o grande desafio. 

Por exemplo, cada vez que escrevo um livro novo, não sei o que esperar. Talvez o leitor ou a crítica espere que usemos o mesmo ambiente. Eu gosto muito de ambientar as personagens das histórias que eu escrevo em locais periféricos, mas isso nem sempre acontece. 




Às vezes eu escrevo uma crônica e penso em experimentar essa história na vivência de um personagem. Tem assuntos que eu abordo, que eu fiz com a crônica e também com o conto e com o romance; por exemplo, são sempre experiências. Assim como diz a dona Conceição Evaristo, às vezes escrevemos por vingança, mas às vezes por amor, por indignidade, mas às vezes também só porque quer se divertir, porque eu acho que escrever tem que ser divertido também para nós, que escrevemos, e ainda bem, isso acontece comigo. Então, varia, como disse, são momentos. Em que momento eu estou? E hoje e amanhã vou estar em um momento diferente; dependendo, posso enveredar por caminhos distintos.

Recentemente, a escritora Eliana Alves Cruz recebeu o prêmio Jabuti de melhor romance com o seu livro “Meridiana”. Quanto você acha que a gente avançou em termos de mais presença de pessoas negras produzindo literatura no Brasil e sendo reconhecidas e o quanto ainda temos que percorrer?




Se parece muito com a questão das cotas. Enquanto a gente não estiver ocupando esses espaços, fatalmente nós vamos concorrer menos, ganhar menos prêmios e ser menos lidos. Então a tendência é que isso aumente conforme a gente escreve e vai publicando.

 Conforme a gente ganha espaço, a tendência é que nós vamos ter mais visibilidade. Obviamente, acho que realmente era difícil para que escritores negros estivessem nesses lugares, porque a nossa literatura ficava muito confinada aos nossos lugares, aos lugares que a gente frequentava. Não porque nós não estivéssemos escrevendo ou produzindo arte, mas agora a distribuição tem sido mais ampla e com toda a questão da internet, em que a gente consegue se comunicar melhor. 




Não vai ser uma surpresa que esses números [de negras sendo premiadas] e que essas notícias sejam cada vez mais divulgadas nessas premiações. Parabéns para a Eliana e parabéns, viva a Meridiana!

title: Groupe de parole & d'organisation anarchiste contre l'inceste
content:
Groupe de parole & d'organisation anarchiste contre l'inceste




 

 

 

 




On vous invite chaleureusement à notre prochain groupe de parole et d'organisation anarchiste contre l'inceste, qui se tiendra le vendredi 27 novembre à partir de 18h30 au 

CICP

, 21 rue Voltaire, 75011, Paris (salle verte, 1

er

 étage).




 




Puisque l'inceste nous concerne tous.tes, mais aussi parce que s'y reconnaître n'est pas toujours chose facile, l'espace est ouvert à tous.tes. On pourra se scinder en deux si besoin : un groupe de parole + un groupe d'organisation.




L'idée du groupe de parole




Elle part de nos besoins : celui de casser les silences qui nous détruisent, en parlant collectivement d'inceste. Mais aussi celui de se reconnaître pour s'entraider face à la famille, au trauma, aux institutions, face aussi à la vie qui ne nous épargne pas, voire face à nous-même et à la reproduction des violences que nous avons subies.




L'idée du groupe d'organisation







Elle part de notre envie de diffuser une culture de lutte contre l'inceste, d'organiser des événements publics, de faire de l'agitation autour du sujet, des tags, d'écrire ou de dessiner ensemble pour faire des tracts, des revues, des livres ou des podcasts, ou toute autre chose qui nous paraîtra nécessaire et nous fera envie

 

!




Pourquoi un groupe anarchiste contre l'inceste

 

?







Il existe de nombreux groupes de parole et d'organisation contre l'inceste qui basculent souvent dans le développement personnel ou dans l'organisation autour de leaders ou de figures individuelles (pour ne citer que ces deux exemples). On a envie de pouvoir attaquer la famille, l'État, la police et la justice et on a envie de faire les choses par nous-mêmes. Politiser l'inceste nous paraît être une donnée essentielle de notre démarche puisque le système-inceste se fonde sur l'autorité familiale, la domination adulte et/ou patriarcale. On avait envie de pouvoir tisser des discussions qui nous ressemblent et de développer ensemble une analyse politique à la fois pragmatique et radicale contre l'inceste.




Amène de la nourriture à partager si tu peux

 

!


Hâte de vous y voir

 

!




Des incesté.es révolté.es
