title: Ozgur Ozel: "Em di Komîsyona Çavdêriyê de cih nagirin"
content:
Serokê Parlamentoyê Numan Kurtulmuş di çarçoveya hevdîtinên ji bo avakirina Komîsyona Çavdêriyê de,  li Enqereyê çû serdana Serokê Giştî yê Partiya NÛ Ozgur Ozel.




Ozgur Ozel piştî hevdîtina bi Kurtulmuş re daxuyaniyeke çapemeniyê da û helwesta partiya xwe ya li ser Komîsyona Çavdêriyê eşkere kir.




Ozgur Ozel destnîşan kir ku desthilat di warê demokratîkbûnê de gavên pêwîst navêje û xala 7emîn a rapora Komîteya Parlamentoyê ya ji bo demokratîkbûnê nayê bicihanîn.




Sedemê redkirinê




Ozel ragihand ku sîstema qeyûman berdewam dike, qeyûm li ser 3 kanalên televîzyonê hatine danîn û biryarên Dadgeha Destûra Bingehîn û Dadgeha Mafên Mirovan a Ewropayê nayên bicihanîn.




Ozel ev yek wekî sedemên cihnegirtina partiya xwe ya di nav Komîsyona Çavdêriyê de destnîşan kir.




Ozgur Ozel da zanîn ku Partiya NÛ dê ji ber van sedeman endaman nede Komîsyona Çavdêriyê ya ku biryar e li Parlamentoyê were damezirandin.




Serokê Giştî yê Partiya NÛ rexne li helwesta hikûmetê girt û diyar kir ku desthilat tenê jibo parastina pêgeha xwe gavên siyasî diavêje û got:







"Tekane tiştê ku di berjewendiya vî welatî de ye, rawestandina vê desthilatê ye. Hinekan tenê ji bo ku desthilata xwe bidomînin her tişt kir. Bila kes li ser pişta me hesaban neke"




Ji bo qonaxên piştî vê yên pêvajoyê, bila kes me tevlî hesabên xwe yên şexsî neke û liser pişta me hesaban daneyne. Ji niha û pê ve bila kes bi hizirkirina li ser me hesaban neke. Bila li gorî hebûn an nebûna me hesabên xwe bikin. Kes nikare kesî bixapîne. Dema hûn li wan deriyan dixin, hûn dê wan sozên ku we berê dabûn bînin bîra xwe. Ez dibêjim em di nava vî karî de nînin."







Serokê Parlamentoya Tirkiyeyê Numan Kurtulmuş di çarçoveya hewldanêndamezirandina Desteya Çavdêriyê de bi serok û nûnerên partiyên AK Partî, MHP, DEMPartî û Rêya Nû re jî hevdîtin kiribû.




Ev deste li gorî Yasaya Çarçoveyê ya Tebaxa 2026an li Parlamentoya Tirkiyeyê têavakirin û ji bo şopandina gavên pêvajoya aştiyê û bêçekbûnê hatiye plankirin lê belêredkirina Partiya NÛ dê bandorê li ser hevsengiya nûnertiya partiyan a di nava desteyêde bike.




"Em di nava vî karî de nînin"




Serokê Partiya NÛ Ozgur Ozel di berdewamiya axaftina xwe de got:







"Ji niha û pê ve eger hûn li cihekî deriyê Partiya NÛ bixin, dema hûn tên li wî derî dixin,hûn dê wan sozên ku we berê dabûn bi cih bînin; ne sozên ku we dane Partiya NÛ lê ez behsa wan sozan dikim ku we li ber komîteyê di girtenameyan de xistine bin îmzeyan. Ez ji wan kesên ku gotin 'em dê di demokratîkbûnê de her tim bi hev re bin' û pişt reparçe dikin re dibêjim. Ez ji wan kesên ku teslîmî burokratên Koşkê bûne re dibêjim. Ez ji wan kesên ku bi zext û zordariyê hewl didin tiştekî bikin re dibêjim, em di nava vîkarî de nînin. 




Ew kesên ku dixwazin em di nava van karan de bin, divê pêşî wan sozên ku di dîrokê dedane vî welatî bi cih bînin. Rapor li wir e, komîte li wir e. Ji niha û pê ve ew kesên ku bi serê xwe lîstikademokrasiyê dilîzin, bila kerem bikin bilîzin. Li wir we partiyeke mixalefetê ya 'meqbûl' jî dît; mixalefeta majesteyan!




Heta ji we tê bi kar bînin. Mixalefeteke ku hatiye hilbijartin, di hilbijartinan de bi serketiye, li kolanan bi deh hezaran kes li pey dimeşin û bi milyonan mirovan li meydanankom dike, dê rewabûnê nede wî zemînê ku hûn lê ne. Bi mixalefeta majesteyan re hûn dikarin li ser kîjan rêyê bixwazin bimeşin."







(AEK/AY)

author: EDRi
title: One year later, a broad coalition tells EU lawmakers: do not simplify away people’s rights with the Digital Omnibus
content:
On 19 November 2025, the European Commission presented the Digital Omnibus as an exercise in simplification. One year later, 100 organisations and individuals from across civil society are warning that simplification is turning into deregulation, with consequences far beyond the usual digital-rights debate.

A new open letter calls on EU lawmakers to protect data protection, privacy and other fundamental rights, rather than weakening them in the name of empty promises of competitiveness and the AI hype.

There are plenty of things about EU digital regulation that could genuinely be simpler: people should not have to fight through endless cookie banners, regulators should cooperate better, businesses should not operate in good faith knowing other companies won’t be held accountable when disrespecting the law…

But cutting red tape and cutting rights are not the same thing. The Digital Omnibus proposed, amongst other, significant changes to the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and ePrivacy framework. These affect when information about us is protected, how companies may reuse personal data for AI, safeguards around automated decision-making, access and transparency rights, and protection against unwanted access to our devices.

All of this is happening in a much wider political context. Across different EU policy areas, protections for people, workers, consumers and the environment are increasingly being reopened and deregulated under the language of ‘simplification’ and competitiveness.

One of the clearest examples is AI. Companies developing AI systems want enormous amounts of data. The Digital Omnibus on Data would create a specific route under the GDPR for AI development, training and operation to rely on the so-called legitimate interest legal basis. The existing legal tests would not disappear, but the risk is that large-scale reuse of personal data for AI becomes increasingly normalised, while people are left to find out what happened to their data and try to object afterwards.

This is particularly concerning in a market already dominated by big tech companies with huge advantages in data, infrastructure and capital, which can undermine companies that have invested in more privacy-protective and rights-respecting products and want clear rules and a genuine level playing field.

AI is only one piece of the proposal. Other changes touch sensitive and biometric data, automated decisions, transparency and access rights, and the confidentiality of our devices and communications.

These changes matter differently to different communities. They matter to workers subject to automated management and surveillance, worried about losing their jobs or their tasks becoming even more alienating; patients whose sensitive information needs strong protection; people facing discrimination who rely on transparency and access rights to challenge unfair systems; journalists and human rights defenders who depend on confidential communications; children and young people exposed to commercial tracking; and consumers confronted with companies holding vastly more information and power than they do.

That is why this cannot be treated as a niche dispute, even less when we remember the GDPR is the cornerstone of the EU’s digital rulebook.

To mark the first, and hopefully last, anniversary of the proposal, 100 organisations, academics, researchers, individuals and responsible businesses are coming together around a simple message: the EU can simplify its rules without simplifying away people’s rights.

The open letter calls on the European Parliament and Member States to reject provisions that weaken rights and substantive protections, and to ensure that any evidence-backed genuine problems in the GDPR, ePrivacy or other legislation are addressed through proper democratic processes, backed by evidence, consultation and scrutiny.

Fundamental rights are not red tape, and if we are speaking about simplification, the question should rather be ‘simplification for whom?’

author: CNT Santander
title: 20N: Manifestación Antifascista
content:
Este viernes 20, a las 19:30h en la Plaza Porticada en Santander, tenemos una cita muy importante en las calles con diferentes colectivos, sindicatos, partidos y asociaciones, para dejar claro que no queremos fascistas en nuestros barrios.




Para gritar alto: 

¡Ni juventud para el odio, ni futuro para el fascismo!




Nos hacemos eco del Manifiesto de la Asamblea Antifascista, creado por diferentes colectivos, con un mismo sentir y objetivo común: derrotar al fascismo.




«Europa arde. Es el momento para que el estado español lo haga también. El hartazgo de la clase trabajadora, la población estudiantil, las personas pensionistas, las mujeres, las personas racializadas y las disidencias, se ha pronunciado bien alto en todas las plazas del país, han dicho: ¡basta ya! a este sistema que cada día nos subyuga más.




Nunca hemos creído en su modelo capitalista neoliberal de consumismo desenfrenado impuesto por las élites y los grandes empresarios, ni en su individualismo y competitividad constante para que nos enfrentemos entre nosotras, que nos desgasta, desangra y nos conduce a una vida de miseria y precariedad laboral.




En su delirio por seguir aumentando sus crasas ganancias nos arrastran a una vida de explotación donde el esfuerzo diario nos lleva a vender nuestro trabajo por salarios que ya no dan ni para la básica subsistencia, donde apenas nos queda tiempo libre para vivir y respirar.

Los sueldos no llegan ni para tener un hogar digno porque se lo venden a fondos buitre que nos expulsan de nuestros barrios, están desmantelando todos nuestros servicios públicos y juegan con nuestro dinero destinándolo a seguir financiando las guerras salvajes basadas en el imperialismo, el colonialismo y los genocidios más atroces.




Nos están robando, cada día un poco más, todos los derechos laborales, económicos y culturales, que fueron adquiridos a través de décadas de dura y sangrienta lucha obrera.




El sacrificio de nuestras antepasadas debe servir para prender la mecha de este inconformismo que nos hierve en la sangre y de una valentía sin cadenas que nos aten, porque la batalla será ardua. Nos encontramos en un punto de 

«no retorno»

 con el auge del fascismo y la fuerza represiva desbordada de los perros del estado.




Porque como decía Olmo en ‘Novecento’: 

«Los fascistas no son como los hongos, que nacen así en una noche, no. Han sido los patronos los que han plantado los fascistas, los han querido, les han pagado. Y con los fascistas, los patronos han ganado cada vez más, hasta no saber dónde meter el dinero. Y así inventaron la guerra… Pero siempre pagamos nosotros. ¿Quién paga? El proletariado, los campesinos, los obreros, los pobres»

.




La clase trabajadora ya no enviará a sus hijas e hijos a ninguna guerra.




La libertad nunca fue fácil de conquistar, ahora somos más fuertes, más inteligentes y conocemos cómo acaba la historia si no les hacemos frente estando unidas.




Debemos plantar cara, sin miedo, aunque su fuerza represiva actúe con una violencia descarnada y sin escrúpulos, sobre la clase trabajadora y todas aquellas personas que deciden alzar la voz para pelear por su derecho a una vida digna. En Cantabria, sabemos muy bien lo que sucede cuando esa fuerza se desborda, en nuestra memoria siempre estará Gonzalo Ruiz, obrero campurriano asesinado en Reinosa por la Guardia Civil en la primavera del 87.




Debemos enfrentarnos a ellos, destruir el beneplácito con el que se postran ante el avance de la extrema derecha y el fascismo, permitiendo las expresiones de odio y la violencia contra aquellas personas que piensan diferente, que viven y sienten alejados de la hegemonía heterobásica y tradicional instaurada en su sistema.




Porque siempre vivimos en los márgenes de su mal llamada 

«democracia»

, en un estado que olvida la historia acontecida y que no permite desenterrar la memoria histórica, que no frena la apología de un fascismo, ahora heredado, que llenó todo el territorio español de huesos en las cunetas.




Es hora de avanzar hacia el centro, de tomar las calles, de arder en rabia controlada y lucha colectiva para destruir todos sus pilares, porque como dijo Durruti: 

«Al fascismo no se le combate, se le destruye»

, y el fascismo no es más que una de las fuerzas empleadas por el sistema capitalista para dividir a la población, para mostrar su racismo y su odio, para convertir en culpables de las crisis económicas a las personas migrantes, a las feministas, a las personas del colectivo LGTBIQ+ y aquellas más vulnerables, e intentar ponernos en contra de quienes son iguales a nosotras. Porque todas somos la misma clase trabajadora. ¡Y no podemos olvidarlo!




Por ello, 

reivindicamos la memoria de quienes lucharon antes que nosotras

: obreros/as, estudiantes, el campesinado y todas las personas anónimas que se negaron a aceptar que unos pocos decidieran el destino de la mayoría, y que se dejaron la vida.




Porque todavía creemos en la 

solidaridad

, en la 

fraternidad

 entre los pueblos y la dignidad, 

sin fronteras ni jerarquías

. Porque en nuestro mundo cabemos todas. Por ello, no daremos ni un solo paso atrás, defenderemos nuestro ideal antifascista sabiendo que lo que nos une es más importante que cualquier línea divisoria.




Hoy, cuando resurgen viejos fantasmas bajo nuevos símbolos y el nacionalismo autoritario pretende convertir la frustración social en odio, necesitamos más conciencia crítica, más organización desde abajo, siempre contra los de arriba, y más solidaridad entre los pueblos del mundo. No para construir nuevos amos ni para sustituir una autoridad por otra, sino para abrir espacios donde las personas puedan decidir colectivamente sobre sus vidas, su trabajo y su futuro.




Porque el viejo sueño de un mundo nuevo sigue más latente que nunca.




Nuestra respuesta no puede ser el miedo ni el silencio indiferente. Debe ser el apoyo mutuo, la defensa de los derechos conquistados, la denuncia de los abusos y la construcción de una sociedad en la que nadie tenga que agachar la cabeza para sobrevivir. Una sociedad sin explotación, sin persecución política ni social, sin cantantes presos por ejercer su derecho de libre expresión, y sin personas condenadas a la miseria para sostener los privilegios de otras.




Porque no hay libertad sin justicia social ni solidaridad, y no hay emancipación mientras unas pocas conserven el poder de decidir por todas o tengan privilegios sobre las demás.




Que no nos dividan las siglas, ni las viejas disputas. Que la memoria antifascista no sea un mero recuerdo vacío de la lucha de nuestras antepasadas, sino una 

responsabilidad presente

, un compromiso cotidiano. Y que, frente a toda forma de autoritarismo y fuerza represiva, mantengamos viva la convicción de que 

otro mundo es posible

, pero ha de ser una tarea colectiva y urgente. 

Ni sumisión ante el poder, ni odio entre los pueblos

. Dignidad, conciencia de clase, libertad y apoyo mutuo. La historia no está escrita de antemano; la escribimos quienes nos negamos a obedecer ante las injusticias.




Las personas convocantes de esta manifestación antifascista del 20N denunciamos el incremento de las agresiones fascistas y represivas en las calles y del discurso ultraderechista en las instituciones y en los medios de comunicación, a la par que crece la pobreza entre la clase obrera. Y llamamos a la organización colectiva, las de abajo siempre contra las de arriba.




Como dijo Bertolt Brecht… 

«Estar contra el fascismo sin estar contra el capitalismo, rebelarse contra la barbarie que nace de la barbarie, equivale a reclamar una parte del ternero y oponerse a sacrificarlo»

. Por eso, es fundamental luchar contra el capitalismo que genera las condiciones para el surgimiento del fascismo y que lo alimenta cuando le es necesario.




¡Viva la lucha de la clase obrera!




¡Viva la lucha internacionalista de los pueblos!




¡Viva la lucha antifascista!







La entrada 

20N: Manifestación Antifascista

 se publicó primero en 

CNT Santander

.

 se publicó primero en

author: Brett Wilkins
title: Israel extends imprisonment of Gaza doctor Hussam Abu Safiya for 6 more months
content:
Israeli authorities on November 18 extended the detention without charge of Dr Hussam Abu Safiya, the former director of northern Gaza’s Kamal Adwan Hospital, for another six months, prompting outrage from human rights defenders and renewed calls for the release of the pediatrician and scores of other imprisoned Palestinian medical professionals.

According to Abu Safiya’s lawyer, Nasser Odeh, an Israeli court in Beersheba extended the 53-year-old’s indefinite imprisonment through May 2027.

“Why must I spend another six months away from my family?” Dr Abu Safiya reportedly asked the court, claiming he is being punished for doing his job.

According to Al Jazeera, the court justified the continued detention by declaring that Abu Safiya “poses a threat to the state of Israel.”

Israel claims Abu Safiya is a colonel in Hamas’ Military Medical Services and has shown a photo of the doctor wearing a uniform that Al Jazeera said belongs to the Palestinian Directorate of General Military Medical Services, an organization providing healthcare to Gaza security personnel and civilians. The Qatar-based news network said that wearing the agency’s uniform does not establish Hamas membership.

There is also a dispute over the word “colonel”. Critics of Israel’s allegation say this is a professional or honorary designation within the medical services, not proof of a Hamas military command position, much like the United States surgeon-general is not an actual general.

The court’s decision came despite mounting international concern over Abu Safiya’s health and treatment in Israeli custody.

“The information that we are receiving about the health conditions of my father and how he’s being treated is very concerning,” Elias Abu Safiya, the imprisoned doctor’s son, told Al Jazeera on November 12. “My father weighs only 53 kilograms now, and he’s been suffering from very harsh conditions, three floors underground. He is in a solitary room, deprived of food, water, and medicine.”

Elias Abu Safiya continued: “We know he’s been subject to torture and bad treatment. My father still has some shrapnel stuck in his body, and he’s not seen a surgeon. This is inhumane, very harsh conditions that not even animals should be living in inside Israeli prisons. To add to this, he’s not been charged with anything. I don’t know why he’s being tortured this way. He’s a doctor, not a criminal or a murderer. He doesn’t deserve to be treated this way. The court denied the appeal to release him and 14 other doctors.”

Last week, Israel’s Supreme Court rejected a petition seeking the release of Abu Safiya and those 14 doctors, who are also imprisoned without charge or trial.

In July, the United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights urged Israel to release the doctor immediately, or charge him and hold a fair trial. OHCHR said there were indications that Abu Safiya had been tortured and subjected to other abuse, including prolonged solitary confinement, repeated severe assaults resulting in serious injuries, and denial of medical care.

Abu Safiya’s 15-year-old son, Ibrahim Abu Safiya, was killed in an Israeli drone strike at the entrance to Kamal Adwan Hospital, where he was sheltering with his family, in October 2024. The following month, Abu Safiya suffered severe shrapnel wounds during yet another Israeli drone strike on the facility.

Israeli troops detained Abu Safiya on December 28, 2024 amid a prolonged siege and assault of the hospital after the director defied a forced displacement order and refused to evacuate the facility as long as patients were still being treated.

Former detainees released from Sde Teiman, the notorious torture prison in southern Israel, said they saw and met Abu Safiya there. According to testimonies collected by the Geneva-based Euro-Mediterranean Human Rights Monitor, Abu Safiya was tortured prior to his arrival at Sde Teiman, and also while imprisoned there.

A United Nations commission concluded in 2024 that “Israel has perpetrated a concerted policy to destroy Gaza’s healthcare system as part of a broader assault on Gaza” that has left more than 250,000 Palestinians dead, maimed, or missing. The commission — which separately found that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza — further accused Israeli forces of “committing war crimes and the crime against humanity of extermination with relentless and deliberate attacks on medical personnel and facilities.”

Responding to the extension of Abu Safiya’s imprisonment, Amnesty International USA said on November 18 that the doctor “is being held without charge, separated from his family, his colleagues, and the children he lovingly treated.”

“Israeli authorities must immediately and unconditionally release Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya and all other arbitrarily detained Palestinians,” Amnesty added.

[Reprinted from Common Dreams.]

2023–26 Israeli genocide on Gaza

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Eastern Visayas farmers suffer from El Niño
content:
TACLOBAN CITY – “All the crops I planted, even if they are supposed to withstand heat, all died because of the extreme drought caused by the El Niño.”

Gil Gacus, a farmer from Samar, stressed this point at the October 28 forum at the University of the Philippines Tacloban titled “Istorya Pankalibungan: A Forum on Climate Change and Environmental Challenges.”

The event was attended by members of organizations of fisherfolk and farmers, environmental defenders, development workers from Leyte and Samar, youth groups, and students from different universities in Tacloban. Farmers from Magsasaka at Siyentipiko para sa Pag-unlad ng Agrikultura (MASIPAG) shared the impact of Super El Niño on their crops.

Gacus said that the lack of a reliable irrigation system adds up to farmers’ burdens. “We have irrigation canals but there is little to no water due to drought so our crops end up dying.”

Jeremias Maligmat, a farmer from Leyte, stressed the need for government action now that farmers are suffering from the effects of El Niño. He also criticized Marcos Jr.’s lack of urgency and genuineness to help them. “He [Marcos Jr.] is asking us to use pails to collect rainwater, but how will we collect it if there is no rain?”

“If Marcos is genuine about helping farmers, his government should focus on addressing the challenges on irrigation and invest in machinery that could pump out underground water to help us farmers during times like this,” Maligmat said.

Maligmat added that on top of the environmental challenges and outright neglect from the government, landlessness is also a major problem faced by farmers. “The government should address these challenges affecting us farmers if they are so genuine about helping us as we are the ones producing food for the country.”

Roque Regis of Save Kanbatok Advocacy criticized the government’s reaffirmation to continue the halted construction of the Causeway Project in Cancabato Bay. “Since the construction of the Causeway started last 2023, there have already been recorded, irreversible damages to the bay. It destroyed the then thriving ecosystem of the bay by obstructing the natural flow of water.”

Regis said that some of his fellow fisherfolk have stopped from fishing due to the deteriorating state of the Bay. “These so-called developmental projects like the causeway project do not benefit the community or the poor, but instead benefit the rich who embezzle money through these projects.”

“Fisherfolk like Mano Roque struggled heavily, so much so that the fish, crabs, and other seafood they catch, if they have any at all, shrunk in size over the years since land was dumped on Cancabato Bay to build that Causeway,” said Jerx Aliposa of Save Kankabato Advocacy.

“Instead of coming up with solutions to address their concerns like providing subsidies and investing on technologies that could help them, the government would always think of developmental projects like the causeway project, with little to no regard of their repercussions to our communities,” Aliposa said.

Nemesio Baldesco of Tinambacan Environmental Advocates Coalition (TEAC), a network of environmental defenders from Calbayog City in Samar, said that their group opposes the Gemini Wind Power Project by Vena Energy in their city. “[I]t will greatly affect the biodiversity of our forests and will pollute our sources of clean water.”

Although their group and other advocates succeeded in getting at least five wind turbines removed from Pan-as Hayiban watershed, Calbayog’s protected landscape, Nemesio said that the project is yet to be abandoned. “Their [Vena Energy] alternative route is to install the turbines outside the watershed but still within our forests where it could still disrupt the biodiversity and result in the cutting down of hundreds of trees.”

WATCH : Envi advocates oppose Gemini Wind Project in Samar

Ronnel Arambulo, Vice Chairperson of Pambansang Lakas ng Kilusang Mamamalakaya ng Pilipinas (PAMALAKAYA), stressed the importance of collective action as well as the youth’s participation to oppose projects that damage the environment and livelihoods of farmers and fisherfolks. “Let us not allow our schools to become producers of brains that will only be used by the rich to forward their anti-poor agenda.” Ronnie Manalo, secretary-general of the Kilusang Magbubukid ng Pilipinas (KMP), called on the farmers to fight for their rightful claim on the P45-billion funds allocated for El Niño. “Let us mobilize our farmers to compute all their losses and damages due to El Niño and collectively submit petitions to government agencies like the Department of Agriculture and our respective local government units.”

Jasmin Aguisanda-Jerusalem of Leyte Center for Development and Empowerment (LCDE), linked the challenges of our farmers and fisherfolks to our country’s economic policies. “Our economy is import-dependent when we have our local producers. It is clear that the policies we have in place are all for the profit of the few.” As a development worker for 45 years, Jerusalem witnessed the dire economic and political conditions of people in Eastern Visayas. “Despite helping almost 800,000 people since LCDE started in 1988, we were slapped with criminal cases all because we decided to help those who are in need.”

“A strong people’s movement deeply rooted in communities–in schools, farms, factories–is what we need to change the very system [that] is rotten to the core,” Jerusalem said. (RTS, DAA)

author: Maverick Avila
title: 3 UN experts alarmed over mass detention during ASEAN Summit
content:
Three United Nations Special Rapporteurs have publicly called out the Philippine government over the reported detention of more than 300 people during protests at the opening of the ASEAN 2026 summit, warning that the arrests point to a broader squeeze on dissent.

The mass arrest happened last November 15, 2026 when demonstrations broke out across Metro Manila to coincide with the regional summit to oppose the U.S.-led Pax technology and mining initiative and the presence of U.S. President Donald Trump. They were released on the night of November 18, following a decision of the Muntinlupa prosecutor.

Read: Police violently disperse, arrest hundreds in Muntinlupa protest

Among the arrested are mostly members of the Southern Tagalog group Lakbayan in Muntinlupa City, alongside media workers including student journalists, and progressive groups at Liwasang Bonifacio in Manila, and Bulacan.

Andrea Bolaños Vargas, Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights defenders, said she is concerned by reports of police violence against peaceful protesters and is monitoring the safety and protection of human rights defenders.

?? I am concerned by reports of police violence against peaceful protesters and arrests in the ?? #Philippines amid #ASEAN2026. I have received worrying information about the situation and am closely monitoring developments, including regarding the safety and protection of human…

“I have received worrying information about the situation and am closely monitoring developments, including regarding the safety and protection of human rights defenders,” Vargas said.

Gina Romero, UN Special Rapporteur on the rights to freedom of peaceful assembly and of association, wrote she received reports that security officials earlier in the week urged groups to hold off on protests until after the summit, reportedly to avoid a bad image before foreign visitors.

#Philipines today's police behaviour mirror a wider crackdown on dissent in the country. I have been receiving worrisome information about sedition subpoenas for anti-corruption protests, authorities tagging student leaders as "wanted", military home visits & campus lockdowns 3/

“Peaceful protests are not a PR question, they are a (human rights) issue,”

Romero added that this goes beyond the image of the ASEAN Summit taking place in the country. “(The) Philippines prior protests on related issues such as the pax silica have also been harassed,” she wrote.

Astrid Riano, Special Rapporteur on the right to a clean, safe and healthy environment, also said she is closely following the situation in Manila and in demonstrations elsewhere in the country.

Read: ‘Make Pax Silica deal public’

Riano also emphasized that ASEAN’s efforts should be aligned on its declaration to the right of a safe, clean, healthy, and sustainable environment at the 47th ASEAN Summit in Kuala Lumpur on October 26, 2025. This declaration aimed to address climate change, biodiversity loss, and environmental pollution.

“The right to a #healthyenvironment includes access to information and public participation, which includes peaceful demonstrations,” Riano said.

The same police brutality during Anti-Pax Silica protests are also prevalent across the regions of the country.

author: Maverick Avila
title: 3 UN experts press the Philippines over mass detentions of ASEAN summit protesters
content:
Three United Nations Special Rapporteurs have publicly called out the Philippine government over the reported detention of more than 300 people during protests at the opening of the ASEAN 2026 summit, warning that the arrests point to a broader squeeze on dissent.

The mass arrest happened last November 15, 2026 when demonstrations broke out across Metro Manila to coincide with the regional summit to oppose the U.S.-led Pax technology and mining initiative and the presence of U.S. President Donald Trump. They were released on the night of November 18, following a decision of the Muntinlupa prosecutor.

Read: Police violently disperse, arrest hundreds in Muntinlupa protest

Among the arrested are mostly members of the Southern Tagalog group Lakbayan in Muntinlupa City, alongside media workers including student journalists, and progressive groups at Liwasang Bonifacio in Manila, and Bulacan.

Andrea Bolaños Vargas, Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights defenders, said she is concerned by reports of police violence against peaceful protesters and is monitoring the safety and protection of human rights defenders.

?? I am concerned by reports of police violence against peaceful protesters and arrests in the ?? #Philippines amid #ASEAN2026. I have received worrying information about the situation and am closely monitoring developments, including regarding the safety and protection of human…

“I have received worrying information about the situation and am closely monitoring developments, including regarding the safety and protection of human rights defenders,” Vargas said.

Gina Romero, UN Special Rapporteur on the rights to freedom of peaceful assembly and of association, wrote she received reports that security officials earlier in the week urged groups to hold off on protests until after the summit, reportedly to avoid a bad image before foreign visitors.

#Philipines today's police behaviour mirror a wider crackdown on dissent in the country. I have been receiving worrisome information about sedition subpoenas for anti-corruption protests, authorities tagging student leaders as "wanted", military home visits & campus lockdowns 3/

“Peaceful protests are not a PR question, they are a (human rights) issue,”

Romero added that this goes beyond the image of the ASEAN Summit taking place in the country. “(The) Philippines prior protests on related issues such as the pax silica have also been harassed,” she wrote.

Astrid Riano, Special Rapporteur on the right to a clean, safe and healthy environment, also said she is closely following the situation in Manila and in demonstrations elsewhere in the country.

Read: ‘Make Pax Silica deal public’

Riano also emphasized that ASEAN’s efforts should be aligned on its declaration to the right of a safe, clean, healthy, and sustainable environment at the 47th ASEAN Summit in Kuala Lumpur on October 26, 2025. This declaration aimed to address climate change, biodiversity loss, and environmental pollution.

“The right to a #healthyenvironment includes access to information and public participation, which includes peaceful demonstrations,” Riano said.

author: Josiah David Quising
title: Legality of burning effigies
content:
Throughout history, the burning of effigies was never shown to be with intent to injure another, but rather consistently presented as a form of expression and indignation.

Filipinos using effigies to depict resistance and protest is said to have originated from the higantes of Angono, Rizal as a way to mock abusive hacenderos in the late Spanish colonial period. Decades later, Filipino activists have kept the tradition alive across multiple administrations, but not without opposition. The Philippine National Police (PNP) often releases warnings against burning effigies ahead of protests, claiming that burning protest materials would violate either the Republic Act No. 8749 (Clean Air Act) or Batas Pambansa No. 880 (Public Assembly Act). Just yesterday, Cebu activists were accused by the local police of violating the law when they set an effigy on fire.

But does burning effigies really violate the law? The PNP has cited Section 20 of the Philippine Clean Air Act which bans incineration of “municipal, biomedical, and hazardous waste” as the basis of their warning, stating that burning effigies would pollute the air.

A plain reading of the law would show that the ban on incineration does not prohibit all types of burning but instead specifically prohibits the burning of “waste”. While the Clean Air Act itself does not define “waste”, Section 3(kk) of R.A. 9003 or the Solid Waste Management Act defines “solid waste” as “all discarded household, commercial waste, non-hazardous institutional and industrial waste, street sweepings, construction debris, agricultural waste, and other non-hazardous/non-toxic solid waste.”

By plain definition, effigies cannot be categorized as “waste” as they are not “discarded” materials but rather art forms created for a specific purpose. The Supreme Court clarified this in MMDA v. Jancom (2002) where it held that Section 20 of the Philippine Clean Air Act does not absolutely prohibit incineration. It prohibits only burning processes involving municipal, biomedical, or hazardous wastes that emit poisonous and toxic fumes. This means that even in the absurd scenario where effigies are considered as “waste” materials, burning of the same would still not be considered a violation of the Philippine Clean Air Act.

“Poisonous and toxic fumes” are defined by Section 5(t) of the Clean Air Act as “any emissions and fumes which are beyond internationally-accepted standards, including but not limited to the World Health Organization (WHO) guideline values.”

This shows that without proof that the burning of effigies during protests would result in emissions of fumes “beyond internationally-accepted standards,” burning of effigies does not automatically violate the Philippine Clean Air Act.

Another law commonly cited by the PNP is Section 13(g)(3) of the Public Assembly Act which prohibits the “malicious burning of any object in the streets or thoroughfares”. The Supreme Court in Villareal v. People (2012) has defined “malice” or “malicious” as the deliberate, wrongful, or evil intent to injure another, or an act done with criminal indifference to another’s rights and without legal justification.

In other words, the intent or reason for the burning matters. Throughout history, the burning of effigies was never shown to be with intent to injure another, but rather consistently presented as a form of expression and indignation.

Ultimately, no law directly prohibits the burning of effigies. The PNP should stop distracting everyone from the issues brought to light by setting fire to art. At the end of the day, the government should address the message itself rather than fixate on how it was delivered – perhaps then we can return to calmly submitting position papers. (DAA)

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Lawyers condemn human rights violations vs protesters
content:
The National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers (NUPL) condemned the arrest, restricted legal access, and prolonged detention of more than 300 protesters apprehended during demonstrations at Liwasang Bonifacio and Sucat People’s Park ahead of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit.

During a press conference at the Liwasang Bonifacio on November 17, the lawyers’ group stressed that human rights violations were committed against the detained protesters.

Legal counsels assisting the detainees criticized law enforcement authorities for allegedly delaying their access to clients, filing sweeping criminal complaints, and leaving them in detention over a long non-working holiday period.

Ephraim Cortez, president of NUPL, denounced police authorities for requiring clearance from higher authorities before allowing legal counsels to confer with their detained clients.

He said, “A lawyer’s access to their clients cannot rely upon clearance from higher-ranking officials, as this is our clients’ right to counsel.”

Cortez added that the detention already exceeded the 18 hours allowed by the law. “Those arrested are innocent. They were just protesting. They should be released.”

The protesters were taken into custody during standoffs at the Liwasang Bonifacio and Sucat People’s Park.

Lawyer Mary Jane Real said that arresting demonstrators inside Liwasang Bonifacio violates the law on public assemblies. She stressed that Liwasang Bonifacio is a freedom park. “You cannot be arrested for protesting here, because we have the freedom to protest in this place.”

According to Real, the nine individuals arrested in Manila are facing multiple charges including illegal assemblies, direct assault, resistance and disobedience to a person in authority, tumults and other disturbances of public order, and violations of the Public Assembly Act.

Real also raised alarm over procedural delays caused by the ASEAN Summit work suspension in Metro Manila, noting that even if bail is recommended, detainees remain behind bars since there will be no court personnel to process release orders.

“The inquest concluded yesterday… We are currently awaiting the prosecutor’s decision, but since today is a holiday, no action can be taken until everyone returns to the office on Thursday,” Real said. “Consequently, even posting bail is not possible, as there is no one available to sign the necessary documents.”

On the other hand, lawyer Zoe Caballero of Sentro Para Sa Tunay Na Repormang Agraryo

denounced the reported P9-million cumulative bail required for the detained protesters, most of whom are farmers, workers, and students from the Southern Tagalog region.

“They themselves have nothing to eat, so where are they supposed to get the P9 million? If they actually had P9 million, they wouldn’t have marched all the way to Manila just to make their voices heard,” Caballero said. “Now, we’re being told: ‘Yes, you have the right to speak, but this is the price you must pay to say what needs to be said.’ It turns out you have to be wealthy just to be heard.”

Real urged the public to stand in solidarity with the detained demonstrators, stressing that their protests against Pax Silica are meant to protect ordinary Filipinos from worsening poverty and hunger. “If we don’t oppose this, all we’ll get here in this ‘Pax Silica’ is hunger and poverty. These people, they are the ones making sacrifices so that we may uphold our rights.”

“We have a responsibility toward them; we must help them gain their freedom, because they risked their own lives and peace so that we could be free,” Real said. (AMU, DAA)

author: Lindsay McCabe
title: Changes to coronial legislation to broaden next-of-kin determinations
content:
Readers please be advised that this article mentions First Nations people who have passed away, including children.




On Tuesday 22nd September 2026, the Minns Labor Government announced changes to the 

Coroners Act 2009

 NSW, specifically, the section of the legislation that instructs coroners to determine and appoint a Senior Next-of-Kin. This followed a statutory review of the Act, and is in response to one of the many recommendations made by the review. 




When a person’s death is reported to the coroner, a Senior Next-of-Kin is appointed. The Senior Next-of-Kin has the exclusive authority to make decisions regarding the person who has died while they are in the care of the coroner. For example, the Senior Next-of-Kin can object to a post-mortem examination being conducted. Being appointed Senior Next-of-Kin also means that the coroner has an obligation to provide mandatory notifications about the progress of a coronial investigation to the Senior Next-of-Kin. When, where and how a person is laid to rest is also under the authority of the Senior Next-of-Kin. 




Who is appointed as Senior Next-of-Kin is decided by a strict legal framework. The 

Coroners Act 2009

 (NSW) s 6A states that the Senior Next-of-Kin must be the deceased person’s spouse or de facto partner; if they have no spouse or de facto partner, then any of the adult children of the deceased person can be appointed. If the person has no adult children, then the person’s parent/s may be appointed. 




This appointment-flow hierarchy has been problematic for Mob for many years, across many jurisdictions. It does not take into account our kinship systems, laws, or spiritual beliefs. One of the earliest challenges of the Senior Next-of-Kin hierarchy involved 

two Aboriginal parents

 who could not agree on where to bury their deceased adult child. The mother wanted to hold a Catholic ceremony and burial in Darwin; the father however wanted to have a burial on their homelands, Bardi Country, and provided the Court with supporting information outlining the cultural obligations to do so. The Court ruled in favour of the mother. 




In 

2016

, the NSW Supreme Court was asked to rule on a matter where the Senior Next-of-Kin appointment had been challenged. In this matter, the coroner had appointed a deceased man’s de facto partner as the Senior Next-of-Kin, as per the legislation. This allowed the partner, a Gumbaynggirr woman, to make arrangements for the deceased man’s burial to take place in Bowraville. The man’s sister however, wanted the man to be taken home to Weilwan Country and to be buried alongside his ancestors. The Court ruled in favour of the man’s de facto partner, citing common law precedent. Further, because the de facto partner of the deceased man established her de facto status to the Court, she held ‘administrative priority’; in other words, she had the highest right as per the legislation. 




More recently, in 2024, the Supreme Court of NSW decided on a dispute between a deceased man’s de facto partner and mother who could not agree on where to bury him. The de facto partner of the man insisted he wanted to be buried in La Parouse; his mother wanted to take him home to his father in Cherbourg, Wakka Wakka Country, where he could be buried on Country. The Court held in favour of the man’s de facto partner, accepting that she was the deceased man’s de facto partner at the time of his death. 




So, who is appointed Senior Next-of-Kin when a person dies has significant ramifications for where, when, and how a person is returned to Country. 




There have however been instances where the appointment of Senior Next-of-Kin has affirmed cultural responsibilities and laws, albeit outside of NSW. In 

1999

, the non-Aboriginal spouse of a deceased Aboriginal man sought to bury them in Port Augusta. The deceased man’s father wished to bury him in Oodnadatta, where other members of the family had been buried, and on Yankintatjara Country. Several affidavits were presented to the Court, highlighting that, according to cultural responsibilities and practices, the head of the family should be empowered to make these decisions, not the spouse. The deceased’s spouse, on the other hand, argued that the children of the deceased would not be able to visit their father’s grave if it were located 700kms away in Oodnadatta. Significantly, the Court ruled in favour of the father of the deceased man, allowing him to take his son home, and to be buried according to Aboriginal law and custom.  




The announcement by the Minns Labor government then is a welcome one indeed. It was sparked by a completely different issue, though. As we have seen, when a person dies, and in particular where there is no will, the legislation states that the person’s spouse or de facto partner holds administrative priority, and so is often appointed as Senior Next-of-Kin. Unfortunately, this too often means that for women who have experienced domestic violence at the hands of their partner, that partner is very likely to be appointed as Senior Next-of-Kin, and can therefore make decisions about the laying to rest of the deceased. 




Advocacy by the parents and families

 of women who have died, and who have had an abusive partner appointed as Senior Next-of-Kin, have campaigned for the legislation to be amended for years. This is a necessary change, and one that gives the coroner the power to appoint a different Senior Next-of-Kin in cases where there is family and/or domestic violence. This is a really, really important outcome/change, and one that will allow families to focus on their grief instead of fighting for the right to lay their person to rest. 




In the 

media release,

 the Minns Labor government noted the ‘changes regarding senior next of kin appointments will also recognise extended familial or kinship structures among different cultures such as Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities’. As briefly shown here, and with 

plenty of evidence elsewhere

, this is something that we have been arguing for for many years. Had successive governments listened to us, perhaps the families who advocated for this change would not have had to. 




Despite the Minns Labor government’s pretense that they had Mob in mind all along, this reform was never about us, or it would have been done years ago. There has been little information about how the legislation will be amended to recognise our kinship systems or laws, or what criteria coroners will use in their application of this reform. With our collective lived experiences, it is perhaps right to be cautious of another government reform, particularly one that includes us 

after

 the fact.




This doesn’t take away from the benefits that these reforms will have for families when their person dies, and for whom an abuser has been granted all the rights of Senior Next-of-Kin. The advocacy of the families who fought for this, through their grief and their trauma, is applauded. Achieving this kind of reform is momentous. As many of us have been saying all along, though, 

if you get it right for Mob, you get it right for everyone

.

author: Unknown
title: Agnes Grundel - Novemberminnen
content:
Författare

: Agnes Grundel

Titel

: Novemberminnen

Källa

: Allarm november 1916




 Ett år har förflutit sedan vår kamrat, frihetskämpen Josef Hillström slöt sina av förtryck betyngda ögon, för att aldrig mera skåda den värld som fråntog honom allt - ja till och med rätten att leva. I den värld där han strävade att frigöra människorna, var hans egen frihet osäker. I det samhälle där han agiterade med varje gnista av sin outtröttliga energi, var hans liv icke tryggat. 




Varför?

 Jo: Därför att han hade hjältemod nog att trotsa, att opponera sig mot våldets blodtörstige tyranner, som alltid mördat och stympat, bränt och krossat alla dem som försökt vrida makten ur deras järnklor, samt ersätta människornas lidande med lycka. 




 Alla dem som i någon mån försökt att förbättra mänsklighetens förhållanden, alla dem som vågat fråga: med vad rätt kunna dessa legaliserade ogärningsmän tvinga mig att arbeta för dem, samt bestjäla mig produkten av mitt arbete, alltid ha de fått falla offer för den s. k. rättvisan. Sådana män äro farliga för förtryckarna, enär de ha förmågan att väcka andra och få dem att göra gemensam aktion mot förtrycket, därför måste de rödjas ur vägen. 




 Josef Hillström var en av de oböjlige. Ingenting förfärade honom, in i dödens käftar trotsade han dem alla. De togo hans unga kraftiga, förhoppningsfulla liv, men hans skändligt utgjutna blod ropar på hämd, från alla delar av jorden juder det som av en tordönsstämma: 

hämnd

. Så länge här finnes en slav, komma hans brännande odödliga ord och eldiga entusiasm inspirera miljoner till verksamhet. 




 Josef Hillström har ej levat förgäves, oaktat han dog i blomman av sitt liv. Det säges han var en drömmare, kanske så, enär hans idé ännu ej hunnit bliva förverkligad, men han drömde ej när han i sina sånger gav slavarna råd huru att bekriga sina svurna dödsfiender. Det var realisten Joe Hill vi minnas och vörda. 




 Joe Hill drömde om en bättre värld där arbetaren skördar fulla produkten av sitt arbete, där nyttiga medborgare styra samhället till allas bästa, där list, lögn, våld och bedrägeri ej längre triumferar, där små barn vårdas som praktfulla blommor. 




 Att han lärde slavarna att förverkliga detta, däri låg Joe Hills brott. Någon invände hånfullt att han gick i döden för en kvinnas skull. Ja alltid ha frihetshjältar förhånats av den okunniga massan. Vi minnas kanske Robert Emmet, Irlands store frihetskämpe, en Voltaire, Thomas Payne m. fl. 




 Samtidigt som Joe Hill mördades i SAlt Lake hade de samhällsbevarande här i staden konferens varvid en av de viktigaste frågorna för dagen var: 

hur skola vi kunna fördriva I. W. W. männen ur U. S. A.

 Detta visar att dessa herrar tycka sig redan nu se hur deras makts sista dagar börja randas. De mötas för att uppgöra planer huru att på bästa sätt tillintetgöra denna organisation. En av deras planer är väl känd och praktiseras ofta, den att mörda de aktive ledande männen. För denna metod föll vår präktige Joe Hill, för samma försöka de få de tre kamraterna i norra Minnesota: Joe Smidt, Carlo Tresca och Sam Scharlet. Allt beror på er arbetare om de även i detta fallet skola lyckas. Skola vi låta våldets bödlar döda våra bästa och aktivaste kamrater. Nej. Låt oss visa att vi äro män och kvinnor med ett för rätt och frihet klappande hjärta och med mod att handla. 




 Vi kunna ej bättre vörda Joe Hills minne än att följa hans sista uppmaning till världens arbetare: 

Organisera.

author: Unknown
title: Carl Ahlteen - Josef Hillström
content:
Författare

: Carl Ahlteen

Titel

: Josef Hillström

Undertitel

: (1 års minne)

Källa

: Allarm november 1916




 Ett år har nu gått till ända sedan den tiden då vi ännu hade vår präktige kamrat i livet. 




 Vi alla, som i fjor i slutet av oktober och b örjan av november månad tillhörde organisationen, minns allt för väl med vilken spänning vi emotsågo den dagen då Hillström skulle återfå friheten. 




 Få av oss kunde trots allt tro att den 

kristna statsliga

 mordlusten skulle ta ett sådant uttryck som detta: mörda en människa, endast därför att hans hjärta klappade för proletariatets frigörelse. Han, denne präktige kamrat anklagades för mord av en f. d. polisman, handlare, där tyckte man sig finna bevis nog. Hur hade det varit om det endast hade varit en handlande, ej en f. d. polisman? Å på det sätt den kristna staten gick tillväga mot Josef Hillström kunde de utan vidare anklaga en som fanns i New York eller någon annan avlägsen stad, för brottet i Salt Lake, Utah. Man behövde ej det ringaste bevis i fallet Josef Hillström därför skulle det givetvis ej behövas i det andra fallet heller. 




 En sak var det som var nog: Josef Hillström diktade arbetarsånger av sådan art att gamla och unga rycktes med för dess känslighet och sanningsrika manande innehåll. 




 Hade Hillström diktat kristna sånger, hade han levat den dag som i dag är, och varit omgjordad med lyx och överflöd. Hade Bruno ljugit lika fräckt som de kristna prästerna i Rom hade han ej blivit bränd på bål. 




..Å du förbannade kristna rättvisa, du mördar ädla män och sanningssökare. Hitintills har du undgått straffet, men det väntar dig! Lederna tätna!




 Den kristna fräcka råheten har förmått att hålla sig vid liv en rätt lång tid, men den tidens längd som återstår är nog snart räknad. Över hela jorden höres hoten av starka män, och lederna tätna. Det bådar domsdagar för förtrycket. 







 Strax efter Hillströms häktning erhöll jag brev från honom vart han omtalade hur det kom sig att han var i fängelset. Han själv ansåg det hela som en komedi, och kunde givetvis aldrig tro att man i en tidsålder som denna kunde begå ett sådant brott mot honom som blev gjort. 




 Regelbundet hade jag brev och vykort från honom, och regelbundet sände jag honom tidningar, vilka han fick mottaga ända tills i juni månad 1915. Han bad mig då sända dem till en kvinnlig kamrat som personligen gav honom dem. Inom kort blev detta också omöjligt. 




 Hela tiden hade vår präktige kamrat hoppet framme, alltid framhöll han att snart skola de väl i alla fall inse sitt brott mot mig och frigiva mig. Efter möjligheterna att få läsa böcker och tidningar blevo stängda, förstod vår kamrat vad saken gällde, han förstod att det kristna packet ej kunde tillfredsställas med mindre än att se hans huvud på ett fat. 




 Han förstod att endast en räddning återstod för honom, det var att massorna organiserade sig och ryckte honom ur mördarhordens händer. Rättvisan genom borgarnas lag trodde han berättigat nog ej mera på. 




 Över hela Amerika hölls "Joe Hill" möten, över hela Amerika talade man sympatiskt, och i form av kontanter lade man sin tribut. Man gjorde allt man kunde sade man. 




 Ja man gjorde allt man kunde fredligt - vad som var tillåtet av Hillströms mördare - men var det nog? Tänk än en gång efter arbetare om det var nog. Vi ha tre kamrater nu sittande väntande på samma som "Joe Hill" kamraterna på "Messeba Range". Skall man även i detta fall hålla sig inom ramen av borgarnas lag? Skall man efter den blodiga rättvisan fullbordat sitt verk med dem säga: vi gjorde allt vi kunde. 

vad är rätt för borgaren och borgarens stat?




Jo! att fylla sitt eget behov, göra vad som passar deras intresse. Om detta blir gjort inom eller utom ramen av den s. k. rättvisan, eller med eller mot slavarnas vilja bekymrar ej dem det minsta. Slavarna de måste innan de handla ha reda på om det är rätt, och i sin stora enfald gå de till sina dödssvurne fiender och fråga om det är rätt.




Idiotiskt handlingssätt, utfört av slavar och viljelösa, och av dem endast.




 Borgarna ha, på grund av slavarnas feghet 

makt

 och detta är nog för dem att få rätt. 




 Slavarna uraktläto att organisera sig och med makt uttaga Hillström. 

Den 19 november kom, och hydran frossade av det unga, flytande, varma, kamratblodet.

 Några minuters blodflöde och hon var tillfredsställd. Han låg där nu dödad denne vår präktige kamrat. Hans ädla hjärta hade upphört att slå, hans hand kunde ej mera föra den penna som på en kort tid sände ut så många vackra maningar, hänryckte så många tusenden för proletariatets rättvisa sak. Hans sista maning var i samma stil som den han gav de sista tre månaderna av sitt liv: 

ORGANISERA, Sörj ej mig, endast organisera!




 Han gav den maningen för att möjliggöra hans frihet. Friheten kom dock ej för honom, men den idla själen förbannade dock ej slavarna, utan gav åter och åter igen samma maning, detta för att hindra nya kamrater att falla offer för samma legda mördarhop. 




 Svaret återstår. Nya kamrater äro redan utvalda offer, vad blir edert svar, ni slavande millioner? 




 Efter mordet av Hillström var begånget, har det till och med i s. k. radikala kretsar diskuterats frågan: "Var han oskyldig eller skyldig?" Många ha framfört sådana dumma meningar som denna: Han sade att han var i sällskap med en kvinna den natten. varför uppgav han ej hennes namn? 




...

author: Unknown
title: John Nyström - Ett ve!
content:
Författare

: John Nyström

Titel

: Ett ve!

Källa

: Allarm november 1916




 Du mördarliga i Saltsjöstaden;

 Vi glömma aldrig den hemska dagen,

 Då du vår sångarvän lät mörda -

 Men som du sår får du också skörda. 




 Ett hat, ett ve ha vi alla svurit,

 Ty Hillströms hjärta har du sönderskurit

 Och detta hat rört upp en stark orkan,

 Som snart skall nedslå uti Saltsjösta'n. 




 Rebellens liv det var en väldig gnista

 Som modet tände intill det sista.

 Ja, in i döden ljöd hans maningsord:

 "Kom, tag tillbaka, slav, din stulna jord." 




 En man, som Hillström, ej finnes många,

 Därföre skulle du honom fånga.

 Och bjuda gengälden en säker död.

 Du, världens avskum, du överflöd! 




 I tvänne år låg han där inburad

 Bak grå och dödstysta fängselmurar.

 Han gick till döden som till dukat bord,

 Men glöm ej, mördare, hans sista ord! 




 Ett tack du kämpe, för vad du stridit,

 För vad du plågats och för vad du lidit.

 Så sant vi lever skall vi hatet så

 Och fler och fler skall i ledet stå.

author: Unknown
title: Walfrid Engdahl - Joe Hill
content:
Författare

: Walfrid Engdahl

Titel

: Joe Hill

Källa

: Allarm november 1916




 Hans sånger leva, men han är död. Varför skola vi nu igen gräva upp honom för dyrkan och kanonisering? Varför skall han prisas? Därför att han var en man! Kunde han hjälpa att han var det? Borde inte alla revolutionärer vara män? 




 Sannerligen han var bätter än vi. I ett av sina sista brev till en kamrat skrev han något liknande: 







 "Slösa ej tid över mitt minne - organisera." 







 Det var manliga ord, värda att minnas av envar. 




 Han skrev sånger, låt oss sjunga dem. De väcka slavarna mer än artiklarna om den döde och de döda gör. 




 Skall en människa prisas därför att hon skrivit sånger, eller skrivit vad som helst? Kunde han undgå att skriva dem? Han kunde det lika litet som näktergalen kan undgå sjunga vackra sånger i härliga aftnar och länder som äro gynnade av hans närvaro. 




 Vi tyckte alla om Josef Hillström och vi talade och skrev därom för ett år sedan. Vår tid är kanske för dyrbar för att offra den på döda ben, nära och hur kära de voro oss. 




 Det är väl knappast en dygd att vara revolutionär. Det är snarare den vakne arbetarens självskrivna plikt. Det är vårt intresse att vara det och ingen som helst moralisk känsla. Att hans liv var en strid, som slutade så tragiskt, det hembar han njutning av själv medan han levde. Ty striden ger en njutning. På själva avrättningsplatsen stod han ännu som den betvingade segraren: han darrade ej så mycket som de, vilka sköto honom. 




 Han var segrare över alla känslor, stod över mängden, och han kände det. Hans arbete levde efter honom. Han dog i rätta ögonblicket, aktad, ärad, avhållen av alla, utom de svarta mördarna. Han var rörelsen och rörelsen var han, liksom han var en del i universum, avskild genom sin individuella kropp och dock ett med det hela. Den skarpsynte revolutionären vet, att hans avrättning är ett tecken på organisationens livskraft och så går han beslutsamt in i dödens omfamning i förvissningen därom. 




 Joe Hill hade njutning nog, ty det finnes ingen njutning så stor som känslan av en manlig gärning. 




 Vi bli sjuka om någon vågar kritisera medlemmarna i vår organisation. Varför skola vi då ej vara rättrådiga nog att ta bort även berömmet. Är det ena klandervärt borde det andra vara det också, utan att meningen med en rörelse och dess organ är ett inbördes beundra och smickra varann. 




 Min enskilda mening är, att det är nödvändigare för oss att kritisera och få fram våra fel och våra bristfälligheter än det är att få fram våra fördelar. Våra gärningar och vårt uppträdande återspelgar allt. De stora handlingarna tala alltid väl om oss, i sig själva, men det är de låga handlingarnas sätt att tala på sitt vis också. Den värdefullaste kritik en rörelse får är från dess egna medlemmar och den oskattbaraste kritiken individen mottager är från sin bästa vän. Endast en sådan medlem - endast en sådan vän är värd att äga. 




 Jag vill ej följa med på smickrets dyiga väg. På höjderna där de stora och mäktiga stormarna gå fram, där den eviga spänningen är, där är revolutionärens givna plats. 




 Vad är berömmet värt? Ännu aldrig fanns en människa som vann det minsta grand därpå. Jag har sett människor som ständigt erhållit smicker och beröm, och hurdana ha de blivit! Äckliga, vämjeliga, självförnöjda stackare. Fy fan! Å andra sidan har jag sett dem, som dag ut och dag in utstått kaskader af klander och kritik och de ha varit män: djärva, dådlystna, energiska, viljestarka - djävliga. 




 Låt oss inte skända de dödas gravar med årliga kanoniseringar. Vi bör inte tänka om vad vi tänkte i fjol, utan tänka något nytt. Ha vi inte handlingar nu att tänka på mångfaldiga gånger mera aktuella än en kamrats avrättning? I gruvor, på banor och fält avrättas oupphörliga människor med samma varma blod och känslor. Bör vi inte tänka på dem? 




 Ha vi inte militärvansinnet att bekämpa och tala och skriva om? Står ej ännu privatkapitalismen utmanande blodtörstig och stark? 




 Vi kan göra mycket mot dessa drakar. Joe Hill kunde ej göra mer än vi, än hans dikter göra i dag. Utrustade med dem äro vi lika starka, lika väckande som han. De voro ej hans mer än de äro våra. Han skrev dem törhända medan vi höllo gatumöten och sjöngo andra sånger, eller medan vi sålde tidningar och klistrade affischer. Den ene är lika oumbärlig som den andre, och varför skall den ene glömmas medan den andre höjes över skyarna? 




 Medan hans minne firas blir vår dumhet firad med. Vet ni, vi borde skämmas över att vi ej förvandlade hans fängelse till en ruin. Ack, vi voro så snälla och hovsamma, vi skrevo våra radikala namn på listor, som skulle presenteras för gov. Spry i Utah, då vi skulle rivit listorna och gått ut i handling. 




 Det är större förlora i en ärlig strid för vår rätt än att inte våga en strid. 




 Vi vilja understundom sträjka för ett öres förhöjning i vår avlöning, men känna ingen lust därtill nära våra käraste kamraters liv stå på spel. 




 Varför skriva vi inga petitionslistor då en förhöjning i avlöningen är önskad? Tror ni det skulle hjälpa oss någon vart? 




 Jag hörde revolutionärer säga, att vi böra kompromissa ibland, tror ni att de visste vad de sade? 




...

author: Chris Lang
title: The Antalya AI pledge: Voluntary commitments to greenwash a destructive industry
content:
The COP31 Presidency and the International Telecommunication Union, the United Nations agency for digital technologies launched the Antalya AI Pledge at COP31 in Türkiye, on November 16.

The Pledge is yet another voluntary pledge produced over more than three decades of COP meetings that will do less than nothing to address the climate crisis. Worse, the governments endorsing the Pledge are actively supporting a massively polluting industry that is accelerating the climate crisis.

The Antalya AI Pledge was launched at a “High-level Green Digital Action Roundtable on AI”. The Roundtable discussion is available here.

Tomas Lamanauskas, the deputy secretary-general of the International Telecommunication Union told the meeting that, “AI is really the technology that’s transforming our lives and mostly for good, I should say. From our daily ability to write speeches ... to much more high level aspects from medicine to agriculture, to education, as well as industries.”

Obviously, Lamanauskas didn’t give any concrete examples of any of this. Neither did he mention that the AI bubble is threatening another global financial crisis. Or that the main use of AI is to extract ever more fossil fuels. And he made no mention of the military AI industry.

“It has a really transformative potential to make everyone’s lives much better,” Lamanauskas said. Presumably Lamanauskas is oblivious to the recent United States elections in which voters made their feelings crystal clear about the data centres that have devastated so many communities.

Lamanauskas talked about AI’s energy use as a “challenge that we need to rein in if we want AI to sustainable power the world and to make sure that AI is a solution not the problem”.

Simon Stiell, executive secretary of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, told the meeting that, “AI and other frontier technologies are a double edged sword. The task ahead is to blunt their dangerous edges, sharpen their catalytic ones, and put these technologies responsibly to work.”

Stiell noted that communities are “pushing back against data centres, concerned about their water, their energy bills, and their environment. So public support is already sinking deeper under water.”

Companies should, according to Stiell, “power data centres with renewable energy”.

But the Pledge makes no mention of fossil fuels. Instead it consists of vague statements about powering and building AI “sustainably”, managing AI “responsibly”, reporting the environmental impacts, and strengthening “financial support and technical infrastructure for AI for climate action”.

There is no mechanism to hold any of the companies or governments that sign the Pledge to account if they breach the terms of the Pledge.

The reality is that the Antalya AI Pledge is greenwashing a massively destructive, extractive, unethical, thieving industry. “AI companies’ license to operate is already on thin ice, right across political spectrums in many countries. And under that thin ice lie some potentially very deep regulatory waters, as political landscapes shift,” Stiell said in his speech at the launch.

“Very deep regulatory waters” is exactly what the world needs to prevent the damage that AI is already causing — damage that is accelerating every day.

“CEOs and boards need to step-up, and align business and investment plans with the world’s agreed climate goals,” Stiell said. The voluntary Antalya AI Pledge exists to allow the AI industry to continue its destructive business as usual.

Justine Calma, writing in The Verge, describes the Pledge as a “cruel joke”.

She points out that the Pledge even states that, “these objectives of the pledge are voluntary and non-prescriptive, create no new obligations, and are to be implemented in accordance with national circumstances”.

“In other words,” Calma writes, “these are voluntary commitments that countries can choose to follow or not follow based on their whims”.

On the same day as the launch of the Antalya AI Pledge, an assessment of the carbon emissions and energy consumption of US hyperscale data centres was published in Nature Sustainability. This is the first peer-reviewed estimate of the climate impact of data centres in the US.

The study estimates that hyperscale data centres in the US emitted between 21-31 million metric tonnes of CO₂ from May 2024 to April 2025 and used about 2% of US electricity. As Emily Atkin writes in Heated, these are big numbers, but “they’re also massive underestimations”.

Hundreds of hyperscale data centres were left out of the study because we simply do not know how many hyperscale data centres there are in the US

The electricity consumption isn’t the only problem with data centres. The equipment that keeps the servers in data centres from overheating leaks refrigerants that are potent greenhouse gases.

The researchers had to make assumptions about how the electricity powering the data centres was generated: gas, coal, renewables, etc. The researchers couldn’t tell how much electricity came from the grid and how much was generated from gas turbines built specifically to power the data centres.

And the study looked at data centres’ emissions in the 12 months up to April 2025. “The data center boom hasn’t slowed down since our study period ended in April 2025,” lead author Gianluca Guidi said in a press release. “New facilities have been built, existing campuses have expanded, and demand for AI computing continues to grow. That means the electricity use and carbon footprint we're reporting could already be substantially larger now in 2026.”

In August 2026, Business Insider and Insider Tech reported that there are 2228 new data centres currently planned or under construction across the US.

Atkin points out that she’s not criticising the study. “It’s clear the researchers did everything they could possibly do with the paltry information they had,” Atkin writes.

So far, only 10 governments have endorsed the Antalya AI Pledge: Andorra, Brazil, Colombia, Germany, Luxembourg, Republic of Korea, Sierra Leone, Somalia, Türkiye, and Uganda. Seven academic organisations have endorsed it, 21 civil society organisations, 47 companies, and seven other organisations.

The US, China, and the EU have not endorsed the Pledge. Neither have major AI companies such as Nvidia, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, or Meta.

“The AI pledge risks giving Big Tech a green stamp without requiring it to address the real climate impacts of its infrastructure,” Jill McArdle, a campaigner with the Berlin-based organisation Beyond Fossil Fuels told Nature magazine.

Indigenous Climate Action, Mohawks United in Safety and Health, and Woven put out a response to the Antalya AI Pledge. They point out that, “Hyperscale data centers are actively threatening Indigenous communities such as Tonawanda and Akwesasne; hundreds of Filipino activists organizing against AI mega-center Pax Silica have been arrested in this past week alone; experimental AI surveillance is being weaponized against Palestinians; and rare earth mineral mining such as uranium in Dine Territory and lithium in Aranã Caboclo is proliferating- all to feed the AI machine.”

And they conclude that “Implementation of AI for climate change solutions without systemic change that prioritises Indigenous liberation and sovereignty, is a FALSE climate solution.”

author: Jack Munafo
title: City of Newcastle chooses business bottom line over the climate
content:
The Newcastle City Council has voted to ban Rising Tide, Australia’s largest climate activist group, from hosting events on council-owned land. The motion, put by right-wing independent mayor and former weather reporter Gavin Morris, has sought to rid Newcastle of climate protests.

For many years, Rising Tide has forced the Newcastle City Council to confront the reality of hosting the world’s largest coal port. One hundred and fifty million tonnes of coal left the port in 2025, over 95 percent of which was sold to various Southeast Asian countries. Emissions from its usage, which are approximately 1 percent of Earth’s total CO2 emissions each year, are not counted towards Australia’s CO2 emissions.

The council motion passed 7-6. Voting against were three Greens and three Labor councillors. One Labor councillor, failed mayoral candidate Declan Clausen, voted for the bill. He attended the council meeting over Zoom from the COP31 climate conference in Türkiye. 

The council’s ban is not restricted to Rising Tide. It also applies to “its associates, subsidiaries, affiliated Issue Motivated Groups; and individuals”. Who counts as an “issue motivated group or individual” is at the discretion of the council. When interviewed by ABC Radio the morning after the vote, Morris said he “would be comfortable with” the wide-reaching powers of prohibition granted to the council targeting other groups. He specifically mentioned Palestine-related groups as being potentially affected by this motion.

Morris’ principal bugbear is Rising Tide’s annual People’s Blockade, where protesters take to Newcastle Harbour to prevent coal ships from moving into the port. Morris couched his motion in terms of community safety, but Business Hunter CEO Bob Hawes, in his letter of support for the motion, was willing to say the quiet part out loud:

“[Rising Tide] continues to have adverse impacts on regional businesses and the local visitor economy ... Rising Tide supporters might not like what some of these operators do but they are undertaking legal business activities ... and they have a right to undertake them without disruption.”

The operation of the port alone generated about $107 million in 2025, let alone the profits that come from actually selling the goods that move through it. 

Morris also received letters of support from NSW Premier Chris Minns and police minister Yasmin Catley. Their support tells you everything you need to know about Labor’s stance on climate change. These letters came only weeks after Minns’ approval of the largest coal expansion in NSW history, and months after his announcement that the Great Koala National Park will be funded by pay-to-pollute carbon credits.

Morris was elected in February this year. He has taken his election as a mandate from “the community” to clamp down on Rising Tide. We must show him that the Newcastle community stands with Rising Tide and for real action on climate change, not the profits of the coal industry.

author: L214
title: Enquête élevage de cochons E.Leclerc
content:
L214 publie sa onzième enquête sur les conditions de vie désastreuses des cochons élevés pour E.Leclerc. Les images proviennent d’un élevage intensif de cochons situé sur la commune de Poullaouen, dans le Finistère (Bretagne). Elles témoignent des infractions répétées et des pratiques sources de souffrance pour les animaux : porcelets castrés à vif, coupe des queues de tous les porcelets et sans anesthésie, meulage des dents systématique...

L214 demande à E.Leclerc de s’engager à respecter la réglementation et à interdire les cages dans les élevages qui l'approvisionnent. L’association se mobilise devant les 16 centrales d'achats de E.Leclerc et porte plainte contre l’élevage et E.Leclerc pour sévices graves et mauvais traitements sur les animaux.

Depuis 2024, l’association L214 a rendu publiques des images issues de onze élevages de cochons approvisionnant les magasins E.Leclerc. Les pratiques qui y ont été constatées sont cruelles et, pour certaines, illégales :

Les truies passent la moitié de leur vie enfermées dans des cages où elles ne peuvent même pas se retourner ;

Les queues des porcelets sont coupées à vif de façon systématique ;

Les porcelets subissent d’autres mutilations, comme le meulage des dents et la castration, souvent sans anesthésie ;

Les cochons sont détenus sur caillebotis, au-dessus de leurs déjections, sans matériaux manipulables (paille, etc.) pour satisfaire leurs besoins essentiels.

En votre qualité de présidents de centrales d’achats (SCA), vous siégez au comité stratégique de E.Leclerc, ce qui vous confère un rôle important dans l’élaboration du consensus interne de l’enseigne. Vous avez la responsabilité de porter au sein de cette instance un engagement contre les pires pratiques d'élevage pour les cochons

Nous, signataires de cette pétition, demandons à E.Leclerc de mettre fin à l’enfermement des truies en cage et de respecter la réglementation, afin d’épargner aux cochons les souffrances les plus extrêmes.
