title: Solidarity of Intellectuals: The status of Rojava University must be preserved
content:
The 

Solidarity of Intellectuals of Western Kurdistan

 (

Hevgirtina Rewşenbîrên Rojavayê Kurdistanê 

– HRRK) issued a written statement condemning the attack against students of Rojava University. The HRRK called for the university’s status to be preserved and for students to be included in decisions affecting their academic future. The HRRK added that it would not accept unilateral integration decisions, and confirmed it was  following with great concern the integration of educational institutions into Syrian state institutions, particularly the future of Rojava University in Qamishlo, and condemned the disregard for students’ rights and academic futures.




The HRRK condemned the attack by security forces on university students on 16 November, adding: “The forcible suppression of peaceful freedom of expression constitutes a violation of students’ rights and the sanctity of their universities.”




The HRRK called for an independent investigation to shed light on the attack and urged that those responsible be brought to justice.




No to unilateral integration 




The HRRK said that protecting the Kurdish language, culture, and freedom of expression is a fundamental duty, and added that the integration of institutions can only take place through dialogue and agreement between the parties.




The statement said: “We reject any form of integration imposed from above and carried out through unilateral decisions. Integration that erases the academic, administrative, and linguistic characteristics of these institutions would pose a threat to the future of the Kurdish language and culture in Rojava.”




HRRK’S demands 




At the end of its statement, the HRRK outlined the following demands concerning the future of Rojava University:




"- The decision to merge Rojava University with Euphrates University must be annulled. The university must be recognized as an independent university within Syria’s higher education system, and all its faculties and departments must be included in the official accreditation process.




- The diplomas issued by the university must be recognized. All procedures aimed at closing the university or transferring students to other universities must be halted.




- Kurdish must be recognized as an official language in the constitution, and the right to education in Kurdish must be guaranteed. Kurdish must be accepted as a language of instruction and scientific research at Rojava University.




- An urgent official dialogue must be initiated with the participation of representatives elected by the university administration and students. Students must be included in decisions determining their academic future and the future of their university."

author: Unknown
title: Activists in Strasbourg: Our vigil will continue until Abdullah Öcalan is free
content:
The Freedom for Öcalan Vigil, launched on 25 June 2012 in Strasbourg to demand the physical freedom of the Kurdish people's leader, is continuing into its 751st week.




This week, the vigil was taken over by Kadriye Alptekin, Merve Zîlan and Ömer Kurtgözü, who travelled from Brussels.




Speaking at the event, Kadriye Alptekin thanked everyone who had contributed to the action over the past 15 years, stating that they would continue their struggle until Öcalan achieved physical freedom.




“Until our Leader achieves physical freedom, we will all be here, we will all stand firm, and we will all continue to make our call,” Alptekin said.




She concluded her speech with the words: “Long live the Kurds and Kurdistan; long live Abdullah Öcalan, the leader of the people of Kurdistan.”




Merve Zîlan, another activist who took over the vigil, said they had come from Brussels and would continue their vigil and actions until Öcalan's physical freedom was secured.




Calling on European public opinion to show greater awareness, Zîlan said: “We have joined this vigil, which has been continuing for 15 years. We will continue our vigils and actions until our Leader is free and achieves physical freedom. Our appeal to Europe is to show support for our struggle for our Leader's freedom.”




Addressing the Kurdish people and patriotic families, Zîlan added: “Come, let us stand up for our Leader; come, let us stand up for our own efforts and our freedom.”




Continuing her speech in Kurdish, Zîlan said: “The freedom of the Leader is the freedom of the Kurdish people. Long live the resistance of the Kurdish people.”

author: Unknown
title: Iraqi Court orders closure of Yazidi Youth Party
content:
The Iraqi Federal Court ruled on 13 October 2026, to dissolve the Yazidi Youth Party. An appeal against the decision was filed with the Iraqi Federal Court and accepted. However, at the request of the Political Parties Department of the Iraqi High Electoral Commission, the Court ruled on 15 November to shut down the party.




Following the 13 October closure decision by Iraq’s Electoral Legal Committee, the president of the Yazidi Youth Party appealed to the court, arguing that the decision was unjust and requesting its annulment.




The Federal Court found that the appeal had been filed within the legal deadline and accepted it on procedural grounds. However, during its review, the Court upheld the closure decision, stating that it was based on security reports submitted by security forces. According to the Court, the department’s report concluded that the party’s activities “threaten the security, territorial integrity, and sovereignty of the Republic of Iraq.”




Consequently, Decision No. 20, dated 13 October, issued by the Electoral Legal Committee, was upheld. The ruling ordered the party to cease its activities, all its offices to be closed, and its assets to be confiscated.




The Yazidi Youth Party held its founding congress on 9 April 2026, in Shengal. The congress took place under the supervision of a delegation from the Political Parties Department of the Electoral Commission, with no objections raised by the delegation.

author: Unknown
title: Iran attacks Pêncewîn and Qandil in Southern Kurdistan
content:
Iranian regime forces carried out several attacks on areas along the border between Southern and Eastern Kurdistan on Tuesday. In addition to mortar attacks on the Qandil region, a drone attack on Pêncewîn (Penjwen) in Sulaymaniyah Governorate was also reported in the evening.




According to a statement issued by the Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK), regime forces targeted several locations in the Pêncewîn region with an explosive-laden kamikaze drone at around 7:30 pm. The PJAK stated that the attack had caused no fatalities among its ranks.




Mortar shelling of villages in the Qandil region




Earlier in the day, Iranian regime forces had subjected several areas in the Qandil Mountains to mortar fire. According to information from the region, the areas of Şehîd Harûn and Şehîd Ayhan, as well as the villages of Elî Reş and Goyêz along the border between Southern and Eastern Kurdistan, were affected. No information was initially available on the extent of the damage or possible casualties from the shelling.

author: Unknown
title: American philosopher Caputo voices support for the Peace and Democratic Society Process
content:
International solidarity continues with the Call for Peace and Democratic Society issued by Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan on February 27, 2025. American philosopher John David Caputo has also expressed his support for the international campaign being conducted as part of the call.




In a message sent to Mezopotamya Agency (MA), Caputo expressed his hopes for the ongoing peace process in Turkey in the following words:




“My hope is that the ongoing peace process in Turkey will embrace the following principles: Diversity fosters a deeper unity; a genuine community is formed by weaving bonds across differences; and true peace is the fruit of justice.”




John David Caputo




Born in 1940, John David Caputo is an American philosopher and philosopher of religion. One of the prominent figures in contemporary continental philosophy, Caputo is particularly known for his work on Jacques Derrida’s deconstruction, hermeneutics, and radical theology.




A leading representative of radical hermeneutics and “weak theology,” Caputo has served as a professor at Villanova University and Syracuse University.




His major works include 

Radical Hermeneutics

 (1987), 

The Weakness of God: A Theology of the Event

 (2006), and 

The Insistence of God: A Theology of Perhaps

 (2013).

author: Fabrizio Floris
title: The Sahara was never a border
content:
In July, Algeria and Mali reinstated their ambassadors and reopened their airspace to each other, more than a year after Algerian forces shot down a Malian drone near the border town of Tin Zaouatine. 

Al Jazeera reported the thaw

; Agence France-Presse (AFP) 

added

 that rebel advances in northern Mali had accelerated it, and that restoring cross-border security cooperation was a priority. In September, Algeria’s prime minister was 

received in Bamako with military honors

. 

The reconciliation is about a border that both governments say they cannot control.

Farther east, on the Algeria–Niger frontier, the same logic works differently. The Niger-based NGO, Alarme Phone Sahara, counted more than 34,000 people 

expelled from Algeria to Niger in 2025

, a record, up from 31,404 in 2024 and 26,031 in 2023. Migrants who are not Nigerien are left at a desert spot known as Point Zéro and they walk about 15km to Assamaka.

Both stories treat the Sahara as a line to be secured: a front to be held, a space to be cleared of the wrong people. Judith Scheele’s 

Shifting Sands: A Human History of the Sahara

 (2025) is a sustained argument that this is the wrong picture. An anthropologist at the 

École des hautes études en sciences sociales

, Scheele 

combines historical archives, including many Arabic-language accounts, with decades of fieldwork

 and interviews with Saharans themselves. Edward Said taught us that places are imagined before they are governed; Fernand Braudel, that seas link as much as they divide. Scheele applies both lessons to a desert.

Scheele’s Sahara is a human world. The book moves from a city-building civilization in Libya’s Fezzan, contemporary with the Roman Empire, through the caravan trades that carried gold, salt, textiles, and enslaved people to the borderlands of Algeria, Mali, Niger, Chad, and Libya that she knows from her own travels.

The caravan of gold and spice is the image that outsiders inherited, and Scheele asks readers to separate Saharan from trans-Saharan trade: the second is the part that crosses the region and so leaves traces in archaeological sites and in sources written beyond it. Most Saharan trade, she suggests, was in staples, the cereals, dates, salt, cloth, dried meat and skins that groups such as the Arba’a and the Tubu carried. The fabled gold was something the explorer René Caillié never saw in Timbuktu.

The trade in staples survives, and it remains, in Scheele’s phrase, “relatively democratic”: anyone with a four-by-four, some capital and enough cousins along the road can become a carrier or trade on their own account, and negotiate with Malian customs officials. She also notes that the advance of trade routes, and the political rivalries that followed in the Maghreb, pushed North Africans deeper into the desert until they had little choice but to become trans-Saharan traders. Mobility, here, was as much pressure as opportunity. In northern Mali, she visits al-Khalil in 2009 and finds its trade booming. The oldest permanent house there dates from 1993 and began as a store for arms for the separatist rebellion of the early 1990s. Commerce, rebellion and settlement, in the Sahara, are often built with the same walls. What these cases share is a desert that is never empty. It is inhabited not by permanent settlements alone but by routes, encounters, negotiations, and obligations.

Scheele applies the same method to the subjects that dominate the headlines. Slavery, racism, religious militancy, terrorism and desertification each get their own treatment, and in each case, as a 

reviewer for

 

Foreign Affairs

 

notes

, she shows how familiar narratives often grow out of outsiders’ fantasies of the desert as an inhospitable, impermeable barrier. She does not romanticize that circulation. The same routes carried enslaved people, reproduced racial hierarchies and concentrated wealth in few hands. Nor did colonial rule invent every division: Saharan societies had their own rivalries and territorial distinctions. But colonial administrations hardened them into borders drawn around distant capitals, and began to treat older routes as marginal, illicit, or dangerous. Independent states inherited that architecture, and with it a contradiction: communities keep depending on cross-border movement, while official policy reads that movement as a failure of control.

This is why emptiness is never an innocent description. Calling an inhabited space empty lets existing relationships be ignored and makes outside intervention look like the first arrival of order, development or connectivity. Once a territory is imagined as a void, the people who live there are easily treated as obstacles to somebody else’s project.

That contradiction is not a historical footnote; it is what the current diplomacy is fought over. Tin Zaouatine is a border town that both capitals see as a security problem. 

ADF Magazine

 

reports

 that Algeria fears fighting between Mali’s army and Tuareg rebels could spread to Algeria’s own Tuareg population. For the people who live there, kinship, trade and pasture run across a line that governments treat as the front of a dispute. Scheele’s history makes visible what the security language hides: that the border cuts through communities, rather than between them.

The same tension runs through the Alliance of Sahel States. Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger left the Economic Community of West African States in 2025 in the name of sovereignty, and their ministers have discussed 

harmonized travel and identity documents

 to ease movement among their own citizens. Yet, as the Migration Policy Institute observes, their exit 

exposed a tension between regional free-movement commitments and tightening security controls

. Mobility is being re-sorted by membership: it is a right for some and suspicious for everyone else.

Niger shows how fast the rules can turn. In November 2023, its military government repealed a 2015 law that had criminalized the transport of migrants. By April 2025, it was warning, 

according to AFP

, that mass arrivals of non-Nigerien migrants expelled from Algeria could upset the country’s security balance. The same movement is a trade, a crime, or a threat, depending on who is moving, in which direction, and which capital is speaking.

Policy built on the same imagination misses what keeps people alive. Security strategies aim to close routes without asking what work, exchange, and mutual dependence those routes sustain. Development programs talk of integrating peripheral regions that have long been integrated into networks that do not follow national maps. And the cost of getting it wrong falls on the people with the least power to contest it: those left at Point Zéro, who must walk through the desert to Assamaka, with some reportedly dying along the way, according to 

UNHCR, IOM and the Mixed Migration Centre

.

Scheele’s book resolves none of this. But it changes what counts as normal. If circulation has been the Sahara’s ordinary condition for centuries, then drivers, traders, pastoralists, and migrants are not anomalies to be managed; they are the region’s own infrastructure. The question for the people in and around the desert is not what Europe should learn from the past. It is who decides which crossings count as trade, which as trafficking, and which as a threat; and who ends up at Point Zéro when the answer changes.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Shameful": Fossil Fuel Industry Blocks U.N. Climate Action as Global Warming Reaches 1.5°C
content:
As 

Democracy Now!

 continues broadcasting from the U.N. climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, we speak with Rachel Cleetus, climate program director at the Union of Concerned Scientists, about climate finance — the notion that efforts to mitigate the climate crisis must be funded. “Climate finance is not an abstract thing. It’s what countries need to be able to transition away from fossil fuels,” says Cleetus. “And right now we have pennies in these funds.” She notes that at a pledging event for the Adaptation Fund, which supports climate finance for developing countries, a mere $50 million was pledged. “It’s shameful, absolutely unjust, what’s happening here. And richer countries are continuing to block progress.” This comes as scientists say the world is set to overshoot the target, set by the 2015 Paris Agreement, of limiting global heating to 1.5 degrees Celsius.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Ecocide": Colombia's New Right-Wing Gov't Ends Amazon Protections, Rejects Fossil Fuel Phaseout
content:
The U.N. climate summit comes seven months after a major climate meeting was held in Santa Marta, Colombia, where more than 50 countries gathered for a groundbreaking effort to push for phasing out fossil fuels to combat the climate crisis. The initiative was championed by Colombian President Gustavo Petro, whose term ended in August, but Colombia’s new right-wing President Abelardo de la Espriella has withdrawn Colombia from the Santa Marta coalition.




“Colombia has just reversed the protection of the Amazon,” says Irene Vélez-Torres, former Colombian environment minister under Petro. “What we are seeing is really an ecocide taking place in Colombia.”




Meanwhile, at COP31, “there are petro lobbyists, people here defending the interest of the corporations, and therefore the discussions cannot make any progress,” Vélez-Torres adds. “The agreements cannot even mention the word 'fossil fuels.'”

author: James Hamill
title: A Disaster Waiting to Happen?  Brent Bozell and the US-South Africa Relationship
content:
President Donald Trump’s appointment of Leo Brent Bozell as the United States ambassador to South Africa in 2025 was a deliberately provocative act on his part. The appointment always seemed purposely designed to further damage a US-South Africa bilateral relationship which was already fraught due to differences over South Africa’s domestic and foreign policy choices. Put bluntly, for decades Bozell has been a conservative activist not a diplomat and he lacks the basic skills set to hold such an important and sensitive position Trump appoints Leo Brent Bozell III, a defender of apartheid in the 1980s, as ambassador to South Africa | U.S. | EL PAÍS English. As his behaviour in South Africa is demonstrating, that is an environment likely to produce partisan ideologues rather than people with the tact, nuance, patience, and knowledge required for high level inter-state diplomacy. Since taking up the role of US ambassador in February 2026, he has consistently abused his position through hostile posturing and ‘megaphone diplomacy.’ He has disrespected South Africa’s independent judiciary, publicly berated the host government, and has persistently interfered in South African domestic politics – in clear violation of Article 41.1 of the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, 1961– by aligning himself with Afrikaner nationalist groupings, Afriforum and Solidarity, and amplifying their grievances Between candour and coercion — why SA won’t bend to Washington’s dictates. He has issued a series of ‘asks’ – US demands in effect – on issues such as farm murders and rural crime, Black Economic Empowerment, land expropriation without compensation in exceptional circumstances US to make SA to pay the price of doing nothing. Consequently, he has now been démarched – summoned to receive a diplomatic reprimand – by the South African Department of International Relations and Co-operation on no less than three separate occasions in 2026: in March (after less than one month in position), June and September Dirco summons US ambassador Bozell again over ‘undiplomatic conduct’.

Bozell’s ‘extraordinary experience’ All of this was very predictable. Bozell’s appointment has captured in microcosm the broader failings of the Trump administration’s approach to diplomacy and international relations: it was incendiary and was designed primarily to appease white nationalist opinion within Trump’s MAGA base rather than to help mend US-South African relations. In a reversal of standard diplomatic practice, Bozell was sent to South Africa to exacerbate rather than ease tensions and to promote discord. Although Trump stated that Bozell brought ‘extraordinary experience’ to his role Trump appoints Leo Brent Bozell III, a defender of apartheid in the 1980s, as ambassador to South Africa | U.S. | EL PAÍS English, it is actually his South African ‘experience’ which is the main problem. Bozell has a long history of opposition to the African National Congress (ANC) whom he labelled ‘terrorists’ during the 1980s liberation struggle era. He enlisted his National Conservative Political Action Committee in a so-called ‘Coalition Against ANC Terrorism’, a collection of American conservative groupings supportive of the apartheid regime. He strongly opposed the US’s opening of formal diplomatic contacts with the ANC, initiated by then Secretary of State George Shultz in January 1987, in which the Reagan administration effectively acknowledged that there could be no long term South African settlement without its involvement Trump’s Pick For Ambassador To South Africa Actively Opposed Fight To End Apartheid. Bozell was also hostile to the liberation struggle per se as was demonstrated by his support in the 1980s for the regime of President P W Botha, his opposition to the global anti-apartheid movement, and his opposition to the US sanctions contained in the Comprehensive Anti-Apartheid Act (CAAA) of October 1986. The CAAA proved to be of crucial importance in intensifying pressure on the regime and helping to move South Africa beyond apartheid. Anyone doubting its impact need only look at the striking similarity between the US demands, as set out in the CAAA, and the changes announced by President F W De Klerk in his historic speech of 2nd February 1990, over three years later. Bozell was profoundly wrong on everything South Africa-related in the 1980s: wrong to attempt to shore up a failing Botha regime which was leading the country to destruction, wrong to oppose US sanctions, and wrong in his animus towards the most important liberation movement, the ANC. Had Bozell’s approach prevailed, South Africa’s post-Botha breakthrough in 1989-90 would have been delayed and the country would have continued along a path of terminal political and economic decline. His prejudices were advertised again when he bemoaned the ‘mythologizing’ of Nelson Mandela following the iconic former president’s death in 2013 Trump’s Pick For Ambassador To South Africa Actively Opposed Fight To End Apartheid. Causing offence Appointing someone with such a track record to the post of US ambassador to South Africa, a country in which the ANC is the largest party in a government of national unity, was designed to cause offence and provided legitimate grounds for South Africa to refuse Bozell agrément under Article 4.2 of the 1961 Vienna Convention Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, 1961. By choosing not to do so, South Africa was taking a more conciliatory approach, opting to look forward not back and signalling its openness to a genuine bilateral dialogue. This stood in marked contrast to the Trump administration’s behaviour when it declared Ebrahim Rasool, South Africa’s ambassador to the US, persona non grata in March 2025 for comments he had made criticising Trump. Unfortunately for Pretoria, this has been interpreted in Washington as weakness, and it has given greater impetus to its determination to bring an errant South Africa to heel. The Bozell appointment confirmed the Trump administration’s overt hostility – and that of its support base – to a post-1994 democratic South Africa which, it is worth noting, would not exist at all had Bozell’s approach prevailed. South Africa is viewed by Washington as a standard bearer for the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion policies so loathed by this administration. Its opposition to the US attacks on Iran in 2025-26 and the genocide case it has brought against Israel before the International Court of Justice have only deepened the antagonism. Stormy waters On Ambassador Bozell’s watch, US-South Africa relations are set to deteriorate further as a confrontational relationship now seems to be Washington’s objective. This was confirmed on November 2 by its decision to remove South Africa from the US African Growth and Opportunity Act of 2000 under which many products from African states enjoy duty free access to the American market US removes South Africa from Agoa trade pact. That expulsion will take effect from January 2027. True, South Africa is not unique among contemporary democracies in having its sovereignty persistently challenged and undermined by the current US administration. Brazil, Canada, Denmark, Germany, Poland, Romania, Spain, and Ukraine have all found themselves at the sharp end of this established pattern of US interference and coercion The U.S. Is Bullying Europe Like Never Before – The Atlantic. However, in a world where we are witnessing genocidal violence in Gaza, Myanmar, Sudan, and Ukraine, the Trump administration has chosen to identify South Africa as an adversary deserving of special opprobrium and punitive sanctions. This is a South Africa which, despite its many failings and huge challenges, has a robust democratic infrastructure with regular free elections (its latest municipal elections were held on 4 November), an admirable constitution, a free press, a thriving civil society, and an independent judiciary. That it has become the target of such deep and sustained US hostility perhaps tells us more about the Trump administration than it does about contemporary South Africa.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Voices from Turkey: "The More Oppressive the Regime Gets, the More Resilient People Become"
content:
As climate negotiations enter their crucial final stretch in the last few days of COP31, held in Antalya, Turkey, dozens of human rights groups urged Turkish authorities to release four LGBTQ+ activists ahead of a hearing that has just begun at a court in Istanbul. Back in September, Turkish authorities began a large-scale crackdown on LGBTQ+ organizations and activists, raiding offices, blocking social media accounts and websites, arresting at least 116 people and launching criminal investigations into at least 160 people. Meanwhile, since last month, Turkey’s last two remaining opposition television channels have been brought under government control. This follows the Turkish government’s widespread crackdown on the main opposition party with dozens of mayors arrested since 2024.




Despite Turkey’s authoritarianism, in Antalya, many of the Turkish groups critical of the government gathered in large numbers at the People’s Climate Summit, an alternative gathering to the U.N. climate summit organized by a coalition of Turkish environmental groups. For more, we hear from a number of activists from across Turkish civil society, including Berkan Özyer, the director of Greenpeace Türkiye, who tells us that “the more oppressive [a] regime gets, the more resilient people become.”

author: Dominique Gené - Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: No charges to be laid against police in 2024 Salluit shooting
content:
Police won’t face charges in a 2024 shooting incident in Salluit that left a 26-year-old dead and his twin brother injured.




Quebec’s director of criminal and penal prosecutions announced the decision Tuesday in a news release.




Prosecutors reviewed an independent investigation report into the incident prepared by Bureau des enquêtes indépendantes, Quebec’s police watchdog, and determined there is no evidence that the officers involved committed a crime.




Early on Nov. 4, 2024, two Nunavik Police Service officers responded to a report of impaired driving, a news release from Bureau des enquêtes indépendantes said at the time of the incident.




Minutes later, an altercation broke out between the officers and two people, later identified as Joshua Papigatuk and Garnet Papigatuk. Police used a stun gun and pepper spray to try to control them.




An officer fired a gun once in the direction of one of the individuals, who was injured. A struggle continued with the second person, and more shots were fired. Joshua Papigatuk was 

pronounced dead

, and Garnet Papigatuk was medevaced.




The incident, which was the first of 

several

 deaths to occur in incidents with Nunavik Police officers, 

spurred protests

 in multiple Nunavik communities and 

calls for police reform

.
















Garnet Papigatuk, who has since recovered from his injuries, 

faces

 assault and obstruction charges in connection with the incident.




Prosecutors met with relatives, including Garnet, Tuesday to inform them of the decision, the prosecutor’s office news release said.




No further details about the decision will be released while charges against Garnet Papigatuk remain before the courts, the release said. Prosecutors cited the need to protect the fairness and integrity of the judicial process.




Once a verdict has been reached, prosecutors will meet again with Garnet Papigatuk and his relatives to explain in detail why no charges were laid against the officers.




Prosecutors also said they will release a public statement summarizing the events and explaining the reasons behind the decision.

author: anred
title: El cine argentino tendrá una maratón federal de 24 horas de películas, debates y actividades gratuitas
content:
Este viernes 20 de noviembre, a las 19, comenzará “24 horas por el Cine Argentino”, una iniciativa colectiva que propone una transmisión gratuita e ininterrumpida por YouTube hasta las 19 del sábado 21, que reunirá películas de distintos géneros y épocas, conversaciones, entrevistas y debates con realizadores, actores y trabajadores de la industria audiovisual. La propuesta tendrá también una dimensión presencial: salas alternativas, centros culturales, cineclubes y festivales de distintas localidades organizarán proyecciones y actividades para compartir el cine nacional. Entre las directoras que impulsan la convocatoria se encuentran Celina Murga, Jazmín Stuart, Ana García Blaya y Virna Molina. La convocatoria es una apuesta a visibilizar la importancia del cine como expresión artística e industria cultural, en un escenario atravesado por el ajuste sobre el Instituto Nacional de Cine y Artes Audiovisuales (INCAA), el debilitamiento de los organismos públicos y los recortes presupuestarios en distintas áreas culturales impulsadas por el gobierno de Javier Milei, donde las trabajadoras y los trabajadores del sector buscan sostener espacios de producción, exhibición y circulación de las obras nacionales. 

Por ANRed.







El cine argentino tendrá una jornada especial de celebración colectiva con una maratón federal de películas, encuentros y actividades gratuitas. Se trata de 

“24 horas por el Cine Argentino”

, una iniciativa que comenzará este viernes 20 de noviembre a las 19 y se extenderá hasta el sábado 21 a la misma hora, con una transmisión ininterrumpida a través de YouTube y propuestas presenciales en distintos puntos del país.




La convocatoria reúne a 

realizadores, directores, actores, productores, técnicos, estudiantes y trabajadores de la industria audiovisual

. Entre las referentes que impulsan la iniciativa se encuentran las directoras 

Celina Murga, Jazmín Stuart, Ana García Blaya y Virna Molina,

 junto a un colectivo de personas vinculadas con la producción, exhibición y difusión cinematográfica.




La propuesta busca generar un espacio de encuentro entre quienes hacen cine, quienes trabajan para que las películas lleguen a las pantallas y el público. Durante las 24 horas habrá una transmisión gratuita por el canal de YouTube 

@24hsporElCineArgentino

, con películas, entrevistas, conversaciones, mesas de debate, invitados especiales y conexiones con distintas provincias.







En paralelo, salas alternativas, centros culturales, cineclubes y festivales de diferentes localidades organizarán proyecciones de películas nacionales, charlas y debates. La convocatoria permanece abierta a los espacios culturales y de exhibición que quieran sumarse, así como a espectadores y espectadoras que deseen participar de las actividades en sus ciudades.




La programación busca mostrar la amplitud de la cinematografía nacional: desde el cine de autor y experimental hasta las películas populares y de género, con producciones de distintas épocas.

 Entre los títulos mencionados se encuentran obras de Leopoldo Torre Nilsson y Leonardo Favio, junto a realizaciones contemporáneas.




“

El cine nacional siempre estuvo ahí, contando nuestras historias; las que solo puede contar alguien de acá. Celebrarlo es una tarea cotidiana, pero el objetivo ahora es ir por más

”, expresaron desde la organización en el comunicado de lanzamiento. Y agregaron: “

una obra audiovisual no termina al llegar a la pantalla, el televisor o los dispositivos móviles; cobra su verdadero sentido cuando encuentra a su público y, muy especialmente, cuando se comparte

”.







La iniciativa propone, así, una celebración que trasciende la pantalla y apuesta a fortalecer los vínculos entre las películas y sus públicos. En un contexto en el que la producción y la circulación del cine nacional necesitan espacios de visibilidad y encuentro, la convocatoria invita a participar de una jornada colectiva para compartir historias, miradas y expresiones de la cultura audiovisual argentina.




La transmisión podrá seguirse gratuitamente desde el canal de YouTube 

@24hsporElCineArgentino

.

 Para conocer las actividades presenciales, la organización invita a consultar las redes oficiales y comunicarse con las salas alternativas, centros culturales, cineclubes y festivales de cada localidad.




La convocatoria también es 

una forma de organización y resistencia cultural col

ectiva frente a las políticas de desfinanciamiento y desarticulación de la cultura impulsadas por el gobierno de Javier Milei

. En un escenario atravesado por el 

ajuste sobre el Instituto Nacional de Cine y Artes Audiovisuales (INCAA), el debilitamiento de los organismos públicos y los recortes presupuestarios en distintas áreas culturales

, las trabajadoras y los trabajadores del sector buscan sostener espacios de producción, exhibición y circulación de las obras nacionales. 

Frente a un modelo que pone en riesgo la continuidad de proyectos, fuentes laborales y políticas de fomento, la iniciativa apuesta a visibilizar la importancia del cine como expresión artística, industria cultural y herramienta para contar las propias historias

.

author: Gastbeitrag
title: Jetzt wird abgerechnet! – Wie das Gaza Tribunal die deutsche Komplizenschaft im Genozid auf die Anklagebank setzt
content:
Deutschland auf der Anklagebank: Wie lautet das juristische Urteil über die jahrelange deutsche Unterstützung Israels bei dem brutal wütenden Genozid an der palästinensischen Bevölkerung? Das Gaza Tribunal der Initiative 

„

Deutschen JuristInnen für das Völkerrecht“

 rechnet mit der deutschen Komplizenschaft ab und zeigt die zahlreichen Verletzungen des Völkerrechts durch die deutsche Beteiligung am Genozid in Gaza unerbittlich auf.







In Deutschland werden völkerrechtliche Bestimmungen wie die UN‑Charta der Menschenrechte in manchen Fällen wirklich ernst genommen. So ernst, dass sie hervorragend als Rechtfertigungen für militärische Interventionen im globalen Süden taugen, die für Region häufig destabilisierend sind, sich aber gut in die eigene Interessenslage fügen. Währenddessen werden die völkerrechtlichen Bestimmungen zur Verhinderung vom Genozid im Fall von Gaza eher als optionale Handlungsgrundlage angesehen. Dieser Doppelstandard, der für den Großteil der Weltbevölkerung unschwer zu erkennen ist, bleibt in Deutschland selbst ein hochumstrittenes Thema.




Die Initiative „

Deutschen JuristInnen für das Völkerrecht“

 hat bereits zum zweiten Mal am 24.10.2026 – dem 81. Jubiläum der UN‑Charta – mit hochkarätigen Expert:innen zum 

Gaza Tribunal

 geladen. Von Ärzt:innen, die in Gaza vor Ort sind, über Teilnehmende der Flotilla, Rechtsanwälte, kritische Journalist:innen, über den ECCHR und Berater:innen der EU wird sachlich und juristisch fundiert ein vernichtendes Urteil über die letzten drei Jahre der deutschen Unterstützung des Genozids gefällt.




„Die völkerrechtlichen Rechtsbrüche sind so eindeutig wie zahlreich. Wo soll man anfangen, wo kann man aufhören?“




In sechs Sessions wurden Rechtsbrüche wie die genozidale Zerstörung des palästinensischen Gesundheitssystems, deutsche Waffenexporte, die Repression von Widerstand, der fehlende Schutz der Flotilla-Teilnehmenden und die Rolle der Medien sowie der EU beleuchtet. Es geht beim Gaza Tribunal nicht um eine rein moralische Anklage: Es ist eine sachliche Abrechnung und Untersuchung der deutschen Regierung an dem völkerrechtlichen Maßstab, den sie selbst propagiert.




Sei es die Verletzung von Art. 2 der Völkermordkonvention, bei der nicht nur unmittelbare Tötungen zählen, sondern auch auferlegte Lebensbedingungen, die auf die physische Zerstörung einer Gruppe ausgerichtet sind. Die genozidale Absicht der israelischen Regierung wird von der Initiative 

Physicians for Human Rights Israel

 an zahlreichen Punkten nachgewiesen: An der Zerstörung von Krankenhäusern, Netanyahus Riviera-Vorstellung und an Aussagen wie „no electricity, no food, no fuel“ durch israelische Amtsträger:innen. Karam Chehade 

(

Gaza Care Bridge

)

 berichtet von 18.000 Schwerkranken, die ein Jahr nach dem „Waffenstillstand“ auf Evakuierung warten. Die Rechtsanwältin Tugba Sezer erklärt, warum die Gruppenaufnahme palästinensischer Geflüchteter am Einvernehmen des Bundesinnenministeriums scheitert.




Auch die weiter stattfindenden Waffenlieferungen von Deutschland als zweitwichtigstem Lieferanten Israels verstoßen offensichtlich gegen Völkerrecht, da sie gegen Zivilist:innen oder medizinisches Personal eingesetzt werden. Alexander Schwarz vom ECCHR berichtet, dass in rund einem Dutzend Verfahren kein deutsches Gericht die Rechtmäßigkeit einer Genehmigung überhaupt inhaltlich überprüfte – ironischerweise aber die Existenz dieser Verfahren vor dem IGH gerne als Beleg für umfassende gerichtliche Kontrolle angibt.




Bei der deutschen Repression des Widerstands gegen den Genozid, wird Entrechtung bereits systematisch als Methode verwendet, wie Alexander Gorski erläutert. Er vertritt als Rechtsanwalt sowohl Abdallah A., dem die 

Einbürgerung wegen zweier Social-Media-Posts verweigert wurde

, als auch 

Hüseyin Doğru

, der wegen seiner kritischen Berichterstattung mit EU‑Sanktionen belegt wurde. Zudem ist auch der Anwalt von Z., der nach dem Samidoun-Verbot mit einem Ausweisungsverfahren belegt wurde und mittlerweile auf der US-amerikanischen Terrorliste steht – ohne überhaupt irgendwelche Vorstrafen zu haben. Alle drei Fälle haben eins gemeinsam: Der deutsche Staat schärft seine juristischen Repressionswerkzeuge und bringt das Migrations- und Staatsangehörigkeitsrecht in Anschlag gegen die von Migrant:innen getragene palästinensische Solidaritätsbewegung.




Auch die Verteidigung der 

„Ulm 5“

 berichtet über die fragwürdigen juristischen Methoden, mit denen fünf Aktivist:innen, die im September 2025 bei Elbit Systems in Ulm Geräte zerstörten und laut Verteidigung friedlich auf ihre Festnahme warteten, konfrontiert werden. Beweisanträge zu Elbit und zum Genozid in Gaza blieben sechs Monate unbeantwortet, die geladenen Sachverständigen wurden nicht gehört und ihre Expertise für irrelevant erklärt. Zugleich verneinte das Gericht einen Zusammenhang zwischen den Ulmer Produkten und der israelischen Kriegsführung.




Die Teilnehmenden der 

Global Sumud Flotilla

 berichten wiederum von brutaler sexualisierter Gewalt, Schlägen, Elektroschocks und der schweren Misshandlung palästinensischer Gefangener. Das Auswärtige Amt blieb untätig. Auch wenn sie als deutsche Staatsbürger die relative Gewissheit einer späteren Freilassung gehabt haben, stellt der Rettungssanitäter Johannes Happel klar: 

„[Das ist eine] Gewissheit, die tausende palästinensische Geiseln in den israelischen Konzentrationslagern bis heute nicht haben.“




Auch Prof. Nick Maynard, Vorsitzender von 

Medical Aid for Palestinians

, berichtet von der unfassbaren sexualisierten Gewalt, die gegen palästinensische Männer, Frauen und Kinder in Gaza, in israelischer Haft und im Westjordanland angewendet wird. Die jahrzehntelang dokumentierte Gewalt ist Teil einer systematischen Politik ethnischer Säuberung, die den Willen der palästinensischen Bevölkerung zu brechen versucht.




Auch die deutschen Medien machen sich häufig zum Komplizen des Genozids. Dazu zählt nicht nur die 

skandalöse Berichterstattung

 von den großen Leitmedien, die, wie die Tagesschau, in ihrer höchst ausgewogenen Berichterstattung so gut wie keine palästinensische Stimme zu Wort kommen lässt und allzu häufig mit der IDF als einziger Quelle auskommt, wie Sabine Schiffer vom 

Institut für Medienverantwortung

 klarmacht. Auch berichtet der Journalist Mirko Keilbert, dass Chefredaktionen bei vermeintlich „zu pro-palästinensischen“ Beiträgen Anrufe der israelischen Botschaft erhalten, um das ein oder andere Wort zu streichen. Kein Wunder, dass nur noch 27 Prozent der Deutschen die Nahost-Berichterstattung für glaubwürdig halten.




Nicht zuletzt gibt es die wirklich unschwer zu verstehende Tatsache, dass die EU rechtlich daran gebunden ist, keine Staaten zu unterstützen, die einen Genozid begehen. Dafür braucht es kein weiteres Gerichtsurteil, keine Genehmigung des EU‑Rats. Die UN‑Untersuchungskommission hat bereits die genozidale Absicht der israelischen Politik festgestellt. Die schiere Anzahl an verletzten europäischen Abkommen, Verträgen und Gerichtsurteilen, die der ehemalige EU-Berater Lucio Gussetti und weitere Referent:innen aufzeigen, ist erdrückend.




Was in Deutschland gerne als hochkomplexes Thema dargestellt wird, das unfassbares Fachwissen erfordert, ist bei einer juristischen Untersuchung doch recht eindeutig: Deutschland macht sich auf skandalöse und brutale Art an dem Genozid in Gaza mitschuldig und muss diese Beteiligung nach Befolgen seines eigenen Rechts sofort beenden.




Die grausame Ironie einer so bedingungslosen deutschen Unterstützung eines weiteren Genozids, der mit der historischen Verantwortung für den Holocaust gerechtfertigt wird, ist so absurd wie verheerend. Wichtige völkerrechtliche Bestimmungen wie die UN‑Charta und die Genozidkonvention wurden nach dem Zweiten Weltkrieg auf Initiative der Alliierten u.a. als Reaktion auf den Holocaust und die vielen weiteren genozidalen Verbrechen während des deutschen Faschismus geschaffen. Klar kann man sich fragen: Was, wenn nicht der Genozid in Gaza, hat gezeigt, dass das Völkerrecht aber nur dann gilt, wenn sie für die Interessenslage der mächtigen Staaten des globalen Nordens nützlich sind? Und es quasi konsequenzenlos ignoriert wird, wenn Staaten wie die USA oder Deutschland von der Unterstützung eines Genozids politisch profitieren?




Klar sollte man den universellen Charakter und die edlen Absichten hinter der Schaffung des Völkerrechts in Zweifel ziehen. Allerdings nicht auf Kosten einer Strategie, die alle Register zieht und auch die breite Bevölkerung mit einbezieht, die bisher doch eher untätig bleibt bei ihrer doch mehrheitlichen Nichtzustimmung zum Genozid. Die juristische Einordnung und öffentliche Skandalisierung dieser völkerrechtlichen Rechtsbrüche ist und bleibt eine wichtige Grundlage dafür. Denn der Kampf gegen den Genozid muss an allen Fronten gekämpft werden: vor den Waffenfabriken, auf den Demos, im Betrieb, an den Unis, in den Medien und juristisch. Das Gaza Tribunal hat gesprochen. 




Das komplette Tribunal kann man hier anschauen.




Foto: 

Vordergrund




Der Beitrag 

Jetzt wird abgerechnet! – Wie das Gaza Tribunal die deutsche Komplizenschaft im Genozid auf die Anklagebank setzt

 erschien zuerst auf 

Lower Class Magazine

.

author: anred
title: Mala Fama y los desaparecidos de Lozadur: los crímenes de la dictadura llegaron al prime time televisivo
content:
El popular cantante contó en el programa de Andy Kusnetzoff que su padre fue un perseguido de la represión por su participación en el sindicato ceramista. Al otro día, la Comisión Provincial por la Memoria dio a conocer que esa persecución está registrada en el archivo de la Dirección de Inteligencia de la Policía de la Provincia de Buenos Aires (DIPPBA). Un relato inesperado que colocó a la lucha por los derechos humanos en el pico del rating. Aquí, toda la historia.

 

Por Leo Vázquez, para Canal Abierto.







El fin de semana tuvo una insospechada declaración televisiva vinculada a los crímenes de la dictadura. El cantante 

Hernán Coronel

, más conocido como 

Mala Fama

 por su trayectoria en el grupo de cumbia de ese mismo nombre, contó en el programa 

Podemos Hablar

 que conduce 

Andy Kusnetzoff

 

en Telefé

 que su padre fue un perseguido por las patotas del terrorismo de Estado.




Así, una historia de las tantas que componen la lucha del movimiento de derechos humanos llegó sorpresivamente al prime time televisivo, de la mano de un declarante también poco habitual.




El músico, que además está en un altísimo nivel de exposición pública por su participación en el programa 

Máster Chef

, recordó que su papá tenía que dormir en una carpa en la azotea de la casa porque era buscado por la represión por ser parte del sindicato de 

Lozadur

, la fábrica de platos y tazas de loza y cerámica de Villa Adelina, partido de San Isidro, que tiene al menos diez desaparecidos

 entre sus trabajadores.







«MI PAPÁ SE IBA A DORMIR AL TECHO POR SI VENÍAN LOS MILITARES A SACARLO»: BRUTAL RELATO DE HERNÁN DE MALA FAMA




«Mi papá pertenecía a un sindicato.. la dictadura hizo desaparecer al presidente del sindicato, al otro, y como que se venía él»




«Me imagino él, lo que es estar ahí durmiendo en esa carpa, si entran y matan a mi familia o si matan a mí, mi familia se queda sin el sostén»




#PodemosHablar




— Revolución Popular (@RPN_Oficial) 

November 15, 2026







Al otro día, la 

Comisión Provincial por la Memoria

 dio a conocer que esa persecución está registrada en el archivo 

DIPPBA

, la Dirección de Inteligencia de la Policía de la Provincia de Buenos Aires.




“En 1975 los ceramistas reclamaban mejoras salariales pese a los intentos del gobierno de Isabel Perón de congelar los salarios. La represión en Lozadur se sintió antes del golpe: el 13 de febrero de 1976 fue asesinado Juan Pablo Lobos, delegado gremial de fábrica y vocal suplente de la Federación de Obreros Ceramistas”, comenzó narrando el organismo de derechos humanos.







“Posiblemente, esta sea la historia detrás de lo que contó Hernán sobre su padre”.




Lozadur fue una fábrica de cerámicos instalada en Villa Adelina en 1939. Llegó a tener una planta de 1.200 trabajadores, en su mayoría mujeres.







“Las condiciones de trabajo –pago por pieza terminada y no por tiempo de trabajo, altas temperaturas y enfermedades respiratorias por falta de extractores de polvillo- fueron algunos de los factores que llevaron al movimiento obrero ceramista a impulsar ocupaciones fabriles”, siguió describiendo la CPM.




“Ya en la dictadura –continúa el relato-, 

los primeros informes de inteligencia sobre la actividad fabril comienzan con un legajo de la serie “Huelgas y conflictos” donde se comunica que los trabajadores de la planta realizan trabajo a desgano como medida de fuerza

. Según la DIPPBA, el conflicto comenzó durante los primeros días de octubre de 1977”.




“El 3 de noviembre de 1977 la dictadura secuestró trabajadoras y trabajadores de Lozadur: Dominga Abadía Crespo, Felicidad Abadía Crespo, Sofía Cardozo, Elba Puente, Ismael Notaliberto, Francisco Palavecino y Ramón Pablo Villanueva. Todavía continúan desaparecidos”.







El 3 de noviembre de 1977 la dictadura secuestró trabajadoras y trabajadores de Lozadur: Dominga Abadía Crespo, Felicidad Abadía Crespo, Sofía Cardozo, Elba Puente, Ismael Notaliberto, Francisco Palavecino y Ramón Pablo Villanueva. Todavía continúan desaparecidos.




Varios de ellos fueron fichados por la DIPPBA. Podés conocer sus historias en https://t.co/70LYGVfu2d




— Comisión Provincial por la Memoria (@CPMemoria) 

November 15, 2026







Varios de ellos fueron fichados por la DIPPBA. Sus historias están en 

https://siemprepresentes.org.ar




La asamblea, la fábrica y la memoria




En la actualidad, la 

Asamblea Lozadur Para los Vecinos

 intenta lograr que una parte del lugar donde funcionó la histórica fábrica de cerámicas sea destinada a un parque de la memoria y a un centro de formación profesional con orientación ceramista. Luchan por preservar la historia obrera del lugar y recuperar para uso comunitario un sector que actualmente se encuentra semiabandonado.




La pelea es contra la amenaza de que en ese lugar se construyan edificios a partir de la reciente modificación del Código de Ordenamiento Urbano que habilitó la construcción de torres más altas.




El intendente actual del partido de San Isidro es Ramón Lanús, del PRO / Juntos por el Cambio, quien junto a los bloques oficialistas y aliados del Concejo Deliberante local impulsan un desarrollo inmobiliario.




Uno de los principales reclamos está vinculado con la memoria de los trabajadores de la fábrica. Los vecinos buscan reconstruir esa historia mediante la recopilación de documentos, testimonios y otros materiales.




Canal Abierto

 dio cuenta de la iniciativa 

en un extenso artículo que refleja la voz de los vecinos organizados:




“Es un reclamo que representa intereses comunitarios, esa historia trágica tiene un pasado bastante sombrío y sangriento, hay trabajadores desaparecidos, la nomina de la embajada de Estados Unidos habla de más de 20, nosotros damos fe de que son seguro 10 obreros de la planta, entonces queremos preservar esa memoria”.




El sitio podría tener el mismo triste destino que el Astillero Astarsa en Tigre, transformado a partir de 2011 en el barrio náutico privado Venice Ciudad Navegable. El taller de barcos fue escenario de grandes conflictos y represión durante la dictadura, fue ocupado por el ejército desde 1976 y al menos 16 trabajadores fueron desaparecidos.




Lesa humanidad




En 2014, un juicio por delitos de lesa humanidad que investigó la represión al cordón fabril de la zona norte del conurbano bonaerense terminó con condenas para el genocida de Campo de Mayo Santiago Omar Riveros, el dictador Reynaldo Bignone y otros siete represores. Muchos de los delitos probados en el debate fueron perpetrados contra 32 trabajadores de los astilleros Astarsa y Mestrina, Cerámicas Cattáneo y Porcelanas Lozadur.




De esa causa se desprendió otro expediente que apuntó contra la participación civil. En 2023, la jueza de San Martín Alicia Vence citó a un grupo de exdirectivos y exgerentes de las dos compañías ceramistas a prestar declaración por su participación en 15 secuestros. Se trata de los empresarios Carlos Garparutti, Alfredo Katzenstein, Alfonso Amoroso, José Penas y Miguel Puigdevall. El proceso es uno de los tantos que espera llegar a juicio oral.







La historia




Lozadur era una empresa ceramista líder a nivel nacional e internacional, asentada desde hacía varias décadas en Villa Adelina. Proveía de vajilla de loza y porcelana a todo el país y a países vecinos. Su productividad se basaba en la numerosa mano de obra, con más de 1.000 trabajadores y momentos de 3.000, en su mayoría mujeres y con bajos salarios.




Sus orígenes se remontan a 1939 y en plena dictadura, tras los conflictos de finales 1977, la planta fue intervenida y varios de sus delegados y obreros fueron detenidos y desaparecidos. En el 85 la empresa se convirtió en cooperativa y en el 87 finalmente cerró. En memoria de esas luchas, el 30 de octubre se conmemora el Día del Trabajador Ceramista.

title: Lettere occupata: abbiamo detto che volevamo tutto, è tempo di prendercelo. Il nostro momento è ora!
content:
In un ateneo che svende il diritto allo studio e ci leva ogni spazio di socialità, occupare e riprenderci i nostri luoghi è il primo passo per rendere l’università davvero nostra; in un paese governato da chi risponde esclusivamente a interessi che non sono i nostri, la mobilitazione è l’unica strada che possiamo percorrere, la nostra generazione ha già riempito le piazze contro il caro vita, noi sappiamo benissimo contro chi puntare il dito: chi impoverisce questo paese per devastarne altri; chi specula sulle nostre città erodendo i diritti allo studio e alla casa.




Università e carovita

Ci siamo rottз di questo clima di precarietà, che aggravato da un mostruoso aumento dei prezzi ha reso insostenibile pagare un affitto, fare la spesa e fare il pieno alla macchina. Nel nostro caso ciò vuol dire anche fare i conti con tasse universitarie spropositate se confrontate con i servizi offerti e con il carovita generale: studiamo infatti in aule sovraffollate, con libri costosissimi, senza nessuna agevolazione rilevante su affitti, trasporti, mense e materiale universitario. La risposta della governance, attenta solo a difendere il sacrosanto travertino, a queste mancanze è del tutto inappropriata: Ci confrontiamo infatti con un approccio che offre silenzio, se non condanna, alle istanze degli studenti e dei lavoratori precari da un lato; partnership e collaborazione a chi vende guerra dall’altro. In questo la direzione dell’ateneo si allinea perfettamente con la politica governativa che si rifiuta di adottare misure che possano contenere la crisi e persiste nella più ottusa e violenta repressione del dissenso pur di non uscire dal solco tracciato dall’economia della corsa alle armi. Il piano di riarmo dell’unione europea da 800 miliardi, la NATO che impone il 5% del PIL in spesa militare entro il 2028 rappresentano infatti le scelte che nei prossimi anni orienteranno le politiche economiche dei governi.

Scegliere di investire soldi in progetti di riarmo vuole dire ignorare i bisogni sociali e creare una società sempre più chiusa. In questo contesto si inserisce riforma Bernini che dopo decenni di tagli alla ricerca, va ad approfondire un processo di trasformazione strutturale dell’università. Dove mancano fondi si inserisce l’ingerenza di aziende come Leonardo che finanzia borse di ricerca, dottorati e laboratori.

Enormi finanziamenti che riceviamo in quanto Ateneo provengono infatti da realtà operanti nel settore bellico, le quali ovviamente non hanno a cuore il benessere di chi studia alla sapienza, ma solamente il poter ingrossare le tasche della propria filiera facendo fruttare gli investimenti condotti sui saperi prodotti dalla nostra generazione.

Nel territorio di Roma questo sistema è dimostrato dalla realizzazione del Technopole nella zona di Pietralata, accanto al polo industriale di Leonardo, MBDA, Avio.

Tutto ciò porta spesso le studentз a scegliere tra un futuro di precarietà e l’ingresso al servizio della macchina della guerra. I dati non mentono a riguardo. || 55% dellз studentз delle facoltà umanistiche, non direttamente funzionali a questo tipo di produzione, a tre anni dalla laurea magistrale ha un contratto instabile, almeno quellз che hanno la fortuna di trovare un lavoro (circa il 75%); mentre, nelle facoltà dove si insegnano discipline più direttamente applicabili alla filiera bellica (quali ingegneria), già dopo un anno l’occupazione raggiunge più del 90%, di cui buona parte a tempo indeterminato.

Negli ultimi anni la guerra si è imposta come condizione quotidiana del presente e unico scenario del futuro. La guerra parte anche da qui: l’istituzione universitaria sottopone il sapere prodotto collettivamente dallз studentз alle logiche di profitto, dandoci come unica prospettiva quella di servire il sistema stesso. Questo sapere vogliamo riprendercelo, soffiando via le fondamenta del castello di carte su cui si regge la loro guerra.




Contro la vostra università

Contro la vostra guerra

Contro il vostro mondo

SARÀ LA NOSTRA SAPIENZA CONTRO LA LORO

L’ASSEMBLEA DEGLI OCCUPANTI PRESENTA LE SEGUENTI RIVENDICAZIONI




Al governo chiediamo:







Sottrazione dall’accordo NATO che prevede un investimento pari al 5% del PIL nel comparto della difesa e sottrazione dal piano di riarmo europeo




Rinvestimento di fondi in istruzione, ricerca, sanitá. Aumento FFO




Ritiro dal Board of Peace







Al comune e alla regione chiediamo:







Riconversione del terreno e dell’edificio “Technopole” a Pietralata in uno studentato pubblico e gratuito




Riconversione del Social Hub a San Lorenzo in uno studentato pubblico e gratuito




Aumento delle borse di studio, rapidità nella pubblicazione delle borse, conseguente liquidazione immediata e riorganizzazione dei criteri adeguati all’aumento del costo della vita




Eliminazione del criterio sul merito







All’università e al rettore chiediamo:







Interruzione degli accordi con aziende belliche e entità sionista, trasparenza sulle partnership




Chiusura del commissariato, espulsione della DIGOS dall’università




Eliminazione della sovrattassa per gli studenti fuori corso, aumento degli appelli straordinari per tutt*




Apertura di un centro anti violenza conforme alle reali esigenze dell* student*







Da contro sapienza

author: David Venn
title: Woman found dead in cabin fire nearRankin Inlet
content:
Rankin Inlet RCMP and the Nunavut fire marshal’s office are investigating after a woman was found dead in a cabin fire outside the community early Sunday morning.




Police were called to an area outside the community called Johnson’s Cove at around 2:15 a.m. Sunday, RCMP said Tuesday in a news release.




Rankin Inlet fire fighters extinguished the fire and found a woman inside the cabin.




She was pronounced dead at the scene, according to the release.




The Nunavut coroner’s office is also assisting in the investigation.
