author: Brian Hioe
title: New Taipei Mayoral Debate Revolves Around Infrastructure, Urban Needs
content:
THE NEW TAIPEI mayoral debate was held on November 13th. The race is between Su Chiao-hui of the DPP and Lee Shu-chuan of the KMT. Fringe candidate Su Hui-huang also participated in the debate, making outlandish suggestions unlikely to be adopted, such as allowing marriages involving multiple partners in order to solve the issue of Taiwan’s declining birthrate.

The debate between Su and Lee primarily revolved around infrastructure and New Taipei’s urban needs, with many New Taipei residents commuting to work elsewhere. As such, Lee doubled down on his career as an administrator and civil engineer, promising to reduce commute times. Lee also called for increased AI development in New Taipei, stating that New Taipei should strengthen links to the Beitou-Shilin Technology Park and Shezidao in Taipei. Lee positioned himself as building on the policy of his predecessors, Eric Chu and Hou You-yi. Lee also emphasized cooperation between himself and Chiang Wan-an in Taipei, stressing New Taipei’s links to Taipei infrastructure, such as the Taipei Dome.

Su Chiao-hui, in the meantime, emphasized residential policy. Su called for allowing New Taipei residents to live comfortably; young people should have more access to housing, while also allowing for cultural development, preserving heritage areas, developing tourism, and providing opportunities for young people. Su stressed her background as a New Taipei resident who was familiar with the different districts of New Taipei, and who would bring out the specificity of each area. Su also called for AI development for New Taipei, as well as suggested that New Taipei should form a special bureau in order to retain talent among civil servants, stating that this was an issue faced by New Taipei.

Apart from AI, urban renewal emerged as a common theme between the two candidates. Both candidates promised to implement urban renewal in a more streamlined manner, to keep pace with the demands of the city. All candidates, unsurprisingly, promised to quickly implement policy if elected.

A point of conflict between Su and Lee emerged regarding the central government’s role, as well as who would foot the bill for policy proposals. Su emphasized that she would put the needs of New Taipei residents first if it came to a conflict in imperatives between the central government and New Taipei, but that she could coordinate between the two sides. On the other hand, Lee sought to attack Su multiple times by claiming that she was unaware of where money for her policy proposals would come from. In response, Su cited that this would utilize higher tax revenue for New Taipei than in past years, but Lee still circled back to this point several times.

In closing, Su criticized the KMT for maintaining a negative campaign and attacking her family, seeing as she is the daughter of Premier Su Tseng-chang. Su stated that she could have focused attacks on Lee’s brother had she chosen, with Lee Shu-chuan’s brother Lee Szu-fu having been found guilty of extortion of tourism operators in Xiaoliuqiu earlier this year. Su then emphasized her campaign as forward-looking, seeking to establish a new future for New Taipei, but that this was a decision about the better choice for New Taipei, acknowledging where past KMT administrations of New Taipei had improved infrastructure.

Lee defended himself by stating that he viewed his brother as needing to face legal punishment. Lee also sought to defend himself against allegations he has increasingly faced about not declaring his assets or owning luxury properties, instead trying to emphasize that he was a regular person. Lee emphasized his past record as an administrator and stated that as a public servant, he was willing to face criticism. In his closing, then, Lee attempted to depict Su as not being of the people, circling around to this point several times, and attacking her past record as a legislator.

On the whole, Su’s debate performance was stronger than Lee due to better public speaking and debating skills. It is not for nothing that Lee has struggled in New Taipei despite that he otherwise should be in a more advantageous position after New Taipei was controlled by the KMT for two mayoral administrations, his poor campaigning skills have hindered him. Lee may have had a reputation as a competent administrator in the past, but he is not as skilled a politician. Nevertheless, he probably managed well enough in the debate that it will not have any significantly negative impact on voting.

New Taipei will be a hotly watched race going into the local elections, seeing as the race was already one in which Su seemed to possibly be doing better than Lee even before the “Ocean Current” phenomenon surged across Taiwan, impacting races across the country. Even if Shen were to be defeated in Taipei, it may actually be in New Taipei that the DPP has a chance to take northern Taiwanese territory traditionally controlled by the KMT.

author: CNT Iruña
title: 11N: Valoración de la jornada de huelga general
content:
Desde CNT Iruñea valoramos la huelga del pasado 11 de noviembre como 

un paso fundamental dado por la clase trabajadora en Navarra

. El importante seguimiento que tuvo en la industria, el escaso movimiento que constatamos en los polígonos además de los cierres de comercios y supermercados, previa o posteriormente al paso de los piquetes, dan muestra de la fuerza que atesoramos cuando la conciencia de clase se pone en movimiento. Asimismo, nuestro comité de huelga pudo constatar el bajo ritmo de producción al entrar en diferentes empresas para informar a las trabajadoras y asegurarse de que el derecho a la huelga se estaba respetando.




Hemos de agradecer, también, 

la implicación de nuestra militancia, sin la cual nada de esto habría sido posible y quien se mantuvo activa desde primerísima hora de la mañana

 en los diferentes piquetes y actos propios que se dieron a lo largo del día e incluyendo el éxito multitudinario de la manifestación de la Plaza del Castillo y la de la tarde, donde cobraron protagonismo sindicatos de vivienda y movimientos sociales. La capacidad para responder a los diferentes momentos de la jornada son una muestra ilusionante del presente y el futuro del sindicato.




Asimismo, 

queremos extender el agradecimiento a CGT Nafarroa y a Solidari así como al Punto de Información para Personas Migradas, a las Trabajadoras de Hogar y Cuidados de Navarra y a las personas simpatizantes con quienes compartimos acto en la Plaza del Vínculo

, un entorno que continúa consolidándose como un espacio alternativo en las huelgas desde el que dar voz al sindicalismo de clase y los colectivos más precarizados. Un entorno, a su vez, desde el que marcamos distancias con el uso electoralista de la lucha de clases y señalamos la necesidad de que los sindicatos mantengan una independencia radical frente a partidos políticos y estado.




En el discurso, 

las organizaciones convocantes quisimos señalar que la cuestión de la vivienda se encuentra estrechamente vinculado a la del salario, el coste de la vida y las pensiones, y que nuestros intereses como clase son contrapuestos por completo a los de las élites económicas y políticas

. Cada ataque que recibamos por su parte en forma de degradación de los servicios públicos, de represión policial, escalada militar, extensión de los discursos machistas, tránsfobos y racistas o de persecución de nuestras compañeras más precarizadas y vulnerables tendrá su respuesta.




Con CGT, a su vez, cabe señalar que compartimos algo más que una concentración. Reunido desde las 6 de la mañana en el polígono de Landaben, el bloque anarcosindicalista no sólo hizo efectivas sus acciones combativas, sino que se expuso también al hostigamiento policial

, verbal y físico, tanto de la Nacional como de la Foral, el cual llegó a retener a quienes participaban en el piquete procediendo a identificarles en su totalidad mientras amenazaba con multas y represalias. Desde aquí, denunciamos con rotundidad las distintas actuaciones policiales a lo largo del día 11, quienes coaccionaron el derecho a la huelga con las diferentes dinámicas represivas que tienen por costumbre, damos todo nuestro apoyo a las personas atacadas y criminalizadas y exigimos la liberación inmediata de la persona detenida en el piquete a las puertas de la oficina de CaixaBank en la avenida Carlos III.




El movimiento por la vivienda ha demostrado que cuenta con una gran capacidad de convocatoria que ha conseguido llegar a personas que nunca antes habrían considerado el sindicarse. Hemos de analizar las razones y, a la vez, sus consecuencias, potencialidades y límites. Al mismo tiempo, 

conviene poner el acento en un aspecto fundamental de esta huelga: la lucha por la vivienda es inseparable de la lucha por el salario y las condiciones de trabajo por lo que es imprescindible, de cara a parar la producción, la organización en sindicatos de clase dentro de las empresas y centros de trabajo.




Por otro lado y en última instancia, no se ha de perder la perspectiva de que el nacionalismo, si bien puede pretender el articularse desde una perspectiva de clase dentro de un marco de luchas propio, encontrará siempre sus límites en el momento de profundizar con todas sus consecuencias en la solidaridad de clase, el apoyo mutuo y la autogestión obrera. 

Las organizaciones de clase debemos extender el conflicto con la patronal, el rentismo y el Estado a todos los rincones de la sociedad, en el mayor número de territorios posible y por encima de toda frontera

.




El 11 de noviembre ha sido el inicio de una época que nos va a pedir que demos lo mejor de cada una de nosotras mismas. 

Nuestra lucha no se agota en esta huelga, ni atiende a cálculos que se resuelvan tras unas elecciones, sino que su horizonte revolucionario se extiende más allá del 29.

 En estos tiempos de conflicto, es la hora del fortalecimiento de las instituciones populares para aumentar nuestras capacidades y energías. Es momento de continuar extendiendo nuestro modelo sindical y social hasta conseguir que la capacidad de lucha de nuestra clase no se encuentre sometida a los actuales sindicatos mayoritarios. Es la hora de la militancia. Unamos las luchas de la clase trabajadora. Adelante, compañeras, no dejemos que esta llama se extinga.




La entrada 

11N: Valoración de la jornada de huelga general

 se publicó primero en 

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

.

author: CNT Guadalajara
title: Crónica de la huelga del 11N
content:
En Guadalajara la jornada comenzó con los piquetes del turno de noche en la zona de los polígonos de Marchámalo, Cabanillas y Azuqueca principalmente donde nos concentramos miembros del comité unitario de huelga para paralizar la logística de la ciudad y sus alrededores donde se concentra el grueso de lxs trabajadorxs. Lxs compañerxs de CNT nos concentramos en el de la ciudad del transporte (Marchámalo) donde se consiguió bloquear la entrada a las empresas allí ubicadas durante al menos un par de horas aguantando bajo la lluvia.




A lo largo de la noche las personas que participaban en los piquetes se fueron moviendo por los diferentes centros para reforzar los mismos.




En plena noche nos concentramos frente a la estación de autobuses para intentar que solo salieran los servicios mínimos junto con otras personas del comité unitario, pero nos encontramos con una fuerte presencia policial que impidió llevar a cabo nuestro objetivo y donde se vivieron momentos de tensión cuando un compañero del sindicato fue agarrado del cuello por un policía que lo tiro al suelo provocándole serias contusiones en brazo, espalda y cuello y debió de ser atendido en el hospital, hecho que será denunciado debidamente.




A primeras horas de la mañana volvieron los piquetes a los polígonos para informar al turno de mañana donde algunos compañeros tuvieron un encontronazo con un camionero esquirol haciendo alarde de simbología fascista del grupo Núcleo Nacional que fue arropado por las fuerzas de seguridad.




A media mañana se realizó una concentración en las inmediaciones de la Plaza del Ayuntamiento de Guadalajara para informar y denunciar la precaria situación laboral y de vivienda que vivimos en nuestra provincia con gran afluencia de gente.




Para rematar la jornada se llevó a cabo la manifestación convocada por el comité unitario de huelga que paralizo el centro de la ciudad durante un par de horas. A pesar de una climatología adversa conseguimos llevar a cabo una de las mayores movilizaciones ciudadanas que se hayan realizado nunca en Guadalajara, y una vez llegamos a la Plaza del Infantado y coreamos cánticos y consignas dimos por concluida la jornada de huelga del 11N.




La valoración que hacemos desde CNT es que el seguimiento de la huelga varió bastante por sectores, si bien es verdad que en la logística que es donde se concentra el grueso de lxs trabajadorxs de la provincia tuvo un mayor seguimiento (en torno al 70%) en otras áreas como el transporte, los supermercados y comercios o las administraciones publicas fue muy escaso; por lo que, aunque podamos estar contentas de lo que logramos no podemos decir que saliera tan bien como nos hubiera gustado. Aunque si tenemos en cuenta todo el trabajo que ha hecho la patronal junto con la ultraderecha para desinformar, desmotivar y desmovilizar a la clase trabajadora podemos decir que lo hemos hecho muy bien.




Pero para nosotras esto no acaba aquí, la huelga del 11N ha sido el punto de partida debido al hartazgo de la clase trabajadora para poner freno al rentismo instaurado en el gobierno y las condiciones de miseria que nos condenan a matarnos a trabajar para poder pagar un alquiler y hacer frente al coste de la vida que es cada vez mayor mientras unos pocos se lucran de manera mezquina haciendo de la vivienda un negocio.




Ahora toca seguir organizándose en los sindicatos y organizaciones de base para lograr nuevas conquistas para la clase trabajadora y no perder las que a día de hoy damos por seguras y que penden de un hilo.




Por eso seguiremos saliendo a las calles 10, 100, 1000 y las veces que hagan falta para luchar por lo que es de justicia contra la patronal, el gobierno y este sistema que nos roba la vida.










 







 







 







 







 







 







 







 







 







 







 







 
















La entrada 

Crónica de la huelga del 11N

 se publicó primero en 

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

.

author: CNT Aragón-Rioja
title: Crónica y fotografías de la Huelga General del 11N en La Rioja
content:
La lucha desde el apoyo mutuo y el trabajo colectivo




Las trabajadoras de La Rioja hemos dado un golpe sobre la mesa. Que el poder capitalista diga lo que quiera, lo que hemos vivido no ha sido un simple paro puntual de un día, ha sido una 

Huelga General

 

indispensable

 por la vivienda, los salarios, las pensiones y los servicios públicos, con una repercusión mediática sobresaliente.




Desde CNT sabíamos que partíamos con 

todo en contra

. Nos enfrentamos a la clase política, a la clase empresarial, al avance del fascismo y, lamentablemente, a la mitad de una población intoxicada por la polarización, las mentiras y el odio que los tres primeros inyectan a diario a través de unos medios de comunicación mayoritariamente hostiles. A esto se sumó la imposición de unos servicios mínimos abusivos, decretados desde la autoridad frente a cualquier intento real de negociación, y a una 

actuación policial desproporcionada

 en algunos momentos del desarrollo de los piquetes informativos.




Sin embargo, 

el resultado ha desbordado todas las expectativas

. Mientras la patronal se ríe y se burla asegurando un seguimiento inferior al 3%, la realidad en los centros de trabajo demuestra que el seguimiento alcanzó el 60% en varios sectores, especialmente el industrial. Incluso el consumo eléctrico bajó un 13% durante la mañana y hasta el mediodía.




Piquetes informativos mixtos y represión policial




La jornada comenzó en Logroño a las 20 h. de la víspera del 11N con la 

concentración de todos los piquetes informativos

 de la totalidad de sindicatos en la confluencia de las Avenidas de la Solidaridad y Colón, visualizándolo ante los medios, la policía y las autoridades. Desde ese momento y hasta las 11 h. del 11N, los piquetes informativos recorrieron puntos neurálgicos de la ciudad y polígonos industriales:







Polígono Cantabria:

 Estuvimos presentes en varios puntos de acceso. Los piquetes informativos fueron efectivos y procedieron con tranquilidad a pesar de la presencia policial.




MercaRioja:

 Un piquete no muy numeroso pero efectivo, marcado por una desproporcionada presencia policial y apertura de un acceso inesperado.




Polígono La Portalada:

 Fue uno de los puntos más nutridos, pero la policía nos impidió realizar nuestra labor informativa. Aunque en algún momento puntual, en uno de los accesos, logramos alcanzar acuerdos con los agentes para realizar nuestra labor, en otro punto (Bolera) no fue así. 

Denunciamos las cargas injustificadas y la violencia ejercida por algunos policías

. Esta actuación se saldó con un compañero del SVLR agredido y detenido y compañeras de distintos sindicatos, una de ellas de CNT, también agredidas.




Rotonda de Las Gaunas (Av. Madrid):

 Un piquete numeroso y muy efectivo logró entorpecer la entrada durante más de una hora. La respuesta policial fue, cuando nos íbamos, retener y tratar de amedrentar a una veintena de compañeras, cebándose especialmente con las jóvenes del Sindicato de Vivienda de La Rioja.




UNIR:

 Empresa educativa privada pagada con dinero público. Tiene 1.000 trabajadoras (buena parte de ellas en condiciones laborales lamentables y amenazadas) solo en Logroño, 400 presenciales en la sede central. Con presencia policial y de medios, logramos realizar un piquete efectivo en los accesos al centro.




Avenida de la Paz:

 Realizamos concentraciones y lanzamos consignas a las puertas de Mercadona y de varias entidades bancarias, señalando a los responsables de la especulación, de la explotación laboral y de la carestía de la vida.







A las 11 h., tras la intensa jornada de piquetes, nos sumamos para apoyar y participar activamente en 

la manifestación estudiantil

, que recorrió importantes arterias de la ciudad desde la Glorieta del Doctor Zubía hasta el Espolón, demostrando que la juventud también está en pie de guerra frente a los desmanes y las amenazas contra la educación pública.




Alianzas fructíferas y esperanza en la juventud




Uno de los hitos más enriquecedores de este 11N ha sido la 

unidad de acción

. Desde CNT hemos trabajado codo con codo con los sindicatos CCOO, UGT, CGT y STE, organizaciones con las que mantenemos profundas diferencias en las formas de entender y practicar el sindicalismo. Sin embargo, el trabajo conjunto ha sido fluido y muy satisfactorio.




Pero si algo nos llena de orgullo es haber cumplido nuestro objetivo de cooperar y caminar junto al 

Sindicato de Vivienda de La Rioja (SVLR)

. Ya las admirábamos, pero compartir esta lucha nos ha enseñado que cuando al correcto sentido de la justicia se lo riega con ilusión y trabajo duro, incluso en este mundo patriarcal e inhumano puede brotar la esperanza. 




Frente al socavón patriarcal, sindicalismo de clase feminista




En un sistema patriarcal donde siempre se olvida a las mujeres, que son la mayoría de la población, CNT ha alzado con fuerza la bandera de la 

lucha feminista

. Lo que sufrimos no es una simple brecha de género, es un auténtico socavón estructural: cobramos un 16% menos de salario, sufrimos el triple de hostigamiento y acoso laboral, y nuestras pensiones son un 30% más bajas tras toda una vida marcada por el machismo, la precariedad, la temporalidad y la carga de los cuidados.




Esta 

desigualdad

 se ceba en lo más básico: necesitamos casi cuatro años más que los hombres para poder comprar una vivienda, destinamos hasta dos tercios de nuestro sueldo para pagar un alquiler, representamos a dos de cada tres personas desahuciadas y llenar el carro de la compra se nos hace cada día más cuesta arriba. Ayer gritamos por todas nosotras. Y seguiremos mañana.




Una tarde histórica en las calles de Logroño




A las 18 h., bajo el lema 

“Vivienda, salarios, pensiones y servicios públicos”

, comenzó una 

manifestación que ya forma parte de la historia de nuestra ciudad

. Una afluencia masiva y combativa, sin incidentes reseñables, desbordó el recorrido desde la Glorieta del Doctor Zubía hasta el Espolón, pasando por Portales, Murrieta, Gran Vía y Vara de Rey. Las cifras del éxito de la convocatoria hablan por sí solas: 30.000 personas.




El broche final en el Espolón puso la piel de gallina a todas las presentes: la lectura del 

manifiesto

 a cargo del SVLR y la emocionante interpretación de 

“

No hay tanto pan

”

 (ni vivienda) por parte de la cantante Elena Aranoa resonaron como un recordatorio de por qué luchamos.




El 11N no es un punto final, sino un punto de inflexión

. La lucha sigue en las calles y con futuras movilizaciones. Gracias de corazón a todas por el inmenso trabajo realizado: al Comité de Huelga, a las militantes, a las afiliadas, a las pensionistas, a las simpatizantes, a los sindicatos participantes y, muy especialmente, a las compañeras del Sindicato de Vivienda de La Rioja. 




Si hay lucha, hay esperanza. Nos vemos en el sindicato y nos vemos en las calles.

¡Que viva la lucha de la clase obrera!

https://aragon-rioja.cnt.es/cronica-y-fotografias-de-la-huelga-general-del-11n-en-la-rioja/




La entrada 

Crónica y fotografías de la Huelga General del 11N en La Rioja

 se publicó primero en 

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

.

author: infolibre
title: Κινητοποιήσεις και δράσεις κατά μεγάλων ενεργειακών έργων σε όλη την Ελλάδα
content:
Σε εξέλιξη βρίσκονται δημόσιες διαβουλεύσεις για την περιβαλλοντική αδειοδότηση μεγάλων ενεργειακών και βιομηχανικών έργων σε διάφορες περιοχές της Ελλάδας. Στη 

Ροδόπη

 και στα 

Λευκά Όρη της Κρήτης

 εξετάζεται η εγκατάσταση νέων αιολικών σταθμών, στο

 Κρυονέρι Αττικής

 η κατασκευή μεγάλου κέντρου δεδομένων, ενώ στον 

Παρνασσό

 και στον

 ποταμό Ερύμανθο

 προωθούνται υδροηλεκτρικά έργα. Παράλληλα, στην 

Πελοπόννησο

 660 πολίτες και φορείς έχουν ήδη καταθέσει αντιρρήσεις για εκτεταμένο συγκρότημα έργων ανανεώσιμων πηγών ενέργειας.




Οι δημόσιες διαβουλεύσεις δίνουν τη δυνατότητα σε πολίτες, συλλόγους και επιστημονικούς φορείς να εξετάσουν τις Μελέτες Περιβαλλοντικών Επιπτώσεων και να καταθέσουν 

τεκμηριωμένες αντιρρήσεις μέσω των σχετικών εντύπων Δ11

, επισημαίνοντας  επιπτώσεις στα δάση, στους υδάτινους πόρους, στην άγρια πανίδα και στις τοπικές κοινωνίες. Για αρκετά από τα έργα έχουν ήδη συνταχθεί υποδείγματα αντιρρήσεων, τα οποία μπορούν να αξιοποιήσουν οι ενδιαφερόμενοι για τη συμμετοχή τους στη διαδικασία.




Οι προθεσμίες είναι ιδιαίτερα σημαντικές

, καθώς οι διαβουλεύσεις ολοκληρώνονται στις 16 και 17 Νοεμβρίου για τα έργα στην Κρήτη, στη Ροδόπη και στο Κρυονέρι, στις 25 Νοεμβρίου για την Τιθορέα και στις 7 Δεκεμβρίου για τον Ερύμανθο. Η συμμετοχή πραγματοποιείται μέσω της ηλεκτρονικής πλατφόρμας περιβαλλοντικής αδειοδότησης του Υπουργείου Περιβάλλοντος και Ενέργειας, όπου οι ενδιαφερόμενοι μπορούν να υποβάλουν τις παρατηρήσεις και τις αντιρρήσεις τους πριν από την ολοκλήρωση της σχετικής διαδικασίας.


































ΡΟΔΟΠΗ:  

Νέα αιολικά απειλούν δάση, άγρια πουλιά και χωριά.




ΑΣΠΗΕ στη θέση «ΔΟΡΥ», κοντά στον Κάρδαμο και την Κύμη




Ένα ακόμη έργο εγκατεστημένης ισχύος 28 MW, που προβλέπει την εγκατάσταση τεσσάρων ανεμογεννητριών ύψους 200 μ.




Σύμφωνα με το Δ11, οι επιφάνειες επέμβασης για την οδοποιία και τις πλατείες ανέγερσης αφορούν κυρίως δασικές εκτάσεις και καταλαμβάνουν συνολικά 85.003 τ.μ.




Προθεσμία συμμετοχής στη διαβούλευση: 17 Νοεμβρίου.




Μια περιοχή ήδη ασφυκτικά επιβαρυμένη από αιολικά έργα




Τα δύο έργα χωροθετούνται σε μια περιοχή εξαιρετικής οικολογικής σημασίας. Ο ΑΣΠΗΕ «ΔΟΡΥ» βρίσκεται εντός της Σημαντικής Περιοχής για τα Πουλιά GR008 «Κοιλάδα Φιλιούρη και ανατολική Ροδόπη» και εντός κύριου μεταναστευτικού διαδρόμου. Σε απόσταση περίπου 5,5 χλμ. βρίσκεται η Ζώνη Ειδικής Προστασίας Natura 2000 «Κοιλάδα Φιλιούρη» (GR1130011).




Στην περιοχή καταγράφονται προστατευόμενα αρπακτικά και πτωματοφάγα είδη, όπως ο 

Μαυρόγυπας,

 το

 Όρνιο

, ο 

Χρυσαετός

 και ο 

Φιδαετός

. Μάλιστα, η ίδια η Ειδική Οικολογική Αξιολόγηση αναγνωρίζει ότι δεν μπορεί να αποκλειστεί ο κίνδυνος πρόσκρουσης Μαυρόγυπα και Όρνιου στις ανεμογεννήτριες.




Το Δ11 επισημαίνει επίσης το τεράστιο πρόβλημα των σωρευτικών επιπτώσεων: στην ευρύτερη περιοχή μελέτης συνεργιστικών επιπτώσεων, που περιλαμβάνει τη ΣΠΠ GR008 και τη ΖΕΠ GR1130011, καταγράφονται ήδη 178 ανεμογεννήτριες σε λειτουργία, ενώ άλλες 182 έχουν βεβαίωση παραγωγού. Πρόκειται για μια τεράστια συγκέντρωση αιολικών εγκαταστάσεων, η οποία απειλεί να μεταβάλει ριζικά το φυσικό περιβάλλον και τους βιότοπους των προστατευόμενων ειδών.




ΝΑ ΣΥΜΜΕΤΕΧΟΥΜΕ ΜΑΖΙΚΑ ΣΤΙΣ ΔΙΑΒΟΥΛΕΥΣΕΙΣ!




Σύνδεσμοι διαβουλεύσεων και έντυπα Δ11 στα σχόλια.




Η προστασία των βουνών, των δασών και των άγριων πλασμάτων είναι υπόθεση όλων μας!




#ροδοπη




Η εικόνα είναι από το χωριό Άνω Κάρδαμος στην περιοχή εγκατάστασης των έργων.

Μέχρι τις 16 Νοεμβρίου

 βρίσκεται σε δημόσια διαβούλευση η Μελέτη Περιβαλλοντικών Επιπτώσεων (ΜΠΕ) για την εγκατάσταση αιολικού σταθμού της ΔΕΗ ΑΝΑΝΕΩΣΙΜΕΣ ισχύος 52,8 MW, κοντά στο χωριό 

Ασή Γωνιά

 του Δήμου Αποκορώνου στην Κρήτη.




Το έργο προβλέπει:




– 8 ανεμογεννήτριες ισχύος 6,6 MW και ύψους περίπου 185 μέτρων η καθεμία.




– 14,2 χλμ. οδοποιίας, από τα οποία 6,2 χλμ. νέες διανοίξεις.




– Επεμβάσεις σε περίπου 437 στρέμματα, κυρίως δασικών εκτάσεων.




– Νέο υποσταθμό εντός περιοχής Natura 2000.




Η επιστημονική κοινότητα κρούει τον κώδωνα του κινδύνου!




Το ΤΕΕ – Τμήμα Δυτικής Κρήτης γνωμοδότησε αρνητικά επί της ΜΠΕ και ζητά την επιστροφή της, επισημαίνοντας σοβαρές ελλείψεις και προβλήματα περιβαλλοντικής τεκμηρίωσης.




Μεταξύ άλλων, αναδεικνύει:




Απειλή για την ορνιθοπανίδα:

 Τα φαράγγια των Λευκών Ορέων, μόλις 1,7 χλμ. από την περιοχή εγκατάστασης, αποτελούν βιότοπους προστατευόμενων αρπακτικών, όπως ο Γυπαετός, το Όρνιο και ο Χρυσαετός. Η ΜΠΕ δεν περιλαμβάνει επαρκείς εργασίες πεδίου ούτε ολοκληρωμένη εκτίμηση του κινδύνου πρόσκρουσης.




Κίνδυνοι για το υδρολογικό σύστημα της Λίμνης Κουρνά:

 Οι εκσκαφές, οι θεμελιώσεις και η διάνοιξη δρόμων σχεδιάζονται χωρίς επαρκή υδρογεωλογική και γεωτεχνική διερεύνηση του καρστικού συστήματος που τροφοδοτεί τη λίμνη, από την οποία αντλείται και νερό ύδρευσης.




Αλλοίωση του τοπίου:

 Δεν αξιολογούνται επαρκώς οι επιπτώσεις στη Λίμνη Κουρνά, στους παραδοσιακούς οικισμούς και στην ιστορική περιοχή της Αργυρούπολης.




Επιπτώσεις από τον θόρυβο:

 Η μελέτη παρουσιάζει προβλήματα στη μοντελοποίηση, ενώ για τον οικισμό Πάτημα υπολογίζει αύξηση της νυχτερινής στάθμης θορύβου κατά 2,9 dB, πολύ κοντά στο όριο των 3 dB που χρησιμοποιεί η ίδια.




Σωρευτική επιβάρυνση:

 Το έργο εντάσσεται σε ευρύτερο συγκρότημα αιολικών σταθμών συνολικής ισχύος 1.023,5 MW στη Δυτική Κρήτη, χωρίς να αξιολογούνται επαρκώς οι συνολικές επιπτώσεις.

Προβλέπονται 31 εφεδρικές ηλεκτροπαραγωγές γεννήτριες και νέος υποσταθμός υψηλής τάσης. Το έργο βρίσκεται μόλις περίπου 560 μέτρα από τον οικισμό του Κρυονερίου και 410 μέτρα από τα όρια του Αγίου Στεφάνου, ενώ σε απόσταση περίπου 1,3 χλμ. βρίσκεται η προστατευόμενη περιοχή Natura 2000 «Όρος Πάρνηθα» και στην ευρύτερη περιοχή το ρέμα Φασίδερι.

Τεράστιες ενεργειακές απαιτήσεις και θερμική επιβάρυνση.

 Στο δυσμενέστερο σενάριο συνεχούς λειτουργίας, η ετήσια κατανάλωση μπορεί να φτάσει τις 342.516 MWh. Σχεδόν όλη η ηλεκτρική ενέργεια που καταναλώνεται μετατρέπεται τελικά σε θερμότητα και αποβάλλεται στο περιβάλλον, με πιθανές επιπτώσεις στο τοπικό μικροκλίμα.




Εκπομπές ρύπων από τις γεννήτριες.

 Η εγκατάσταση προβλέπει 31 εφεδρικές γεννήτριες πετρελαίου. Το Δ11 εντοπίζει σοβαρές ασυνέπειες στις παραδοχές της ΜΠΕ για την ισχύ, την κατανάλωση καυσίμου, τις ώρες λειτουργίας και τις εκπομπές τους. Επισημαίνει επίσης ότι δεν έχει αξιολογηθεί επαρκώς το σενάριο λειτουργίας τους σε περίπτωση διακοπής ηλεκτροδότησης.

Ελλιπής αξιολόγηση ηλεκτρομαγνητικών πεδίων

. Η Ελληνική Επιτροπή Ατομικής Ενέργειας, με έγγραφό της στις 3/11/2026, δήλωσε αδυναμία γνωμοδότησης λόγω απουσίας της απαιτούμενης ειδικής μελέτης.




Αντιπλημμυρική προστασία και διαχείριση υδάτων.

 Το Δ11 επισημαίνει κενά στην τεκμηρίωση της διαχείρισης των ομβρίων και των πιθανών διαρροών, καθώς και στην αξιολόγηση της προστασίας του γειτονικού ρέματος από ενδεχόμενη μεταφορά ρύπανσης.




Σωρευτικές επιπτώσεις.

 Δεν αξιολογείται επαρκώς η συνολική επιβάρυνση από τις υφιστάμενες και σχεδιαζόμενες εγκαταστάσεις της περιοχής, τις κοινές ηλεκτρικές υποδομές, τον θόρυβο, την κατανάλωση ενέργειας και τις εκπομπές.

Το ζήτημα έχει φτάσει και στη Βουλή. Παράλληλα, η Διαπαραταξιακή Επιτροπή του Δήμου αποφάσισε ομόφωνα να εισηγηθεί αρνητική γνωμοδότηση για το έργο, ενώ ο Δήμος Διονύσου έχει διατυπώσει αρνητική γνώμη επί της ΜΠΕ.

]

, qu'on va suivre dans ses aventures médiatiques, entrepreneuriales et sexuelles dans le Paris des années 2010-20 : un social-démocrate (donc de droite) : « Mathieu peut enfin faire rayonner l'ensemble de ses connaissances acquises en journalisme et en géopolitique avec ses convictions humanistes en matière de défense des minorités », l'un de ces macronistes qui n'a aucun problème pour dégraisser une masse salariale quand un actionnaire hétérosexuel et londonien l'attend : « c'est ainsi qu'un hétérosexuel et un homosexuel se marièrent, unis par le sacrement de la prospérité. Dans le ciel, un oiseau était mort de honte ».




Voilà l'un des livres les plus drôles — et assassin — que j'aie lu depuis longtemps. Monté au hachoir, alternant régime réaliste et fantastique, 

Les grandes puissances de mon cœur

 est la télé-novella des années Macron. En ce sens, elle dépasse largement le seul milieu gay parisien pour nous faire sentir le parfum à la fois pourri et ambiancé dans lequel nous vivons depuis dix ans.




Une fois passée une partie polyphonique (qui est, en elle-même, une parodie des polyphonies dont on est saturé.es, au cinéma comme en littérature) où 

Laurence, Gaëtan, Sébastien, Roland

 et 

Caroline

 (qu'on découvrira être un Yorkshire femelle) donnent leur point de vue sur Mathieu, tout commence à partir, il faut bien le dire, en couilles.







 

 










=> Le Centre Pompidou devient une gigantesque usine à twinks, « les vrais, les beaux, les suçables » — le twink est une sorte de minet, un Claude François jeune et dégénéré —, des twinks excitants mais monstrueux, plus proches des 

droogs 

d'

Orange mécanique

 que du Patrick Juvet d'

Où sont les femmes ? 




=> Mathieu se met à avoir des visions à la fois étranges et logiques : « Il croit voir, mais alors il ne peut en avoir le cœur net, un tout petit être parcourir une plinthe avant de disparaître dans la cage d'escalier. Son sang ne fait qu'un tour car il ne s'agit clairement pas d'une souris mais d'une sorte d'humain miniature, entièrement vêtu de blanc avec un turban et une longue robe blanche et des sandales en cuir ». Un Arabe, bien sûr ! Sa chienne Caroline en a d'ailleurs « après tous les étrangers ! », dit-il à Mehdi avant une baise et qu'il ne le (Mehdi) « range dans son placard, après l'avoir soigneusement replié comme on plie un tee-shirt, parfaitement plat et symétrique ».




=> enfin invité à son émission de télévision préférée QUOTIDIENNE, Mathieu commence hélas à avoir de sérieux problèmes de vue après s'être frotté un œil — « un milliard de merdes de chiens sur la cornée » — et s'être révélé dans un sourire en Dorian Gray d'envers du tableau… 




Car 

Les grandes puissances de mon cœur 

sont nourris d'influences cinématographiques 

et

 littéraires, Wilde, sans doute, mais aussi Lautréamont — cette course finale dans un Paris atroce et nocturne, annoncée par une scène d'anthologie (que je ne peux décemment pas spoiler) avec Rachida Dati. Parfois, on frôle le conte, quand Mathieu, Chaperon rose, porte « une brique de lait et du pain » au vieil homme solitaire de son immeuble qui, bien sûr, se fera expulser.




Par sa cruauté, son intelligence et son sens de la formule, 

Les grandes puissances de mon cœur

 est à la hauteur des plus belles pancartes vues ces dernières semaines (« La police nous prothèse ») et fait oublier les vains débats autour, plus que sur, les romans censés se vendre en septembre-octobre. 




Nathalie Quintane




Les grandes puissances de mon cœur

 (Mickaël Tempête, éd. Trou Noir, 144 pages, 12 €)










[

1

] 

On reconnaîtra sans peine 

Têtu,

 qui a encore fait parler de lui récemment en envoyant 2 journalistes en Seine Saint-Denis qui n'ont pas trouvé mieux que de couper les propos tenus par des habitants dès qu'iels parlaient de la question sociale…







[

2

] 

« Comme un vol de gerfauts / Hors du charnier natal » (premiers vers des 

Conquérants

… (José Maria de Heredia, 

Les trophées,

 1893).

author: ACG
title: The Proletariat and the Possibility of Revolution
content:
We re-publish below a text from the Spanish historian

 

Agustin Guillamón

, author of among other books, The Friends of Durruti Group 1937-1939 and  

Ready for Revolution

: 

The CNT Defense Committees in Barcelona, 1933-1938. This is the first of two interesting texts from Spanish writers that we will be putting up on the ACG website.




Introduction




The difference between Miquel Amorós and myself doesn’t lie in one wanting revolution and the other rejecting it, nor in one defending autonomy and the other not. We both start from a radical critique of capitalist society and the conviction that emancipation cannot be the work of institutions separate from those who struggle. We both reject the integration of struggles into state institutions and deeply distrust any organisation that seeks to replace direct worker action. However, when we try to define what this autonomy means, what relationship it should have with the transformation of society, and, above all, who can carry this transformation to its ultimate consequences, a fundamental difference emerges between us.




I would say that this difference can be formulated as follows: Amorós emphasises the concrete reconstruction of autonomous forms of life, while I consider it necessary to ask about the social subject capable of transforming these necessarily partial experiences into a general transformation of capitalist relations. This is not about denying the value of autonomous experiences, nor about postponing emancipation to an indefinite future. It is about determining what social force can transform what today appears as a limited experience into a general way of organising life. This question necessarily leads to the proletariat, and in it, in my view, lies the essential difference between our respective positions.




Amorós begins with a historical observation that cannot be ignored. The traditional forms of the workers’ movement have been profoundly weakened by the evolution of capitalism. Political representation, union integration, the fragmentation of labour, and the transformation of lifestyles have destroyed a good part of the conditions that allowed the proletariat to constitute itself, at certain historical moments, as a visible, organised revolutionary force capable of directly intervening in society. Faced with this situation, passively awaiting a future revolutionary recomposition would be a form of impotence. If emancipation has any real content, it must begin in the present.




Hence the importance that autonomy, community, and concrete utopia acquire in Amorós’s work. Revolution cannot be a promise that indefinitely justifies the acceptance of a subjugated life. We must reclaim now the capacities that capitalism has taken from us: To decide collectively, to produce and reproduce life without delegating it, to rebuild community ties, to recover knowledge, and to create spaces where human relations are not entirely determined by commodities and the state. This “concrete utopia” precisely expresses the desire not to postpone freedom until an uncertain future.




This demand strikes me as profoundly revolutionary. A revolution that doesn’t transform life would be a purely political revolution and, therefore, insufficient. We don’t want to change those who govern only to continue living under social relations we don’t control. We want the production, reproduction, and organisation of our existence to cease appearing to us as external powers. Emancipation cannot be reduced to modifying the administration of a society that remains essentially the same.




But precisely for this reason, I consider it necessary to raise a question that cannot be resolved by appealing solely to autonomy: What happens when an autonomous experience, even if real and transformative for those who participate in it, continues to develop within a capitalist society whose general relations remain intact?




An autonomous experience can profoundly transform the lives of those who participate in it and yet continue to exist within the market. It can create cooperative relationships and still need money; it can function without internal hierarchies and still have to buy goods produced by other workers; it can collectively organise a space and still remain subject to the property relations that govern the whole of society. It may even explicitly reject the logic of profit and yet depend, for its own reproduction, on an economy that remains dominated by that logic.




This does not prove that autonomous experiences are false or useless. It demonstrates something far more important: that an experience can begin to negate capitalism without yet having acquired the necessary strength to abolish it.




Herein lies the question I consider crucial. Autonomy is indispensable, but how can it cease to be a particular experience? How can it extend beyond a community, a territory, or a specific network of affinities? How can it confront a system that is not organised communally, but rather through general economic relations imposed on all its members, even against their will?




In other words, the fundamental question is not merely how to begin living differently, but 

which force can transform that possibility into a general transformation of society.




My answer to this question is the proletariat, because it is a class antagonistic to capital.




Hence, the question of revolution cannot be separated from a fundamental slogan: 

The self-organisation of the proletariat.

 It is not simply a matter of asserting that workers must emancipate themselves, but of arguing that they must organise their own struggle, their own decisions, and their own capacity to transform society. Autonomy then ceases to be a mere particular experience and acquires a class dimension: 

The proletariat must self-organise in order to cease being a force subordinate to capital and become a force capable of abolishing it.




The class struggle as a way of being in the world




There is also a difference in our political and intellectual background that helps to better understand our divergences. Miquel Amorós does not come from anarcho-syndicalism, although his thinking has frequently engaged with the history and experiences of the anarchist movement, but rather from Situationism and the various intellectual currents that followed the crisis and dissolution of that movement. His fundamental starting point lies in the critique of everyday life, alienation, technology, urbanism, and modern forms of domination, and from there he has developed a radical critique of industrial and capitalist society. In this evolution, the revolutionary centrality of the class struggle tends to be displaced in favour of other categories: Community, territory, autonomy, the defence of certain ways of life, or resistance against the multiple manifestations of domination.




My trajectory and my way of being in the world are different. Born in 1950 into a family of textile workers, the class struggle is not for me a choice or an intellectual preoccupation, nor is it an inherited theoretical category that can be replaced by another, as ideological or cultural fashions change. It is a lived reality, a way of understanding society 

and knowing

 one’s place within it. My priority has been, and continues to be, the class struggle and the emancipation of workers by the workers themselves. Not emancipation granted from above by the State, directed by a party, or administered by a bureaucracy, but the conscious self-emancipation of the proletariat through its own struggle and its own organisation. Elitist free islands, whether libertarian, liberal, or libertine, neither interest me nor are they part of my horizon.




And this is not workerism. I don’t idealise the worker, nor do I believe that being born into a working-class family confers any moral, political, or revolutionary superiority. Nor do I identify the proletariat with a specific working-class culture, the traditional factory, or an inherited identity. The centrality I grant to the proletariat doesn’t stem from nostalgia for the old working-class world or from defending a sociological identity. It arises from the recognition of a fundamental social reality: we live in a class-divided society, and as long as there are those who own the means of production and those who, in order to live, must sell their labour power, class antagonism will persist.




My way of being in the world is marked by this awareness. Not because workers are better than others, nor because they possess a moral superiority or an innate revolutionary virtue, but because their position in capitalist society places them in a specific relationship with capital. They are the ones who, through their daily activities, reproduce existing society and, precisely for that reason, are the ones who have the power to stop reproducing it and reorganise it on other foundations.




Class struggle is therefore not, for me, a theoretical preference among other possibilities, nor a category that can be abandoned when new forms of domination or new political sensibilities emerge. Capitalism has profoundly transformed the composition of the proletariat, dispersed its workplaces, fragmented its experiences, and multiplied the forms of exploitation and precarity. But it has not eliminated the fundamental separation between those who possess the material conditions of existence and those who must sell their labour power in order to live.




Perhaps this is one of the most profound differences between Amorós and myself. While his reflection, stemming from Situationism and its subsequent intellectual developments, tends to seek the possibilities of emancipation in the autonomy of ways of life, in community, in territory, and in resistance against the multiple manifestations of domination, I continue to believe that the core of all revolutionary possibility lies in the class struggle and in the emancipation of workers by the workers themselves.




Autonomy, community, and concrete experiences of liberation are indispensable. But they cannot replace the need for those who live by their labour to recognise themselves as a social force capable of transforming the entirety of existing relations. Defending this centrality does not mean worshipping the worker, but rather rejecting any emancipation granted from above and affirming that the liberation of the exploited can only be the conscious work of the exploited themselves.




It is not, therefore, a question of identity, nostalgia, or workerism. It is a way of being and existing in the world: Understanding that freedom cannot be granted, represented, or administered by others, and that the emancipation of workers will be the work of the workers themselves or it will not be.




The proletariat is not an identity, but a social relation.




To understand it, we must abandon an overly narrow view of the proletariat, such as Amorós’s. The proletariat is not simply the industrial worker in the large factory, nor a particular working-class culture, nor a political identity inherited from the 19

th

 or 20

th

-century labour movement. It is a class defined by a social relation: That of those who, being separated from the means necessary to autonomously produce their existence, must sell their labour power to capital in order to live.




This definition is crucial because it allows us to understand why the proletariat occupies a position that no other social category can replace. The worker does not simply stand before capital as a victim of an external power. Their own labour power constitutes one of the conditions for the reproduction of capital. Capital buys this labour power because it needs to use it in the production process and obtain from it a value greater than what it has paid. Without wage labour, there is no valorisation of capital; and without valorisation, there is no reproduction of capital as a social relation.




The relationship between capital and the proletariat thus contains a contradiction that cannot be resolved through reforms or the mere creation of alternative spaces. Capital needs the proletariat to reproduce itself, while the proletariat can only emancipate itself by ceasing to reproduce capital. This contradiction explains the revolutionary centrality of the proletariat in a far more compelling way than any moral, historical, or identity-based consideration.




The proletariat is not the protagonist of the revolution because it is «the poorest», nor because it possesses a supposed ethical superiority, nor because a political tradition has decided to assign it that role. It is the protagonist because it occupies a unique material position within the capitalist structure: 

It produces that which allows capital to valorise itself and, precisely for this reason, can interrupt the valorisation process and begin to destroy the relationship that sustains it.




Herein lies the fundamental difference. A community can resist capital, but it does not, in itself, constitute the relationship that allows capital to reproduce itself. A territory can defend itself against capital, but it does not necessarily contain the antagonism capable of abolishing the wage relationship. A cooperative can organise an economic activity differently and still continue to function within the market. A self-managed experiment can demonstrate that it is possible to collectively organise certain tasks and, at the same time, be forced to reproduce economic relations that exist outside of it.




The proletariat, on the other hand, is at the very heart of the valorisation process. Therefore, their action can have a consequence that no isolated experience can produce: The interruption of the social reproduction of capital.




The revolution is not about managing capital differently.




This point also helps us understand what proletarian emancipation truly means. The proletariat is not called upon to seize power in order to manage capitalist society from a new position. A revolution that replaced private owners with a state or bureaucratic administration would have changed the form of ownership without necessarily abolishing the social relations that make capital possible.




Proletarian emancipation is more radical. The proletariat cannot liberate itself simply by becoming the collective owners of businesses, because that would preserve fundamental forms of separation between producers and the social conditions of production. Nor can it limit itself to improving the conditions of wage labour, because wages themselves presuppose the separation that constitutes the worker as a proletarian.




The revolutionary goal, therefore, is not for the proletariat to find a better place within capitalist society. Its goal is for it to cease to exist as a proletariat through the abolition of the social relations that constitute it as such.




This is why proletarian protagonism does not lead to a new class society, but rather to the possibility of abolishing classes altogether. The working class does not emancipate itself to become the ruling class. It emancipates itself by destroying the conditions that make the existence of ruling and dominated classes possible. Therein lies the universal character of its struggle.




The transformation of the proletariat does not mean its disappearance




It could be objected that all of this pertains to a class composition that no longer exists. Indeed, the contemporary proletariat does not present the same forms it had in other eras. But to confuse the historical transformation of the proletariat with its disappearance would mean accepting precisely the superficial definition that should be rejected.




Capitalism has fragmented labour, shifted production to a global scale, multiplied forms of employment, and extended precariousness. The contemporary worker can be found in a factory, a hospital, a hotel, a logistics warehouse, a digital platform, an office, a farm, or in the care economy. The traditional boundaries between production and reproduction have become much more complex.




But none of these transformations eliminates the fundamental relationship of those who need to sell their labour power to reproduce their existence. The class has changed its composition because capitalism has changed; it has not disappeared because its composition has changed.




Precisely because capitalism has dispersed the proletariat, the political question is to rebuild its unity based on what it has in common, not to replace it with a vaguer category. This is especially important in an era when the fragmentation of social experiences can give the impression that there is no longer a subject capable of acting upon the whole.




The revolutionary problem of our time is not to find a new identity to replace the proletariat. It is 

to find the proletariat where capitalism has dispersed it.




Community cannot take the place of class.




Community can be an extraordinarily important space of resistance. It can protect needs that the market destroys, rebuild bonds that competition dissolves, and produce concrete experiences of cooperation. It can even become a privileged terrain for revolutionary organisation.




But community and class are not equivalent concepts.




A territorial community can bring together people subjected to different social relations. It can include workers and owners, wage earners and rentiers, exploited people and people who benefit from certain forms of ownership. They can unite against a specific enemy and yet separate when the question of ownership or the appropriation of wealth arises.




Therefore, territorial struggles can be contemporary expressions of the class struggle without territory becoming the new universal subject. The issue is not to deny these struggles, but to understand when and how they express class antagonism and how they can be integrated into a struggle capable of challenging capitalist relations as a whole. The same applies to ecology, housing, care work, and territorial defence. Capitalism permeates all these dimensions of existence, and for that very reason, they are fundamental arenas for contemporary proletarian struggle. But they remain intertwined with class. The issue is not finding a new subject to replace the proletariat, but rather recognising the proletariat wherever capitalism has extended and transformed its forms of exploitation.




Autonomy needs a force capable of generalising it.




Herein lies the point where the question of the proletariat acquires its full importance. Autonomy is not the problem; the problem is its limits when it remains isolated.




If an autonomous experience remains separate, capitalism can surround it, condition it, absorb it, or simply wait for its exhaustion. If it manages to spread, the question of its coordination and its confrontation with general social relations immediately arises. At that point, it is no longer enough to speak of community: The need for a force capable of intervening in social reproduction emerges.




The revolution cannot consist of endlessly multiplying small exceptions to capitalism. It must transform these exceptions into a new and general form of the reproduction of life. To do this, it is necessary to appropriate what is currently organised by capital: workplaces, the means of production, distribution networks, infrastructure, urban spaces, and, ultimately, the material conditions of existence.




This appropriation cannot be carried out by an isolated community. Only a class that, by virtue of its position in the production process, has the capacity to halt and reorganise that process can achieve this. At this point, autonomy ceases to be merely a mode of organisation and becomes a question of social power: Who has the effective capacity to stop the functioning of capitalist society and set in motion another form of life reproduction? The answer remains the proletariat.




The question of parliamentarism




Parliamentarism occupies a much smaller place in this difference than is sometimes claimed. We are both anti-parliamentarian, but we don’t understand exactly what needs to be overcome when parliamentarism is rejected: Amorós insists more on the incompatibility between emancipation and institutional representation, while I link this critique to a broader issue: The autonomy of the proletarian movement in the face of any form of separate power and the need for decisions to remain in the hands of those directly involved in the struggle.




Therefore, the problem is not simply refusing to participate in Parliament. The problem is preventing the separation between those who struggle and those who speak on their behalf from recurring. And this question only acquires its full meaning when it is linked to the central problem: Which class should retain in its own hands the capacity to decide on its struggle and on the transformation of society.




1936: When autonomy ceased to be an idea




The Spanish revolutionary experience allows us to understand this issue concretely. In 1936, the workers did not wait for any institution to recognise their right to transform society. They created their own organisations, occupied factories and land, organised militias and collectives, and effectively altered power relations. This was much more than a communal experience: It was a proletarian uprising capable of profoundly altering the existing social reproduction.




But that experience also revealed the decisive difficulty: As long as state structures capable of regaining authority existed, and as long as revolutionary organisations could not impose autonomous social coordination against them, the gains could be contained and ultimately defeated. The events of May 1937 constituted a brutal expression of this contradiction.




The lesson is not to claim that the collectives were a mistake. It is to understand that they were insufficient because their social force did not become widespread enough to destroy the relations that could return power to the State and capital.




This is a fundamental difference. Revolutionary autonomy does not fail because it is too autonomous; it fails when it cannot become a sufficiently broad social force to prevent the reconstruction of what it seeks to abolish. And this problem brings us back to the proletariat.




Here, therefore, appears the slogan that summarises the fundamental political problem: 

The self-organisation of the proletariat.

 If capitalism has fragmented the workers, dispersed their experiences, and weakened their traditional forms of organisation, the task is not to wait for an institution to once again represent their unity. Nor is it to replace the proletariat with a sum of particular communities, movements, or identities. The task is for the proletarians themselves to rebuild their capacity to recognise, deliberate, decide, and act collectively.




Self-organisation

 means precisely that the organisation of the struggle cannot be separated from those who struggle. It means that decisions remain in the hands of the workers and that no external leadership can appropriate their power, speak permanently on their behalf, or replace their initiative. But it also means something more: That organisation is not an external instrument simply intended to achieve reforms, but rather the process by which the proletariat begins to recognise itself as a common social force, capable of halting the reproduction of capital and reorganising life on other foundations.




Therefore, the slogan cannot simply be “autonomy,” but rather 

the self-organisation of the proletariat.

 Autonomy signifies the need for independence from the state, political parties, integrated trade unions, and all forms of separate power; self-organisation indicates 

who

 should exercise that autonomy and 

how

 it can become an effective historical force. The crucial issue is that those who produce and reproduce capitalist society must learn to organise themselves in order to cease reproducing it.




Autonomy as a form of proletarian revolution




From this perspective, defending the proletariat does not mean abandoning autonomy, but rather giving it concrete social content. Autonomy means that the class organises itself and that no institution, party, union, or external leadership can replace it. It does not mean building a sphere separate from capitalism, but rather acquiring the capacity to confront it and transform the relations that organise society.




Therefore, it also does not mean living indefinitely in small, alternative spaces. It means beginning to build, from concrete struggles, a different form of social reproduction. And it does not mean replacing the State with an organisation that governs in the name of the workers, but rather preventing the re-emergence of a separation between those who decide and those who obey.




The proletariat is the protagonist of the revolution precisely when it ceases to be understood as a passive sociological category and begins to act as a social force conscious of its position. It is a class that produces, transports, cares, builds, cleans, cultivates, distributes, and maintains the infrastructure and services upon which society depends. It does so, however, under conditions determined by capital. This position constitutes its weakness as long as it remains subordinate, but this is also its historical strength, because those who participate decisively in the material reproduction of society possess the power to disrupt and reorganise it.




The bourgeoisie possesses capital, and the state has coercion at its disposal, but neither can replace the activity of the proletariat. When this activity ceases to be subordinate to capital, the material foundation of existing society begins to disappear.




Revolutionary optimism




Defending proletarian leadership today should not be a defensive stance, a nostalgic exercise, or a ritualistic repetition of old formulas. On the contrary, it is a profoundly optimistic affirmation. It means recognising that capitalism is not an invulnerable whole and that society is not condemned to reproduce itself eternally under the same relations. It means understanding that the force that keeps this society functioning is also the force that can stop it.




We don’t need to invent the subject of revolution from the outside. That subject already exists. It exists wherever someone has to sell their labour power to live; it exists wherever an activity necessary for society is subordinated to the production of value; it exists in the factory and the hospital, in the hotel and the logistics warehouse, in the countryside, in transportation, on the digital platform, and in care work. It exists wherever capital needs labour to reproduce itself.




What still doesn’t exist to the necessary degree is the awareness of that force, its autonomous organisation, and its capacity to recognise itself as a common force. That is the fundamental political problem of our time.




The issue, therefore, is not abandoning concrete utopia, but preventing concrete utopia from becoming a substitute for revolution. It is not a matter of choosing between living now and transforming the world, but of transforming the world so that what we can only experience today as an exception can become the common condition for all.




The proletariat and the possibility of revolution




This is, ultimately, the reason why I defend the proletarian leading role in the revolution. Not because all other struggles are unimportant, nor because the entire working class automatically acts in a revolutionary manner, nor because the proletariat possesses an innate revolutionary consciousness, and certainly not because one must uphold a promise out of fidelity to tradition. I defend it because its position within capitalism contains a possibility that no other social position contains in the same way: 

The possibility of abolishing the relationship upon which the reproduction of capital depends.




Capital has done everything possible to fragment the proletariat, to individualise it, to make it precarious, to pit it against itself, and to convince each worker that they exist solely as an individual competing with others for survival. But this fragmentation has not destroyed the social relationship that binds them together. Wherever there is wage labour, wherever life depends on selling one’s labour power, wherever capital needs to appropriate the labour of others to increase its value, antagonism still exists.




The revolutionary task is not to invent something else to replace it. It is to make conscious, organised, and effective the force that already exists. Therefore, the revolutionary horizon is not a community that has managed to escape the world, but a world from which escape is no longer necessary. We do not want to conquer a corner of freedom while the rest of society remains subjugated. We want freedom to cease being the privilege of those who have managed to build a protected space and to become the material condition of everyone.




We do not wait for a historical saviour to appear. We do not wait for a vanguard to think for us. We do not wait for the State to grant us freedom. The force capable of radically transforming the world already exists within it: It is the force of those who, working every day to reproduce capitalist society, can one day decide to stop reproducing it.




The revolution begins when the proletariat understands that it is not condemned to be the labour force of capital, but that it can become the social force capable of abolishing it. Then the struggle ceases to be a desperate defence against advancing barbarism and becomes a conscious offensive for human emancipation. It is no longer a question of conquering a more dignified place within a world that condemns us to exploitation, but of ending the social relations that make exploitation possible; it is no longer a question of preserving a few spaces of freedom within existing society, but of making freedom the foundation of all society.




Because this is, ultimately, the question before us: 

Either capital leads humanity toward ever-deepening barbarism, or the proletariat finds in its own strength the capacity to stop it and pave the way for a world without classes, without exploitation and domination, without police, without armies, without borders, without states.




The revolution will not be the administration of an inherited world, but its conscious abolition to make another possible. The slogan that emerges from all of the above is, therefore, simple and at the same time decisive: 

the self-organisation of the proletariat.

 We do not expect anyone to organise from the outside the force capable of emancipating us. We do not expect an institution to represent us, a vanguard to think for us, or a State to transform existing social relations from above.




Revolutionary organisation can only arise from the struggle itself, from the capacity of the exploited to recognise themselves as a common force and to take into their own hands the decisions that affect their existence. 

Self-organisation

 does not mean confining oneself to a working-class identity or building an organisation separate from society; 

it means collectively organising the force of those who live by their labour to abolish the social relations that make them proletarians.




Therefore, in the face of fragmentation, representation, and delegation, the slogan remains: 

self-organisation of the proletariat.

 Not as an empty formula, but as the concrete process by which the class that reproduces the world of capital today can begin to organise its abolition.




And this time we will not fight to conquer the future: We will fight so that, at last, the future ceases to belong to capital and belongs to emancipated humanity.

title: Senado fecha projeto de Ajuste Fiscal essa semana e envia para Câmara dos Deputados
content:
Com a aprovação do texto principal do projeto de Ajuste Fiscal apresentado pelo governo no Senado, os destaques devem ser votados nesta terça-feira, 17 de novembro. O projeto, PLP 299/2026, com relatoria do senador Eduardo Braga (MDB-AM), foi aprovado com 45 votos a favor.




Agora, senadores votarão quatro propostas apresentadas pelos senadores Alan Rick (Republicanos-AC), Izalci Lucas (PL-DF) e Rogério Marinho (PL-RN) antes de ir para análise da Câmara dos Deputados.




Os destaques envolvem a retirada da regra de adiar R$ 12 bilhões de transferências entre 2027 e 2030, a separação do dispositivo que limita as compensações financeiras entre regimes previdenciários a R$ 3 bilhões anuais

; o fim das restrições ao uso de créditos dos contribuintes e a redução para 0,6% do crescimento das despesas em determinadas operações.




O ajuste já aprovado no Senado prevê que o governo poderá bloquear despesas no orçamento, reduzir o orçamento com gastos acima da inflação de 2,5% para 2% e reduzir de R$ 4 bilhões para R$ 1 bilhão os repasses para os estados e municípios. O ministro do Planejamento e Orçamento, Bruno Moretti, durante a Comissão Mista de Orçamento, declarou que, com a aprovação do novo ajuste fiscal, a redução dos gastos em 2027 poderá chegar a até R$ 60 bilhões.




Entretanto, a proposta foi criticada por alguns apoiadores do governo. A deputada federal eleita, 

Ana Elisa (PT-MG), fez uma postagem contra o ajuste fiscal, dizendo que “responsabilidade fiscal não significa sacrificar a população para atender aos interesses do mercado financeiro”

. Já o deputado eleito Jones Manoel (PSOL-PE) também se posicionou contra a proposta em seu canal do YouTube, falando que o novo ajuste pode “destruir o futuro do Brasil”.




Na Câmara dos Deputados, Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), presidente da Casa, já anunciou que, assim que aprovado no Senado Federal, deve colocar o ajuste fiscal em votação com urgência.

 Na última sexta-feira, Motta se reuniu com Davi Alcolumbre, presidente do Senado, e com o líder do PT, Pedro Uczai (PT-SC), e o ministro das Relações Institucionais, José Guimarães, que pediu uma votação do PLP 299/2026 com celeridade na Câmara.




Reforma do Judiciário




O presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), ministro Edson Fachin, deve realizar na próxima quarta-feira, 18 de novembro, uma reunião para debater a Reforma do Judiciário, segundo 

apuração do G1

. O grupo que participa do encontro foi formado pelo ministro com o objetivo de discutir a Reforma e conta com outros membros do Supremo, além de representantes do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) e do Superior Tribunal de Justiça (STJ).




Entre seus objetivos está apresentar propostas para a modernização do sistema judicial.

 A expectativa inicial de Fachin era apresentar o projeto de Reforma do Judiciário em dezembro, mas o prazo deve ser estendido até 2027 diante da complexidade do tema.




Estão na agenda da semana de 02 a 06 de novembro:




DIREITOS HUMANOS







Câmara







Padrão Nacional Mínimo do Boletim de Ocorrência (CPD, 17/11, 14h):

 Comissão debate a integração dos estados e do Distrito Federal ao Sistema Nacional de Informações de Segurança Pública (SINESP), criando um padrão nacional do boletim de ocorrência e prevê a identificação de mulheres com deficiência nos registros de ocorrências policiais;










STF







Cota mínima em fundo partidário (ADI 7419, 18/11, 14h):

 Ministros julgam se a anistia para partidos políticos que não cumpriram as cotas raciais e de gênero e a destinação de recursos mínimos para candidaturas de pessoas negras e mulheres em eleições anteriores a 2022;




Pagamentos de honorários (ADI 7694 e 5405, 18/11, 14h):

 Ministros julgam determinação que dispensa do pagamento de honorários advocatícios em casos de acordos com o poder público e limita remuneração dos procuradores na defesa dos interesses do estado;




Crimes patrimoniais (ADPF 1185 e ADPF 1241, 18/11, 14h):

 Ministros julgam se homens que cometem crimes patrimoniais contra suas esposas ou familiares no contexto de violência doméstica podem continuar isentos de punição;




Liberdade de imprensa (Rcl 78354, 17/11, 14h)

: Ministros julgam se a condenação imposta pelo tribunal do Paraná à Rádio e Televisão Iguaçu S.A. realmente violou a liberdade de imprensa garantida pela Constituição;













ECONOMIA







Câmara







Pirataria e falsificação de bebidas e cigarros (CEXBRLEG, 17/11, 15h):

 Comissão sobre os atos de pirataria e a agenda do “Brasil Legal” discute o impacto econômico e mecanismos de combate à falsificação no mercado de bebidas e cigarros;




PLOA 2027 (CICS, 17/11, 15h):

 Comissão vota em sugestões de emendas do PLOA 2027;










Senado







CBS de 2027 (CAE, 17/11, 10h):

 Comissão discute, em audiência pública, o cálculo da alíquota de referência da Contribuição Social sobre Bens e Serviços. (CBS) para o exercício de 2027. Debate terá a presença de Dario Durigan e do Secretário Especial da Receita Federal do Brasil, Robinson Barreirinhas;













POLÍTICA







Câmara







Instalação da comissão (CMMPV 1393/2026, 17/11, 14h30):

 É instalada a comissão sobre a medida provisória 1393/2026, que debate o plano Desenrola Brasil 3.0; é votado o presidente e vice-presidente da comissão;










STF







Nepotismo em serviço público (RE 1133118, 18/11, 14h):

 Ministros julgam se a proibição do nepotismo também vale para cargos políticos do primeiro escalão do Poder Executivo nas esferas federal, estadual e municipal.

Pública

 

é um serviço apresentado aos leitores, concebido com base nas informações dos portais da Câmara, Senado e STF.
