title: The memory of a cartoon: From Qırıx to Bajar
content:
Doğan Güzel's cartoons carry a collective memory stretching from the streets of Diyarbakır (Amed) in the 1990s to the present day. Born out of everyday life, political conflicts and social contradictions, Qırıx gradually became more than a cartoon character, emerging as a figure representing the youth of the period and the transformation experienced by Kurdish society. Güzel's work, which continued through humor publications such as Gırgır, TEW-LO, Pîne and Zrîng, has now taken a new form with Bajar magazine. This long-running journey seeks not only to preserve the collective memory of the past but also to create space for the written use of Kurdish through cartoons and comics.




Güzel's journey as a cartoonist began with a character he created by observing the people around him and the political atmosphere of the time. Doğan Güzel, who spoke to ANF, said that he began drawing cartoons for Gırgır magazine and described his need to create a character he could draw every day.




Güzel said: "Since I was among patriotic young people, I wanted to create a character I could draw every day without too much difficulty whenever I needed to produce something in response to newspaper headlines. I looked around and observed my fellow students. I tried to create a character by combining Kurdish culture with something familiar to me. I think the character resonated with people because I drew him sincerely, without forcing myself too much.




Although my drawings were amateurish, I was naturally reflecting the period as I tried to portray the people around me. I was depicting the world of young people who were just becoming involved in politics, taking part in protests and experiencing uncertainty. I combined the experiences of students in Istanbul with the social reality of Kurdish people. Perhaps that is why the character became popular. When you draw by observing your surroundings, you also reflect the pulse of the country you live in."




Qırıx first appears in Özgür Gündem




Qırıx appeared in the pages of Özgür Gündem between 1992 and 1995. Politics in the character's world was not limited to developments reported in newspaper headlines. Young people's friendships, everyday decisions, uncertainties about joining the struggle and questions about how to lead their lives were also part of that world.




Güzel described the political atmosphere in which the character emerged and the uncertainties experienced by young people. 




Güzel said: "There was intense political activity in Istanbul in 1991, 1992 and 1993. It was a period when Kurdish young people were discovering their identities and becoming involved in politics, with demonstrations taking place every day. Young people felt they had to make major decisions. They were asking themselves, 'What should I do? How should I act? Where do I stand in this struggle?' This atmosphere was reflected in my cartoons. Keko's incomplete understanding of politics, his uncertainty about whether to join the struggle, his constant changes of mind and the ambiguity over whether these feelings were sincere or driven by other reasons reflected the experiences of young people at the time. There were strong similarities between what was happening in Kurdistan and the experiences of young people in Istanbul. The problems were shared, and young people were confronting similar questions."




Qırıx's significance lay not in being a character who observed the political struggle from the outside, but in embodying the contradictions experienced by young people in his own everyday life. The character reflected a generation struggling to make decisions, changing alongside social conditions and sometimes confronting its own contradictions.




T

he politics of everyday life







The years in which Qırıx emerged were marked by armed clashes, detentions, village evacuations and state violence that shaped everyday life in Kurdish cities. Güzel's cartoons, however, portrayed this harsh reality not simply through political messages but also through the seemingly ordinary lives of people.




Güzel said that he had not initially expected his drawings to attract so much attention. He described his style as different from conventional newspaper humor and reflected on both the character's popularity and the discomfort it caused.




Güzel also said: "I started drawing cartoons at a very young age. Initially, I did not think my work would attract so much attention. My style was different from conventional newspaper humor. I had a more absurdist approach to humor, and I did not expect my drawings to receive much attention. Over time, however, I realized that portraying Kurdish experiences so naturally and as something legitimate through a character loved in patriotic circles was itself enough to cause discomfort.




I was portraying someone who could be seen as a terrorist by Turks and as an adventurer by Kurds, but I was showing his human side. I drew him as one of us, someone who lived and thought like us. I think that was what attracted the most attention."




The human qualities, fears, weaknesses and contradictions of Güzel's characters also found expression in his drawings. A way of life portrayed from the outside as dangerous or extraordinary was thus depicted through the everyday reality of the people who experienced it.







Güzel particularly valued the character's ability to express Kurdish politics and social life in his own language. He also believes that this aspect of his cartoons contributed to his prosecution and imprisonment: "Keko was a character who could speak about Kurdish politics and social reality in his own language without being ashamed of himself. At the time, it was unusual to portray Kurdish political experiences, the struggle and everyday life so naturally. Newspapers featured harsher, more rigid drawings with explicit political messages. But portraying our experiences from within, sincerely and as an ordinary part of everyday life, had a different impact. For us, these experiences were already a natural part of life.




What Keko did was make a reality portrayed from the outside as frightening or dangerous visible in its natural form. I believe this approach was also a factor behind my prosecution and imprisonment over these works."




Cartoons on trial




Doğan Güzel was prosecuted in 1993 over the Qırıx cartoon strips he drew for Özgür Gündem. He was charged under Article 159 of the Turkish Penal Code in force at the time and sentenced to a total of 40 months in prison in 1998. Güzel was imprisoned on 31 July 1998 and released on 16 September 1999. That same year, he received the Courage in Editorial Cartooning Award from Cartoonists Rights Network International.




Güzel's experiences became one example of the repression of the Kurdish press and freedom of expression in the field of cartooning. In his account, the underlying issue was his approach to portraying Kurdish experiences naturally, within the context of everyday life.







From Pîne to Zrîng




Güzel continued producing work for different publications after Qırıx. Pîne magazine, which began publication in 1999, marked a new period in Kurdish-language humor and continued until 2002. Years later, in 2019, Zrîng, edited by Doğan Güzel and İmam Cici, began publication. The magazine was planned to appear in two separate editions, in Kurmanji and Kirmanjki.




These publications were part of an effort not only to sustain Kurdish-language humor but also to create opportunities for new cartoonists and stories. However, the future of written humor depended not only on publishing conditions but also on the development of reading habits and the wider use of Kurdish as a written language.




Güzel said that he does not follow contemporary Kurdish-language humor very closely, although he has seen work produced on platforms such as YouTube: "Sometimes amateur productions can be of higher quality than work created with professional equipment and resources. This development was natural, and I believe even better work will emerge. In this sense, we continue to learn and develop."




Güzel believes that the relationship between cartoons and written language is both one of the art form's defining characteristics and a challenge for written culture. He said that the decline of humor magazines has also affected Kurdish-language publications, emphasizing the need to develop the written use of Kurdish and reading habits: "An important characteristic of cartoons is that they exist alongside writing. The combination of drawings and words in humor distinguishes it from other forms of expression. However, its dependence on written culture also creates difficulties. Today, humor magazines are declining not only in Kurdistan but throughout the world.




In Turkey, magazines have closed one after another. It is impossible for this not to affect Kurdish-language humor. But there is another issue concerning Kurdish: the need to develop its written use and a culture of reading. Kurdish needs to be taught in schools, used as a written language and made more widespread. For people to engage with written humor, they need to have developed reading habits to some extent. Although this presents a challenge, it also offers an important opportunity. Cartoons and comics can help encourage people to start reading in Kurdish."




Continuing to draw in exile




The legal cases and pressure Güzel faced also changed the course of his life. He applied for political asylum in Spain in 2012 and subsequently obtained Spanish citizenship. He continued producing work for the Kurdish press while living in Europe.




Exile, however, did not erase Diyarbakır from Güzel's drawings. The city remained present in his work as a world where language, characters and collective memory came together.




Detained again




Doğan Güzel was among the journalists detained during a police operation against the Özgür Gündem newspaper on 17 August 2016. A photograph showing his torn shirt as police took him away during the raid on the newspaper's offices became one of the symbols of repression against the press. Güzel and the other journalists were released two days later.




Güzel, who had been imprisoned years earlier over his cartoons, was now detained outside the newspaper where he worked. The incident showed how questions of press freedom and freedom of expression had resurfaced at different stages of his life.




Bajar: Comics to encourage reading in Kurdish




One of the latest chapters in Güzel's artistic journey is Bajar magazine, which began publication in 2026. The Kurdish-language cartoon and comic magazine, produced under the auspices of Diyarbakır Metropolitan Municipality, is edited by Doğan Güzel and İmam Cici. The first issue of the magazine, published in Kurmanji, was introduced in June 2026. It aims to support the practical use of Kurdish and encourage children to begin reading in the language.




Güzel emphasized that the idea behind Bajar was to establish a mutually supportive relationship between Kurdish and publishing: "We thought that publishing the magazine only in Turkish would limit our ability to reach readers. Instead, we wanted to establish a reciprocal relationship with Kurdish and the language itself. Our aim was to create a publication that could contribute to the written use of Kurdish and help people learn the language through reading. That was why we launched Bajar. The magazine is currently published every two months and consists of 24 pages.




I believe this is a project that can be developed further in the coming period. If Kurdish-language education becomes more widespread in schools and courses, publications of this kind could once again play an important role. The magazine contributes to the development of Kurdish while also drawing strength from the language's continued existence and development. I consider this mutually beneficial relationship important."




Bajar takes the aspirations behind Güzel's earlier publishing experiences into a new field. The cartoons that spoke from within everyday life and political transformation in the world of Qırıx took on new forms in Kurdish-language humor magazines through Pîne and Zrîng. Bajar, meanwhile, approaches comics as a means of helping children develop reading habits in their mother tongue.




Why is Qırıx still remembered?




Qırıx is remembered decades later not simply because he was a humorous character. He portrayed the youth of the 1990s, Diyarbakır's neighborhood culture and the political atmosphere of the period through everyday life. Young people's uncertainties, social transformation and their changing relationship with politics were central elements of the cartoons.




The character reached new generations when Diyarbakır City Theatre brought Qırıx to the stage in 2017. Moving from newspaper pages to the theater, the character found a new form of storytelling.




Güzel's work was not limited to a single character. The artist, who portrayed the youth, everyday life and social contradictions of the 1990s through Qırıx, continued his work in Kurdish-language humor in subsequent years through publications such as Pîne and Zrîng.




Bajar carries this legacy forward through a new publishing approach aimed at helping children develop the habit of reading in Kurdish.




The memory carried by cartoons




Qırıx portrayed the young people of his time, Diyarbakır's neighborhood culture and its political atmosphere through everyday life. The character's adaptation for the theater years later also demonstrated that his story had not remained confined to newspaper pages but could reach new generations in different forms.




Pîne and Zrîng represent different periods of Güzel's work in Kurdish-language humor, while Bajar approaches cartoons and comics as tools that can encourage children to read and write in their mother tongue. Güzel's artistic journey therefore encompasses not only a cartoonist's decades of work but also an effort to give Kurdish a greater place in everyday life through humor and publishing.




The journey from Qırıx, which portrayed the youth and contradictions of an era in newspaper pages, to Bajar, which aims to encourage children to enjoy reading in Kurdish, reflects a change in both the audience and the purpose of the cartoons. Yet the effort to tell stories through drawings, document lived experiences and create space for the written use of Kurdish continues to connect the different periods of Güzel's work.

title: Zidane'dan Mbappe açıklaması: Türkiye maçında oynayabilecek mi?
content:
Fotoğraf: Кирилл Венедиктов/Wikimedia Commons CC BY-SA 3.0

Fransa A Milli Futbol Takımı Teknik Direktörü Zinedine Zidane ve futbolcu Lucas Da Cunha, yarın Türkiye ile oynanacak kritik karşılaşma öncesinde Bordeaux şehrindeki Matmut Atlantique Stadı'nda basın toplantısı düzenledi. İtalya deplasmanında mağlup olduklarını hatırlatan Zidane, yarın sahadan galibiyetle ayrılmaktan başka düşünceleri olmadığını vurguladı.

Üst tura yükselmek için kazanmak zorunda olduklarının altını çizen Fransız teknik direktör, "Türkiye yarın bize zorluk çıkaracak. Buna çok dikkat etmeliyiz. Fransa olarak iyi bir maç ortaya koymalıyız" dedi. İtalya maçında yedikleri 3 golün savunmanın zayıflığından kaynaklanmadığını ifade eden Zidane, milli takımlarda antrenman yapmaya vakit bulamadıklarını, belirli bir oyun felsefeleri olduğunu ve tek amaçlarının üst tura çıkmak olduğunu belirtti.

Basın toplantısında en çok merak edilen konuların başında gelen Kylian Mbappe'nin sakatlık durumuna da değinen Zidane, yıldız oyuncunun herhangi bir problemi bulunmadığını ve yarın Türkiye karşısında forma giyebilecek durumda olduğunu açıkladı.

Toplantıya katılan futbolcu Lucas Da Cunha ise teknik direktörünün kendisine duyduğu güvenden duyduğu memnuniyeti dile getirerek, tek hedeflerinin sahadan galibiyetle ayrılmak olduğunu söyledi.

author: Natália Perez
title: Bolsonarismo além da presidência: “Extrema direita não sai derrotada”, avalia especialista
content:
Desde o dia seguinte à derrota de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) nas eleições presidenciais de 2026, o senador da República segue morando nos Estados Unidos, para onde fugiu após o ministro Alexandre de Moraes determinar a entrega de seus passaportes – o mesmo caminho do irmão e ex-deputado Eduardo Bolsonaro, no ano anterior, também para evitar os inquéritos dos quais são alvo na Justiça.




Nos EUA, os Bolsonaros buscam a proximidade com Donald Trump e seu entorno político. Mas a recente derrota dos republicanos nas eleições legislativas de meio de mandato pode representar um enfraquecimento da extrema direita defendida por essas figuras políticas?

 Este é o tema do 

Pauta Pública

 desta semana que recebe Odilon Caldeira Neto, historiador, professor da Universidade Federal de Juiz de Fora (UFJF) e coordenador do Observatório da Extrema Direita. Para ele, “a despeito da imensa vitória que foi a reeleição do presidente Lula, o campo da extrema direita brasileira não sai derrotado”.




Na conversa com Andrea Dip, ele também analisa os desafios do campo progressista para os próximos anos. “O processo que culminou nas mobilizações para a eleição de Lula não é o ponto final, na verdade são pontos de partida […] assim como a direita criou uma nova geração a partir das mobilizações das ruas, a partir das formas de pulverização e de atuação na sociedade, as esquerdas também precisam pensar a partir dessa realidade ou, se não, essas conquistas muito importantes podem ser espécies de respiros, podem ser ganhos pontuais”, afirma.




Leia os principais pontos da conversa e ouça o podcast completo abaixo.























































EP 242


											O início do fim do bolsonarismo? — com Odilon Caldeira Neto							













13 de novembro de 2026


					·
				


				Historiador reflete sobre os rumos da extrema direita e os desafios do campo progressista





























































0:00




-:–



















15




15
































































Veja mais episódios desta série










Após a fuga e as cartas atrapalhadas de Flávio, as três versões delas, qual análise pode ser feita sobre as reconfigurações do bolsonarismo e como a figura do Tarcísio se encaixa nesse momento?




Existe um espólio em disputa no campo bolsonarista que se configura de diversas maneiras, inclusive intrafamiliar. O caso de Eduardo Bolsonaro e o caso de Flávio Bolsonaro trazem consigo alguma espécie de capital, mas distantes do cenário político brasileiro.

 É interessante focar a análise nas figuras que vão, em certa medida, buscar articular atores e atrizes – atrizes, justamente, pela presença da Michele Bolsonaro –, e talvez um ator do campo bolsonarista familiar, o Carlos Bolsonaro. Agora, Carlos assumiu posição de um certo protagonismo, tendo visitado o pai na prisão domiciliar, em sua residência, ele tem sido uma espécie de interlocutor.




Porém, a figura de Michelle Bolsonaro não pode ser menosprezada de maneira alguma, por várias razões: da capacidade política à forma como ela liderou até recentemente o PL Mulher, a forma como ela integra setores eleitoralmente muito interessantes, com relação aos setores do conservadorismo evangélico, de um voto feminino que é sempre um gargalo para a extrema direita brasileira. Então, sem dúvida alguma, a Michelle é uma atriz de fundamental importância.




Inclusive, o campo bolsonarista tem manifestado, de maneira crescente, espécies de reações à figura de Michelle. Tem sido muito comum a referência à utilização de outros sobrenomes atribuídos à Michelle, que não o Bolsonaro, ou seja, existe uma tensão familiar, que pode ser resolvida dependendo da capacidade política de Michelle Bolsonaro.




Um campo que ainda há de se configurar, mas tem um elemento importante de situar que é o desejo de reflexões e de mudanças no caráter da prisão de Jair Bolsonaro, ou seja, mais uma vez a questão da anistia.

 O quadro de Jair Bolsonaro lida ainda um pouco com a questão, não somente da tensão entre o STF e o campo bolsonarista, mas também pela configuração da Câmara e do Senado.




Por outro lado, existe um campo de disputa da juventude de extrema direita que tem sido mobilizado nas últimas semanas pelo partido Missão. Renan Santos conseguiu articular bem um certo domínio do cenário das redes nas últimas semanas, inclusive, da forma um tanto ambivalente ou paradoxal que ele se colocou ao longo do segundo turno.




Outro cenário é o campo dos mais jovens eleitos nesse dado momento. A figura do Pavanato parece uma figura importante e, claro, a Eduarda Campopiano. É claro que tanto Pavanato quanto Eduarda Campopiano saem um pouco machucados deste processo da eleição de Lula, mas ainda assim, saíram em alguma medida vitoriosos no processo da eleição da Câmara e do Senado. Então, existe um campo em disputa que convém considerar muitas dessas figuras jovens do campo bolsonarista.




Por fim, fica a figura de Tarcísio, que tem como desafio talvez pensar uma articulação com Michelle Bolsonaro. Não sei se será feito, mas à primeira vista parece uma saída.

 A articulação com Carlos Bolsonaro não parece uma questão muito capaz de ser concretizada, porque diz respeito às estratégias e a natureza política de Carlos Bolsonaro. Já a juventude, acredito, há de ser eventualmente mobilizada por Tarcísio, até porque muitas dessas figuras não têm sequer idade para serem alçadas à candidatura presidencial. 




Então, Tarcísio tem um desafio pela frente. Não me parece muito clara a forma como esse campo, que denominamos até dado momento de bolsonarismo, vai se consolidar. Inclusive, é importante, analiticamente falando, olharmos esse quadro a partir daquilo que esses fenômenos: o fato é que são figuras, lideranças, representantes da extrema direita brasileira.




Quais são os perigos reais que a extrema direita ainda apresenta, inclusive na juventude, pensando na candidatura de Renan Santos e nas votações expressivas de Nikolas Ferreira. Eles são de fato uma ameaça?

Renan Santos tem uma capacidade de oratória muito interessante. Tem um certo carisma na forma como ele se comunica, mas estruturalmente falando, do ponto de vista da sua legenda partidária e capacidade de criar pontes – que na política é uma questão de fundamental importância –, Renan Santos não demonstra muita disposição.




O 

Partido Missão

 é um projeto que almeja uma longa duração em dois termos: longa duração do projeto que busca construir e também de um eventual e hipotético sucesso que talvez tarde a acontecer.

 Um processo que concretize uma cultura de extrema direita, inclusive com viabilidade política além da efemeridade do campo institucional.




Nesse sentido, do ponto de vista de um projeto político, o Partido Missão é muito ambicioso. Não me parece, nesse dado momento, que ele consiga, mas o estilo comunicacional que tem sido colocado em prática tem suscitado não apenas uma boa indústria de takes e de cortes, mas vejo que o discurso de Renan Santos tem se tornado muito palatável.




É um ponto inicial importante a considerar: existe um projeto aqui sendo colocado, existe um projeto que é parte deste universo do extremismo de direita e pode render frutos. Agora, nesse contexto, a figura do Nikolas Ferreira é uma figura de liderança muito grande, muito forte no cenário bolsonarista. É claro, parte disso é consolidado a partir da forma de aliança das big techs com o cenário da extrema direita global e particularmente brasileira.




Mas mesmo diante disso, não podemos desconsiderar a quantidade de votos que o Nikolas teve: foram mais de 3 milhões de votos, não é algo a se desconsiderar. 

Agora, embora seja uma liderança proeminente, não me parece que nesse dado momento Nikolas Ferreira tenha capacidade de articulação central do campo bolsonarista.




Talvez seja uma estratégia que ele vá colocar em prática a partir desse mandato. Ou seja, se descolar um pouco da eterna indústria de códigos, de vídeo, de reacts, para se transformar, efetivamente, em um formulador para a extrema direita brasileira. Mas o problema do Nikolas é que ele terá de lidar com as disputas do campo bolsonarista. É uma espada de dois gumes. Por um lado, Renan tem uma grande capacidade e um campo, onde ele consegue conceber uma ideia de pureza ideológica, mas que é limitado. Por outro lado, o Nikolas Ferreira tem uma máquina muito grande, mas não adquire espaço de centralidade.




O mais importante é considerar que a despeito da imensa vitória que foi a reeleição do presidente Lula, 

o campo da extrema direita brasileira não saiu derrotado. Ele saiu efetivamente fortalecido e demonstra que figuras que estavam no segundo escalão podem subir para o primeiro escalão.

 Já as figuras que estavam ali na liderança dentro do rol da família Bolsonaro podem dar lugar às novas figuras. E o mais preocupante é que esse cenário continua a ser normalizado, naturalizado por parcelas significativas das elites brasileiras e parcelas significativas da imprensa hegemônica brasileira, ou seja, o problema não está solucionado.




Além do Brasil, nas midterms nos Estados Unidos, Netanyahu aparentemente enfraquecido em Israel e outros exemplos pelo mundo, parece que temos um momento novo de enfraquecimento da extrema direita. Mas olhando, por exemplo, o Congresso Brasileiro tomado pelo PL ou os democratas nos Estados Unidos, que tiveram uma grande vitória mas ainda vão ter que lidar com o Trump na presidência, Israel ainda tenta formar coalizões, Alemanha enfrentando várias questões para manter o cordão sanitário com relação à AFD nas últimas eleições. Como podemos analisar esse momento mundialmente? Entramos, de fato, em um novo momento de perdas para a direita? E, se sim, o que causou esse desgaste?




É um pouco apressado, ao meu ver, afirmar que o momento, realmente, é o fim e o esgotamento de um ciclo político. A gente pensa na realidade brasileira, mas sem dúvida alguma, colocando isso em uma perspectiva global, ainda vivemos um ciclo ou de hegemonia ou de dominação de parcelas significativas das direitas e, particularmente, da extrema direita no cenário político global.

 Não é uma tentativa de desmerecer o que foi a eleição de Lula, o resultado nos Estados Unidos ou mesmo a possibilidade daquilo que pode acontecer nas próximas semanas no Paraguai, por exemplo.




Sem dúvida alguma, existe uma certa crise do modelo da extrema direita, existe uma certa limitação do processo político, mas acredito ser ainda muito apressado dizer que esse ciclo se esgotou, por diversas razões, seja por questões das lideranças que ainda existem, seja pela maneira como determinadas conquistas foram colocadas em prática por esse campo, seja para a dimensão da política atribuída ou mesmo colocada em prática pelas principais big techs, como elas assumiram contorno político.




Também é importante considerar que os frutos dessas conquistas se transformam em uma nova geração que foi moldada a partir dessas questões. Então, não podemos olhar a política apenas do processo eleitoral em si, fenômenos político-eleitorais são baseados a partir de grandes processos históricos, nos quais os indivíduos são uma força de fundamental importância, inclusive do ponto de vista da produção e reprodução desses valores intrínsecos às determinadas correntes político-ideológicas.




Em contrapartida, não podemos desmerecer de maneira alguma o que foi uma certa revolução democrática – como alguns autores colocaram a partir da eleição de Lula –, por exemplo, com o “janonismo” que foi colocado e tem tido até uma tentativa de adaptação e  reprodução a partir da realidade de outros países, e de um fator ainda de maior importância que foi a volta das esquerdas às ruas.




Não somente no campo brasileiro, a volta das esquerdas às ruas demonstra também que é possível, a despeito desses congressos e senado, na particularidade brasileira é possível pensar saídas à esquerda a partir da mobilização não contínua, mas em momentos adversos ou estratégicos do campo progressista. E parece que o presidente Lula leu perfeitamente isso, inclusive disse em pronunciamento que é necessário contar com aqueles que participaram desse grande evento para os próximos quatro anos. 

Não serão quatro anos fáceis, longe disso, mas a saída à esquerda, inclusive, do ponto de vista da campanha de Lula, necessitava radicalizar sua proposta e seguir em diante.




Ou seja, quando passamos por grandes eventos, evidentemente, os grandes eventos ficam mais ou menos cristalizados e se tornam um pouco patrimônios da nossa memória coletiva na atualidade, mas o processo que culminou nas mobilizações para a eleição de Lula não é o ponto final, na verdade, são pontos de partida.

title: Fransa-Türkiye maçı ne zaman, saat kaçta, hangi kanalda?
content:
A Milli Futbol Takımı, UEFA Uluslar A Ligi 1. Grup'taki altıncı ve son maçında Fransa'ya konuk olacak. Bordeaux kentindeki Matmut Atlantique Stadı'nda oynanacak karşılaşma saat 22.45'te başlayacak. Mücadeleyi İngiltere Futbol Federasyonundan hakem Chris Kavanagh yönetecek.

A Ligi'nde oynadığı ilk 5 maçta puan alamayan Türkiye, grupta son sırada bulunuyor. Türkiye İtalya'ya Bursa'da 4-1, deplasmanda Belçika'ya 3-0, Bologna'da İtalya'ya 3-1 ve İzmir'de Belçika'ya 2-1 mağlup oldu.

İki takım grubun ilk maçında Kocaeli Stadı'nda karşı karşıya gelmiş, Fransa mücadeleyi Kylian Mbappe'nin golüyle 1-0 kazanmıştı. Türkiye ile Fransa bugüne kadar 7 kez karşılaştı. Bu maçların 5'ini Fransa kazanırken Türkiye 1 galibiyet elde etti, 1 karşılaşma ise beraberlikle sonuçlandı. Söz konusu maçlarda Fransa 14, Türkiye 5 gol kaydetti.

Türkiye, gruptaki 5 maçını da kaybetmesine rağmen A Ligi'nde kalma ihtimalini koruyor. A Ligi'ndeki dört grubun son sırasında yer alan takımlardan puan ve averaj bakımından en kötü durumda olan ikisi doğrudan B Ligi'ne düşecek. Diğer iki takım ise B Ligi'nden gelecek takımlarla play-off oynayacak.

Kart cezası sona eren Abdülkerim Bardakcı, Fransa karşısında forma giyebilecek. Belçika maçında gördüğü kart nedeniyle cezalı duruma düşen Ozan Kabak ise karşılaşmada görev alamayacak.

Fransa: Maignan, Gusto, Konate, Jacquet, Truffert, Rabiot, Da Cunha, Cherki, Doue, Olise, Barcola.

Türkiye: Uğurcan, Zeki, Merih, Abdülkerim, Ferdi, Salih, Orkun, Arda, Yunus, Barış Alper, Enes.

title: Rusya'dan açıklama: 'Ukrayna'nın enerji, liman ve demir yolu altyapı tesislerini vurduk'
content:
Görseller: Pixabay | Kolaj: Evrensel

Rusya Savunma Bakanlığı, Ukrayna'daki eylemlerine ilişkin açıklama yaparak ülkedeki kritik altyapı tesislerinin hedef aldıklarını duyurdu.

Bakanlıktan yapılan açıklamada, Rus ordusunun gece saatlerinde askeri amaçla kullanılan enerji, liman ve demir yolu altyapı tesislerine saldırı düzenlediği belirtilerek şu ifadelere yer verildi:

"Rivne bölgesinde Ukrayna ordusu için kullanılan lojistik tesislerinin çalışmalarını sağlayan trafo merkezi, Odessa bölgesindeki Çornomorsk Limanı'nda feribot terminali ve trafo merkezi ile Dnipropetrovsk kentindeki bir tren istasyonu yakınlarında iki lokomotif vuruldu."

Saldırıların insansız hava araçları (İHA) kullanılarak gerçekleştirildiği aktarılan açıklamada, Karadeniz'de askeri yükler taşıyan bir geminin de hedef alındığı kaydedildi. Öte yandan açıklamada, gece boyunca Ukrayna'ya ait 533 İHA'nın çeşitli bölgeler üzerinde hava savunma sistemleri tarafından düşürüldüğü de belirtildi.

title: AKP ilçe başkanıyla görüşmeyen ilçe sağlık müdürüne "istifa" baskısı iddiası
content:
Rize – Pazar İlçe Sağlık Müdürlüğü görevinden alınan İ.Ö'nün, AKP Pazar İlçe Başkanı Furkan Namlı’nın ziyaret talebini kabul etmediği gerekçesiyle geçen günlerde istifaya zorlandığı iddia edildi. Yeni Parti Rize İl Başkanı Saltuk Deniz, İ.Ö'nün görevine iadesini isteyerek, AKP yetkililerine “Kurum amirleri sizin hizmetkârınız değildir” dedi.

Edinilen bilgilere göre, 4 Ağustos 2026 tarihinde AKP Pazar İlçe Başkanı olan Furkan Namlı ve beraberindeki yönetim kurulu üyeleri, kurum ziyaretleri kapsamında Pazar İlçe Sağlık Müdürlüğü’nden telefonla randevu talep etti. İlçe Sağlık Müdürü Dr. İ.Ö’nün ilk talebin ardından müsait olmadığını belirttiği, ikinci telefon görüşmesinde ise 657 sayılı Devlet Memurları Kanunu’na tabi bir kamu görevlisi olduğunu ifade ederek siyasi parti ilçe başkanlarıyla makamında görüşmeyeceğini bildirdiği ileri sürüldü.

Rize'deki AKP yetkililerince bunun İl Sağlık Müdürü Prof. Dr. Gökhan Demiral’a ileterek Dr. İ.Ö’nün görevden alınmasını ya da istifa etmesinin istendiği, bunun ardından Dr. İ.Ö’ye istifa etmesi yönünde telkinde bulunulduğu ancak ilçe sağlık müdürünün bunu kabul etmediği savunuldu.

Dr. İ.Ö. bir süre sonra ise İlçe Sağlık Müdürlüğü'nden alındı.

Pazar İlçe Sağlık Müdürlüğü çalışanları da Dr. İ.Ö’ye istifa etmesi yönünde baskı yapıldığını ifade etti.

Yeni Parti Rize İl Başkanı Saltuk Deniz, Dr. İ.Ö’nün Pazar İlçe Sağlık Müdürlüğü'nden alınmasına tepki gösterdi. Kamu kurumlarında görev yapan yöneticilerin siyasi parti temsilcilerinin hizmetinde olmadığını vurgulayan Deniz, şu açıklamayı yaptı:

“Devlet kurumlarında çalışan görevlilerimiz siyasi parti temsilcilerinin hizmetkârı değillerdir. Kurum amirleri, hiçbir siyasi parti temsilcisi ile görevleri dışında görüşmek zorunda değildir. Daha önce de benzeri olaylar ilimizde yaşanmıştı. Rize İl Milli Eğitim Müdürü Halil İbrahim Akmeşe de İl Milli Eğitim Müdürlüğü görevine atanır atanmaz, daha koltuğuna oturmadan soluğu AKP İl Başkanlığı’nda aldı. Bunlar doğru şeyler değildir. Kurum amirleri sizlerin hizmetkârı değildir. Rahat bırakın çalışanları. Kurumlarda iş barışını bozmanın, amirleri ve memurları siyasal gücünüzü kullanarak görevlerinden almak ya da uzaklaştırmakla diğer kurum çalışanlarına gözdağı vermenin siyasi ahlakla da bağdaşmadığını düşünüyoruz. AKP sözcülerini ve İl Sağlık Müdürlüğü’nü bu konuyla ilgili açıklama yapmalarını, görevinden alınan doktorumuzun yeniden görevine iade edilmesini kamuoyu adına talep ediyoruz.”

author: Liza Stephens
title: Students strike against Hanson
content:
For the third time this year, thousands of high school students across the country walked out of class on 12 November to reject One Nation’s far-right agenda. Buoyed by the youth revolt igniting Europe, the protesters drew direct links between their fight and the one against our own monsters here in Australia. 

Students faced a deluge of condescending articles in the media decrying the long-term developmental dangers of missing an afternoon of classes. Minister for Social Services Tanya Plibersek suggested it was just an excuse for students to wag school, "We'll see how many kids turn up if it's a Saturday”. One Nation leader Pauline Hanson said, “These kids really need to get back to class”.

Students proudly clapped back though creative handmade signs which read: “We are skipping class to teach you a lesson” and “The only minority destroying Australia is the rich”. In Sydney, protesters were cheered on by workers at a construction site as they made their way through the CBD.

“Migrants are welcome, Hanson is not” was a popular chant, an expression of solidarity between the protesters and their migrant classmates who are facing the brunt of One Nation’s extreme racism. Minh, a Vietnamese university student speaking at the Adelaide rally, pointed out Labor’s complicity in the increasingly right-wing climate:

“Labor’s tripling of student visa fees and the barring of international student family members is an attack on the rights of migrants. These cowards are happy to appease Hanson while punching down on the rest of us.”

References to the courageous student movements overseas were met with huge cheers. Australian young people connect with the problems driving students in Europe to protest, including having their futures sold off to the highest bidder, the racist politicians who legitimise genocide and then speak down to young people who call them out, and the schools left under-funded while governments hand tax cuts to the rich and billions to the military.

Luca, a high school speaker in Brisbane, spoke to the sentiment underpinning the protests: 

“I refuse to sit and accept the terror inflicted all across the planet by the minority ruling class. We must rise up and join France, Spain, Germany, Serbia and many more in their fight. We all have the same goal, and we can only win if we move together.”

author: @ndy
title: The struggle is real with Jillian Segal.
content:
See also : Jillian Segal and husband funding far-right group “Advance”, Anthony Klan, The Klaxon, July 12, 2025.

Jillian Segal — the South African–born Australian lawyer, business executive, and Australia’s Special Envoy to Combat Antisemitism — recently dropped another Report, ASECA Priorities. According to the Special Envoy, a newly-hatched “modern progressive antisemitism” … is taking “the hostility of Islamic extremism and far-left antisemitism, together with traditional antisemitic tropes”.

My first reaction on reading this passage was to recall the unforgettable 2014 framing by the Australian Defence League of the alleged “evil anarcho-pinko-anarchist-islamic cabal of dirt”; the wicked coalition then allegedly intent on turning Penrith into a no-go zone for patriots.

In any case, inre the Report, Jeffrey Loewenstein doesn’t hold back in It’s time to sack Jillian Segal (Deepcut News, November 2, 2026), the Jewish Council of Australia (October 30, 2026) has slammed it, and Jeff Sparrow has characterised it, not unfairly, as a Trumpian plan to curtail free speech (Crikey, November 2, 2026). The Report is also subject to critical scrutiny by Robert Manne, who examines it in On the Rise of Antisemitism in Australia (November 8, 2026), along with the thoughts of Lord Andrew Roberts and Sir Simon Schama on the subject of ‘antisemitism’. Manne concludes that:

Schama believes he can help combat the rise of antisemitism in the Diaspora by defending the indefensible, the war crimes of the IDF under Benjamin Netanyahu. I believe a more likely remedy would be for leading Diaspora thinkers, like Schama, and influential publishers, like Morry Schwartz, and the leaders in Australia of the principal Israel and Jewish lobbies, like Jillian Segal, to speak the truth about what, under Netanyahu and the two Kahanist-fascist members of his Government, Israel has become, and the moral revolution that has to happen in Israel if Jews in the Diaspora are to be spared from the dreadful rise of antisemitism that is spreading around the Western world.

FWIW, for over 20 years I’ve been attempting, inter alia, to monitor and document organised, public expressions of antisemitism and other racisms in Australia — the better to disrupt it. I’m also an anarchist, and one of many people to hold the view that the Israeli state has engaged in a genocidal assault upon Palestine in the three years since October 7 (the latest chapter in a much longer history of deadly state violence). On that basis, I assume that Segal et. al. would categorise myself as an exponent of ‘far-left antisemitism’, the meaning of which is elaborated upon in this passage:

Far-left antisemitism or issue-motivated antisemitism

Far-left ideology and associated activism feature a worldview that casts the world in terms of ‘oppressors’ and ‘oppressed’. Within this binary framework, Israel is portrayed as a colonial project that is inherently racist and Jews who support Israel’s existence are portrayed as representatives of ‘whiteness’ (regardless of their ethnicity), privilege (regardless of their means), imperialism (notwithstanding the absence of an empire), greedy capitalism and the projection of Western power.

This framing allows longstanding antisemitic motifs to be repackaged in the academic language of anti-racism, decolonisation, human rights, social justice and intersectionality, often in service of a traditional Marxist revolutionary agenda.

When a cause is believed – with ideological fervour – to be absolutely just, its ends can come to justify any means and its adherents can feel free to vilify, harass and seek to destroy those who associate with what is framed as evil.

Over time, the language of human rights and its greatest crimes – apartheid, ethnic cleansing, genocide, etc. – has increasingly been appropriated to portray Israel (and, relevantly, members of the Jewish community who support it) as morally evil, often to the point of being equated to Nazis.

In contemporary Australia, elements of Australia’s historically fringe radical left have sought to appeal to well-meaning mainstream progressive Australians who may perceive the Palestinian cause as a matter of social justice. This ‘gateway’ issue, of sorts, has been used by far-left activists to magnify their appeal and prominence and to attempt to introduce traditionally moderate Australians to radical and anti-Jewish propaganda that would previously have been of little interest.

The strange – but not unprecedented – alignment of Islamic extremist antisemitism in the modern day combined with far-left extremism finds a common ground in 3 things:

• an extreme hatred of Israel, including a desire to eliminate it

• the representation of Israel as a kind of uniquely evil, demonic, cruel force in the world

• a conspiratorial view of Israel and Zionism and of Jews as controlling Western governments, undermining Islam and causing world war.

Despite their many obvious ideological differences, the 2 groups coalesce around a shared desire to undermine or overturn the existing social structures and institutions of Western societies, including moderate political consensus and social cohesion.

Where to begin with this ideological porridge? If I was to address all its specious claims and historical revisionism in detail, I’d be writing many thousands more words, drawn from millions more, written by some very smart people, over a very long period of time. Instead, I’ll just note the following:

I started writing this on the 88th anniversary of Reichskristallnacht, the orgy of antisemitic violence that characterised November 9–10, 1938 in Nazi Germany. The events signalled a further dark turn in Nazi antisemitism, and was ‘the culmination of a third wave of antisemitic violence — worse than those of 1933 and 1935 — that had begun in the spring of 1938 and run on as the domestic accompaniment to the foreign-political crisis throughout the summer and autumn’ (Kershaw, p.131). In this context, I can remember being struck by the image that accompanied the double-page spread in the September 1993 edition of Love & Rage (by the North American Love & Rage Revolutionary Anarchist Federation: 1989–1998), which loudly declares:

Contemporary US antifa dates back to the late 1980s when anarchists and punks in Anti-Racist Action (ARA) developed a revitalized strategy of militant anti-fascism to combat the growing power of the far right. This history has received new attention since Trump’s election, and Anti-Racist Action was even featured in a 2021 PBS Frontline documentary. But despite this renewed attention, the foundational role played by revolutionary anarchism in the development of Anti-Racist Action has thus far gone under-examined in mainstream accounts, which has obscured the historical lessons it offers.

Love and Rage regularly published writings on anti-fascism and anti-racism. And, oddly enough, the same edition promoting remembering Pogromnacht also contains the first installment of Ron Taber’s anarchist critique of Marxism. (FWIW, Taber also wrote A Look A Leninism, originally published by the Revolutionary Socialist League (1973–1989) in 1988; the RSL dissolved into L&R at its foundation. See also : The Utopian, which Taber and others published following L&R’s dissolution.) The point being, I guess: historical and contemporary anarchists have always fought, and continue to fight, fascism; critiques of capitalism and the state, colonialism and nationalism and so on are hardly confined to The Academy, or to Marxism.

In any case, while the analysis of ‘far-left antisemitism’ barely rises above the level of an average undergraduate essay, I’m nonetheless tickled that Segal’s Report suggests that the authors are familiar with Jordan Peterson’s Weltanschauung: ‘far-left ideology and associated activism feature a worldview that casts the world in terms of ‘oppressors’ and ‘oppressed”, after all. Otherwise, there are two (2) references cited in the passage on far-left antisemitism: 1) L Klaff, ‘A new form of the oldest hatred: mapping antisemitism today’ (in A Johnson (ed), Mapping the New Left Antisemitism: The Fathom Essays, Routledge, London and New York, 2024, pp.13–27 [PDF]), and 2) Dr Dave Rich MBE, Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion, transcript, Hearing Block 1, Day 8, 14 May 2026, p.723. Both are available online, and while the new (new) antisemitism is actually a few decades-old, at the Royal Commission Dr Rich was subject to cross-examination by Peggy Dwyer on behalf of the JCA, and is the author of The Left’s Jewish Problem: Jeremy Corbyn, Israel and Anti‑Semitism (Biteback, 2016). Corbyn and antisemitism is a whole other kettle of fish but, for the defence, Nathan Robinson argued in Current Affairs in 2020 that ‘Corbyn’s suspension from the Labour Party is the culmination of an absurd series of attacks. It’s a lesson in how ruthlessly the left’s opponents will try to destroy it’, while Jake Romm argues that Zionism itself is ‘an antisemitism’ (Elements of Anti-Semitism: The limits of Zionism, Parapraxis, November 2024).

• I view Zionism as one particular expression of generic nationalism — a hegemonic discourse and political and structure which, as an anarchist, I reject.

• Zionism was initially conceptualised by its proponents in the nineteenth century as a form of colonialism which, contra other strands of Jewish thought (especially but not only Bundism), conceived of the Jews as a racial-national category which, like other nations, can and should construct its own state.

• It is both possible and desirable to reject the state form — as German Jewish anarchist Gustav Landauer (1870–1919) argued, “The State is a condition, a certain relationship between human beings, a mode of behaviour; we destroy it by contracting other relationships, by behaving differently toward one another … We are the State and we shall continue to be the State until we have created the institutions that form a real community”.

• On the subject of Jews and whiteness, see, for example, Off-White: The Truth About Antisemitism (One World, 2024) by Rachel Shabi (reviewed here by Natasha Walter), who was also interviewed by Max Kaiser last year during her book tour.

• The idea that Australia — fulla ‘traditionally moderate Australians’, apparently — has always been a welcoming territory for Jewish peoples, but that recent events have disrupted this openness, brings to mind the Evian conference of July 1938, at which delegates from 32 countries, including Australia, confirmed their unwillingness to increase immigration quotas for Jews. In which context, the JCA writes: ‘Rhetoric directed against Palestinian refugees is reminiscent of the same rhetoric used to vilify Jewish refugees in the 1940s and 1950s who were frequently labeled ‘security risks’. T.H. White, Australia’s delegate to the 1938 Evian Conference famously said with reference to German and Austrian Jewish refugees, Australia has “no real racial problem [and is] not desirous of importing one”. This rhetoric is also part of a long history of racism and exclusion in Australia, from the White Australia Policy to the War on Terror’s exclusion of people from the Middle East.’

• Opposition to the genocidal assault upon Palestine neither requires nor is it assisted by a false notion, attributed by the Report to the ‘far left’, that ‘Israel [is] a kind of uniquely evil, demonic, cruel force in the world’. On the contrary, even a brief glimpse at modern history reveals that one of the main functions of the state is as an engine of war and colonialism.

• Along with being an expression of the simple-minded liberal fatuities that saturate the text, to seek to ‘undermine or overturn the existing social structures and institutions of Western societies, including moderate political consensus and social cohesion’ may be a very wrogn-headed proposition for the Report’s authors, but: 1) as Some Guy said, ‘Truth does not become more true by virtue of the fact that the entire world agrees with it, nor less so even if the whole world disagrees with it’; 2) I make a modest, alternative, proposal: dismantle the rule of state, capital and patriarchy, and reconstruct a free society in harmony with non-human nature: a good thing for ecological sustainability and a critical contribution to establishing a genuine, egalitarian form of ‘social cohesion’.

author: Administrador
title: Preparativos Zapatistas para el Encuentro Abrazo con familias Buscadoras. Parte 6: REGALOS
content:
Música: «Es que yo te quiero a ti», Kevin Kaarl Imágenes, edición y producción: Terci@s Compas Zapatistas

Creo fue en el mes de julio, cuando el Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés anunció la salida e inicio de la primera etapa de la “Gira por la Vida- Capítulo México”. Entonces creo que dijo, palabras más, palabras menos, que las madres buscadoras eran como nuestras mamaces. Ahí fue cuando empezó, como quien dice, la problema.

Porque todas y todos de la tropa pensamos: “Ah caray, son nuestras mamaces y las vamos a ir a ver. Ni modos que llegamos y sólo decimos “Ya vine jefa, ¿qué hay de comer?”. No, si se llega así pos sólo un chanclazo, un zape o un pellizco malo (porque los hay buenos), vamos a conseguir. Porque el novio, la novia o loa novioa, vaya y pase, repones y ya. Pero si se enojan las mamaces, ay diositillo, ni dónde esconderse.

“Llevemos regalo”, dijo uno. “Sí”, dijo una insurgenta, “así como a la madre tierra se le regala el trabajo honrado”. El capitán dijo: “sí, es un regalo preventivo. O sea antes del regaño, ya tienes el regalo y cuando empieza la tormenta, sacas el regalo y sonríes y pones cara de “mamá, soy marquitos, no haré travesuras”.

“Ni quien te crea”, interviene el SubMoy y agrega, “además, todas las redes dicen que no tienes madre”.

Siguió la discusión y se llegó al consenso de que un regalo. Pero luego se hizo la bulla de que cuál regalo. Que si flores. “No compita, en lo que subes al autobús ya valieron”. “Una puema”, dice otra insurgenta. El SubMoy: “los pueblos ya van a mandar cartas, poesías, canciones. Aunque no sé si a las madres buscadoras les guste el hip hop y el rap y esas cosas”.

Siguió la discusión. Tardamos. Y entonces se puso peor, porque un insurgente dijo “regalémosles un recuerdo”.

Empezó la bulla. Todas y todos hablando al mismo tiempo: que cuál recuerdo, que dónde lo va a poner, que no es buena idea, que sí es, porque la memoria es lo que importa porque por eso son buscadoras. Viera que no tienen memoria, pues se rinden, se desmayan.

Entonces las mujeres, con esa mala costumbre que tienen las mujeres de acabar las discusiones cuando apenas se está poniendo buena la cosa, dijeron: bordados y muñecas. “Que lo sepan y lo recuerden que tienen familias acá”.

Los insurgentes, encabezados por el capitán, dijeron que no, que eso de muñecas y bordados es para niñas, que ya tienen juicio las madres buscadoras, que no están para andar jugando y con bordados otra vez, que de una vez no se puede creer. Las insurgentas se embravecieron, que eso no sirve pensar así, que porque son recuerdos, no juguetes ni adornos.

Y que sigue la discusión, pero ya revuelto todo, porque el insurgente que le tocaba la intendencia quemó los frijoles, y todo por andar en el chisme del regalo. Y, por un momento, hay una unión del común de mujeres y hombres, porque una cosa es, como quien dice, la chinga, y otra es el frijol quemado. Pero todos se consolaron comiendo tostadas y arroz estilo vietnamita. Pero era apenas una tregua, inestable como el temperamento del Trump. Así que, después de lavar los platos y darles de comer a los chuchos y a los gatitos, siguieron.

En eso apareció el SubMoy: “¿Qué tanto alegan?” Todos empezaron como quien dice a exponer el problema. “Ya párenle”, gritó el SubMoy. Todo quedó en silencio. Los varones esperando que el Sub hiciera honor a la solidaridad de género. Las mujeres esperando que tuviera bueno el juicio.

El SubMoy encendió un cigarrillo, quedó pensando. Después de un rato dijo: “hagan la lista de lo que hay que conseguir”.

Las insurgentas aplaudieron. Los insurgentes hicieron caras, pero no dijeron nada porque el arresto era comerse el frijol quemado.

Entonces, en todas las posiciones insurgentes, empezaron a darle a confeccionar regalos. A las carreras, porque ya estaba cerca la salida.

Y empezaron tarde por su culpa del capitán, que empezó con la bulla de que muñecas y bordados no, que eso es de niñas. Y además hizo una trinchera con las mesas y las sillas, y ahí estaban todos los insurgentes parapetados. Porque resulta que las insurgentas los atacaban con bolitas de lodo que, dicen, les enseñaron a hacer las del Comando Palomitas. Entonces tardaron reacomodando y limpiando.

Así que, si no se acompletan los regalos, va en su cuenta del capitán.

A mí ni me culpen. Yo sólo soy un escarabajo y caballero andante, el muy grande y memorioso “Don Durito de la Lacandona. A.C. de C.V. de I.I”. Y yo no tuve nada que ver. Pero yo lo miré todo. Y no les vengo a chismear, no, les estoy compartiendo una información.

Así que, cuando lo vean al capitán, regáñenlo, así como las mamaces regañan a sus crías cuando se portan mal. Pero el capitán es cabeza dura, así que no sobran los chanclazos y los coscorrones.

Es toda mi información. Si hay más chism…, quiero decir más informaciones para compartir, les aviso.

Desde las montañas del Sureste Mexicano.

El muy grande Don Durito de la Lacandona. México, noviembre del 2026.

P.D.- No le crean, yo ni estaba. Doy fe: El capitán (con casco bicicletero anti- chancla y negociando con el Comando Palomitas un embargo de municiones a las insurgentas) ¡Volveremos!

¡Jajajajajaja! 😂❤️ ¡Don Durito, qué maravilla de informe! Ya me imagino al capitán parapetado detrás de las mesas, negociando con el Comando Palomitas y tratando de salvarse de los chanclazos de las insurgentas. ¡Pobre capitán, tanto trabajo para conseguir un regalo y todavía con riesgo de terminar lleno de bolitas de lodo! 😂 Pero entre tanta travesura hay algo que nos llega muy hondo al corazón. A las familias buscadoras nos han faltado muchas cosas, pero nunca nos ha sobrado el cariño, la solidaridad ni la esperanza. Por eso, cualquier detalle que venga de ustedes, ya sea una muñequita, un bordado, una carta, una canción o un recuerdo, será recibido con inmenso cariño. Porque no se trata del tamaño del regalo, sino de todo lo que lleva dentro: las manos que lo hicieron, el tiempo que le dedicaron y el corazón que lo pensó, y con todo y frijoles quemados y bolitas de lodo compartidos, aunados a esos recuerdos es que recibiremos aún con más cariño cualquiera de sus atesorados detalles. Y si algo queremos decirles desde este lado es que también nosotros les mandamos un abrazo enorme, de esos que no necesitan conocerse de toda la vida para sentirse sinceros. Quizá las circunstancias no siempre nos permitan encontrarnos físicamente, pero las causas, la dignidad, la memoria y el amor por la vida también encuentran caminos para acercarnos. Gracias por hacernos sonreír en medio de tantos días difíciles. No saben cuánto vale una sonrisa cuando el corazón lleva tanto dolor. Por favor, herman@s de lucha, y de historias memorables, reciban de todo corazón un abrazo fraterno, cariñoso y solidario para el capitán, las insurgentas, los insurgentes, el Comando Palomitas, Don Durito y todas las comunidades zapatistas. Y al capitán le decimos: ¡no se preocupe por los regalos, que aquí no somos exigentes! Aunque, eso sí, si vienen con muñequitas y bordados, ¡ya tienen ganado un lugar muy especial en nuestro corazón! Con cariño, respeto y esperanza, Laura Palafox Colectivo Esperanza de Vida CDMX Familias buscadoras. ❤️ Por la verdad, la justicia y el regreso de nuestros corazones. author: anred
title: MetroGAS: una distribuidora, un negocio y responsabilidades que no se tercerizan
content:
La responsabilidad de la muerte de un obrero y una treiuntena de heridos con gravedad en la explosión tras la fuga de gas en Remedios de Escalada no puede reducirse a la empresa Exgadet que operaba la tuneladora. MetroGAS es la distribuidora que tiene a su cargo la red y el servicio en buena parte del Área Metropolitana de Buenos Aires. La contratación de una firma externa no la exime de garantizar que las obras se realicen bajo condiciones adecuadas ni de supervisar los procedimientos de seguridad. Los trabajadores venían advirtiendo de las malas condiciones de trabajo. ¿Como operó el lobby Vila Manzano en la justicia? . Por ANRed




La propia empresa cuenta con un Programa de Prevención de Daños que establece responsabilidades compartidas entre quienes ejecutan excavaciones y la distribuidora. MetroGAS debe garantizar la integridad de la red y brindar asistencia técnica durante las obras. Por eso, la investigación debe establecer qué controles realizó sobre Exgadet, qué instrucciones había impartido y cómo respondió cuando recibió el aviso de la rotura.




La actuación de la distribuidora quedó especialmente comprometida por lo sucedido después de las 9.44. Según la reconstrucción municipal, recibió el aviso de la fuga, envió una cuadrilla y no activó el sistema local de emergencias. La decisión de mantener el episodio bajo control de la propia empresa, sin alertar a los organismos municipales, dejó expuesta a toda la población de la zona.




Mientras tanto, el Gobierno nacional avanza con un esquema de desregulación y reorganización del mercado energético que favorece la concentración empresarial y la rentabilidad privada. En agosto de 2026, YPF acordó vender el 70% de MetroGAS a Edenor por 780 millones de dólares. La operación fue impulsada por el grupo empresario integrado por José Luis Manzano, Daniel Vila y Mauricio Filiberti, y quedó sujeta a las autorizaciones correspondientes.




La operación se inscribe en un proceso más amplio de concentración de empresas de servicios públicos. Edenor, que ya controla la distribución eléctrica en una extensa zona del AMBA, busca incorporar a su estructura una de las principales distribuidoras de gas del país. Al mismo tiempo, el nuevo marco regulatorio energético contempla revisiones tarifarias y una eventual extensión de la concesión de MetroGAS hasta 2047.




En este escenario, la pregunta por los controles adquiere una dimensión política. ¿Qué lugar ocupa la seguridad de los usuarios y trabajadores en un modelo donde los servicios esenciales se organizan alrededor de grandes negocios privados? ¿Quién garantiza que la búsqueda de eficiencia y rentabilidad no termine descargando los costos sobre quienes trabajan y viven en los territorios?




La desregulación no significa solamente modificar normas o reducir la intervención estatal. También implica discutir qué controles se mantienen, quién los ejecuta y qué capacidad tienen los organismos públicos para fiscalizar a empresas que manejan infraestructuras fundamentales para la vida cotidiana.







Dos directivos de MetroGAS y una investigación que debe avanzar




La gravedad de lo ocurrido llevó a la fiscal Yanina Estévez, de la UFI N.º 6 de Lanús, a disponer inicialmente la detención de dos responsables jerárquicos de MetroGAS que se encontraban en el lugar. La medida fue informada por el director de Defensa Civil municipal y estuvo vinculada al presunto incumplimiento de los protocolos de emergencia.




Posteriormente, fuentes judiciales informaron que los dos directivos habían sido trasladados para su identificación y puestos preventivamente a resguardo, y aclararon que no estaban formalmente detenidos ni aprehendidos. La diferencia entre ambas versiones deberá quedar esclarecida en el expediente.




La investigación debe determinar qué hicieron los responsables de la distribuidora durante la hora que transcurrió entre la detección de la fuga y la explosión. También deberá establecer quién decidió que la situación estaba controlada, por qué no se dio intervención inmediata a los servicios municipales y qué responsabilidad tuvieron los directivos en la cadena de decisiones.




No se trata solamente de establecer quién rompió el caño. La responsabilidad empresarial incluye la prevención, la supervisión de las contratistas y la respuesta ante una emergencia. Son obligaciones que no desaparecen cuando una empresa decide tercerizar sus trabajos.




El lobby de Vila-Manzano para liberar a los directivos




La trama empresarial también tuvo un capítulo judicial. Según fuentes de la Intendencia de Lanús que hablaron bajo reserva, el grupo empresario de Daniel Vila y José Luis Manzano habría intercedido ante la Justicia para conseguir la liberación de los dos responsables jerárquicos de MetroGAS.




La presunta intervención resulta especialmente significativa porque ambos empresarios están vinculados al grupo que acordó la compra de la participación mayoritaria de la distribuidora. De confirmarse, se trataría de una gestión del poder económico en una causa que investiga responsabilidades por una tragedia que dejó una persona fallecida y decenas de heridos.




La versión de las fuentes municipales plantea un interrogante sobre la relación entre los grandes grupos empresarios y el sistema judicial: ¿hasta dónde llega la influencia de quienes controlan empresas de servicios esenciales cuando sus propios intereses quedan involucrados en una investigación?




 




Los trabajadores y vecinos pagan las consecuencias




En Remedios de Escalada, los primeros en sufrir las consecuencias fueron los trabajadores que estaban junto a la cañería y los vecinos que viven y trabajan en la zona. Cinco de los seis operarios que permanecían internados en estado grave pertenecían a Exgadet. Comercios destruidos, viviendas afectadas y familias evacuadas completan el saldo de una explosión que pudo tener consecuencias todavía mayores.




La tragedia expone una cadena que comienza con la tercerización de una tarea de riesgo, continúa con la falta de prevención y supervisión y termina con una respuesta empresarial que, según las autoridades municipales, no respetó los protocolos de emergencia.




No alcanza con responsabilizar a los operarios que estaban trabajando ni con presentar lo ocurrido como una falla técnica. Hay que investigar a la contratista, a la distribuidora, a sus responsables jerárquicos y a los organismos encargados de fiscalizar el servicio.




Cuando las empresas privadas administran servicios esenciales, la seguridad de trabajadores y usuarios no puede quedar subordinada a los costos, los contratos y las ganancias. La red de gas no es una variable de ajuste y la vida de quienes habitan los barrios no puede depender de que una empresa decida cuándo considera necesario activar una emergencia.




Los trabajadores del gas denuncian: «El gas no perdona»




La explosión de Remedios de Escalada también provocó un fuerte pronunciamiento de la Asociación de Personal Jerárquico de la Industria del Gas Natural, Derivados y Afines (APJ Gas), que el 14 de noviembre difundió un comunicado en el que responsabilizó a la política sistemática de tercerización de las distribuidoras por el deterioro de las condiciones de seguridad en el servicio.




«Lo que ocurrió no fue un hecho inesperado del destino. Es la consecuencia de una sistemática estrategia de tercerización de las concesionarias de distribución de gas natural en el AMBA desde la privatización», sostuvo la organización sindical. En su declaración, señaló que este esquema profundiza la precarización laboral, fragmenta los controles sobre el cumplimiento de las tareas, impide establecer criterios comunes para aplicar las normas de seguridad y subestima la importancia de la capacitación continua y la transmisión de la experiencia acumulada por los trabajadores.




La APJ Gas también apuntó directamente contra Exgadet, la contratista de MetroGAS involucrada en los trabajos que precedieron a la explosión, y denunció que había advertido en reiteradas oportunidades sobre las irregularidades y los métodos de trabajo de empresas tercerizadas como esta. «No fuimos escuchados por las empresas concesionarias del servicio ni por el Estado», afirmó.




El comunicado pone en discusión un aspecto central que excede las circunstancias particulares del siniestro: la fragmentación de las tareas y de las responsabilidades dentro de una industria en la que la seguridad requiere experiencia, capacitación permanente y criterios unificados. La tercerización no solamente modifica las condiciones de contratación de los trabajadores; también puede debilitar los mecanismos de control y transmisión de conocimientos necesarios para prevenir accidentes.




La organización gremial advirtió que las consecuencias de este modelo recaen sobre los trabajadores del gas y los usuarios. «Nuestras tareas llevan incluidas un riesgo permanente que debe ser minimizado», expresó, y cuestionó que se utilice la tercerización para sostener la precarización de miles de trabajadores, en detrimento de una política integral de seguridad.




La declaración termina con una advertencia contundente: «El gas no perdona. No es un instante. Es un encadenamiento de decisiones que toman las autoridades de las empresas privadas y repercute en el servicio».




El pronunciamiento de APJ Gas resulta especialmente significativo porque proviene de trabajadores jerárquicos de la propia industria, que conocen los procedimientos, las condiciones de operación y los riesgos de la actividad. Su denuncia introduce una dimensión estructural en la investigación: la explosión no puede analizarse solamente como una falla durante una obra, sino también en el marco de décadas de privatización, tercerización y fragmentación de los controles.




«Metrogas y las distribuidoras de gas natural lo saben. El camino es otro. Hay que recorrerlo con urgencia», concluye el comunicado de la Comisión Directiva de APJ Gas.

title: Se encadenaron frente a la Catedral para exigir la libertad de Milton Tolomeo y Eneas Gallo
content:
Este jueves, integrantes de la Coordinadora por la Libertad de los Presos Políticos realizaron una acción de protesta frente a la Catedral Metropolitana de Buenos Aires. Se encadenaron a una de las columnas de la Catedral para exigir la libertad inmediata de Milton Tolomeo y Eneas Gallo, detenidos por participar de la movilización contra la reforma laboral del 11 de febrero.

La intervención buscó visibilizar también el agravamiento de las condiciones de detención de ambos trabajadores en el Complejo Penitenciario de Marcos Paz. Denunciaron la falta de atención médica, la suspensión de actividades educativas y recreativas y las restricciones a las visitas de organismos de derechos humanos.




Milton Tolomeo inició una huelga de hambre el pasado 8 de noviembre

 para reclamar respuestas frente a las condiciones de alojamiento y las vulneraciones de derechos que sufren en el penal.




El encarcelamiento de Milton y Eneas se inscribe en una política de criminalización de la protesta social que busca disciplinar a quienes salen a la calle y enfrentan las políticas del Gobierno. Frente a la Catedral, el encadenamiento convirtió el reclamo en una acción directa contra el silencio y la indiferencia. La exigencia sigue siendo clara: ¡Libertad inmediata a Milton Tolomeo y Eneas Gallo! ¡Luchar no es delito!

title: El teatro se sumó a la ronda de las Madres de Plaza de Mayo Línea Fundadora
content:
Este jueves, la tradicional ronda de las Madres de Plaza de Mayo Línea Fundadora contó con la participación de integrantes de la obra “Fuerza Mayor”, del Frente Cultural Che Adelita, en el marco del festival homenaje “Briski en Escena”, dedicado al actor, director y dramaturgo Norman Briski. Como cada jueves, las Madres volvieron a ocupar la Plaza para sostener una lucha que lleva décadas y que enfrenta el olvido, la impunidad y las políticas de reconciliación con los responsables del genocidio.

Anarchism and art: Democracy in the cracks and on the margins. Mark Mattern. State University of New York Press, x+187 pp., ISBN: 978-1-4384-5920-2

Anarchism and Art takes its cue from British theorist Colin Ward’s observation that anarchist modes of social organizing can multiply and exist side-by-side with and ‘in spite of’ antithetical authoritarian societal ‘trends’ (p. 5). These practices are regarded as prefigurative: they model aspects of the future society anarchists seek to establish (p. 2). As such, anarchists regard them as powerful tools for revolutionizing the entire political, social, and economic order in times of upheaval (Gordon, 2007, p. 38). We have an unfolding example of what this entails in northern Syria, where anarchists have seized territory in three decentralized ‘cantons’ and are remodeling society based, in part, on anti-sexist organizing pioneered by fighters in the People’s Defence Forces and Women’s Defence Units (Strangers in a Tangled Wilderness, 2015, pp. 33–35). However, perusing Anarchism and Art for a discussion of prefiguration’s role in anti-state social transformation is a futile exercise. ‘Revolution’ does not even make it to the index.

Instead, Mattern subsumes anarchist modes of prefiguation within a ‘participatory democracy’ model of social change that ‘does not advocate the complete abolition of the state’ (p. 29). Over a page and a half, he sketches out his hypothetical program for reconstructing society along ‘participatory democracy’ lines, effectively purging anarchism’s anti-statist history and principles from his framework (pp. 21–22). This echoes the argumentative style of philosopher Simon Critchley, who, with a cursory nod toward contemporary anarchist-inspired activism, has coined his own hypothetical formulation, ‘neo-anarchism,’ to encapsulate a ‘politics at a distance from the state’ perpetually incapable of superseding what it opposes, a formulation Critchley champions in his much-praised statement, Infinitively Demanding, as the only option for ‘new social mobilizations’ (Critchley, 2008, p. 148).

What we have, then, is a study that must, perforce, decouple its field of inquiry from post-statist ends to make its case. Accordingly, Mattern gently nudges the movement’s revolutionary ambitions regarding ‘state and capital’ to the sidelines, suggesting that ‘in the last several decades’ anarchists have ‘broadened’ their ‘focus’ to encompass other pressing matters, notably animal rights, the environmental crisis, patriarchy, white supremacy, speciesism, and heterosexism (p. 30). In fact, anarchists have long engaged with such issues, and the implication that they are now treated as spheres of domination apart from ‘state and capital’ is disingenuous (Gelderloos, 2010); but on the plus side, putting ‘state and capital’ in its place helps grease the elision of ‘anarchism’ with ‘participatory democracy.’ In short, Mattern’s book should be entitled Participatory Democracy and Art. However, in the absence of a ‘participatory democracy’ social movement or any evidence that the theory he promotes has impacted the arts under discussion, we have only a ‘sleight of hand’ exercise.

The analysis of the ‘popular’ art practices he consigns to the ‘cracks and margins’ of society – Chapter 3 ‘DIY (Do It Yourself) Punk Music’; Chapter 4 ‘Poetry Slam’; Chapter 5 ‘Graffiti and Street Art’; and Chapter 6 ‘Flash Mobs’ – is sieved, formulaically, through four questions:

What form (s) of social organization and political action does this popular art form model? How does it challenge domination while increasing capacity? What does it say about equality and freedom? And, in each case, how does it prefigure a more democratic future? (pp. 37–38)

To this end, each chapter is divided into subsections (social organization; political action; power; equality; and freedom), presumably for ease of comparison. But a disquieting sense of de´ja` vu animates the discussion. For example, in Chapter 3 ‘DIY (Do It Yourself) Punk Music,’ under the subheading, ‘social organization,’ we learn ‘the highly decentralized and extensively networked world of DIY punk music closely resembles the rhizomatic model of social organization characteristic of contemporary anarchism’ (p. 41). Turning to ‘social organization’ in Chapter 4 ‘Poetry Slam,’ we are told, ‘slam poetry resembles the rhizomatic model familiar to anarchists’ (p. 64). Flipping forward to the ‘freedom’ subheading in Chapter 5 ‘Graffiti and Street Art,’ we discover ‘the kind of freedom embraced by anarchists requires a capacity for critical consciousness and autonomous choice’ (p. 98). Ditto for ‘freedom’ in Chapter 6 ‘Flash Mobs,’ which announces, ‘critical consciousness is essential for anarchist and participatory democratic understandings of freedom and autonomy’ (p. 121). Hitting reverse, the ‘power’ subheading in Chapter 6: ‘Flash Mobs,’ proclaims ‘flash mobs challenge the established, conventional order that is structured and controlled by state and corporate power’ (p. 113) while, in Chapter 5 ‘Graffiti and Street Art,’ under ‘power,’ graffiti and street art ‘represent direct, explicit attacks on capital and the state and their control over urban public space’ (p. 91). These are broad-brush generalizations that belie reality, as Mattern frequently concedes.

For example, graffiti and street art are not immune to commodification (pp. 100–102); businesses mobilize flash mobs to market products (p. 118); slam poets have courted corporate sponsorship (p. 75); and the punk rock scene has serious gender-inequality issues to work through (p. 55). These and other fissures cast doubt on Anarchism and Art’s equation of modes of art production with a singular political tradition, even if there are powerful anarchizing currents, the British punk rock group Crass being a case in point (pp. 44–46).

Mattern does make a convincing case for the value of prefigurative activism and the ways in which anarchist theory and practice pivots on radicalizing everyday life. His opening chapter on ‘Anarchism and Democracy’ also mounts a convincing critique of liberal democratic institutions and their connivance with capitalism while outlining, by way of contrast, how anarchism’s grassroots activism expands the range of democratic expression (pp. 17–38). That said, social revolution is central to anarchism’s radicalization of culture, including the arts: Mattern’s study flounders because he refuses to probe the implications.

Critchley, S. (2008) Infinitely Demanding: Ethics of Commitment, Politics of Resistance (p. 2008). London: Verso Press.

Gelderloos, P. (2010) Anarchy Works: Examples of Anarchist Ideas in Practice. Oakland, CA: Ardent Press.

Gordon, U. (2007) Anarchy Alive!: Anti-Authoritarian Politics from Practice to Theory. London: Pluto Press.

Strangers in a Tangled Wilderness (ed.). (2015) A Small Key can Open a Large Door: The Rojava Revolution. San Bernardino, CA: Combustion Books.
